fact_bis: Ang mga sulod nga planeta batoon tungod sa init duol sa Adlaw, metal ug bato ra ang nagpabiling solido, samtang sa bugnaw nga layo nga bahin ang dagkong gas giant nakatigom og daghang gas ug yelo.

q: What makes the Tañon Strait in the Philippines a popular destination for tourists?
options: It is home to many dolphins and whales, making dolphin watching popular there.
It has the largest coral reef in the Philippines, attracting scuba divers.
It is where the most powerful typhoons enter the Philippine archipelago.
It is a protected area where endangered sea turtles lay their eggs.
explanation: The Tañon Strait is home to many dolphins and whales, which is why dolphin watching is popular there.
fact_tl: Ang Kipot ng Tañon ay tahanan ng maraming lumba-lumba (dolphin) at balyena, kaya sikat doon ang dolphin watching.
fact_bis: Ang Kanal sa Tañon puy-anan sa daghang lumba-lumba (dolphin) ug balyena, mao nga sikat didto ang dolphin watching.

q: How do millipedes help Philippine forests?
options: They eat and crush fallen leaves so nutrients return to the soil.
They dig deep burrows that let rainwater reach the tree roots.
They prey on termites that would otherwise damage the trees.
They carry seeds on their bodies to help plants spread across the forest.
explanation: Millipedes eat and crush leaf litter on the forest floor, preventing it from building up and helping nutrients return to the soil.
fact_tl: Sa mga gubat sa Pilipinas, makapal ang nahuhulog na dahon sa lupa. Tinutulungan ng millipede na kainin at durugin ang mga ito, kaya hindi naiipon ang basura at bumabalik ang sustansya sa lupa.
fact_bis: Sa mga lasang sa Pilipinas, baga ang nahulog nga dahon sa yuta. Ang millipede motabang sa pagkaon ug pagdugmok niini, mao nga dili magtapok ang basura ug mobalik ang sustansya sa yuta.

q: Where is the tikling bird often seen?
options: In rice fields, grasslands, and wet areas
In dense mountain forests far from water
On rocky ocean cliffs near the sea
In dry desert-like lowland regions
explanation: The tikling is often seen walking in rice fields, grasslands, and wet areas.
fact_tl: Ang tikling ay madalas makita na naglalakad sa mga palayan, damuhan, at basang lugar.
fact_bis: Ang tikling kanunay makita nga naglakaw sa kaumahan sa humay, sagbutan, ug basa nga mga dapit.

q: What makes the map on your phone able to show exactly where you are?
options: GPS satellites circling Earth that send signals down to your phone
A radio tower in every city that tracks phone locations
Underground cables that measure the vibrations of your footsteps
A built-in compass that connects to the internet for updates
explanation: GPS satellites orbit Earth and send signals to phones, allowing map apps to pinpoint your exact location.
fact_tl: Ang mapa sa telepono na nagsasabi kung nasaan ka ay gumagana dahil sa mga GPS satellite na umiikot sa Earth at nagpapadala ng senyas pababa.
fact_bis: Ang mapa sa telepono nga nagpakita kon asa ka molihok tungod sa mga GPS satellite nga naglibot sa Earth ug nagpadala ug senyas paubos.

q: Why does the left side of your brain control your right hand?
options: The nerves leaving the brain cross over on their way down the body.
The brain is positioned slightly to the right, so it naturally reaches the left side.
The right hand is stronger and needs to be connected to the more powerful left brain.
Blood flows from the left brain directly to the right arm, carrying nerve signals.
explanation: The nerves from the brain cross over as they travel down the body, so the left brain commands the right hand and the right brain commands the left hand.
fact_tl: Ang mga nerbiyong nagmumula sa utak ay nagkukurus pababa sa katawan, kaya ang kaliwang utak ang nag-uutos sa kanang kamay at kabaligtaran.
fact_bis: Ang mga nerbiyos nga gikan sa utak magkurus paubos sa lawas, mao nga ang walang utak maoy nagmando sa tuong kamot ug sukwahi.

q: Why does cogon grass spread so easily even after a fire?
options: Its roots survive underground, allowing it to regrow quickly after fire.
It releases seeds by exploding during the fire so they scatter far.
Its leaves are fireproof so the whole plant survives the flames.
Insects carry cogon seeds away from the fire to new open land.
explanation: Cogon grass spreads easily after fires because its roots survive underground and can regrow on open, sunny land.
fact_tl: Ang cogon ay isang matigas na damo na mabilis tumubo sa mga bukas at maaraw na lupa, at madali itong dumami pagkatapos ng sunog dahil nakaligtas ang mga ugat nito sa ilalim ng lupa.
fact_bis: Ang kugon usa ka gahi nga sagbot nga paspas motubo sa abli ug init nga yuta, ug dali kini modaghan human sa sunog kay maluwas ang mga gamot niini ilalom sa yuta.

q: Which organ do we use for the sense of hearing?
options: Ears
Eyes
Nose
Tongue
explanation: We use our ears for the sense of hearing, which lets us detect sounds.
fact_tl: Ginagamit natin ang mga tainga para sa pandinig, ang pandamang nakakarinig ng tunog.
fact_bis: Gigamit nato ang atong mga dalunggan alang sa pandungog, ang igbalati nga makadungog og tingog.

q: Why must a patient's blood type be checked before receiving a blood transfusion?
options: The blood types must match to make the transfusion safe.
Different blood types carry different vitamins that may not be needed.
Matching blood type is only required for children, not adults.
Checking blood type speeds up the process but is not strictly required.
explanation: Before a transfusion, blood types must be matched because giving the wrong type of blood can be dangerous.
fact_tl: Bago bigyan ng dugo ang isang pasyente, kailangang tugma ang uri ng dugo upang maging ligtas ito.
fact_bis: Sa dili pa hatagan og dugo ang usa ka pasyente, kinahanglan magkatugma ang klase sa dugo aron luwas kini.

q: About how long does a frog usually live?
options: 5 to 10 years
1 to 2 years
20 to 30 years
Less than one year
explanation: A frog usually lives about 5 to 10 years.
fact_tl: Ang isang palaka (frog) ay karaniwang nabubuhay nang mga 5 hanggang 10 taon.
fact_bis: Ang baki (frog) kasagaran mabuhi og mga 5 ngadto sa 10 ka tuig.

q: What material do paper wasps use to build their nest?
options: Chewed wood mixed with saliva, making a paper-like material
Mud and clay gathered near a river or pond
Wax produced from glands in their own body
Leaves glued together with a sticky liquid from flowers
explanation: Paper wasps chew wood and mix it with their saliva to create a paper-like material, which they use to build their hexagonal-celled nests.
fact_tl: Ang paper wasp ay gumagawa ng pugad mula sa napag-usap na kahoy at laway na gumagawa ng isang uri ng papel—ang mga selula ng pugad ay hexagonal tulad ng sa bubuyog.
fact_bis: Ang paper wasp nagbuhat og pugad gikan sa gikuya nga kahoy ug laway nga nagbuhat og klase nga papel—ang mga selula sa pugad hexagonal, sama sa sa honeycomb sa bubuyog.

q: What does the prefix "nano" mean in scientific measurement?
options: One billionth
One millionth
One thousandth
One hundredth
explanation: The prefix "nano" means one billionth (1/1,000,000,000), so a nanometer is one billionth of a meter.
fact_tl: Ang unlaping "nano" ay nangangahulugang ika-isang-bilyon (1/1,000,000,000 o 0.000000001).
fact_bis: Ang prefix nga "nano" nagpasabot og usa-ka-bilyon-ka-bahin (1/1,000,000,000 o 0.000000001).

q: What natural spectacle is Mount Pulag famous for at sunrise?
options: A spectacular sea of clouds over its alpine grassland summit
A bubbling crater lake that glows at night
A waterfall that is only visible during the rainy season
Colorful flowering trees that bloom only on the summit
explanation: The summit of Mount Pulag is covered by cool alpine grassland and is famous for the breathtaking sea of clouds often visible at sunrise.
fact_tl: Ang tuktok ng Mount Pulag ay tinatakpan ng malamig na alpine grassland at sikat sa napakagandang 'sea of clouds' na karaniwang makikita sa pagsikat ng araw.
fact_bis: Ang tuktok sa Mount Pulag gitabonan sa bugnaw nga alpine grassland ug bantog sa makapahingangha nga 'sea of clouds' nga kasagaran makita sa pagsidlak sa adlaw.

q: Which continent is unique because it is also a single country?
options: Australia
Antarctica
Africa
Europe
explanation: Australia is special because it is both a continent and a single country, the only one in the world with this distinction.
fact_tl: Ang Australia ay natatangi dahil ito ay isang kontinente at isang bansa rin.
fact_bis: Ang Australia talagsaon kay kini usa ka kontinente ug usa usab ka nasud.

q: Who first used the word 'cell' to describe tiny spaces in living things, and when?
options: Robert Hooke in 1665, when he looked at cork under a microscope
Louis Pasteur in 1850, when he studied bacteria in broth
Anton van Leeuwenhoek in 1700, when he saw tiny moving creatures in water
Charles Darwin in 1859, when he studied island plants and animals
explanation: Robert Hooke first used the word 'cell' in 1665 after seeing tiny empty spaces in cork under a microscope.
fact_tl: Si Robert Hooke ang unang gumamit ng salitang 'cell' noong 1665 nang makita niya ang mga maliliit na puwang sa balat ng tapon (cork) sa ilalim ng mikroskopyo.
fact_bis: Si Robert Hooke mao ang unang migamit sa pulong nga 'cell' niadtong 1665 dihang nakita niya ang gagmayng bakanteng espasyo sa cork ilalom sa mikroskopyo.

q: If you eat very salty food, will your blood become much saltier?
options: No — the body carefully controls the salt level in blood and removes extra salt in urine.
Yes — blood becomes saltier whenever you eat salty food.
Only if you eat salty food every day for a week.
Yes, but the extra salt leaves the blood after a night of sleep.
explanation: The body carefully regulates the amount of salt in the blood and removes any excess through urine, so eating salty food does not simply make your blood saltier.
fact_tl: May mga nag-iisip na maalat ang dugo dahil sa asin na kinakain natin. Totoo ngang may kaunting asin ang dugo, pero hindi ito basta dumarami kapag kumain ka ng maalat. Maingat na binabantayan ng katawan ang tamang dami ng asin sa dugo at inaalis ang sobra sa ihi.
fact_bis: Naay mga nagtuo nga parat ang dugo tungod sa asin nga atong gikaon. Tinuod nga naay gamay nga asin ang dugo, apan dili lang kini modaghan kung mokaon kag parat. Maampingong gibantayan sa lawas ang husto nga asin sa dugo ug ginakuha ang sobra pinaagi sa ihi.

q: What happens to an observer who is in the penumbra during an eclipse?
options: They see only a partial eclipse because the penumbra is the lighter outer part of the shadow.
They see a total eclipse because the penumbra is the darkest central shadow.
They see no eclipse at all because the penumbra is completely outside the shadow.
They see a ring of fire because the penumbra acts like a lens focusing sunlight.
explanation: The penumbra is the lighter, outer part of the shadow during an eclipse, so people standing in it see only a partial eclipse.
fact_tl: Sa panahon ng eclipse, ang shadow ng Moon o Earth ay may dalawang bahagi: ang gitna at pinaka-madilim na bahagi (umbra) at ang mas maliwanag na panlabas na bahagi (penumbra). Ang mga tao na nasa penumbra ay nakakakita ng partial eclipse lamang.
fact_bis: Panahon sa eclipse, ang anino sa Moon o Yuta adunay duha ka bahin: ang sentro, pinakangitngit nga bahin (umbra) ug ang mas hayag nga panlabas nga bahin (penumbra). Ang mga tawo nga anaa sa penumbra nakakita lamang sa partial eclipse.

q: Which of the following can also cause a tsunami besides an earthquake?
options: A volcanic eruption underwater
A strong typhoon hitting land
Heavy rainfall over the ocean
A very high tide during full moon
explanation: Besides earthquakes, a volcanic eruption or a big underwater landslide can also start a tsunami.
fact_tl: Bukod sa lindol, maaari ring magbunsod ng tsunami ang pagsabog ng bulkan o malaking pagguho ng lupa sa ilalim ng dagat.
fact_bis: Gawas sa linog, ang pagbuto sa bulkan o dakong dahili sa yuta ilawom sa dagat makahimo usab ug tsunami.

q: How are the bodies of starfish and sea urchins arranged?
options: Divided into two equal left and right halves like a butterfly
Divided into four parts pointing north, south, east, and west
Divided into five matching parts arranged in a circle around the center
Divided into eight equal sections spiraling outward
explanation: The bodies of starfish and sea urchins are divided into five matching parts arranged in a circle around the center, called five-fold radial symmetry.
fact_tl: Ang katawan ng starfish at tihik ay nahahati sa limang magkakaparehong bahagi na nakaayos paikot mula sa gitna, isang anyo na tinatawag na limang-bahaging simetriya.
fact_bis: Ang lawas sa starfish ug tihik gibahin sa lima ka managsama nga bahin nga gihan-ay palibot gikan sa tunga, usa ka porma nga gitawag og lima-ka-bahin nga radial symmetry.

q: Why does the makahiya plant fold its leaves when touched?
options: Its leaves have sharp spines that curl inward to protect the plant
A tiny joint called the pulvinus pumps water out, making that side go soft so the leaf folds
The leaf cells release a chemical that shrinks the leaf instantly
Tiny hairs on the leaf send an electric signal that pulls the leaf closed
explanation: When the makahiya is touched, the pulvinus joint at the base of the leaf pumps water out of one side, making that side go soft and causing the leaf to fold.
fact_tl: May maliit na 'kasukasuan' sa puno ng bawat dahon ng makahiya na tinatawag na pulvinus. Kapag ginalaw mo ang halaman, pinapalabas nito ang tubig mula sa isang panig ng kasukasuan, kaya lumalambot ang panig na iyon at tumitiklop ang dahon.
fact_bis: Sa pundasyon sa matag dahon sa makahiya naa gamay nga lutahan nga gitawag og pulvinus. Kon hikapon ang tanom, ipagawas niini ang tubig gikan sa usa ka kilid sa lutahan, mao nga muhumok kana nga kilid ug mutiklop ang dahon.

q: Where does a firefly get the energy it needs to glow?
options: From absorbing sunlight through its wings during the day
From the energy it gets from food, which its body uses to make cold light
From a chemical reaction with water that it drinks
From electricity stored in special cells near its tail
explanation: A firefly gets its energy to glow from the food it eats, and its body uses that energy to run the reaction that makes cold light.
fact_tl: Saan kumukuha ng lakas ang alitaptap para kuminang? Mula sa enerhiya na nakuha nito sa pagkain, parang tayo rin. Ginagamit ng katawan nito ang enerhiyang ito para paganahin ang reaksyong gumagawa ng malamig na ilaw. Kaya ang pagkain ay nagiging ilaw sa kanyang katawan.
fact_bis: Asa magkuha og kusog ang aninipot aron mosiga? Gikan sa enerhiya nga makuha niini sa pagkaon, sama nato. Ang lawas niini mogamit niini nga enerhiya aron paganahon ang reaksyon nga maghimo og bugnaw nga kahayag. Busa ang pagkaon mahimong kahayag sa iyang lawas.

q: What special ability helps the eagle spot prey from very far away?
options: Its very large wings that let it fly silently above prey
Its very sharp eyesight that lets it see prey from a great distance
Its sensitive hearing that picks up tiny sounds on the ground
Its ability to smell prey even when hidden under leaves
explanation: The eagle has very sharp eyesight, so it can spot prey from very far away.
fact_tl: Napakatalas ng paningin ng agila kaya nakikita nito ang biktima mula sa napakalayo.
fact_bis: Tin-aw kaayo ang panan-aw sa agila mao nga makita niini ang biktima gikan sa layo kaayo.

q: In what direction does centripetal force point when an object moves in a circle?
options: Away from the center, outward along the path
Along the edge of the circle in the direction of motion
Toward the center of the circle
Straight up against the pull of gravity
explanation: Centripetal force is directed toward the center of a circle, which keeps an object following its curved, circular path.
fact_tl: Ang centripetal force ay ang puwersang nakaturo papunta sa gitna ng bilog, at ito ang humihila sa isang bagay para manatili sa pabilog nitong landas.
fact_bis: Ang centripetal force mao ang puwersa nga nagtumong ngadto sa tunga sa lingin, ug mao kini ang nagbira sa butang aron magpabilin sa iyang kurba, lingin nga agianan.

q: How does nitrogen fixed by lightning eventually reach animals and people?
options: Lightning sends nitrogen directly into the bloodstream of nearby animals
Animals breathe in nitrogen gas that lightning releases into the air
Animals eat plants that were grown with the nitrogen, and then people eat those animals or vegetables
Lightning strikes water and dissolves nitrogen into rivers where fish absorb it
explanation: Nitrogen fixed by lightning helps plants grow, and when animals eat those plants and people eat animals or vegetables, the nitrogen travels through the whole food chain.
fact_tl: Ang tulong ng kidlat ay hindi lang para sa halaman. Kapag kumain ang hayop ng halamang malusog dahil sa nitrogen, napupunta rin sa kanila ang sustansya. At kapag kumain ang tao ng gulay o hayop, naabot din sa atin ito. Kaya ang maliit na nitrogen mula sa kidlat ay umiikot sa buong food chain.
fact_bis: Ang tabang sa kilat dili lang para sa tanom. Kon mokaon ang hayop og himsog nga tanom nga mitubo tungod sa nitrogen, ang sustansya moadto usab kanila. Ug kon mokaon ang tawo og utanon o hayop, moabot usab kini kanato. Busa ang gamay nga nitrogen gikan sa kilat molibot sa tibuok food chain.

q: In what year did Valentina Tereshkova become the first woman in space?
explanation: Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space in the year 1963.
fact_tl: Si Valentina Tereshkova ang naging unang babae sa kalawakan noong taong 1963.
fact_bis: Si Valentina Tereshkova nahimong unang babaye sa kawanangan niadtong tuig 1963.

q: What does a barnacle actually eat when it attaches itself to a whale?
options: The skin and blubber of the whale
Tiny things floating in the water, not the whale
Parasites and dead cells on the whale's skin
Food scraps that fall from the whale's mouth
explanation: A barnacle eats tiny things floating in the water — not the whale — and just hitches a ride to reach clean water full of food.
fact_tl: Maraming akala na kinakain ng barnacle ang whale na kinakapitan nito—pero karaniwang HINDI! Ang barnacle ay kumakain ng maliliit na lumulutang sa tubig, hindi ng whale. Nakikisakay lang ito para madala sa malinis na tubig na maraming pagkain.
fact_bis: Daghan ang naghunahuna nga ang barnacle mukaon sa balyena nga iyang gikuptan—apan kasagaran DILI! Ang barnacle mukaon sa gagmay nga naglutaw sa tubig, dili sa balyena. Nagsakay lang kini aron madala sa limpyo nga tubig nga puno sa pagkaon.

q: Which best describes the eyes of a horseshoe crab?
options: It has only two large eyes on the front of its head like most crabs
It has no eyes at all and finds food by smell
It has many eyes, including two large eyes on its shell plus smaller ones that sense light
It has a single large eye on the top of its shell
explanation: The horseshoe crab has many eyes, including two large eyes on its shell plus smaller ones that sense light.
fact_tl: Ang horseshoe crab ay may napakaraming mata, kasama ang dalawang malalaking mata sa balat at iba pang maliliit na nakakaramdam ng liwanag.
fact_bis: Ang horseshoe crab adunay daghang mata, lakip ang duha ka dagkong mata sa kabhang ug uban pang gagmay nga makabati sa kahayag.

q: What does the female kalaw do inside her nest after sealing herself in?
options: She builds a second inner nest from feathers and waits for eggs to hatch alone
She stays sealed inside with only a small slit so the male can feed her
She calls loudly through the opening to attract more males to guard the tree
She breaks out after two days to find food while the male takes over incubating
explanation: The female kalaw seals herself inside the nest with mud, leaving only a small slit so the male can feed her.
fact_tl: Isinasara ng babaeng kalaw ang sarili sa loob ng pugad gamit ang putik, na nag-iiwan lamang ng maliit na siwang para pakainin siya ng lalaki.
fact_bis: Ang bayeng kalaw mosira sa iyang kaugalingon sulod sa salag gamit ang lapok, nga magbilin lang og gamayng liki aron pakan-on siya sa laki.

q: Why can running or jumping warm you up the same way shivering does?
options: Exercise raises your blood pressure, which forces warm blood to the skin faster
Both shivering and on-purpose movement use muscles to produce heat
Running increases your breathing rate, which releases warm air that heats the body
Exercise burns stored fat, and the melting fat releases heat into the blood
explanation: Shivering and on-purpose movement like running or jumping both use muscles to generate heat, which is why being active can warm you up and even stop shivering.
fact_tl: Parehong gumagawa ng init ang nginig at ang sadyang paggalaw tulad ng pagtakbo o pagtalon — pareho silang gumagamit ng kalamnan. Kaya kapag malamig, kusa kang gumagalaw para magpainit, at minsan tumitigil ang nginig kapag aktibo ka.
fact_bis: Ang kurog ug ang tinuyong paglihok sama sa pagdagan o paglukso parehong maghimo og kainit — parehong mogamit og kaunoran. Mao nga kon bugnaw, kusog kang molihok aron magpainit, ug usahay mohunong ang kurog kon aktibo na ka.

q: When sugar dissolves in water, what is the sugar called?
options: The solvent
The mixture
The solute
The solution
explanation: When something dissolves, the substance that dissolves (like sugar) is called the solute, and the liquid that dissolves it (like water) is the solvent.
fact_tl: Kapag may natutunaw, ang sangkap na natutunaw ay tinatawag na solute at ang likido na tumutunaw nito ay solvent.
fact_bis: Kung adunay matunaw, ang butang nga matunaw gitawag og solute ug ang likido nga magtunaw niini mao ang solvent.

q: Why does the Philippines experience so many volcanic eruptions and earthquakes?
options: It is located on a large flat plain where soft rock cracks easily under the weight of islands
It is located in the Ring of Fire, where tectonic plates meet in the Pacific
It is close to the equator, where the Sun's heat causes rocks to expand and break
It has many rivers that erode the ground and weaken the land beneath volcanoes
explanation: The Philippines is located in the Ring of Fire, an area in the Pacific full of active volcanoes and frequent earthquakes due to the meeting of tectonic plates.
fact_tl: Matatagpuan ang Pilipinas sa tinatawag na Ring of Fire, isang lugar sa Pasipiko na puno ng mga aktibong bulkan at madalas na lindol dahil sa pagtatagpo ng mga plaka ng lupa.
fact_bis: Ang Pilipinas nahimutang sa gitawag og Ring of Fire, usa ka lugar sa Pasipiko nga puno sa mga aktibong bulkan ug kanunay nga lindol tungod sa pakigtagbo sa mga tectonic plate.

q: What are the smaller tremors that usually follow a strong earthquake called?
options: Foreshocks
Tremors
Aftershocks
Seismic waves
explanation: After a strong earthquake, there are usually smaller follow-up tremors called aftershocks.
fact_tl: Pagkatapos ng malakas na lindol, kadalasang may mga sumusunod na mas mahinang pagyanig na tinatawag na aftershocks.
fact_bis: Human sa kusog nga linog, kasagaran adunay mosunod nga mas huyang nga mga pag-uyog nga gitawag og aftershocks.

q: What causes floating plastic to collect into large patches in certain parts of the ocean?
options: Strong underwater volcanoes that push plastic toward the surface in one area
Whales and large fish that herd plastic into groups while feeding
Large circular ocean currents called gyres that concentrate floating plastic
Seasonal monsoon rains that wash plastic from rivers into one region
explanation: Ocean gyres — large circular currents — concentrate floating plastic from around the world into large patches like the Great Pacific Garbage Patch.
fact_tl: Ang mga ocean gyre — malalaking circular na agos — ay nagtitipon ng mga floating plastic mula sa buong mundo sa malalaking patch; ang Great Pacific Garbage Patch ay mas malaki pa sa Texas at nagbabanta sa kaligtasan ng mga hayop ng dagat kasama na ang mga Philippine marine species.
fact_bis: Ang mga ocean gyre — dagkong circular nga mga agos — nagtipon sa nagutay-utay nga plastik gikan sa tibuok kalibutan ngadto sa dagkong mga patch; ang Great Pacific Garbage Patch mas dako pa kaysa Texas ug nagbanta sa kaligtasan sa mga hayop sa dagat naglakip sa Philippine marine species.

q: How does a sea sponge filter water to get its food?
options: It traps small fish using sticky threads on its outer surface
It waits for dead animals to drift inside its hollow body and absorbs them
It uses thousands of tiny cells called choanocytes to pump and filter more than ten times its own volume of water per hour
It releases a poison that stuns nearby plankton, then absorbs them through its skin
explanation: A sponge uses thousands of tiny cells called choanocytes to filter more than ten times its own volume of water per hour, removing bacteria and organic particles.
fact_tl: Ang isang espongha (sponge) ay kayang mag-filter ng higit sa sampung beses ng sarili nitong volume ng tubig kada oras sa pamamagitan ng libu-libong maliit na selulang tinatawag na choanocyte.
fact_bis: Ang usa ka espongha makahimo og pag-filter labaw sa napulo ka beses sa kaugalingon niining gidak-on sa tubig matag oras pinaagi sa liboan ka gamay nga selula nga gitawag choanocyte, nagkuha og bakterya ug organic nga mga tipik gikan sa tubig.

q: What happens if too many tuna are caught from the sea?
options: Tuna grow faster to replace the missing fish within a few months
Other smaller fish take over and the ocean stays balanced
Their numbers can run out, so people must care for the tuna in the sea
The remaining tuna migrate to deeper water and are impossible to catch again
explanation: If too many tuna are caught, their numbers can run out, so people must care for the tuna in the sea.
fact_tl: Kapag sobra-sobra ang paghuli ng tuna, maaaring maubos ito, kaya kailangang pangalagaan ang dami ng tuna sa dagat.
fact_bis: Kung sobra ang pagdakop sa tuna, mahimo kining maubos, busa kinahanglan atimanon ang gidaghanon sa tuna sa dagat.

q: Which of the following is a defense that prey animals use to avoid being eaten?
options: Growing sharp teeth to bite predators before being caught
Producing loud sounds to call other predators away
Blending into their surroundings so predators cannot see them
Releasing a scent that attracts larger animals to protect them
explanation: Many prey animals have defenses such as running fast, blending into their color, or hiding to avoid being eaten.
fact_tl: Maraming prey ang may depensa gaya ng bilis tumakbo, pagkukubli sa kulay, o pagtatago para hindi makain.
fact_bis: Daghang prey adunay depensa sama sa kapaspas modagan, pagpasibo sa kolor, o pagtago aron dili kaonon.

q: How is osmosis different from regular diffusion?
options: Osmosis moves any dissolved substance, while diffusion moves only water
Osmosis requires heat energy, while diffusion happens without any energy
Osmosis is only about water moving through a membrane, while diffusion can involve other substances too
Osmosis moves substances from low to high concentration, while diffusion moves them from high to low
explanation: Osmosis is a special kind of diffusion that is only about water moving through a membrane.
fact_tl: Ang osmosis ay isang espesyal na uri ng diffusion na para lang sa tubig na dumadaan sa isang lamad.
fact_bis: Ang osmosis usa ka linain nga matang sa diffusion nga para lang sa tubig nga moagi sa usa ka lamad.

q: What is groundwater?
options: Water that forms when clouds release moisture during heavy rain
Water stored in large lakes and rivers on the surface of the land
Water that collects in the spaces and cracks of rocks and soil beneath the ground
Water that freezes inside glaciers and slowly melts in warm seasons
explanation: Groundwater is water that collects in the spaces and cracks of rocks and soil beneath the ground.
fact_tl: Ang groundwater ay tubig na naipon sa mga butas at siwang ng mga bato at lupa sa ilalim ng lupa.
fact_bis: Ang groundwater mao ang tubig nga natipon sa mga lungag ug liki sa mga bato ug yuta ilawom sa yuta.

q: Why do stars look like tiny dots in the sky even though many are bigger than our Sun?
options: Stars are actually small, about the size of a city, but they glow very brightly
The Earth's atmosphere bends the starlight and squeezes it into a dot shape
Stars are so far away that they look small even though many are bigger than the Sun
Stars only show their full size during a solar eclipse when the Moon blocks the Sun
explanation: Stars look tiny because they are so far away — in truth many of them are even bigger than our Sun, which is already over a million times bigger than Earth.
fact_tl: Maling akala na maliliit lang ang mga bituin dahil parang tuldok sila sa langit. Ang totoo, marami sa kanila ay mas malaki pa kaysa Araw natin — at ang Araw ay milyon-milyong beses na mas malaki kaysa Earth! Mukha lang silang maliit dahil sobrang layo nila sa atin.
fact_bis: Sayop ang pagtuo nga gagmay ra ang mga bituon tungod kay murag tulbok sila sa langit. Ang tinuod, daghan kanila mas dako pa kaysa atong Adlaw — ug ang Adlaw kay milyon-milyon ka pilo nga mas dako kaysa Earth! Murag gamay ra sila tan-awon tungod kay layo kaayo sila kanato.

q: How do termites actually damage wood?
options: They inject a poison into the wood that makes it rot from the inside
They carry acid from the soil that slowly dissolves the wood fibers
They damage wood by eating it and tunneling through the inside, not by using any poison
They spray water onto the wood to soften it, then scrape it away with their claws
explanation: Termites damage wood simply because they eat it and tunnel through the inside — not because of any poison.
fact_tl: May mga nag-aakalang nilalason ng anay ang kahoy para masira. Hindi totoo iyan. Sinisira ng anay ang kahoy dahil kinakain nila ito at inuukit ang loob, hindi dahil sa lason.
fact_bis: Adunay naghunahuna nga gihiloan sa anay ang kahoy aron madaot. Dili kana tinuod. Madaot ang kahoy kay gikaon kini sa anay ug gibangagan ang sulod, dili tungod sa hilo.

q: Can a cold-blooded animal like a lizard have warm blood?
options: No, their blood is always cold because their bodies cannot produce any heat at all
Yes, after basking in the sun their blood can become warm too
Yes, but only during winter when they need extra warmth to survive
No, their blood stays at the same temperature no matter what the weather is like
explanation: Cold-blooded animals do not always have cold blood; after basking in the sun, their blood can become warm too.
fact_tl: Hindi laging malamig ang dugo ng mga hayop na malamig ang dugo; pagkatapos magbilad sa araw, ang dugo nila ay maaaring maging mainit din.
fact_bis: Dili kanunay bugnaw ang dugo sa mga mananap nga bugnaw ug dugo; human magpainit sa adlaw, ang ilang dugo mahimong init usab.

q: What happens to the leftover egg whites when leche flan is made?
options: They are thrown away because leche flan only needs the yolks and whites spoil quickly
They are mixed back into the flan to add extra protein to the dessert
They are turned into meringue, macaroons, or added to other foods so nothing is wasted
They are dried in the sun and ground into powder for use as a thickener
explanation: Because leche flan uses egg yolks, the leftover egg whites are turned into meringue, macaroons, or added to other foods so nothing is wasted.
fact_tl: Dahil pula ng itlog ang ginagamit sa leche flan, maraming natitirang puti ng itlog; sa totoong kusina, ginagawa itong meringue, macaroons, o idinaragdag sa ibang pagkain para hindi masayang.
fact_bis: Tungod kay pula sa itlog ang gigamit sa leche flan, daghang sobra nga puti sa itlog; sa tinuod nga kusina himoon kini nga meringue, macaroons, o idugang sa ubang pagkaon aron walay masayang.

q: What title was given to Andres Bonifacio as leader of the Katipunan?
options: Presidente
Heneral
Supremo
Datu
explanation: Andres Bonifacio was known as the Supremo, the leader of the Katipunan.
fact_tl: Si Andres Bonifacio ay kilala bilang Supremo, ang pinuno ng Katipunan.
fact_bis: Si Andres Bonifacio nailhan isip Supremo, ang pangulo sa Katipunan.

q: What is the main role of sugar in the body?
options: It builds strong bones and teeth by providing calcium
It fights germs and protects the body from getting sick
It gives the body quick energy for daily activities
It carries oxygen through the blood to all the body's cells
explanation: Sugar gives the body quick energy, like fuel for our daily activities.
fact_tl: Ang asukal ay nagbibigay ng mabilis na enerhiya sa katawan, parang gasolina para sa ating mga gawain.
fact_bis: Ang asukal naghatag og paspas nga kusog sa lawas, sama sa gasolina alang sa atong mga buluhaton.

q: What is the Ramon Magsaysay Award given for?
options: Outstanding performance in the Olympic Games by Filipino athletes
Creating the most popular Philippine film or television show of the year
Significant contributions to society, science, and public service by Filipinos and Asians
Earning the highest grades in a national science competition for students
explanation: The Ramon Magsaysay Award is a prestigious international prize given to Filipinos and Asians who have made significant contributions to society, science, and public service.
fact_tl: Ang Ramon Magsaysay Award ay isang prestihiyosong pandaigdigang gantimpala na naibigay sa mga Pilipino at Asyano na naging makabuluhang ambag sa lipunan, agham, at serbisyo publiko.
fact_bis: Ang Ramon Magsaysay Award usa ka prestihiyosong internasyonal nga ganti nga gihatag sa mga Pilipino ug Asyano nga nakahatod og makabulohang kontribusyon sa katilingban, siyensiya, ug serbisyo publiko.

q: How do decomposers like bacteria and fungi break down dead matter?
options: They swallow large chunks of dead matter and grind them up with hard teeth
They burn dead matter using heat from chemical reactions inside their cells
They release special juices called enzymes that dissolve dead matter into tiny pieces, then soak up the nutrients
They wrap dead matter in silk threads and wait for it to dissolve on its own over months
explanation: Decomposers release enzymes that dissolve dead matter into tiny pieces, then soak up the nutrients — they eat without ever biting.
fact_tl: Paano binubulok ng decomposers ang basura? Naglalabas sila ng mga enzyme na parang likido na natutunaw ang patay na bagay sa mas maliliit na piraso, tapos sinisipsip nila ang mga sustansya — kaya parang 'kumakain' sila nang hindi nangangagat.
fact_bis: Giunsa pagdunot sa decomposers ang basura? Mogawas sila og enzyme nga morag tubig nga molusaw sa patay nga butang ngadto sa gagmay nga tipik, dayon suyopon nila ang sustansya — busa morag 'mokaon' sila nga walay paak.

q: What plant does tapioca come from?
options: Sweet potato
Cassava
Corn
Sago palm
explanation: The tapioca pearls in milk tea are made from the starch of cassava.
fact_tl: Ang tapioca o sago na nasa milk tea ay gawa sa almirol ng kamoteng kahoy.
fact_bis: Ang tapioca o sago nga anaa sa milk tea hinimo gikan sa almirol sa balanghoy.

q: How many categories does the Saffir-Simpson scale use to measure typhoon strength?
options: Three categories, from weak to strong
Four categories, from 1 to 4
Five categories, from Category 1 to Category 5
Ten categories, from 1 to 10
explanation: The Saffir-Simpson scale has five categories, from Category 1 to Category 5.
fact_tl: Ang Saffir-Simpson scale ay may limang kategorya, mula Category 1 hanggang Category 5.
fact_bis: Ang Saffir-Simpson scale adunay lima ka kategorya, gikan sa Category 1 ngadto sa Category 5.

q: At what temperature does nitrogen freeze (or melt)?
options: -180 degrees Celsius
-273 degrees Celsius
-210 degrees Celsius
-100 degrees Celsius
explanation: Nitrogen melts (freezes) at -210 degrees Celsius.
fact_tl: Ang nitrogen ay natutunaw (nagyeyelo) sa -210 degrees Celsius.
fact_bis: Ang nitrogen matunaw (mugahi) sa -210 degrees Celsius.

q: Why does a fan make you feel cooler when you are sweating?
options: The fan blows cold air directly from the outside onto your skin
Moving air dries sweat faster on your skin, and as it dries it carries heat away
The fan lowers the temperature of the room so the air itself becomes cold
Moving air thickens the sweat on your skin so heat cannot escape as easily
explanation: Moving air from a fan dries sweat faster on your skin, and as sweat dries it carries heat away, cooling you down.
fact_tl: Mas mabilis kang lumalamig kapag may hanging dumadaloy gaya ng galing sa bentilador o aircon. Ito ay dahil mas mabilis matuyo ang pawis sa balat mo kapag may hangin, at habang natutuyo ito, dinadala nito ang init palayo.
fact_bis: Mas paspas ka mobugnaw kung adunay hangin nga moagos sama sa gikan sa bentilador o aircon. Tungod kini kay mas paspas momala ang singot sa imong panit kung adunay hangin, ug samtang momala kini, gidala niini ang kainit palayo.

q: Why is copper from copper ore used inside most electrical wires in our homes?
options: Copper is very flexible and can be stretched into very thin threads without breaking
Copper is the cheapest metal found in rocks, so it costs less than other materials
Electricity flows easily through copper, making it ideal for wires
Copper is lightweight and does not corrode when exposed to water
explanation: Copper ore gives us copper used in electric wires because electricity flows easily through copper.
fact_tl: Mula sa copper ore nakukuha ang tanso na ginagawang mga kable ng kuryente at tubo ng tubig. Madaling dumaloy ang kuryente sa tanso kaya ito ang laman ng karamihan ng mga kawad sa ating bahay.
fact_bis: Gikan sa copper ore makuha ang tumbaga nga gihimong mga kable sa kuryente ug tubo sa tubig. Sayon nga moagi ang kuryente sa tumbaga maong kini ang sulod sa kadaghanan sa mga kawad sa atong balay.

q: How do mangrove trees help protect the coast?
options: They produce sap that hardens the soil into rock so waves cannot break it apart
They grow very tall and block strong winds before the wind can push waves onto land
Their roots hold the soil in place so the coast does not wash away or erode
They absorb seawater through their leaves, lowering the sea level near the shore
explanation: Mangrove roots hold the soil in place so the coast does not wash away or erode.
fact_tl: Hinahawakan ng mga ugat ng bakawan ang lupa kaya hindi ito naaanod o nagguguho sa baybayin.
fact_bis: Ang mga gamot sa bakhaw maghupot sa yuta aron dili kini maanod o maguba ang baybayon.

q: Is it always true that a bigger country has more kinds of animals than a smaller one?
options: Yes, because more land always means more habitats and more species
Yes, because larger countries get more rainfall which feeds more plant and animal life
No, even small countries like the Philippines can be very rich in animal species because of their islands and climate
No, because large countries have colder climates that are harder for most animals to survive in
explanation: Even though the Philippines is small compared to other countries, its islands and climate make it very rich in animal species — bigger does not always mean more kinds of animals.
fact_tl: Akala ng iba, ang mas malaking bansa ay laging mas maraming uri ng hayop. Hindi ito palaging totoo. Kahit maliit ang Pilipinas kumpara sa ibang bansa, napakayaman pa rin natin dahil sa ating mga isla at klima.
fact_bis: Naghunahuna ang uban nga ang mas dakong nasod kanunay nga adunay daghang matang sa hayop. Dili kini kanunay tinuod. Bisan og gamay ang Pilipinas kumpara sa ubang nasod, dato gihapon ta tungod sa atong mga isla ug klima.

q: Who created the plum pudding model of the atom?
options: Ernest Rutherford
John Dalton
Niels Bohr
J.J. Thomson
explanation: J.J. Thomson created the plum pudding model of the atom in 1904.
fact_tl: Si J.J. Thomson ang gumawa ng 'plum pudding model' ng atom noong 1904.
fact_bis: Si J.J. Thomson maoy naghimo sa 'plum pudding model' sa atom niadtong 1904.

q: Were the flying and swimming reptiles that lived during the dinosaur age true dinosaurs?
options: Yes, all large reptiles living during that period are classified as dinosaurs
Yes, pterosaurs and mosasaurs are both types of dinosaur
No, they were a different group of reptiles and not true dinosaurs
No, only the very large ones like pterodactyls were not dinosaurs
explanation: The flying and swimming reptiles from the dinosaur age were not true dinosaurs but a different group of reptiles.
fact_tl: Ang mga lumilipad at lumalangoy na reptilya noong panahon ng dinosaur ay hindi talaga dinosaur kundi ibang uri ng reptilya.
fact_bis: Ang mga naglupad ug naglangoy nga reptilya sa panahon sa dinosaur dili tinuod nga dinosaur kondili lahi nga grupo sa reptilya.

q: What happens to plastic when it is recycled?
options: It is buried deep underground where it safely breaks down over many years
It is melted down and made into new things
It is shredded into tiny pieces and mixed into soil to help plants grow
It is sent to a special machine that turns it into fuel for cars
explanation: Some plastic can be recycled, meaning it is melted down and made into new things.
fact_tl: Ang ilang plastik ay maaaring i-recycle, ibig sabihin tinutunaw at ginagawang bagong gamit.
fact_bis: Ang ubang plastik mahimong i-recycle, nagpasabot nga tunawon kini ug himoon nga bag-ong gamit.

q: What causes mumps, and how does it spread?
options: Mumps is caused by bacteria that spread through contaminated drinking water
Mumps is caused by a vitamin deficiency that weakens the glands in the throat
Mumps is caused by a virus that spreads through saliva
Mumps is caused by a fungus that grows in warm, humid areas and is breathed in
explanation: Mumps is a disease caused by a virus that spreads through saliva.
fact_tl: Ang beke ay isang sakit na dulot ng isang virus na kumakalat sa pamamagitan ng laway.
fact_bis: Ang beke usa ka sakit nga gikan sa usa ka virus nga mokatap pinaagi sa laway.

q: Why does a giant clam open its colorful mantle toward the sun?
options: To release eggs into the current so they can be carried to other parts of the reef
To attract small fish that clean parasites off the clam's body
So the tiny algae living in it can get light and make food for the clam
To cool down by letting seawater flow over the warm inner surface
explanation: The giant clam opens its colorful mantle to the sun so the tiny algae living in it can get light, and these algae make food for the clam.
fact_tl: Bukas ang makulay na laman ng taklobo sa araw para makakuha ng liwanag ang maliliit na algang nakatira rito, at ang algang ito ang gumagawa ng pagkain para sa kabibe.
fact_bis: Ginabukas sa taklobo ang mabulukon niini nga unod ngadto sa adlaw aron makadawat ug kahayag ang gagmay nga alga nga nagpuyo niini, ug kini nga alga maoy naghimo ug pagkaon para sa kabibe.

q: Why is it important not to judge food safety by looks and smell alone?
options: Food that looks bad is always unsafe, but food that looks good is always safe to eat
Spoiled food always has a very strong or sour smell that warns you before you eat it
Sometimes food with harmful bacteria looks and smells completely normal, so it can still be unsafe
Bacteria only grow on food that has been left open, so sealed food is always safe
explanation: Sometimes food with harmful bacteria looks and smells normal, so it can still be unsafe even if it seems fine.
fact_tl: Minsan ang pagkaing may bakterya ay mukhang normal at walang amoy, kaya delikado pa rin.
fact_bis: Usahay ang pagkaon nga naay bakterya morag normal ug walay baho, busa delikado gihapon.

q: Which Philippine hardwood trees were used long ago to build sturdy ships and galleons?
options: Narra and banaba
Molave and yakal
Kamagong and acacia
Ipil and tindalo
explanation: Long ago, molave and yakal were used to build sturdy ships and galleons.
fact_tl: Noong unang panahon, ginamit ang molave at yakal sa paggawa ng matitibay na barko at galyon.
fact_bis: Kaniadto, ang molave ug yakal gigamit sa paghimo ug malig-on nga mga barko ug galyon.

q: What kind of image does a concave mirror form when the object is placed between the focal point and the mirror?
options: A real, upside-down image that can be projected onto a screen
A virtual, magnified image that appears behind the mirror
A flat image the same size as the object, right-side up
A real, very small image that appears far in front of the mirror
explanation: A concave mirror forms a virtual magnified image when the object is between the focal point and the mirror.
fact_tl: Ang concave mirror ay gumagawa ng real image kapag ang bagay ay malayo sa focal point, at virtual image kapang ang bagay ay nasa pagitan ng focal point at salamin.
fact_bis: Ang concave mirror nagahimo og real image kung ang butang layo sa focal point, ug virtual nga imahe kung ang butang anaa tali sa focal point ug salamin.

q: What is needed to start, stop, or change the direction of a moving object?
options: Mass — a heavier object automatically changes direction when obstacles are near
Speed — an object moving fast enough will naturally slow down on its own
A force must be applied to change an object's motion
Temperature — cold objects slow down while warm objects speed up
explanation: A force is needed to change an object's motion — to start it, stop it, or change its direction.
fact_tl: Kailangan ng puwersa para baguhin ang galaw ng isang bagay—para pakilusin, pahintuin, o palitan ang direksyon nito.
fact_bis: Gikinahanglan ang kusog aron mabag-o ang paglihok sa usa ka butang—aron tukaron, pahunongon, o usbon ang direksyon niini.

q: How do some cacti store extra water when it rains?
options: They grow longer roots that reach deep underground to store water in pockets of soil
Their thick waxy leaves hold water inside like small tanks
Their folded, accordion-like stems swell out as they fill up with water
They absorb water vapor from the air through tiny holes in their skin at night
explanation: Some cacti have folded, accordion-like stems that swell out when they fill with water, allowing them to store extra water.
fact_tl: Ang tangkay ng ilang kaktus ay may mga kunot na parang akordyon na umaalwan kapag puno ito ng tubig.
fact_bis: Ang lawas sa ubang kaktus may mga kunot nga sama sa akordyon nga mamintog kon mapuno kini og tubig.

q: Which animals are horseshoe crabs most closely related to?
options: True crabs and lobsters, because they all live in the sea
Clams and oysters, because they all have hard shells
Spiders and scorpions, because they share special mouthparts called chelicerae
Shrimp and barnacles, because they all filter food from the water
explanation: The horseshoe crab is more closely related to spiders and scorpions than to true crabs — they all share special mouthparts called chelicerae.
fact_tl: Kahit tinatawag itong crab, mas malapit na kamag-anak ng horseshoe crab ang mga gagamba at alakdan kaysa sa tunay na alimango! Pareho silang may mga bahagi ng katawan na tinatawag na chelicerae malapit sa bibig.
fact_bis: Bisan og gitawag kining crab, ang horseshoe crab mas duol nga paryente sa mga lawalawa ug tanga kaysa sa tinuod nga alimango! Silang tanan adunay espesyal nga bahin sa baba nga gitawag og chelicerae duol sa atubangan sa lawas.

q: What are prions, and why are they dangerous?
options: Prions are a type of virus that attacks the heart and can spread through the air
Prions are bacteria that live in soil and cause infections if they enter the bloodstream
Prions are misfolded proteins that cause other normal proteins to misfold too, leading to fatal brain diseases
Prions are toxins made by fungi that damage the liver when eaten in spoiled food
explanation: Prions are misfolded proteins that can cause other normal proteins to misfold too, leading to fatal brain diseases such as mad cow disease.
fact_tl: Ang prion ay hindi virus o bakterya — ito ay isang maling nakayupi na protina na maaaring magdulot ng ibang mga normal na protina na maling mayayupi rin, na nagdudulot ng mga sakit sa utak tulad ng mad cow disease.
fact_bis: Ang prion dili virus o bakterya — kini usa ka sayop nga napilik nga protina nga mahimong magpahinabog uban pang normal nga protina sa paghimong sayop ang pagpilik, nga nagmugna og mga makamamatay nga sakit sa utak sama sa mad cow disease.

q: How many wings does a bee have?
options: Two wings, like a fly
Four wings arranged in two pairs
Six wings for extra flying power
Four wings all the same size with no pairing
explanation: A bee has four wings that are arranged in two pairs — a larger front pair and a smaller back pair.
fact_tl: Ang bubuyog ay may apat na (4) pakpak — dalawang pares.
fact_bis: Ang putyukan adunay upat (4) ka pako — duha ka pares.

q: How do fireflies make their glow?
options: They absorb sunlight and release it at night
They rub their legs together to create friction heat
A chemical reaction between luciferin and luciferase using oxygen
Bacteria inside their bodies produce the light
explanation: Fireflies produce 'cold light' through a chemical reaction between luciferin and luciferase that uses oxygen, generating almost no heat.
fact_tl: Ang alitaptap ay gumagawa ng liwanag sa pamamagitan ng kemikal na reaksyon sa pagitan ng luciferin at luciferase na gumagamit ng oxygen—ito ay 'malamig na liwanag' na halos walang init.
fact_bis: Ang alitaptap naghimo og kahayag pinaagi sa kemikal nga reaksyon tali sa luciferin ug luciferase nga naggamit og oxygen—kini 'bugnaw nga kahayag' nga hapit walay init.

q: What shape are the crystals of halite, the mineral form of salt?
options: Flat hexagonal sheets like snowflakes
Long needle-like pointed shapes
Cube-shaped crystals
Rounded ball-shaped grains
explanation: Halite forms cube-shaped crystals and is the edible mineral form of salt.
fact_tl: Ang halite ay ang mineral ng asin na nabubuo sa kuwadradong kristal at maaaring kainin.
fact_bis: Ang halite mao ang mineral nga porma sa asin nga maporma og kuwadrado nga kristal ug makaon.

q: What happens to a metal rail on a very cold night?
options: It expands and takes up more space
It stays exactly the same size
It shrinks and contracts slightly
It melts and changes shape
explanation: When objects are cooled, they contract and shrink, just like rails getting shorter on a cold night.
fact_tl: Kabaligtaran ng paglaki, lumiliit at umuurong ang mga bagay kapag pinalamig, gaya ng riles na umiikli kapag malamig ang gabi.
fact_bis: Sukwahi sa pagdako, ang mga butang mogamay ug mokunhod kon bugnawon, sama sa riles nga moikli kon bugnaw ang gabii.

q: Why do thousands of shorebirds visit Philippine wetlands every year?
options: They come to breed and lay eggs in Philippine soil
They fly from cold northern regions to rest and feed in our wetlands
They are escaping predators that live in tropical forests
They migrate south to find freshwater rivers to drink from
explanation: Each year, migratory shorebirds fly from the cold north to the Philippines to rest and feed in our wetlands.
fact_tl: Tuwing taon, libo-libong ibong dagat ang lumilipad mula sa malamig na hilaga papuntang Pilipinas para magpahinga at kumain sa ating mga latian.
fact_bis: Kada tuig, liboan ka langgam sa baybayon ang naglupad gikan sa bugnaw nga amihanan padulong sa Pilipinas aron mopahulay ug mokaon sa atong kalatian.

q: Why do mothballs slowly disappear over time without leaving any liquid behind?
options: They dissolve into the air as tiny water droplets
They melt into a liquid that evaporates invisibly
Their solid turns directly into gas — a process called sublimation
They are eaten by tiny insects they were meant to repel
explanation: Mothballs undergo sublimation, meaning their solid state turns directly into gas without becoming a liquid first.
fact_tl: Ang mga mothball o alkampor ay unti-unting naglalaho dahil ang solido nito ay direktang nagiging gas — iyan ang sublimation.
fact_bis: Ang mga mothball o alkampor hinay-hinay nga mawala tungod kay ang solido niini direktang mahimong gas — mao na ang sublimation.

q: Which part of an animal is most likely to be found as a fossil millions of years later?
options: Soft organs like the heart and lungs
Skin and muscle tissue
Hard parts like bones and shells
Eyes and other sense organs
explanation: Hard parts such as bones and shells preserve much longer than soft parts, which decay quickly, making them far more likely to become fossils.
fact_tl: Ang mga fosil ay mas madaling mapreserba kapag ang hayop ay mabilis na nalibing sa sediment; ang mga matitigas na bahagi (buto, shell) ay mas matagal na nananatili kaysa mamamag na bahagi na mabilis na nabubulok.
fact_bis: Ang mga fossil mas sayon mapreserba kon ang hayop paspas nga nalubong sa sediment; ang mga matigas nga bahin (bukog, kabhang) mas dugay nagpabilin kaysa humok nga bahin nga paspas nagkadunot.

q: Which Philippine wild cat has spotted fur and hunts small animals at night?
options: The clouded leopard, which prowls lowland rice fields
The leopard cat, known as maral in the Visayas
The Philippine lynx, which lives near coastal mangroves
The forest civet, a large spotted predator of dense jungle
explanation: The leopard cat, called maral in the Visayas, is a small wild forest cat with spotted fur that hunts at night.
fact_tl: Ang leopard cat (tinatawag na maral sa Visayas) ay isang maliit na ligaw na pusang may batik-batik na balahibo na naninirahan sa kagubatan at nangangaso ng maliliit na hayop sa gabi.
fact_bis: Ang leopard cat (gitawag og maral sa Kabisay-an) usa ka gamay nga ihalas nga iring nga may puntik-puntik nga balhibo nga nagpuyo sa kalasangan ug nangayam og gagmay nga hayop sa gabii.

q: What do the black-and-white bands on many sea snakes do for them?
options: They help the snake blend into colorful coral reefs
They act as a warning signal to other animals
They help the snake attract a mate during breeding season
They reflect sunlight to keep the snake cool in warm water
explanation: Many sea snakes have black-and-white bands that act as a warning to other animals, signaling that the snake is dangerous.
fact_tl: Maraming ahas-dagat ang may itim at puting guhit sa katawan na parang babala sa ibang hayop.
fact_bis: Daghang halas sa dagat adunay itom ug puting mga bagis sa lawas nga morag pasidaan sa ubang mananap.

q: Which planet in our solar system is the only one known to have liquid water on its surface and life?
options: Mars, because it once had rivers long ago
Venus, because it is closest in size to Earth
Earth, our own planet
Europa, the moon of Jupiter with an underground ocean
explanation: Earth is the only planet in our solar system with liquid water on its surface and known life.
fact_tl: Ang Earth ang tanging planeta sa ating solar system na may likidong tubig sa ibabaw at kilalang may buhay.
fact_bis: Ang Yuta ra ang bugtong planeta sa atong solar system nga adunay likidong tubig sa ibabaw ug nailhang adunay kinabuhi.

q: How does a seatbelt protect you when a car suddenly stops?
options: It pushes you back into your seat with extra force
It inflates like a cushion to soften the impact
It stops your body from continuing to move forward, reducing injury
It locks the car doors so you cannot be thrown out
explanation: A seatbelt stops your body from continuing its forward motion when a vehicle suddenly halts, reducing the chance of injury.
fact_tl: Ang seatbelt ay pumipigil sa katawan na magpatuloy sa galaw nito kapag biglang huminto ang sasakyan, na nagbabawas ng pinsala.
fact_bis: Ang seatbelt nagpugong sa lawas sa pagpadayon sa paglihok niini kung kalit nga mohunong ang sakyanan, nga nagkunhod sa kadaot.

q: What is the name of the powerful explosion that happens when a massive star dies?
options: A nebula
A black hole
A pulsar
A supernova
explanation: The powerful explosion of a dying massive star is called a supernova.
fact_tl: Ang malakas na pagsabog ng isang namamatay na malaking bituin ay tinatawag na supernova.
fact_bis: Ang kusog nga pagbuto sa usa ka namatay nga dako nga bituin gitawag og supernova.

q: What is the main purpose of a vaccine?
options: To cure a person who is already seriously ill
To prevent a disease before a person gets it
To remove harmful bacteria from the bloodstream
To reduce fever after a person becomes infected
explanation: A vaccine is designed to prevent a disease before it happens, not to cure someone who is already sick.
fact_tl: Ang bakuna ay para pigilan ang sakit bago ito mangyari, hindi para gamutin ang taong may sakit na.
fact_bis: Ang bakuna alang sa pagpugong sa sakit sa dili pa kini mahitabo, dili aron tambalan ang tawong sakit na.

q: How does vaccinating many people in a community help protect even those who are NOT yet vaccinated?
options: The vaccine chemicals spread through the air to unvaccinated people nearby
Vaccinated people produce antibodies that float into the water supply
When most people are immune, the disease finds fewer people to infect and has a harder time spreading
Vaccines make sick people recover faster so they cannot infect others as long
explanation: When many people are vaccinated, the disease has fewer people it can reach, slowing its spread and protecting those not yet vaccinated.
fact_tl: Ang bakuna ay tumutulong na sanayin ang katawan na kilalanin at labanan ang isang partikular na germ nang hindi muna nagkakasakit nang malubha. Kapag marami ang nabakunahan sa isang lugar, mas mahirap nang kumalat ang sakit dahil kakaunti na ang puwedeng tamaan, kaya protektado pati ang mga hindi pa nababakunahan.
fact_bis: Ang bakuna motabang sa pagbansay sa lawas nga mailhan ug masukol ang usa ka partikular nga germ nga dili una grabe nga magmasakiton. Kung daghan ang nabakunahan sa usa ka lugar, lisod na nga mokalat ang sakit kay gamay na ang puwedeng matakdan, busa protektado bisan ang mga wala pa mabakunahi.

q: How does the kapok tree spread its seeds over large distances?
options: Animals eat the fruits and deposit seeds far away
Seeds are carried away by rivers and streams
Birds carry the seeds in their beaks to new nesting sites
Soft cotton-like fibers attached to the seeds allow them to be carried by the wind
explanation: When the kapok pod splits open, seeds with attached cotton-like fibers are carried by the wind and can disperse over large distances.
fact_tl: Ang kapok tree ay nagbubunga ng mga pod na puno ng malambot na cotton-like na hibla—kapag pumutok ang pod, ang mga buto na may nakakabit na hibla ay lilipad sa hangin at nakakalat sa malayo.
fact_bis: Ang kapok tree nagbubunga og mga pod nga puno sa humok nga cotton-like nga hibla; kung mabuka ang pod, ang mga buto nga adunay nakadugtong nga hibla madala sa hangin ug nagkatag sa layo.

q: Why are earthworm droppings (called castings) good for the soil?
options: They make the soil very hard so plant roots stay in place
They contain chemicals that keep pests away from plants
They contain more nutrients than ordinary soil and improve soil structure
They add water to dry soil so plants do not need as much rain
explanation: Earthworm castings are an excellent fertilizer because they contain more nutrients than ordinary soil and improve soil structure.
fact_tl: Ang dumi ng bulati na tinatawag na castings ay nagsisilbing napakagandang pataba—naglalaman ito ng mas maraming sustansya kaysa sa ordinaryong lupa.
fact_bis: Ang tae sa bulati nga gitawag og castings giisip nga maayong abono—naglangkob kini og mas daghang sustansya kaysa sa ordinaryong yuta ug nagpaayo sa istruktura sa yuta.

q: According to the law of conservation of energy, what really happens to energy when work is done?
options: Energy is slowly used up and disappears over time
New energy is created each time a machine runs
Energy changes from one form to another but is never created or destroyed
Energy is stored inside objects and released all at once when needed
explanation: Energy is not created or destroyed; it only changes form as work is done.
fact_tl: Ang enerhiya ay hindi nalilikha o nawawala, kundi nagbabago lamang ng anyo habang nagagawa ang trabaho.
fact_bis: Ang enerhiya dili mahimo o mawala; nagbag-o lang kini og porma samtang gihimo ang trabaho.

q: In a transverse wave, how do the particles move compared to the direction the wave travels?
options: They move in the same direction the wave travels, pushing it forward
They spin in circles around the path of the wave
They move up and down, at right angles to the direction the wave travels
They stay perfectly still while the wave passes through them
explanation: In a transverse wave, particles vibrate up and down at right angles to the direction the wave travels, just like water waves.
fact_tl: Sa transverse na alon, tulad ng alon sa tubig, ang mga particle ay umuuyog pataas-pababa, pahalang sa direksyon ng paglalakbay ng alon.
fact_bis: Sa transverse nga balud, sama sa balud sa tubig, ang mga partikulo mag-uyog pataas-paubos, taluwas sa direksyon nga ginalakaw sa balud.

q: What is the national flower of the Philippines?
options: Gumamela
Waling-waling orchid
Sampaguita
Ilang-ilang
explanation: The sampaguita is the national flower of the Philippines.
fact_tl: Ang pambansang bulaklak ng Pilipinas ay ang sampaguita.
fact_bis: Ang nasodnong bulak sa Pilipinas mao ang sampaguita.

q: Why can electric current flow easily through metals?
options: Metals have hollow tubes inside that carry electricity like water pipes
Metals are very smooth so electricity slides across their surface
Some electrons in metals are free to move, allowing current to flow through them
Metals absorb heat from the environment and convert it into electricity
explanation: In metals, some electrons are free to move easily, which allows an electric current to flow through them readily.
fact_tl: Sa mga metal, may mga malayang elektron na madaling gumalaw, kaya madaling dumaloy ang kuryente sa mga ito.
fact_bis: Sa mga metal, adunay gawasnon nga mga elektron nga sayon molihok, mao nga dali nga modagayday ang kuryente niini.

q: How many electric organs does an electric eel have inside its body?
options: One large organ that produces all its electricity
Two organs that work in exactly the same way
Three organs — two for strong shocks and one for weak charges
Five organs arranged along its spine
explanation: The electric eel has three electric organs: two large ones that make the strong shock, and the Sachs organ that produces only a weak charge.
fact_tl: Ang electric eel ay may tatlong electric organ sa loob ng katawan nito. Ang dalawang malalaki (ang main organ at Hunter's organ) ang gumagawa ng malakas na kuryente, habang ang Sachs organ ay gumagawa ng mahinang kuryente lang.
fact_bis: Ang electric eel adunay tulo ka electric organ sa sulod sa lawas niini. Ang duha ka dagko (ang main organ ug Hunter's organ) maoy naghimo sa kusog nga kuryente, samtang ang Sachs organ naghimo lang og huyang nga kuryente.

q: Why should you never stare directly at the sun?
options: It makes your eyes water, which can cause infections
Looking at the sun can permanently damage your eyes
Staring at the sun causes headaches but does not harm the eyes
The sun's UV rays only damage skin, not the eyes
explanation: We should never stare straight at the sun because it can damage the eyes.
fact_tl: Hindi dapat tumitig nang diretso sa araw dahil maaari nitong masira ang mata.
fact_bis: Dili gyud angay motan-aw og diretso sa adlaw kay makadaot kini sa mata.

q: What does a healthy gut need to work well?
options: A single dominant strain of bacteria that fights all others
Completely bacteria-free conditions inside the intestines
A balance and variety of different bacteria working together
Only bacteria that produce vitamins and nothing else
explanation: A healthy gut requires a balance and variety of bacteria all working together, not just one type dominating.
fact_tl: Ang malusog na bituka ay may balanse at iba't ibang uri ng bakterya na magkakasamang nagtatrabaho.
fact_bis: Ang himsog nga tinai adunay balanse ug nagkalain-laing matang sa bakterya nga nagtinabangay.

q: When did electric refrigerators first appear in people's homes?
options: In the 1880s, soon after electricity was invented
In the 1910s
In the 1950s, after World War Two
In the 1930s, during the Great Depression
explanation: Electric home refrigerators appeared in the 1910s, though the first working refrigerator was built much earlier by Jacob Perkins in 1834.
fact_tl: Ang unang gumaganang refrigerator ay ginawa ni Jacob Perkins noong 1834, at ang mga elektrikong ref para sa bahay ay lumitaw noong mga 1910s.
fact_bis: Ang unang naglihok nga refrigerator gihimo ni Jacob Perkins niadtong 1834, ug ang elektrikong ref para sa balay mitungha sa mga 1910s.

q: What is the main difference between angiosperms and gymnosperms?
options: Angiosperms only grow in tropical climates while gymnosperms grow in cold areas
Angiosperms reproduce with spores while gymnosperms use seeds
Angiosperms produce flowers and seeds enclosed in fruit while gymnosperms have naked seeds in cones
Gymnosperms grow much faster than angiosperms and have larger leaves
explanation: Angiosperms are flowering plants with seeds enclosed in fruit, while gymnosperms like pine trees have naked seeds in cones and do not produce flowers.
fact_tl: Ang mga angiosperm ay mga halaman na may bulaklak at prutas na nagtatakip sa kanilang buto (tulad ng mangga at saging); ang mga gymnosperm ay may bukas na buto sa loob ng kono (tulad ng pino) at walang bulaklak.
fact_bis: Ang mga angiosperm mga tanum nga adunay bulaklak ug prutas nga nagtiib sa ilang buto (sama sa mangga ug saging); ang gymnosperms adunay bukas nga buto sa kono (sama sa pino) ug walay bulaklak.

q: In the wild, where does the Venus flytrap naturally grow?
options: In tropical rainforests across Southeast Asia
In one small area of the southeastern United States
In swamps and wetlands throughout central Africa
In volcanic soil on the islands of the Pacific Ocean
explanation: In the wild, the Venus flytrap naturally grows in only one small area of the southeastern United States.
fact_tl: Sa ligaw, natural na tumutubo ang Venus flytrap sa isang maliit na lugar lamang sa timog-silangang Estados Unidos.
fact_bis: Sa ihalas, natural nga motubo ang Venus flytrap sa usa lamang ka gamayng dapit sa habagatan-sidlakang Estados Unidos.

q: Bamboo is remarkable because of how fast it grows. How fast can some kinds of bamboo grow?
options: About one centimeter per week
Almost one meter in a single day
About one meter per month
Nearly half a meter every hour
explanation: Bamboo is one of the fastest-growing plants in the world — some kinds can grow almost a meter in just a single day.
fact_tl: Ang kawayan ay isa sa pinakamabilis tumubong halaman sa mundo — ang ilang uri nito ay makakatubo ng halos isang metro sa loob lamang ng isang araw.
fact_bis: Ang kawayan usa sa pinakapaspas motubo nga tanom sa kalibotan — ang ubang matang niini makatubo og halos usa ka metro sulod lamang sa usa ka adlaw.

q: What is the correct name for the hip bone?
options: The femur
The tibia
The pelvis
The sacrum
explanation: The hip bone is called the pelvis.
fact_tl: Ang buto sa balakang ay tinatawag na pelvis.
fact_bis: Ang bukog sa bat-ang gitawag og pelvis.

q: What is the main job of the skull?
options: To help us chew food and bite
To give our face its shape and hold our eyes in place
To protect the brain from injury
To connect the head to the spine so we can turn our neck
explanation: The skull is a hard bone that protects our brain from injury.
fact_tl: Ang bungo ay matigas na buto na nagpoprotekta sa ating utak.
fact_bis: Ang bagol usa ka gahi nga bukog nga nagpanalipod sa atong utok.

q: What holds the soybeans together in tempeh and gives it a firm shape?
options: A starchy paste made from boiled soybeans pressed together
Salt and vinegar that harden the outer layer of soybeans
The white threads of a special mold that grows through the beans
Heat treatment that fuses the soybeans into a solid block
explanation: Tempeh is made from soybeans held together by the white threads of a special mold, which gives it a firm shape and adds extra protein.
fact_tl: Ang tempeh ay gawa sa soybeans na pinagdidikit-dikit ng mga puting sinulid ng isang espesyal na amag, na siyang nagbibigay dito ng matatag na hugis at karagdagang protina.
fact_bis: Ang tempeh hinimo gikan sa soybeans nga gidugtong sa puti nga mga lanot sa usa ka pinasahi nga agup-op, nga maoy naghatag niini og lig-on nga porma ug dugang protina.

q: Which country produces the most abaca in the world?
options: Indonesia
Brazil
Ecuador
The Philippines
explanation: The Philippines is the world's largest producer of abaca.
fact_tl: Ang Pilipinas ang pinakamalaking gumagawa ng abaka sa buong mundo.
fact_bis: Ang Pilipinas mao ang pinakadako nga naghimo ug abaka sa tibuok kalibutan.

q: Why is talc used to make baby powder?
options: It is naturally antiseptic and kills bacteria on skin
It absorbs moisture and prevents rashes better than any other mineral
It is the softest known mineral and can be ground into a very fine powder
It is white in color, which makes it look clean and safe
explanation: Talc has a Mohs hardness of only 1, making it the softest mineral, which is why it can be ground into a fine powder for uses like baby powder.
fact_tl: Dahil napakalambot ng talc (Mohs 1), ginagawa itong pulbos tulad ng baby powder.
fact_bis: Tungod kay humok kaayo ang talc (Mohs 1), ginahimo kini nga pulbos sama sa baby powder.

q: Why does mayonnaise not separate into oil and water layers?
options: The vinegar in mayonnaise reacts with oil and permanently bonds them together
Strong stirring breaks oil into droplets too small to ever recombine
Egg yolk contains lecithin, an emulsifier that keeps oil and water mixed
Salt in the mayonnaise dissolves the oil so it stays blended with water
explanation: Egg yolk contains lecithin, a natural emulsifier that keeps oil and water mixed together in mayonnaise without separating.
fact_tl: Ang pula ng itlog ay naglalaman ng lecithin, isang natural na emulsifier na nagpapanatili ng mantika at tubig na magkasamang halo sa mayonnaise nang hindi naghihiwalay.
fact_bis: Ang pula sa itlog nagdala og lecithin, usa ka natural nga emulsifier nga nagpatago sa mantika ug tubig nga nagkahialo sa mayonnaise nga walay paghiwalay; kon wala kini, dayon sila mahibalag ngadto sa mga patong.

q: When did people first begin living and working on the International Space Station?
options: In 1998, the same year the first module was launched
In 2000, and astronauts have been on board nonstop ever since
In 1995, when the Mir space station was still operating
In 2005, after the Columbia disaster safety reviews were complete
explanation: People began living on the International Space Station in 2000, and it has had astronauts on board nonstop ever since.
fact_tl: Nagsimulang tirahan ng mga tao ang International Space Station noong 2000, at tuloy-tuloy na itong may nakatirang astronaut mula noon.
fact_bis: Nagsugod nga gipuy-an sa mga tawo ang International Space Station niadtong 2000, ug nonstop na kini nga adunay astronaut sukad niadto.

q: What is the 'heading' stage in a rice plant's growth?
options: When the seedling first sprouts from the seed after planting
When the roots grow deep enough to anchor the plant in the mud
When the panicle emerges from the top leaf sheath and pollination occurs
When the grain ripens and turns golden yellow before harvest
explanation: Heading is the stage when the panicle emerges from inside the top leaf sheath; this is critical because pollination occurs at this stage.
fact_tl: Ang heading ay ang yugto kung kailan lumalabas ang uhay (panicle) mula sa loob ng tuktok na dahon; ito ay mahalaga dahil sa yugtong ito nangyayari ang pollination.
fact_bis: Ang heading mao ang yugto kung kanus-a mogawas ang uhay (panicle) gikan sa sulod sa itaas nga leaf sheath; mahinungdanon kini tungod kay mao kini ang panahon sa pollination.

q: How do thousands of electrocytes in an electric eel produce a powerful shock?
options: Each cell stores electricity for months and releases it all at once
They heat up the water around the eel, creating an electric field
They all move charged particles (ions) at the same time, so each small charge adds up into one strong shock
Special bacteria inside each cell convert food energy directly into electricity
explanation: Thousands of electrocytes stack like batteries — when they all move ions simultaneously, each cell's small electrical charge adds up into one very strong shock.
fact_tl: Ang libu-libong electrocyte ay nakasalansan na parang baterya. Kapag sabay-sabay silang nagpapalipat ng maliliit na particle na may charge (ions), nagsasama-sama ang munting kuryente ng bawat isa hanggang maging napakalakas na shock.
fact_bis: Ang liboan ka electrocyte gipundok nga murag baterya. Kon dungan silang molihok og gagmayng particle nga adunay charge (ions), ang gamayng kuryente sa matag usa magtapok hangtod mahimong kusog kaayo nga shock.

q: Why does a toad usually walk or crawl instead of jumping like a frog?
options: Toads are heavier than frogs, so jumping wastes too much energy
A toad's skin is dry and rough, making it harder to land safely after a jump
Toads have shorter legs, so they often crawl or walk more than they jump
Toads only live in water and cannot jump well on dry land
explanation: A toad has shorter legs than a frog, so it often crawls or walks more than it jumps.
fact_tl: Ang palakang-bukid (toad) ay may mas maiikling binti, kaya mas madalas itong gumagapang o naglalakad kaysa lumukso.
fact_bis: Ang kabkab (toad) naay mas mubo nga mga tiil, mao nga kasagaran ni mokamang o molakaw kaysa moambak.

q: How is a person's blood type determined?
options: It changes depending on what foods a person eats as a child
It is decided by what blood type the mother has during pregnancy
It is a trait inherited from both parents through their genes
It depends on which blood type is most common in the country where a person is born
explanation: Your blood type (A, B, AB, or O) is a trait you inherit from your parents through their genes.
fact_tl: Ang uri ng iyong dugo (A, B, AB, o O) ay isang katangiang minana mo sa iyong mga magulang sa pamamagitan ng kanilang gene. Kaya nga maaaring hulaan ng mga doktor ang posibleng uri ng dugo ng anak base sa magulang.
fact_bis: Ang klase sa imong dugo (A, B, AB, o O) usa ka kinaiya nga imong napanunod gikan sa imong ginikanan pinaagi sa ilang gene. Mao nga matag-an sa mga doktor ang posibleng klase sa dugo sa bata base sa ginikanan.

q: Which of these fruit trees grow best in the warm tropical climate of the Philippines?
options: Apple, pear, and cherry
Santol, atis, and guyabano
Strawberry, blueberry, and peach
Pine, maple, and oak
explanation: Santol, atis, and guyabano thrive in the warm, tropical climate like that of the Philippines.
fact_tl: Ang santol, atis, at guyabano ay umuunlad sa mainit at tropikal na klima tulad ng sa Pilipinas.
fact_bis: Ang santol, atis, ug guyabano molambo sa init ug tropikal nga klima sama sa Pilipinas.

q: Why can thick mats of water hyacinth increase the number of mosquitoes in a body of water?
options: Water hyacinth flowers attract mosquitoes from far away to feed on nectar
Mosquitoes eat the roots of water hyacinth to get nutrients for egg-laying
Under the thick mat the water stays still, creating a perfect breeding place for mosquitoes
Water hyacinth releases chemicals that speed up the development of mosquito larvae
explanation: Under a thick mat of water hyacinth the water stays still, making a good breeding place for mosquitoes such as those that spread dengue.
fact_tl: Sa ilalim ng makapal na water hyacinth, hindi gumagalaw ang tubig kaya ito nagiging magandang pamumugaran ng lamok. Dahil dito, maaaring dumami ang lamok na nagdadala ng sakit tulad ng dengue.
fact_bis: Sa ilawom sa baga nga water hyacinth, dili molihok ang tubig busa kini nahimong maayong salaganan sa lamok. Tungod niini, mahimong modaghan ang lamok nga nagdala og sakit sama sa dengue.

q: How is a baby gecko different from a baby frog or butterfly when it hatches?
options: A baby gecko is born live, not from an egg, unlike frogs and butterflies
A baby gecko looks like a tiny adult and does not go through a big change in shape as it grows
A baby gecko has wings at first that it sheds after its first week of life
A baby gecko is completely blind and must grow for a month before it looks like an adult
explanation: When a gecko egg hatches, the baby looks like a tiny version of an adult gecko and does not undergo a dramatic change in body shape like a frog or butterfly does.
fact_tl: Kapag napisa ang itlog ng butiki, ang lumalabas ay tila maliit na bersyon na lang ng nasa hustong gulang na butiki. Hindi tulad ng palaka o paru-paro, hindi na ito dumadaan sa malaking pagbabago ng hugis habang lumalaki.
fact_bis: Kung mopusa ang itlog sa butiki, ang mogawas morag gamayng bersyon lang sa hingkod nga butiki. Dili sama sa baki o alibangbang, dili kini moagi og dakong kausaban sa porma samtang motubo.

q: What makes a thermistor useful in devices like digital thermometers?
options: It glows brighter as temperature rises, letting a camera read the color
It expands and pushes a needle across a dial as it gets hotter
Its electrical resistance changes with temperature, allowing electronic temperature measurement
It converts heat directly into an electric current that powers the display
explanation: A thermistor is a semiconductor whose resistance changes with temperature, making it useful for measuring temperature electronically in devices like digital thermometers and air conditioners.
fact_tl: Ang thermistor ay isang semiconductor na nagbabago ng resistansya nito kapag nagbabago ang temperatura — ginagamit ito sa mga digital thermometer, cellphone, at aircon para sukatin ang temperatura electronically.
fact_bis: Ang thermistor usa ka semiconductor nga nagbag-o sa iyang resistensya kung magbag-o ang temperatura — gigamit sa mga digital thermometer, smartphone, ug aircon sa pagsukod sa temperatura electronically.

q: What can happen if the stress hormone cortisol stays too high in your body for too long?
options: It boosts your memory and makes you perform better on every exam
It turns into adrenaline and gives you extra strength and focus
It can harm your health over time
It triggers your immune system to fight off diseases more effectively
explanation: Cortisol helps you cope with longer-lasting stress, but if it stays too high for too long, it can harm your health.
fact_tl: Bukod sa adrenaline na biglaan, may hormone din na tinatawag na cortisol na lumalabas kapag matagalan ang stress—gaya ng maraming exam o problema. Tumutulong itong harapin ang stress, pero kapag sobra-sobra at matagal, puwede itong makasama sa kalusugan.
fact_bis: Gawas sa kalit nga adrenaline, adunay usab hormone nga gitawag og cortisol nga mosaka sa dugay nga stress—sama sa daghang exam o problema. Motabang kini aron masagubang ang stress, apan kon sobra ug dugay kaayo, makadaot kini sa imong panglawas.

q: Who is known as the 'father of the computer'?
options: Alan Turing
Ada Lovelace
Charles Babbage
Thomas Edison
explanation: Charles Babbage is called the father of the computer for his early work designing mechanical computing machines.
fact_tl: Si Charles Babbage ay tinatawag na ama ng kompyuter.
fact_bis: Si Charles Babbage gitawag nga amahan sa kompyuter.

q: Why is electricity from wind turbines often stored in batteries?
options: Batteries keep the turbine blades spinning when the wind is weak
Wind electricity is too strong and must be weakened before use
Wind comes and goes, so extra electricity is stored for times when the wind is calm
Batteries convert wind electricity into a safer type that can enter homes
explanation: Because wind is intermittent and comes and goes, extra electricity is often stored in batteries for times when the wind is calm.
