options: The Moon's gravity pulling on ocean water
The Sun's heat warming the surface of the ocean
Wind blowing across the ocean for many days
Earth spinning on its axis every 24 hours
explanation: Ocean tides are mainly caused by the Moon's gravity pulling on the ocean water.
fact_tl: Ang pangunahing sanhi ng taog (tides) ng dagat ay ang grabidad ng Buwan na humihila sa tubig ng karagatan.
fact_bis: Ang taob (tides) sa dagat ginahimo sa grabidad sa Bulan nga nagabira sa tubig sa dagat.

q: What do ants, mosquitoes, spiders, snails, crabs, and shrimp all have in common?
options: They are all invertebrates — animals with no backbone
They all live in the ocean or in rivers
They all have exactly six legs
They all can fly or jump long distances
explanation: All of these common Philippine animals are invertebrates, meaning they have no backbone.
fact_tl: Marami ring invertebrate sa ating paligid, gaya ng langgam, lamok, gagamba, kuhol, alimango, at hipon — wala silang gulugod.
fact_bis: Daghan usab ang invertebrate sa atong palibot, sama sa hulmigas, namok, lawalawa, kuhol, alimango, ug pasayan — wala silay gulugod.

q: Which combination of factors drives ocean currents?
options: Surface winds, differences in water temperature and saltiness, and Earth's rotation
Rainfall amounts, depth of the ocean, and the Moon's gravity
The tides, underwater volcanoes, and the movement of continents
Sunlight, river flow, and seasonal storms
explanation: Ocean currents are driven by surface winds, by differences in water density due to temperature and saltiness, and by the bending effect of Earth's rotation.
fact_tl: Ang mga agos ng dagat ay pinapagalaw ng hangin sa ibabaw, ng pagkakaiba sa temperatura at alat ng tubig na nagbabago sa bigat nito, at ng pag-ikot ng Mundo na nagpapaliko sa daloy.
fact_bis: Ang mga sulog sa dagat gipalihok sa hangin sa ibabaw, sa kalainan sa temperatura ug kaparat sa tubig nga nag-usab sa kabug-at niini, ug sa pagtuyok sa Kalibutan nga nagliko sa pag-agos.

q: What are baby carabaos called, and what activity do they learn to enjoy early?
options: Calves; wallowing in water and mud
Foals; swimming in deep rivers
Piglets; rolling in dry dirt
Cubs; jumping into fast-moving streams
explanation: Baby carabaos are called calves, and they learn to enjoy wallowing in water and mud early alongside their mothers.
fact_tl: Maging ang maliliit na anak ng kalabaw ay natututong mahiligan ang tubig at putik nang maaga, kasama ang kanilang ina sa paglublob.
fact_bis: Bisan ang gagmay nga anak sa kalabaw, nga gitawag ug nati, makakat-on nga mahiligon sa tubig ug lapok sayo pa, kauban sa ilang inahan sa paglubog.

q: How ancient are sharks compared to dinosaurs?
options: Sharks lived in the sea even before the dinosaurs came
Sharks and dinosaurs first appeared at exactly the same time
Sharks evolved millions of years after the dinosaurs died out
Dinosaurs were already extinct before the first sharks swam in the sea
explanation: Sharks are very ancient animals that lived in the sea even before the dinosaurs existed.
fact_tl: Ang mga pating ay napakatandang hayop, may pating na nasa dagat na bago pa man dumating ang mga dinosaur.
fact_bis: Ang mga iho karaan na kaayo nga mga hayop; may iho nga buhi na sa dagat sa wala pa moabot ang mga dinosaur.

q: In which direction does a nerve signal cross a synapse?
options: In only one direction — from the sending neuron to the receiving neuron
In both directions depending on the strength of the signal
Randomly in either direction each time
Backward from the receiving neuron to the sending neuron
explanation: A signal crosses the synapse in only one direction; one neuron always sends the chemical and the other always receives it.
fact_tl: Ang signal ay dumadaan sa synapse sa iisang direksyon lang. Ang isang neuron ang laging nagpapadala ng kemikal, at ang kabila ang tumatanggap, kaya hindi ito pabalik-balik.
fact_bis: Ang signal motabok sa synapse sa usa lang ka direksyon. Usa ka neuron kanunay ang nagpadala sa kemikal ug ang pikas mao ang modawat, busa dili kini makabalik.

q: Which nutrients does the body most need to heal a wound and build new cells?
options: Protein and vitamin C from meat, eggs, fruits, and vegetables
Sugar and fat from sweets and fried foods
Calcium and iron from milk and bread
Fiber and starch from rice and root crops
explanation: The body needs protein and vitamin C from meat, eggs, fruits, and vegetables to build new cells and collagen when healing a wound.
fact_tl: Ang masustansyang pagkain ay tumutulong sa paggaling ng sugat. Kailangan ng katawan ng protina at vitamin C mula sa karne, itlog, prutas, at gulay para makagawa ng bagong selula at collagen.
fact_bis: Ang masustansyang pagkaon makatabang sa pag-ayo sa samad. Magkinahanglan ang lawas og protina ug vitamin C gikan sa karne, itlog, prutas, ug utan aron makahimo og bag-ong selula ug collagen.

q: How can you tell if a coconut still has plenty of water inside?
options: Shake it near your ear and listen for sloshing water
Tap it lightly and feel if it vibrates
Hold it up to light to see the shadow of the water
Smell it to detect the sweet scent of fresh liquid
explanation: Shaking a coconut near your ear and hearing the water slosh inside tells you it still has plenty of water.
fact_tl: Paano malalaman kung maraming tubig ang buko? Kalugin mo ito malapit sa tainga. Kung naririnig mo ang tunog ng tubig na lumalagok sa loob, ibig sabihin marami pang tubig ang niyog.
fact_bis: Unsaon pagkahibalo kung daghan ang tubig sa buko? Uyoga kini duol sa imong dalunggan. Kung madungog nimo ang tubig nga nagkabog sa sulod, nagpasabot nga daghan pa ang tubig sa lubi.

q: In incomplete dominance, is the in-between trait always exactly halfway between the two parents?
options: No — it can lean toward one parent depending on how much pigment the single active allele makes
Yes — it is always an exact 50-50 blend of both parents
No — it always looks exactly like the dominant parent
Yes — every offspring shows the same identical blended trait
explanation: In incomplete dominance the blended trait is between the parents but not always exactly halfway — it depends on how much pigment the single active allele produces.
fact_tl: Ang gitnang katangian sa incomplete dominance ay 'pagitan' ng dalawang magulang, ngunit hindi laging eksaktong kalahati—minsan ay mas malapit sa isang panig depende sa dami ng pigment na nagagawa ng iisang aktibong alele.
fact_bis: Ang tunga-tunga nga kinaiya sa incomplete dominance kay 'taliwala' sa duha ka ginikanan, apan dili kanunay eksaktong katunga—usahay mas duol sa usa ka kilid depende sa kadaghan sa pigment nga mahimo sa usa ka aktibo nga allele.

q: What is a lodestone?
options: A naturally magnetic rock that attracts iron without being made by people
A metal bar magnetized by running electricity through it
A type of iron tool used to test for magnetic fields
A man-made stone that was treated to become magnetic
explanation: Lodestone is a naturally magnetic rock that attracts iron even though no person made it, making it the first magnet ever known.
fact_tl: Ang lodestone ay isang likas na magnet na bato na umaakit ng bakal kahit hindi ito ginawa ng tao; ito ang unang nakilalang magnet.
fact_bis: Ang lodestone usa ka natural nga magnetikong bato nga modani ug puthaw bisan walay tawo nga naghimo niini; mao kini ang unang nailhan nga magnet.

q: What is an ocean trench most similar to in shape?
options: A very long, narrow valley on the seafloor
A wide, shallow bowl in the middle of the ocean
A tall underwater mountain range
A flat, broad plain at the bottom of the sea
explanation: An ocean trench is like a very long, narrow valley carved into the seafloor.
fact_tl: Ang isang ocean trench ay parang napakahaba at makitid na lambak sa sahig ng karagatan.
fact_bis: Ang usa ka ocean trench sama sa taas kaayo ug sigpit nga walog sa salog sa dagat.

q: What is the largest living organism on Earth?
options: A honey fungus in Oregon whose underground threads spread across several kilometers
The blue whale, which is the heaviest animal in the ocean
A giant sequoia tree in California that is over 80 meters tall
A coral reef in Australia that stretches for thousands of kilometers
explanation: The largest living thing on Earth is a honey fungus in Oregon, whose underground threads spread across several kilometers.
fact_tl: Ang pinakamalaking nabubuhay na bagay sa mundo ay hindi puno o balyena kundi isang fungus na tinatawag na honey fungus sa Oregon, na may mga sinulid sa ilalim ng lupa na kumalat sa ilang kilometro.
fact_bis: Ang pinakadako nga buhing butang sa kalibotan dili kahoy o balyena kondili usa ka fungus nga gitawag og honey fungus sa Oregon, kansang mga lanot sa ilawom sa yuta mikatag og pipila ka kilometro.

q: What geological process happens at the Philippine Trench?
options: The Philippine Sea Plate sinks beneath the Philippine plate (subduction)
Two plates pull apart, creating a mid-ocean ridge
Plates slide sideways past each other along a fault
The Philippine plate folds upward to form new mountains
explanation: The Philippine Trench is a subduction zone where the Philippine Sea Plate sinks beneath the Philippine plate.
fact_tl: Ang Philippine Trench ay isang subduction zone kung saan lumulubog ang Philippine Sea Plate sa ilalim ng plato ng Pilipinas.
fact_bis: Ang Philippine Trench usa ka subduction zone diin ang Philippine Sea Plate molusbog ilalom sa plato sa Pilipinas.

q: Roughly what percentage of the Sun is made of helium?
options: About 25%
About 10%
About 50%
About 75%
explanation: After hydrogen, the Sun is made of about 25% helium.
fact_tl: Pangalawa sa hydrogen, ang Araw ay may humigit-kumulang 25% helium.
fact_bis: Sunod sa hydrogen, ang Adlaw mga 25% helium.

q: Which types of living things are linked together in a wetland food web?
options: Plants, insects, fish, and birds
Only fish and water birds
Only algae and insects
Only large mammals and reptiles
explanation: In a wetland, plants, insects, fish, and birds are linked together in a rich food web.
fact_tl: Sa latian, ang mga halaman, insekto, isda, at ibon ay magkakaugnay sa isang masaganang kadena ng pagkain.
fact_bis: Sa lamakan, ang mga tanom, insekto, isda, ug langgam nagkalambigit sa usa ka dato nga lambat sa pagkaon.

q: What type of feather is best at keeping a bird warm?
options: Soft, fluffy down feathers
Long, stiff flight feathers
Smooth tail feathers
Colorful outer contour feathers
explanation: Down feathers are the softest and fluffiest and grow thick under a bird's body to keep it warm.
fact_tl: Ang malalambot at mabuhaghag na balahibong tinatawag na down ang pinakamabisang magpainit, kaya makapal ito sa ilalim ng katawan ng ibon.
fact_bis: Ang humok ug bukbok nga mga balhibo nga gitawag og down maoy labing maayo mopainit, busa baga kini molabaw sa ilawom sa lawas sa langgam.

q: Why can rats easily live near people?
options: Because they eat almost anything
Because they are too fast for people to catch
Because they are protected by their hard shells
Because they sleep during the day and are never seen
explanation: Rats eat almost anything, which makes it easy for them to find food and live near people.
fact_tl: Kumakain ang daga ng halos kahit ano, kaya madali itong mabuhay malapit sa tao.
fact_bis: Mokaon ang ilaga sa halos bisan unsa, mao nga sayon ra silang mabuhi duol sa mga tawo.

q: How do onions and garlic reproduce and grow into new plants?
options: They grow from bulbs that store food and can sprout into a new plant
They grow only from seeds planted in soil every year
They spread by sending out long roots that become new plants
They grow from spores carried by the wind to new locations
explanation: Onions and garlic grow from bulbs, which are plant parts that store food and can sprout into new plants.
fact_tl: Ang sibuyas at bawang ay tumutubo mula sa bulb — isang bahagi ng halaman na nag-iimbak ng pagkain at maaaring usbungan ng bagong halaman.
fact_bis: Ang sibuyas ug ahos mutubo gikan sa bulb — usa ka bahin sa tanom nga nagtipig og pagkaon ug mahimong moturok ngadto sa bag-ong tanom.

q: How long does it usually take for caves to form?
options: Thousands of years
A few decades
Several months after heavy rains
Just a few years of slow erosion
explanation: Caves form very slowly, often taking thousands of years to develop.
fact_tl: Napakabagal mabuo ng kuweba—maaaring umabot ito ng libu-libong taon.
fact_bis: Ang langob hinay kaayong maporma—mahimong moabot kini og libo-libo ka tuig.

q: What is the real reason that different constellations are visible in different seasons?
options: Earth orbiting the Sun changes which stars are visible, regardless of temperature
The hot weather causes the stars to shift toward the poles
Cold air makes light bend so we see different stars in winter
The Moon's gravity slowly pushes the stars into new patterns each season
explanation: Constellations change because Earth orbits the Sun, not because of hot or cold weather — the temperature and the constellation change are both results of one orbit.
fact_tl: Maling akala na nagbabago ang konstelasyon dahil sa init o lamig ng panahon. Ang totoo, parehong sanhi — ang pag-ikot ng Earth sa Araw — ang dahilan ng pagpapalit ng konstelasyon AT ng pagbabago ng panahon, pero hindi ang init mismo ang nagbabago ng bituin. Magkapatid silang epekto ng iisang orbit.
fact_bis: Sayop ang hunahuna nga mausab ang konstelasyon tungod sa kainit o kabugnaw sa panahon. Ang tinuod, parehong hinungdan — ang paglibot sa Earth sa Adlaw — maoy hinungdan sa pag-ilis sa konstelasyon UG sa mga panahon, apan dili ang kainit mismo maoy mobalhin sa mga bituon. Managsoon sila nga epekto sa usa ka orbit.

q: Unlike ginger and potato, what plant part is the sweet potato (kamote) that grows underground?
options: A swollen root
A modified stem
An underground bulb
An enlarged rhizome
explanation: The sweet potato is a swollen root, while ginger and potato are underground stems, even though all three grow underground.
fact_tl: Iba sa luya at patatas, ang kamote ay namamagang ugat (root), hindi tangkay, kahit pareho silang tumutubo sa ilalim ng lupa.
fact_bis: Lahi sa luy-a ug patatas, ang kamote usa ka nibukol nga gamot, dili punoan, bisan tanan sila motubo sa ilalom sa yuta.

q: Which moon in our Solar System has the most craters on its surface?
options: Callisto, a moon of Jupiter
Titan, a moon of Saturn
Europa, a moon of Jupiter
Triton, a moon of Neptune
explanation: Callisto, one of Jupiter's moons, is the most heavily cratered world in the solar system.
fact_tl: Ang Callisto, buwan ng Jupiter, ang may pinakamaraming krater sa solar system.
fact_bis: Ang Callisto, bulan sa Jupiter, mao ang adunay kinadaghang krater sa solar system.

q: What does it show about a person if they ask for help when they are struggling?
options: Courage and strength
Weakness and giving up
Laziness and poor attitude
Lack of ability to solve problems
explanation: Asking for help when you are struggling is a sign of courage, not weakness.
fact_tl: Ang paghingi ng tulong kapag nahihirapan ka ay tanda ng lakas ng loob, hindi kahinaan.
fact_bis: Ang pagpangayo og tabang kung naglisod ka maoy timaan sa kaisog, dili kahuyang.

q: What happens to a peacock's long tail feathers after the courtship season?
options: They fall out and grow back each year
They stay permanently and grow longer every year
They are shed only once in a peacock's lifetime
They curl up and shrink until the next mating season
explanation: After the courtship season, the peacock's long train falls out and grows back fresh the following year.
fact_tl: Pagkatapos ng panahon ng panliligaw, nalalagas ang mahabang buntot ng paboreal at muling tumutubo ito bawat taon.
fact_bis: Human sa panahon sa panguyab, mahulog ang taas nga ikog sa paboreal ug motubo kini pag-usab matag tuig.

q: Where exactly does your nail grow from?
options: From a hidden part under the skin at the base of the nail called the matrix
From the visible white tip at the top of the finger
From the hard surface of the nail plate itself
From tiny cells inside the bone of the fingertip
explanation: Your nail grows from the matrix, a part hidden under the skin at the nail's base that keeps making new hard cells.
fact_tl: Ang iyong kuko ay tumutubo mula sa isang bahagi na nasa ilalim ng balat sa puno ng kuko, na tinatawag na matrix. Ang bahaging ito ay gumagawa ng bagong matitigas na cells na nagiging kuko. Kaya naman ang kuko at ang balat mo ay magkamag-anak na materyal.
fact_bis: Ang imong kuko motubo gikan sa usa ka bahin nga natago ilawom sa panit sa punoan sa kuko, nga gitawag og matrix. Kini nga bahin padayong naghimo og bag-ong gahi nga mga cell nga mahimong kuko. Mao nga ang imong kuko ug ang imong panit hinimo sa managsama nga materyal.

q: What does blood deliver to all the cells of the body?
options: Nutrients from the food you eat
Only oxygen from the lungs
Hormones made in the brain
Waste products from the kidneys
explanation: Blood delivers nutrients from the food you eat to all the cells of the body.
fact_tl: Ang dugo ay nagdadala ng sustansya mula sa pagkain papunta sa lahat ng selula ng katawan.
fact_bis: Ang dugo nagdala sa sustansiya gikan sa pagkaon nga imong gikaon ngadto sa tanang selula sa lawas.

q: Who invented the Cinematographe and showed the first motion picture to the public?
options: The Lumiere brothers of France
Thomas Edison of the United States
Alexander Graham Bell of Scotland
George Eastman of the United States
explanation: The Lumiere brothers of France invented the Cinematographe and showed the first motion picture to the public in 1895.
fact_tl: Ang magkapatid na Lumiere ng France ang gumawa ng Cinematographe at unang ipinalabas ang motion picture sa publiko noong 1895.
fact_bis: Ang magsoon nga Lumiere sa France mao ang naghimo sa Cinematographe ug unang gipakita ang motion picture sa publiko niadtong 1895.

q: Why might a wasp sting be very dangerous for some people, even though it only hurts a short time for most?
options: Some people are allergic to it and can have trouble breathing or swell badly
Wasps release a deadly poison that affects everyone equally
People with weak bones are more likely to break the skin after a sting
Repeated stings always cause a serious allergic reaction in everyone
explanation: Some people are allergic to wasp stings, so they can have trouble breathing or swell badly and need to go to a hospital quickly.
fact_tl: Para sa karamihan, ang saksak ng putakti ay masakit pero gumagaling lang. Pero ang ilang tao ay may allergy dito, kaya pwede silang mahirapang huminga o mamaga nang husto. Sila ay kailangang madaling dalhin sa ospital.
fact_bis: Sa kadaghanan, ang tusok sa putyukan sakit lang unya maayo ra. Apan ang uban allergic niini, mao nga mahimong maglisod sila ug ginhawa o maghubag pag-ayo. Kinahanglan sila dad-on dayon sa ospital.

q: Does the water need to be hot to wash germs off your hands effectively?
options: No — cold or lukewarm water with soap and scrubbing is just as effective
Yes — hot water is needed to kill germs because heat destroys them
Yes — lukewarm water only removes visible dirt, not germs
No — plain water alone removes germs without needing soap or temperature
explanation: Cold or lukewarm water cleans just as well as hot water — it is the soap and friction that remove germs, not the heat.
fact_tl: Maraming nag-iisip na kaylangang mainit ang tubig para malinis ang kamay, pero hindi totoo iyon. Ang malamig o malabang tubig ay kasinglinis din basta may sabon at sapat na kuskos — ang sabon at friction ang nagtatanggal ng germ, hindi ang init.
fact_bis: Daghan ang naghunahuna nga kinahanglang init ang tubig aron malimpyo ang kamot, apan dili kana tinuod. Ang bugnaw o mainit-init nga tubig parehas ra kalimpyo basta naay sabon ug igong pagkiskis — ang sabon ug friction maoy mokuha sa germ, dili ang kainit.

q: What type of soil lies under the Agusan Marsh, and how did it form?
options: Peat — soft spongy soil formed from plants that slowly rotted in wet ground over a long time
Clay — hard soil formed from volcanic ash that settled in the water over centuries
Sand — loose soil formed from river sediment carried from the mountains
Loam — rich soil formed from dead leaves mixed with river mud and water minerals
explanation: Under the Agusan Marsh lies thick peat soil, formed from plants that slowly rotted in the wet ground over a very long time.
fact_tl: Sa ilalim ng Agusan Marsh ay may makapal na lupang malambot na tinatawag na peat. Ito ay nabuo mula sa mga halamang nabubulok nang dahan-dahan sa loob ng basang lupa sa napakahabang panahon, kaya parang espongha ito at puno ng tubig.
fact_bis: Sa ilalom sa Agusan Marsh adunay baga ug humok nga yuta nga gitawag og peat. Naporma kini gikan sa mga tanom nga hinay-hinayng nadunot sa basa nga yuta sulod sa taas kaayong panahon, mao nga morag espongha kini ug puno sa tubig.

q: What are the four ingredients that make up concrete?
options: Cement, sand, gravel, and water
Cement, clay, iron, and oil
Limestone, salt, coal, and water
Sand, glass, gravel, and rubber
explanation: Concrete is made by mixing cement, sand, gravel, and water together.
fact_tl: Ang konkreto ay gawa sa semento, buhangin, graba, at tubig.
fact_bis: Ang konkreto hinimo sa semento, balas, graba, ug tubig.

q: When are people most likely to yawn?
options: When they are tired, sleepy, or bored
When they have just eaten a large meal
When they are excited and full of energy
When they are frightened or surprised
explanation: We most often yawn when we are tired, sleepy, or bored.
fact_tl: Madalas tayong humihikab kapag pagod, inaantok, o naiinip.
fact_bis: Sagad ta mohaya kung kapoy, katulgon, o gilaayan.

q: Why are long-distance overhead power lines often made of aluminum instead of copper?
options: Aluminum is much lighter and cheaper, making it more practical for long-distance poles
Aluminum conducts electricity far better than copper at high voltages
Aluminum is stronger than copper and will not break in strong winds
Aluminum does not rust while copper would corrode quickly outdoors
explanation: Even though aluminum carries electricity a bit less well than copper, it is much lighter and cheaper, making it more practical for long overhead power lines.
fact_tl: Ang mahahabang linya ng kuryente na nakasabit sa mga poste ay madalas gawa sa aluminum, hindi tanso. Kahit bahagyang mas mahina ang aluminum sa pagdala ng kuryente, mas magaan ito kaya hindi gaanong bumibigat sa poste at mas mura. Para sa malalayong linya, mas praktikal ang magaan na metal kaysa mabigat na tanso.
fact_bis: Ang taas nga mga linya sa kuryente nga nagbitay sa mga poste kasagaran hinimo sa aluminum, dili tumbaga. Bisan og gamay nga mas huyang ang aluminum sa pagdala sa kuryente, mas gaan kini, mao nga dili kaayo mobug-at sa poste, ug mas barato. Para sa layo nga mga linya, mas praktikal ang gaan nga metal kay sa bug-at nga tumbaga.

q: Why do large rocks slowly become smooth and rounded over time?
options: Because the sharp edges and corners weather faster than the middle of the rock
Because water fills the sharp edges and freezes, pushing them off
Because the rock gets softer at the middle and hardens at the edges
Because wind carries away the smooth center while the edges stay sharp
explanation: The sharp edges and corners of a rock weather faster than the middle, which is why big rocks slowly become smooth and rounded.
fact_tl: Mas mabilis maweather ang matutulis na gilid at sulok ng bato kaysa gitna, kaya unti-unting nagiging makinis at bilog ang malalaking bato.
fact_bis: Mas paspas mo-weather ang talinis nga ngilit ug eskina sa bato kaysa tunga, busa hinay-hinay nga mahimong hamis ug lingin ang dagkong mga bato.

q: What makes a fossil useful as an 'index fossil' for dating rock layers?
options: The organism was widespread but lived for only a short span of time
The organism was rare and only found in one small region of the world
The organism was very large, so its fossils are easy to find and identify
The organism lived for millions of years so it appears in many rock layers
explanation: An index fossil comes from an organism that was widespread but lived for only a short span of time, making it useful for identifying the age of the rock layer it is found in.
fact_tl: Ang index fossil ay galing sa organismong laganap ngunit nabuhay lamang sa maikling yugto ng panahon, kaya nagsisilbi itong gabay para tukuyin ang edad ng layer ng batong kinaroroonan nito.
fact_bis: Ang index fossil naggikan sa organismo nga kaylap apan nabuhi lang sa mubo nga panahon, busa nagsilbi kining giya sa pag-ila sa edad sa layer sa bato diin kini makit-an.

q: Why is the golden apple snail (kuhol) considered a pest in rice fields?
options: It eats young rice seedlings before they can grow
It drinks too much water from the paddy field
It spreads diseases to farmers who touch it
It blocks irrigation canals with its large shell
explanation: The golden apple snail is a pest because it eats young rice seedlings, damaging the crop before it matures.
fact_tl: Ang golden kuhol ay isang suso na nangingitlog ng kulay-rosas na itlog sa mga halaman malapit sa tubig, at itinuturing itong peste dahil kinakain nito ang murang halaman ng palay.
fact_bis: Ang golden kuhol usa ka kuhol nga mangitlog og rosas nga itlog sa mga tanom duol sa tubig, ug giisip kini nga peste kay kan-on niini ang batan-on nga tanom sa humay.

q: What is the main purpose of a marine protected area?
options: To ban swimming and tourism near coral reefs
To limit or stop fishing so sea life can recover and grow
To create an area where only large boats are allowed
To collect entrance fees for the government
explanation: A marine protected area bans or limits fishing so that fish, corals, and other sea life can rest and increase in number again.
fact_tl: Ang marine protected area ay isang bahagi ng dagat kung saan ipinagbabawal o nililimitahan ang pangingisda, upang makapagpahinga at makadami muli ang mga isda, korales, at iba pang buhay-dagat.
fact_bis: Ang marine protected area usa ka bahin sa dagat diin gidili o gilimitahan ang pagpangisda, aron makapahuway ug makadaghan pag-usab ang mga isda, korales, ug uban pang kinabuhi sa dagat.

q: What part of the immune system does HIV attack in the body?
options: Red blood cells that carry oxygen throughout the body
T-cells that help the immune system fight off infections
Platelets that help the blood to clot after an injury
White blood cells called neutrophils that destroy bacteria
explanation: HIV is a retrovirus that attacks the immune system's T-cells, weakening the body's ability to fight infections and potentially leading to AIDS if untreated.
fact_tl: Ang HIV ay isang retrovirus na umaatake sa mga T-cells ng immune system, na nagpapahina ng kakayahan ng katawan na lumaban sa mga impeksyon — na humahantong sa AIDS kung hindi ginagamot.
fact_bis: Ang HIV usa ka retrovirus nga moatake sa T-cells sa immune system, nagpaluya sa katakus sa lawas nga makigbatok sa mga impeksyon — ug mahimong mosangput sa AIDS kung dili tambalon.

q: Why are there closed seasons when fishing is not allowed?
options: So fishermen can repair their boats and nets
So the government can count all the fish in the sea
So fish can lay eggs and breed before being caught
So the water can become cleaner during rest periods
explanation: Closed seasons give fish time to lay eggs and breed, helping fish populations recover.
fact_tl: May mga panahon na ipinagbabawal ang pangingisda para makapangitlog at makapag-anak muna ang mga isda.
fact_bis: Adunay mga panahon nga bawal ang pagpangisda aron makapangitlog ug makaanak una ang mga isda.

q: How does a star's mass affect how long it lives?
options: More massive stars live longer because they have more fuel
More massive stars live shorter lives because they burn fuel faster
All stars live the same length of time regardless of mass
Smaller stars die first because they run out of fuel quickly
explanation: More massive stars burn through their fuel faster and have shorter lives — a star 10 times the Sun's mass may live only 10 million years, while the Sun lives about 10 billion years.
fact_tl: Ang mas mabibigat na mga bituin ay nasusunog nang mas mabilis at mas maikling buhay; ang isang bituin na 10 beses na mas mabigat kaysa sa Araw ay maaaring mabuhay lamang ng 10 milyong taon, habang ang aming Araw (medium mass) ay nagbibigay ng 10 bilyong taon, at ang maliit na red dwarf ay maaaring mabuhay ng higit sa isang trilyong taon.
fact_bis: Ang mas dagkong mga bituin nagsunog sa ilang fuel og mas paspas ug adunay mas mubo nga kinabuhi; ang usa ka bituin nga 10 ka beses nga mas dagko kaysa sa Adlaw mahimong mabuhay lamang og 10 milyong tuig, samtang ang atong medium-mass nga Adlaw nabuhi og mga 10 bilyong tuig, ug ang usa ka gamay nga red dwarf mahimong mabuhay og labaw sa usa ka trilyon ka tuig.

q: Where does the Ring of Fire form?
options: Along the edges of the Atlantic Ocean where plates spread apart
Where Earth's tectonic plates meet along the edges of the Pacific Ocean
In the middle of continents where volcanoes cluster together
Deep under the ocean floor far from any land
explanation: The Ring of Fire forms where Earth's tectonic plates meet and move along the edges of the Pacific Ocean.
fact_tl: Ang Ring of Fire ay nabuo dahil sa mga plakang tektoniko ng Daigdig na nagtatagpo at gumagalaw sa palibot ng Pasipiko.
fact_bis: Ang Ring of Fire mitungha tungod sa mga tectonic plate sa Kalibutan nga nagtagbo ug naglihok sa palibot sa Pasipiko.

q: What is virga?
options: A type of cloud that forms very close to the ground
Streaks of rain that fall from a cloud but evaporate before reaching the ground
A strong wind that blows rain sideways during a storm
A rainbow that appears below the clouds after rainfall
explanation: Virga are streaks of rain that fall from a cloud but evaporate before reaching the ground because the air below is very dry.
fact_tl: Ang virga ay mga guhit ng ulan na bumababa mula sa ulap pero sumisingaw at nawawala bago pa man umabot sa lupa dahil sa tuyong hangin sa ibaba.
fact_bis: Ang virga mao ang mga guhit sa ulan nga manaog gikan sa panganod apan mosingaw ug mawala sa dili pa kini makaabot sa yuta tungod sa uga nga hangin sa ubos.

q: How do deep-sea creatures survive the extreme water pressure in the deep ocean?
options: Their hard shells act like armor to block all outside pressure
Their bodies have fluid-filled spaces that equalize pressure inside and outside
They swim very fast to avoid feeling the pressure
They only live near the ocean floor where pressure is low
explanation: Deep-sea creatures have fluid-filled spaces in their bodies that equalize pressure internally, so they are not crushed by the extreme water pressure.
fact_tl: Ang mga hayop na naninirahan sa kailaliman ng dagat ay may mga katawang naka-adapt sa napakataas na presyon — ang kanilang mga panloob na organo ay naglalaman ng likido upang iwasan ang pagpisil.
fact_bis: Ang mga hayop nga nagapuyo sa kailaliman sa dagat naka-adapt sa grabe nga presyon sa tubig — ang ilang mga lawas naglalaman sa mga fluid-filled nga espasyo nga nagpantay sa presyon sa sulod aron dili sila mapig-ot.

q: How does yeast reproduce?
options: By releasing seeds that drift through the air
By splitting itself exactly in half to make two equal cells
By growing a small bump that breaks off and becomes a new cell
By laying tiny eggs that hatch into new yeast
explanation: Yeast reproduces by budding, where a small bump grows out from the parent cell and eventually becomes a new yeast cell.
fact_tl: Dumarami ang lebadura sa pamamagitan ng budding, kung saan tumutubo ang isang maliit na usbong na nagiging bagong selula.
fact_bis: Modaghan ang lebadura pinaagi sa budding, diin motubo ang gamay nga usbong nga mahimong bag-ong selula.

q: When you look in a flat mirror and raise your right hand, what does your reflection appear to do?
options: Raise its right hand, just like you
Raise its left hand, because left and right seem to swap
Lower its left hand, because the mirror reverses all movements
Not move at all, because mirrors only show a still image
explanation: A flat mirror does not flip top and bottom, but left and right seem to swap — so raising your right hand makes the reflection appear to raise its left hand.
fact_tl: Sa patag na salamin, hindi nababaliktad ang taas at baba — nakatayo ka pa rin nang tuwid; ngunit ang kaliwa at kanan ay parang nagpapalit, kaya kapag itinaas mo ang kanang kamay, mukhang kaliwa ang itinaas ng nasa salamin.
fact_bis: Sa patag nga salamin, dili mabaliskad ang taas ug ubos — nagbarog ka gihapon nga tul-id; apan ang wala ug tuo murag magbayloay, maong kung ipataas nimo ang tuong kamot, murag wala ang gipataas sa anaa sa salamin.

q: Which statement is true about the number of legs on centipedes and millipedes?
options: Centipedes always have exactly 100 legs and millipedes always have exactly 1,000 legs
Most centipedes and millipedes do not actually have the exact number of legs their name suggests
All centipedes have fewer than 100 legs while all millipedes have more than 1,000 legs
Only young centipedes and millipedes have fewer legs; adults grow the full count
explanation: Even though 'centipede' means a hundred legs and 'millipede' means a thousand legs, most of them do not actually have these exact numbers of legs.
fact_tl: Kahit ang pangalan ng centipede ay nangangahulugang 'isang daang paa' at millipede ay 'isang libong paa', karaniwang wala silang ganitong eksaktong bilang ng paa.
fact_bis: Bisan pa nga ang 'centipede' nagpasabot og usa ka gatos nga tiil ug ang 'millipede' usa ka libo nga tiil, kasagaran wala sila niini nga eksaktong ihap sa tiil.

q: What are El Nino and La Nina?
options: Two different types of tropical storms that form in the Atlantic Ocean
Opposite phases of the El Nino-Southern Oscillation, where Pacific surface temperatures and equatorial winds shift back and forth
Two seasons found only in tropical countries near the equator
Names for the warm and cold ocean currents that flow along the coast of the Philippines
explanation: El Nino and La Nina are opposite phases of a natural climate cycle called ENSO, in which the surface temperature of the tropical Pacific Ocean and equatorial winds shift back and forth.
fact_tl: Ang El Niño at La Niña ay magkasalungat na yugto ng isang likas na pabago-bagong sistema na tinatawag na ENSO, kung saan nagbabago ang temperatura ng tubig sa ibabaw ng Karagatang Pasipiko at ang pag-ihip ng hangin sa ekwador.
fact_bis: Ang El Niño ug La Niña kay magkasumpaki nga bahin sa usa ka natural nga nagbalhinbalhin nga sistema nga gitawag og ENSO, diin nagbag-o ang temperatura sa nawong sa Pasipiko nga dagat ug ang huyop sa hangin sa ekwador.

q: What is the SI unit used to measure acceleration?
options: Meter per second (m/s)
Newton (N)
Meter per second squared (m/s2)
Kilogram meter per second (kg m/s)
explanation: The SI unit of acceleration is the meter per second squared, written as m/s2.
fact_tl: Ang yunit ng pagbilis (acceleration) sa SI ay metro kada segundo kwadrado, na ang simbolo ay m/s².
fact_bis: Ang yunit sa pagdugang sa katulin (acceleration) sa SI mao ang metro kada segundo kuwadrado, nga ang simbolo kay m/s².

q: How does antacid medicine help when you have too much acid in your stomach?
options: It is an acid that cancels out the base already in your stomach
It is a base that neutralizes the excess acid in your stomach
It coats the stomach walls so acid cannot touch them
It absorbs the acid and stores it safely in the liver
explanation: Antacid medicine is a base that neutralizes excess acid in the stomach, relieving discomfort.
fact_tl: Ang antacid na gamot ay base na nagne-neutralisa sa sobrang asido sa tiyan.
fact_bis: Ang antacid nga tambal usa ka base nga magneutralisa sa sobra nga asido sa tiyan.

q: Why is an omnivore described as a bridge in the food web?
options: It only eats food from the top of the food chain
It can eat both plants and other animals, connecting two parts of the food web
It is always at the very bottom of the food chain as a producer
It breaks down dead animals and plants like a decomposer
explanation: An omnivore eats both plants and animals, acting as a bridge that connects the plant-eating and animal-eating parts of the food web.
fact_tl: Sa food chain, ang omnivore ay maaaring kumain ng halaman (gaya ng herbivore) at kumain ng ibang hayop (gaya ng carnivore). Kaya nagsisilbi itong tulay na nag-uugnay sa dalawang bahagi ng food web.
fact_bis: Sa food chain, ang omnivore makakaon og tanom (sama sa herbivore) ug makakaon og ubang hayop (sama sa carnivore). Busa nahimo kining taytayan nga nagsumpay sa duha ka bahin sa food web.

q: How does a heron use its long, sharp beak to get food?
options: It uses its beak to scoop up large mouthfuls of water along with fish
It uses its beak like a spear to stab or grab fish and small water animals
It uses its beak to dig burrows along riverbanks to trap prey
It uses its beak to crack open hard shells of crabs and clams
explanation: A heron has a long, sharp, pointed beak like a spear, which it uses to stab or grab fish, frogs, and small water animals.
fact_tl: Mahaba at matulis ang tuka ng tagak, parang sibat. Ginagamit nito ito para tusukin o sakmalin ang isda, palaka, at maliliit na hayop sa tubig.
fact_bis: Taas ug talinis ang sungo sa tagak, sama sa bangkaw. Gigamit niini kini aron tuhogon o sakmiton ang isda, baki, ug gagmay nga mananap sa tubig.

q: How do many microbes survive when a pond completely dries up?
options: They grow wings and fly to a new water source nearby
They form a tough protective coat called a cyst and go dormant until water returns
They quickly dig down into the soil and breathe through roots
They shrink to a microscopic size and hide inside plants
explanation: Many microbes form a tough protective coat called a cyst and go dormant when a pond dries up, becoming active again when water returns.
fact_tl: Paano nabubuhay ang mga mikrobyo kapag natuyo ang pond tuwing tag-init? Maraming species ang gumagawa ng matigas na balot sa paligid nila (cyst) at parang natutulog na lang. Kapag umulan at bumalik ang tubig, lumalabas silang muli at nagiging aktibo.
fact_bis: Unsaon pagkabuhi sa mga mikrobyo kung mauga ang pond panahon sa ting-init? Daghang espisye ang mohimo og gahi nga putos palibot nila (cyst) ug murag matulog. Kung mo-ulan ug mobalik ang tubig, mogawas sila pag-usab ug mahimong aktibo.

q: How does a rocket move upward using Newton's third law?
options: It pulls on the air above it to climb higher
It ejects exhaust gas downward, and the reaction force pushes the rocket upward
It spins its fins very fast to create lift like a helicopter
It builds up heat inside that expands and lifts it off the ground
explanation: A rocket ejects exhaust gas downward, and the reaction force described by Newton's third law pushes the rocket upward and forward.
fact_tl: Ang rocketship ay gumagamit ng ikatlong batas ni Newton: nagtutulak ito ng exhaust gas papalabas sa mababang bahagi, at bilang reaksyon, ang rocket ay inuudlot pataas.
fact_bis: Ang rocketship naggamit sa ikatulong batas ni Newton: nagtulod kini sa exhaust gas pababa, ug ang reaksyon nga puwersa nagtulod sa rocket pataas ug pasulong.

q: Why does a person who is choking need help very quickly?
options: Because the food will spoil inside the stomach if it stays too long
Because food blocking the airway prevents them from breathing
Because swallowed food can press on the heart and stop it
Because choking causes a person to lose their sense of smell
explanation: Choking happens when food blocks the airway, so quick help is needed so the person can breathe again.
fact_tl: Ang pagkabulunan ay nangyayari kapag may pagkain na humaharang sa daanan ng hangin, kaya't kailangan ng mabilis na tulong upang muling makahinga ang tao.
fact_bis: Ang pagkahap mahitabo kung adunay pagkaon nga makababag sa agianan sa hangin, mao nga kinahanglan ang paspas nga tabang aron makaginhawa pag-usab ang tawo.

q: What does the climbing perch do when its pond water disappears completely?
options: It quickly climbs a nearby tree and waits for rain
It buries itself in wet mud and waits there until the rains return
It releases special chemicals into the air to attract rain
It lays eggs in the dry soil before dying, and the eggs hatch after rain
explanation: When water disappears completely, the climbing perch can bury itself in wet mud and stay alive for several days as long as there is a little moisture.
fact_tl: Kapag tuluyang nawalan ng tubig, kaya nitong magbaon sa basang putik at maghintay doon hanggang bumalik ang ulan. Mananatili itong buhay nang ilang araw basta't may konting halumigmig.
fact_bis: Kon mawala na gyud ang tubig, makahimo kini sa paglubong sa kaugalingon sa basa nga lapok ug maghulat didto hangtod mobalik ang ulan. Mabuhi kini og pipila ka adlaw basta adunay gamay nga umog.

q: What material are the famous Chocolate Hills in Bohol made of?
options: Dark soil rich in chocolate-colored iron minerals
Limestone
Hardened volcanic ash from ancient eruptions
Ordinary sandy soil packed tightly over thousands of years
explanation: The thousands of hills in Bohol's Chocolate Hills are made of limestone, not chocolate or ordinary soil.
fact_tl: Ang libo-libong burol ng Chocolate Hills sa Bohol ay gawa sa limestone, hindi sa tsokolate o ordinaryong lupa.
fact_bis: Ang liboan ka bungtod sa Chocolate Hills sa Bohol hinimo sa limestone, dili sa tsokolate o ordinaryong yuta.

q: Which statement best describes plant galls?
options: All galls are exactly the same size and hold exactly one larva
Some galls are small with one larva, while others are large with many rooms for many larvae
Galls are always created by plants to store extra food in winter
Galls only form on the roots of plants, never on leaves or stems
explanation: Some galls are small with just one larva, but others are big with many rooms for many larvae.
fact_tl: May mga gall na maliit lang at may isang uod, ngunit ang iba ay malaki at maraming silid para sa maraming uod.
fact_bis: Adunay mga gall nga gamay ra ug usa ra ka ulod, apan ang uban dako ug daghang lawak alang sa daghang ulod.

q: Approximately how fast does sound travel through air?
options: About 300,000 meters per second
About 3,000 meters per second
About 343 meters per second
About 34 meters per second
explanation: The speed of sound in air is about 343 meters per second.
fact_tl: Ang bilis ng tunog sa hangin ay humigit-kumulang 343 metro kada segundo.
fact_bis: Ang tulin sa tingog sa hangin mga 343 ka metro kada segundo.

q: In which part of the world are vampire bats found?
options: In caves throughout Southeast Asia, including the Philippines
Only in Central and South America
In Africa and South America but not in Asia
Across Europe and the Americas in forested regions
explanation: There are no vampire bats in the Philippines; they are found only in Central and South America.
fact_tl: Walang vampire bat sa Pilipinas; ang mga ito ay matatagpuan lamang sa Gitna at Timog Amerika.
fact_bis: Walay vampire bat sa Pilipinas; makit-an lang kini sa Sentral ug Habagatang Amerika.

q: Which statement about the maya bird is true today?
options: The maya has become very rare and is hard to find in the Philippines
The maya is still very common and easy to see all over the Philippines
The maya was brought back from extinction by conservation programs
The maya is now found only on a few islands in the Visayas
explanation: Even though the maya is no longer the national bird, it is still very common and easy to see all over the Philippines today.
fact_tl: Kahit hindi na ito ang pambansang ibon, ang maya ay marami pa rin at madaling makita sa buong Pilipinas ngayon.
fact_bis: Bisan dili na kini ang nasudnong langgam, ang maya daghan pa gihapon ug sayon makita sa tibuok Pilipinas karon.

q: What famous volcano is found in the Zambales Mountains of western Luzon?
options: Mt. Mayon
Mt. Apo
Mt. Pinatubo
Mt. Pulag
explanation: The Zambales Mountains include Mt. Pinatubo and serve as the boundary between Zambales and Pampanga.
fact_tl: Ang Zambales Mountains ay isang kadena ng bundok sa kanlurang Luzon na binubuo ng mga bundok tulad ng Pinatubo; nagsisilbi itong hangganan ng Zambales at Pampanga.
fact_bis: Ang Zambales Mountains usa ka kadena sa bundok sa kasadpanong Luzon nga naglangkob sa Mt. Pinatubo; nagsilbi kini isip hangganan sa Zambales ug Pampanga.

q: At approximately what temperature does platinum melt?
options: Around 660 degrees Celsius, similar to aluminum
Around 1,064 degrees Celsius, the same as gold
Around 1,768 degrees Celsius
Around 3,410 degrees Celsius, like tungsten
explanation: Platinum melts at a high 1,768 degrees Celsius, making it one of the high-melting-point metals.
fact_tl: Ang platinum ay natutunaw sa mataas na mga 1,768 degrees Celsius.
fact_bis: Ang platinum matunaw sa taas nga mga 1,768 degrees Celsius.

q: Why are giant earthworms important even though they live underground?
options: They hunt and eat harmful insects that destroy crops
They are important components of the soil ecosystem in tropical areas
They produce chemicals that keep the soil moist during dry seasons
They carry seeds underground that help new trees grow
explanation: Giant earthworm species in tropical areas like the Philippines are important components of the soil ecosystem.
fact_tl: Sa ilang tropical na lugar kasama na ang Pilipinas, matatagpuan ang napakalaking earthworm na maaaring umabot ng ilang pulgada ang haba—sila ay mahalagang bahagi ng ecosystem ng lupa.
fact_bis: Sa pipila ka tropical nga lugar apil ang Pilipinas, adunay dakong klase sa bulati nga makatubo og daghan ka pulgada ang gitas-on—importante sila ingon bahin sa ecosystem sa yuta.

q: How does the pitcher plant's rim help it catch insects?
options: The rim produces a sweet smell that makes insects dizzy
The rim and walls are slippery so insects fall inside
The rim glows at night to attract moths and other flying insects
The rim is sticky like glue so insects cannot escape once they land
explanation: The rim and walls of the pitcher plant are slippery, causing insects to slip and fall inside.
fact_tl: Ang labi at loob ng tabo ay madulas kaya nadudulas at nahuhulog ang insekto sa loob.
fact_bis: Ang ngabil ug ang sulod sa tabo danlog, busa madakin-as ug mahulog ang insekto sa sulod.

q: Who first discovered radioactivity, and in what year?
options: Marie Curie, who discovered it in 1903 while studying radium
Henri Becquerel, who discovered it in 1896 using uranium
Albert Einstein, who predicted it in 1905 in his theory of relativity
Ernest Rutherford, who discovered it in 1911 by splitting atoms
explanation: Henri Becquerel first discovered radioactivity in 1896 using uranium.
fact_tl: Si Henri Becquerel ang unang nakatuklas ng radioactivity noong 1896, mula sa uranium.
fact_bis: Si Henri Becquerel ang unang nakadiskobre sa radioactivity niadtong 1896, gikan sa uranium.

q: According to PAGASA, what does an orange rainfall warning mean?
options: Light rain is expected but no danger to the public
Flooding is possible and people should be alert
Serious flooding is occurring and it is very dangerous
Typhoon-force winds will accompany the heavy rain
explanation: PAGASA uses orange to warn that flooding is possible; the warnings go yellow (be alert), orange (flooding possible), and red (serious flooding).
fact_tl: Gumagamit ang PAGASA ng kulay para sa babala sa ulan: dilaw (mag-ingat), orange (posibleng baha), at pula (delikado na baha) — mas pula, mas mapanganib.
fact_bis: Naggamit ang PAGASA og kolor alang sa pasidaan sa ulan: dilaw (pag-amping), orange (mahimong mobaha), ug pula (delikado nga baha) — kon mas pula, mas peligroso.

q: What is the difference between active and passive immunity?
options: Active immunity comes from medicine, while passive immunity comes from food
In active immunity your own body makes antibodies that last long; in passive immunity you get antibodies from another source and they are only temporary
Active immunity only works against bacterial infections, while passive immunity only works against viruses
Passive immunity is stronger and lasts longer than active immunity
explanation: In active immunity your body makes its own antibodies after getting sick or vaccinated (long-lasting); in passive immunity you borrow antibodies from another source like breast milk (temporary).
fact_tl: May dalawang uri ng immunity o depensa ng katawan. Sa active immunity, ang sarili mong katawan ang gumagawa ng antibodies pagkatapos magkasakit o mabakunahan, kaya pangmatagalan ito. Sa passive immunity naman, hiniram lang ang antibodies mula sa iba, gaya ng natatanggap ng sanggol sa gatas ng ina, kaya panandalian lang ito.
fact_bis: Adunay duha ka klase sa immunity o panalipod sa lawas. Sa active immunity, ang imong kaugalingong lawas maoy mohimo og antibodies human masakit o mabakunahan, busa dugay kini molungtad. Sa passive immunity, gihulam lang ang antibodies gikan sa lain, sama sa madawat sa masuso gikan sa gatas sa inahan, busa temporaryo lang kini.

q: What happens to old rubber trees that no longer produce latex?
options: They are burned to clear land for new plantations
Their strong wood is made into furniture, so nothing is wasted
They are left standing as homes for birds and other wildlife
They are ground up and mixed with soil to make compost
explanation: When a rubber tree gets old and stops giving latex, its strong wood is made into furniture like tables and chairs so nothing goes to waste.
fact_tl: Kapag matanda na ang rubber tree at tumigil na sa pagbibigay ng latex, hindi ito itinatapon. Ang matibay nitong kahoy ay ginagawang muwebles tulad ng mesa at upuan, kaya walang nasasayang.
fact_bis: Kung tigulang na ang rubber tree ug muhunong na sa paghatag og latex, dili kini ilabay. Ang lig-on niini nga kahoy himuon nga muwebles sama sa lamesa ug lingkuranan, mao nga walay masayang.

q: What does a carabao usually do before it grazes on grass?
options: It drinks a large amount of water from a river or stream
It wallows in mud first to cool its body
It rests in the shade of a tree until the hottest part of the day is over
It rolls in dry dust to keep insects away from its skin
explanation: A carabao often wallows in mud first to cool its body, then grazes on grass when it is no longer too hot.
fact_tl: Madalas naglulublob muna ang kalabaw sa putik para lumamig ang katawan, at saka ito kumakain ng damo kapag hindi na masyadong mainit.
fact_bis: Kasagaran molublob una ang kalabaw sa lapok aron mabugnaw ang lawas, dayon mokaon kini og kumpay kon dili na kaayo init.

q: Why does a hot road sometimes look like it has water on it?
options: Water vapor from the ground condenses and forms a thin liquid layer on the road
Hot air near the ground bends light from the sky upward toward your eye, creating a mirage
The road material itself heats up and reflects the blue sky like a mirror
Exhaust fumes from cars mix with road dust to create a shimmering effect
explanation: The mirage that looks like water on a hot road is caused by refraction — hot air near the ground bends light from the sky upward toward your eye.
fact_tl: Ang malikmata (mirage) na parang tubig sa mainit na kalsada ay dulot ng refraction: ang mainit na hangin malapit sa lupa ay nagbabaluktot ng liwanag ng langit pataas papunta sa mata mo.
fact_bis: Ang malikmata (mirage) nga morag tubig sa mainit nga karsada gipahinabo sa refraction: ang init nga hangin duol sa yuta mobawog sa kahayag gikan sa langit pataas paingon sa imong mata.

q: How do mangrove forests help coastal communities during typhoons?
options: They produce oxygen that cools the air and weakens the typhoon
They slow down big waves and storm surges, protecting coastal towns
They absorb excess rainwater into their roots so flooding does not occur
They act as windbreaks that stop all wind from reaching the shore
explanation: Mangrove forests slow down big waves and storm surges, helping protect coastal towns during typhoons.
fact_tl: Pinipigil ng kakahuyang bakawan ang lakas ng malalaking alon at daluyong kaya naililigtas nito ang baybaying pamayanan tuwing bagyo.
fact_bis: Ang kabakhawan makapahinay sa kusog sa dagkong balud ug storm surge, busa makapanalipod kini sa kabaybayonang lungsod panahon sa bagyo.

q: How does a lightning rod protect a tall building?
options: It attracts lightning away from the building and sends it to nearby trees
It safely guides the lightning's current down into the ground
It emits an electric charge that repels lightning before it can strike
It breaks the lightning bolt into smaller harmless sparks
explanation: A lightning rod safely guides the lightning strike's electrical current down into the ground so the building is not damaged.
fact_tl: Dahil sobrang init at lakas ng kidlat, nilalagyan ng metal na lightning rod ang matataas na gusali. Ginagabayan nito ang kuryente ng kidlat papunta sa lupa nang ligtas, para hindi masira ang gusali.
fact_bis: Tungod kay init kaayo ug kusog ang kilat, ang taas nga mga building gibutangan og metal nga lightning rod. Giniyahan niini ang kuryente sa kilat paubos sa yuta nga luwas, aron dili madaot ang building.

q: Where in your body is adrenaline produced?
options: In the pituitary gland located at the base of the brain
In the two adrenal glands that sit on top of your kidneys
In the thyroid gland in your neck during moments of stress
In the pancreas when blood sugar levels suddenly drop
explanation: Adrenaline is made by the two adrenal glands that sit on top of your kidneys, and they release it into your blood when you get scared or surprised.
fact_tl: Ang adrenaline ay gawa ng dalawang maliit na glandula na tinatawag na adrenal glands, na nasa ibabaw ng iyong mga bato. Kapag natakot o nagulat ka, agad nilang inilalabas ang adrenaline sa dugo mo.
fact_bis: Ang adrenaline gihimo sa duha ka gagmay nga glandula nga gitawag og adrenal glands, nga naa sa ibabaw sa imong mga kidney o bato. Kon mahadlok o makalitan ka, dali ra nilang ibuga ang adrenaline sa imong dugo.

q: How long can a climbing perch survive out of water, and what limits this?
options: Only a few minutes; it must return to water before its scales dry out
Several hours to a few days, as long as its body stays wet and its labyrinth organ does not dry out
About two weeks, because it stores oxygen in a special air bladder
Indefinitely on land, because it breathes through its skin like a frog
explanation: The climbing perch can stay out of water for several hours and even a few days as long as its body stays wet; if its labyrinth organ dries out, it can no longer breathe.
fact_tl: Hangga't nananatiling basa at malamig ang katawan nito, kaya ng climbing perch na manatili sa labas ng tubig nang ilang oras hanggang ilang araw. Kapag natuyo ang labyrinth organ nito, hindi na ito makakahinga.
fact_bis: Basta magpabilin nga basa ug bugnaw ang lawas niini, makahimo ang climbing perch sa pagpabilin gawas sa tubig og pipila ka oras hangtod pipila ka adlaw. Apan kon mauga ang labyrinth organ niini, dili na kini makaginhawa.

q: How does a mushroom spread to new places?
options: It releases seeds from its cap that travel by water to damp soil
It releases tiny spores under its cap that the wind carries to new damp places
It grows long underground runners that push up new mushrooms nearby
It drops its whole cap, which rolls away and grows into a new mushroom
explanation: A mushroom reproduces with very tiny spores under its cap, and the wind carries these spores so new mushrooms can grow in other damp places.
fact_tl: Ang kabute ay hindi nagpaparami sa pamamagitan ng buto kundi sa pamamagitan ng napakaliliit na spore na nasa ilalim ng cap nito. Tinatangay ng hangin ang mga spore para tumubo sa ibang basang lugar.
fact_bis: Ang uhong dili magsanay pinaagi sa liso kondili pinaagi sa gagmay kaayo nga mga spore sa ilalom sa kalo niini. Ang hangin modala sa mga spore aron motubo ang bag-ong uhong sa ubang mamasa nga dapit.

q: How do platypuses and echidnas feed their young milk, since they have no nipples?
options: They mix milk into food and feed it directly into the young one's mouth
Milk oozes out through their skin, and the young lick it up
They store milk in a pouch and the young drink from it while inside
They chew food and pass it mouth-to-mouth like some birds do
explanation: Although they lay eggs, the platypus and echidna feed their young milk that oozes out through their skin because they have no nipples.
fact_tl: Bagamat nangingitlog, ang platypus at echidna ay nagpapasuso ng gatas na tumatagas sa kanilang balat dahil wala silang utong.
fact_bis: Bisan pa nga mangitlog, ang platypus ug echidna nagpasuso ug gatas nga moagas sa ilang panit kay wala silay utong.

q: How does an electric eel capture its prey?
options: It wraps its long body tightly around prey to squeeze it
It produces electricity to stun its prey
It spits a poisonous liquid that paralyzes nearby animals
It uses sharp teeth to bite and hold onto prey underwater
explanation: The electric eel can generate electricity, which it uses to stun its prey.
fact_tl: Ang electric eel ay nakakagawa ng kuryente na ginagamit nito para tumbahin ang biktima.
fact_bis: Ang electric eel makahimo og koryente nga gamiton niini aron matumba ang iyang biktima.

q: Where was the First Philippine Republic established in 1899?
options: In Kawit, Cavite, where independence was declared
In Malolos, Bulacan
In Manila, which was the capital of the Spanish colony
In Batangas City, where many revolutionary leaders were based
explanation: The First Philippine Republic was established in Malolos, Bulacan in 1899.
fact_tl: Ang Unang Republika ng Pilipinas ay itinatag sa Malolos, Bulacan noong 1899.
fact_bis: Ang Unang Republika sa Pilipinas gitukod sa Malolos, Bulacan niadtong 1899.

q: Why can an eagle see far more detail than a human?
options: Its eyes are much larger, so they gather more light from a wider area
Its eyes have many more light-sensing cells than a human eye
Its eyes can rotate 360 degrees to scan large areas quickly
Its eyes can zoom in and out like a camera lens
explanation: An eagle's eye has many more light-sensing cells than a human eye, allowing it to see far more detail.
fact_tl: Mas marami ang mga selulang sumasagap ng liwanag sa mata ng agila kaysa sa tao kaya mas marami itong detalyeng nakikita.
fact_bis: Mas daghan ang mga selula nga modawat sa kahayag sa mata sa agila kay sa tawo busa mas daghan og detalye ang makita niini.

q: What does the prefix 'deci' mean when used in measurement?
options: One hundredth (1/100)
One tenth (1/10)
One thousand (1,000)
Ten times (x10)
explanation: The prefix 'deci' means one tenth (1/10 or 0.1), as in decimeter or deciliter.
fact_tl: Ang unlaping "deci" ay nangangahulugang ika-sampu (1/10 o 0.1).
fact_bis: Ang prefix nga "deci" nagpasabot og usa-ka-pulo-ka-bahin (1/10 o 0.1).

q: Where are a mudskipper's eyes located, and why is this useful?
options: On the sides of its head so it can see underwater in both directions
On top of its head, letting it see all around while sitting in the mud
In front of its face so it can judge distance when jumping on land
Underneath its head so it can spot prey hiding in the mud below
explanation: The mudskipper's eyes bulge out on top of its head, letting it see all around while sitting in the mud.
fact_tl: Nakaumbok at nasa ibabaw ng ulo ang mga mata ng mudskipper kaya nakakatingin ito sa paligid habang nasa putik.
fact_bis: Ang mga mata sa mudskipper nagbuswak ug naa sa ibabaw sa ulo, mao nga makakita kini sa palibot samtang naa sa lapok.

q: In which body of water is Tubbataha Reef located?
options: The Sibuyan Sea, between Luzon and the Visayas
The Sulu Sea, part of the province of Palawan
The Visayan Sea, near the island of Cebu
The Celebes Sea, near the southern tip of Mindanao
explanation: Tubbataha Reef is located in the Sulu Sea, part of the province of Palawan.
fact_tl: Ang Tubbataha Reef ay matatagpuan sa Dagat Sulu (Sulu Sea), bahagi ng lalawigan ng Palawan.
fact_bis: Ang Tubbataha Reef makit-an sa Dagat Sulu (Sulu Sea), bahin sa probinsya sa Palawan.

q: Why must drivers be extra careful when there is thick fog?
options: Fog makes roads wet and slippery, causing tires to lose grip
Thick fog makes it hard to see distant things, so visibility is very low
Fog brings strong winds that can push vehicles off course
Fog causes engines to overheat because it blocks air from entering
explanation: Thick fog makes it hard to see distant things, so drivers must slow down and be careful to avoid accidents.
fact_tl: Sa makapal na ambon ay mahirap makita ang mga bagay na malayo kaya kailangang mag-ingat ang mga drayber.
fact_bis: Sa baga nga gabon lisod makita ang halayo nga mga butang, mao nga angay mag-amping ang mga drayber.

q: Who was the first person to suggest that the Sun, not the Earth, is at the center of our solar system?
options: Nicolaus Copernicus, who proposed this in the 1500s
Galileo Galilei, who used his telescope to prove it
Aristarchus of Samos, an ancient Greek who proposed it long before Copernicus
Claudius Ptolemy, who mapped the movements of the planets
explanation: Aristarchus of Samos, an ancient Greek, was the first to suggest the Sun is at the center, long before Copernicus proposed the same idea in the 1500s.
fact_tl: Si Aristarchus ng Samos, isang sinaunang Griyego, ang unang nagmungkahi na ang Araw ang nasa sentro, libong taon bago si Copernicus.
fact_bis: Si Aristarchus sa Samos, usa ka karaang Griyego, ang una nga nagsugyot nga ang Adlaw maoy sentro, dugay pa una si Copernicus.

q: Why does a heron stand very still in shallow water?
options: So fish will not get scared and swim away before it strikes
To cool its feet in the water after flying a long distance
To listen for worms underground with its sensitive feet
To sleep while balancing upright without falling over
explanation: A heron stands still so fish do not get scared, then it strikes suddenly when a fish comes close.
fact_tl: Madalas mong makikita ang tagak na nakatayo at parang hindi gumagalaw sa mababaw na tubig. Ginagawa nito ito para hindi matakot ang isda, at saka biglang sumalakay kapag malapit na.
fact_bis: Kanunay nimong makita ang tagak nga nagbarog ug daw dili molihok sa mabaw nga tubig. Gibuhat niini kini aron dili mahadlok ang isda, dayon kalit nga motira kung duol na.

q: What does a grown frog do that starts the life cycle all over again?
options: It returns to the water to lay its own eggs
It burrows deep into the soil to hibernate for a full year
It sheds its skin and becomes a tadpole once more
It climbs trees to find a safe place to lay eggs in leaves
explanation: Once a frog is fully grown, it returns to the water to lay eggs, restarting the life cycle.
fact_tl: Kapag hustong gulang na ang palaka, bumabalik ito sa tubig para mangitlog, kaya nagsisimulang muli ang siklo ng buhay nito.
fact_bis: Kon hamtong na ang baki, mobalik kini sa tubig aron mangitlog, busa magsugod pag-usab ang siklo sa kinabuhi niini.

q: What does the thyroid gland control in your body?
options: How fast your body uses energy
How quickly your bones grow longer each year
How many red blood cells your blood contains
How well your eyes focus on nearby objects
explanation: The thyroid gland releases a hormone that controls how fast the body works — like a speed setting for energy use.
fact_tl: Sa harap ng leeg may glandula na tinatawag na thyroid. Nagbubuga ito ng hormone na kumokontrol kung gaano kabilis gumagana ang katawan mo—parang setting ng bilis kung gaano ka kabilis gumamit ng enerhiya.
fact_bis: Sa atubangan sa imong liog adunay glandula nga gitawag og thyroid. Magbuhi kini og hormone nga magkontrol kon unsa ka paspas molihok ang imong lawas—murag setting sa tulin kon unsa ka paspas mogamit og enerhiya.

q: When rain falls, what happens to the water that does NOT soak into the soil?
options: It flows across the surface into streams and rivers as runoff
It immediately evaporates back into the clouds above
It is absorbed by plant roots before it can travel anywhere
It freezes into ice crystals just below the surface of the ground
explanation: Water that does not soak into the soil (infiltration) flows across the surface into streams and rivers as runoff.
fact_tl: Kapag umulan, ang ilang tubig ay sumisipsip sa lupa (infiltration) at ang iba ay umaagos sa ibabaw papunta sa mga sapa at ilog (runoff).
fact_bis: Kung mo-ulan, ang ubang tubig mosuyop sa yuta (infiltration) ug ang uban modagayday sa ibabaw paingon sa mga sapa ug suba (runoff).

q: How does your brain use loudness to figure out which side a sound is coming from?
options: A sound is louder in the ear closest to it because your head blocks some sound from reaching the other ear
A sound makes the nearer eardrum vibrate faster, sending a stronger signal to the brain
Both ears hear the same loudness but the brain measures how long the sound lasts on each side
The brain counts how many times the sound bounces off the inside of each ear canal
explanation: Your head blocks some sound from reaching the far ear, so the near ear hears it louder, and the brain compares both to find the direction.
fact_tl: Bukod sa oras ng pagdating ng tunog, ginagamit din ng utak ang lakas. Kapag may tunog sa kanan mo, mas malakas ito sa kanang tainga kasi humaharang ang ulo mo sa kaliwa. Sa pagkukumpara ng lakas sa dalawang tainga, nalalaman ng utak kung saang tabi galing.
fact_bis: Gawas sa oras sa pag-abot sa tingog, gigamit pod sa utok ang kusog. Kung naa'y tingog sa imong tuo, mas kusog kini sa tuong dalunggan kay gibabagan sa imong ulo ang wala. Pinaagi sa pagtandi sa kusog sa duha ka dalunggan, mahibal-an sa utok kung asang kilid gikan.

q: What do liquids and gases have in common that gives them both the name 'fluids'?
options: They can both flow and move from one place to another
They both take the shape of their container and cannot be squeezed
They are both invisible and have no color or smell at all
They both turn into solids when the temperature drops slightly
explanation: Liquids and gases are both called fluids because they can both flow and move from place to place.
fact_tl: Ang likido at gas ay parehong umaagos at puwedeng dumaloy mula sa isang lugar papunta sa iba, kaya kapwa sila tinatawag na fluid.
fact_bis: Ang likido ug gas parehong modagayday ug makagawas gikan sa usa ka dapit ngadto sa lain, mao nga parehong gitawag nga fluid.

q: Which of the following is an example of a protist?
options: Amoeba
Mushroom
Earthworm
Moss
explanation: Amoeba is a protist — a mostly single-celled organism with a true nucleus, along with algae and paramecium.
fact_tl: Ang mga protist ay isang malaking at iba-ibang grupo ng mga organismo na karaniwang may isang selula lamang at may tunay na nucleus — kabilang dito ang mga algae, amoeba, at paramecium.
fact_bis: Ang mga protist usa ka dako ug nagkalainlaing grupo sa kasagaran nga single-celled nga organismo nga adunay tunay nga nucleus — lakip niini ang algae, amoeba, ug paramecium.

q: Where can bacteria be found?
options: In soil, water, air, and even on our skin
Only inside the bodies of sick humans and animals
Only in dirty water and rotting food underground
Only in the ocean where it is dark and cold enough for them
explanation: Bacteria live almost everywhere — in soil, water, air, and even on our skin.
fact_tl: May bakterya halos saanman—sa lupa, tubig, hangin, at kahit sa ating balat.
fact_bis: Naa ang bakterya hapit bisan asa—sa yuta, tubig, hangin, ug bisan sa atong panit.

q: Why is cooking with wood or charcoal indoors dangerous without good ventilation?
options: It fills the air with smoke that harms the lungs
It uses up all the oxygen so the food cannot cook properly
It causes the walls and ceiling to become dangerously hot
It produces electricity that can shock anyone touching the stove
explanation: Cooking with wood or charcoal indoors without good ventilation fills the air with smoke that harms the lungs.
fact_tl: Ang pagluluto gamit ang kahoy o uling sa loob ng bahay na walang tamang bentilasyon ay nagpupuno ng hangin ng usok na nakakasama sa baga.
fact_bis: Ang pagluto gamit ang kahoy o uling sulod sa balay nga walay maayong bentilasyon mopuno sa hangin og aso nga makadaot sa baga.

q: For a deep or severe animal bite, why is rabies immunoglobulin given along with the vaccine?
options: It contains ready-made antibodies that fight the virus right away while the body still builds its own defense
It prevents the wound from becoming infected by bacteria while the vaccine is working
It makes the vaccine spread faster through the bloodstream to reach the brain quickly
It replaces the lost blood and reduces pain so the patient can sleep and recover
explanation: Rabies immunoglobulin provides ready-made antibodies that fight the virus immediately, while the vaccine helps the body build its own defense over time.
fact_tl: Para sa malalalim o malalalang kagat, binibigyan ang tao hindi lang ng bakuna kundi pati ng rabies immunoglobulin — handa nang antibodies na agad lumalaban sa virus habang gumagawa pa ng sarili nitong depensa ang katawan.
fact_bis: Para sa lalom o grabe nga mga paak, gihatagan ang tawo dili lang sa bakuna kondili pati sa rabies immunoglobulin — andam na nga antibodies nga dayon mosukol sa bayrus samtang nagtukod pa ang lawas sa kaugalingong depensa.

q: How do head lice survive on a human scalp?
options: By sucking small amounts of blood from the scalp
By eating dead skin flakes and oils from the hair
By drinking moisture that collects between the hairs
By chewing through the hair strands to reach nutrients inside
explanation: Head lice survive by sucking small amounts of blood from the scalp.
fact_tl: Ang kuto ay nabubuhay sa pamamagitan ng pagsipsip ng kaunting dugo mula sa anit.
fact_bis: Ang kuto nabuhi pinaagi sa pagsuyop og gamay nga dugo gikan sa panit sa ulo.

q: What is true about the Moon during its gibbous phase?
options: More than half but not yet all of its lit side is showing
Less than half of its lit side is showing, like a crescent
Its entire lit side is facing Earth, making it look perfectly round
Its lit side is completely hidden and the Moon looks dark
explanation: A gibbous Moon has more than half but not yet the whole of its lit side showing.
fact_tl: Ang gibbous na Buwan ay higit sa kalahati ngunit hindi pa buong bilog ang naliliwanagang bahagi nito.
fact_bis: Ang gibbous nga Bulan kapin sa katunga apan dili pa tibuok lingin ang naghayag nga bahin niini.

q: How do most minerals found in nature form their crystal shape?
options: They form naturally without any help from people
They are shaped by scientists in laboratories using high pressure
They are carved into crystals by running water over millions of years
They are built up layer by layer inside living organisms like shells
explanation: Most minerals in nature are crystals that formed naturally without any human help.
fact_tl: Karamihan sa mga mineral sa kalikasan ay mga kristal na natural na nabuo nang walang tulong ng tao.
fact_bis: Kadaghanan sa mga mineral sa kinaiyahan mga kristal nga naporma nga natural nga walay tabang sa tawo.

q: What makes the box jellyfish one of the most dangerous sea animals?
options: It has true eyes and venom that can kill a person within minutes
It can grow larger than a person and crush divers with its tentacles
It is completely transparent so divers cannot see it coming toward them
It releases an ink cloud that blinds fish and swimmers in the water
explanation: The box jellyfish has 24 true eyes in four clusters and venom so powerful it can kill a person within minutes.
fact_tl: Ang box jellyfish (Cubozoa) ay isa sa pinaka-delikadong hayop sa dagat — mayroon itong tunay na mga mata (24 na mata sa apat na cluster) at ang kanyang lason ay kayang makamatay ng tao sa loob ng ilang minuto.
fact_bis: Ang box jellyfish (Cubozoa) usa sa pinaka-delikadong mga hayop sa dagat — adunay kini og tinuod nga mga mata (24 ka mata sa upat ka cluster) ug ang iyang hilo makakapat sa usa ka tawo sulod sa pipila ka minuto.

q: In caves where no plants can grow, what serves as the main food source for insects, worms, and tiny animals?
options: Guano (animal droppings) left by bats and birds
Minerals that drip from cave walls and dissolve in water
Dead rocks and dust that crumble from the ceiling over time
Spores from underground fungi that float through the air
explanation: Inside caves where no plants grow, guano is the main food for many insects, worms, and other tiny cave animals.
fact_tl: Sa loob ng kuweba kung saan walang halaman, ang guano ang pangunahing pagkain ng maraming insekto, uod, at iba pang maliliit na hayop.
fact_bis: Sulod sa langob diin walay tanum, ang guano mao ang panguna nga pagkaon sa daghang insekto, ulod, ug uban pang gagmay nga mananap.

q: Where did the hummingbird get its name?
options: From the humming sound its super-fast wings make while hovering
From the low humming song it sings to attract a mate in spring
From the humming noise it makes when it drinks nectar from flowers
From the sound it makes when it taps hollow trees looking for insects
explanation: The hummingbird is named for the humming sound its super-fast wings produce while it hovers in the air.
fact_tl: Tinawag na hummingbird ang maliit na ibong ito dahil sa tunog na 'hum' o ugong na ginagawa ng sobrang bilis nitong pakpak habang ito ay lumulutang sa ere.
fact_bis: Gitawag nga hummingbird kini nga gamay nga langgam tungod sa tunog nga 'hum' o ugong nga himoon sa paspas kaayo niini nga mga pako samtang naglutaw kini sa hangin.

q: What country was the scientist Galileo Galilei from?
options: Italy
Greece
Germany
Spain
explanation: Galileo Galilei was an Italian scientist from Italy.
fact_tl: Si Galileo Galilei ay isang siyentipikong Italyano (taga-Italya).
fact_bis: Si Galileo Galilei usa ka siyentipikong Italyano gikan sa Italya.

q: What is true about worker ants in a colony?
options: All worker ants are female
All worker ants are male
Worker ants are an equal mix of male and female
Worker ants change from female to male as they grow older
explanation: The worker ants in a colony are all females.
fact_tl: Ang mga manggagawang langgam ay pawang mga babae.
fact_bis: Ang mga mamumuo nga hulmigas tanan mga baye.

q: Which spacecraft is the farthest human-made object from Earth?
options: Voyager 1
Hubble Space Telescope
Apollo 11
New Horizons
explanation: Voyager 1 is the farthest human-made object from Earth.
fact_tl: Ang pinakamalayong bagay na gawa ng tao mula sa Earth ay ang Voyager 1.
fact_bis: Ang pinakalayo nga butang nga hinimo sa tawo gikan sa Earth mao ang Voyager 1.

q: Why are giant tortoises from the Galapagos and Aldabra islands famous for their age?
options: Some of them have lived almost 200 years, making them among the oldest animals on Earth
They stop aging completely once they reach adulthood and can live forever
They grow new shells every 50 years, resetting their body clock each time
They hibernate for decades at a time, which slows down their aging process
explanation: Giant tortoises from the Galapagos and Aldabra islands are among the oldest animals on Earth, with some reaching almost 200 years.
fact_tl: Ang mga higanteng tortoise sa mga isla gaya ng Galapagos at Aldabra ay kabilang sa pinakamatandang hayop sa mundo, na may ilang umabot ng halos 200 taon.
fact_bis: Ang dagkong tortoise gikan sa mga isla sama sa Galapagos ug Aldabra apil sa pinakatigulang nga mananap sa kalibotan, nga ang uban moabot og hapit 200 ka tuig.

q: What is special about the elements with the highest atomic numbers on the periodic table?
options: They are synthetic — made by scientists in labs — and disappear quickly because they are unstable
They are the heaviest natural metals found deep inside the Earth's core
They were discovered in ancient times and are among the most stable elements known
They are gases at room temperature and glow when exposed to sunlight
explanation: The elements with the highest atomic numbers are synthetic, made in laboratories, and are unstable so they disappear very quickly.
fact_tl: Ang mga elementong may pinakamataas na atomic number ay sintetiko — ginawa ng mga siyentista sa laboratoryo — at karaniwang napakabilis maglaho dahil hindi sila matatag.
fact_bis: Ang mga elemento nga adunay pinakataas nga atomic number kay synthetic — gihimo sa mga siyentista sa laboratoryo — ug kasagaran kusog mawala kay dili sila lig-on.

q: How do most true sea snakes have their young?
options: They give birth to live young in the water
They lay eggs in the sand at the water's edge
They carry eggs inside a pouch on their belly until hatching
They lay eggs attached to underwater rocks or coral
explanation: Most true sea snakes give birth to live young in the water instead of laying eggs on land.
fact_tl: Karamihan ng tunay na ahas-dagat ay nanganganak ng buhay na anak sa tubig, hindi nangingitlog sa dalampasigan.
fact_bis: Kadaghanan sa tinuod nga mga halas sa dagat manganak og buhi nga mga anak sa tubig imbes mangitlog sa baybayon.

q: Which three things does a seed need in order to sprout?
options: Enough water, the right temperature, and oxygen from the air
Sunlight, soil, and a large amount of fertilizer
Water, sunlight, and salt from the earth
Warmth, a living plant nearby, and plenty of carbon dioxide
explanation: For a seed to germinate it needs enough water, the right temperature, and oxygen — if any one is missing, the seed will not sprout.
fact_tl: Para sumibol ang isang buto, kailangan nito ng tatlong bagay: sapat na tubig, tamang init, at oxygen mula sa hangin—kapag nawala ang isa, hindi tutubo ang buto.
fact_bis: Para matubo ang usa ka buto, kinahanglan niini og tulo ka butang: igo nga tubig, hustong init, ug oxygen gikan sa hangin—kung kulang ang usa, dili motubo ang buto.

q: What is your brain doing while you are asleep?
options: Sorting memories and information even while you sleep
Resting completely and doing no work at all during the night
Sending signals to your muscles to prepare them for the next day
Slowing down your heartbeat to save energy for the morning
explanation: Even while we sleep, the brain stays busy sorting memories and information.
fact_tl: Kahit natutulog tayo, ang ating utak ay abala pa rin sa pag-aayos ng mga alaala at impormasyon.
fact_bis: Bisan natulog kita, ang atong utok abtik gihapon sa pag-areglo sa mga panumduman ug impormasyon.

q: What created the Cassini Division, the wide gap in Saturn's rings?
options: The gravitational pull of the moon Mimas repeatedly tugging particles out of that region
A large meteor that crashed through Saturn's rings and swept out the gap
Saturn's magnetic field pushing charged ring particles away from that zone
A former moon that broke apart and left an empty space as its pieces spread out
explanation: The Cassini Division was created by the gravitational resonance of Saturn's moon Mimas, which repeatedly tugs particles away from that region.
fact_tl: Ang Cassini Division ay isang malawak na agwat sa singsing ng Saturn na lumitaw dahil sa gravitational resonance ng buwan na Mimas; nag-aalis ang Mimas ng mga partikulo sa rehiyong ito sa pamamagitan ng paulit-ulit na gravitational pull.
fact_bis: Ang Cassini Division usa ka lapad nga agwat sa mga singsing sa Saturn nga natukod tungod sa gravitational resonance sa buwan nga Mimas; gipaalis ni Mimas ang mga partikulo gikan sa rehiyong ito pinaagi sa paulit-ulit nga gravitational pull.

q: What happens to a reef when giant clams become plentiful again?
options: The reef grows healthier and more fish come to live there
The reef becomes overcrowded and many other animals move away
