explanation: The regional center of Region VI (Western Visayas) is Iloilo City.
fact_tl: Ang sentrong lungsod ng Region VI (Western Visayas) ay ang Lungsod ng Iloilo.
fact_bis: Ang sentro nga siyudad sa Region VI (Western Visayas) mao ang Iloilo City.

q: What is one way to lower plastic pollution in our environment?
options: Buy less plastic and reuse what we already have
Burn plastic waste so it takes up less space in landfills
Bury plastic in the ground where it slowly disappears
Throw plastic into rivers so the current carries it away from towns
explanation: We can lower pollution by buying less plastic and reusing what we already have, which reduces the amount of plastic waste produced.
fact_tl: Mababawasan ang polusyon kung bibili tayo ng mas kaunting plastik at gagamiting muli ang mga ito.
fact_bis: Makunhuran ang polusyon kung mopalit kita og gamay nga plastik ug gamiton balik ang naa na kanato.

q: What makes the glowing lure of a deep-sea anglerfish light up?
options: Tiny bacteria living inside the lure produce the light
The anglerfish generates electricity in its body that lights the lure
A special oil inside the lure catches light from the ocean surface
The lure reflects moonlight that filters down through the deep water
explanation: The light in the lure of many deep-sea anglerfish comes from tiny bacteria living inside it that produce bioluminescence.
fact_tl: Ang liwanag sa pain ng maraming deep-sea anglerfish ay nagmumula sa maliliit na bakteryang nabubuhay doon.
fact_bis: Ang kahayag sa paon sa daghang deep-sea anglerfish gikan sa gagmay nga bakterya nga nagpuyo sa sulod niini.

q: About how much of the body's total energy does the brain use?
options: About one-fifth (20%)
About one-tenth (10%)
About one-half (50%)
About one-third (33%)
explanation: Even though the brain is small, it uses about one-fifth (20%) of the whole body's energy and needs a constant supply of food and blood.
fact_tl: Kahit maliit lang ang utak, gumagamit ito ng halos ikalimang bahagi (20%) ng enerhiya ng buong katawan — kaya kailangan nito ng tuloy-tuloy na pagkain at dugo.
fact_bis: Bisan gamay ra ang utak, mogamit kini og halos ikalima nga bahin (20%) sa kusog sa tibuok lawas — mao nga nagkinahanglan kini og kanunay nga pagkaon ug dugo.

q: How do people actually get sick?
options: When germs enter the body through touch or through the air
When they stay up too late or eat too much sugar
When bad luck or a curse is placed on them
When the weather changes suddenly from hot to cold
explanation: People get sick when germs enter their body — for example by touch or through the air — not because of bad luck or magic.
fact_tl: Hindi nagkakasakit ang tao dahil sa malas o kulam. Nagkakasakit tayo kapag pumasok sa katawan natin ang germs, gaya ng paghawak o pagkalat sa hangin. Kaya kayang iwasan ito sa pamamagitan ng kalinisan.
fact_bis: Dili magsakit ang tawo tungod sa malas o barang. Magsakit ta kung mosulod ang germs sa atong lawas, sama sa paghikap o pagkatag sa hangin. Mao nga malikayan kini pinaagi sa pagkalimpyo.

q: Why does a hot air balloon rise into the sky?
options: Warm air is lighter than cool air, so it rises and lifts the balloon
The fire heats the metal frame and makes it repel the ground below
Heated air expands and pushes out of the balloon, creating thrust
The balloon's fabric traps sunlight and converts it into upward force
explanation: Warm air is lighter than cool air so it rises, and this is what lifts a hot air balloon into the sky.
fact_tl: Ang mainit na hangin ay mas magaan kaysa malamig na hangin kaya ito ay umaakyat, at ito ang nagpapalipad sa hot air balloon.
fact_bis: Ang init nga hangin mas gaan kay sa bugnaw nga hangin busa mosaka kini, ug kini ang nagpalupad sa hot air balloon.

q: Where in the Philippines can you find stonefish and lionfish?
options: In the warm, shallow seas around the Philippines
Only in the very deep ocean trenches far from shore
In freshwater rivers and lakes in Mindanao
Only near the cold waters north of Batanes
explanation: Stonefish and lionfish live in the warm, shallow seas around the Philippines.
fact_tl: Ang stonefish at lionfish ay matatagpuan sa mainit at mababaw na karagatan ng Pilipinas.
fact_bis: Ang stonefish ug lionfish makit-an sa mainit ug mabaw nga kadagatan sa Pilipinas.

q: What is the regional center of the Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR)?
options: Baguio
Bontoc
Bangued
Lagawe
explanation: CAR's regional center is Baguio, even though the region is made up of 6 other provinces.
fact_tl: Ang Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR) ay isa sa 18 rehiyon ng Pilipinas, matatagpuan sa Luzon. Binubuo ito ng 6 na lalawigan: Abra, Apayao, Benguet, Ifugao, Kalinga, Mountain Province. Ang sentrong rehiyonal nito ay Baguio.
fact_bis: Ang Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR) usa sa 18 ka rehiyon sa Pilipinas, nahimutang sa Luzon. Gilangkoban kini sa 6 ka probinsya: Abra, Apayao, Benguet, Ifugao, Kalinga, Mountain Province. Ang sentro nga rehiyonal niini mao ang Baguio.

q: Why do scientists study asteroids and comets to learn about the early solar system?
options: They have barely changed in billions of years, preserving a record of how the solar system formed.
They crash into planets and bring new materials from other star systems.
They emit radiation that scientists can measure to date the age of stars.
They travel in straight paths that reveal the original shape of the solar system.
explanation: Asteroids and comets have barely changed in billions of years, so they act like fossils that preserve the history of how the solar system formed.
fact_tl: Pinag-aaralan ng mga siyentipiko ang mga asteroid at kometa dahil halos hindi sila nagbago sa loob ng bilyong taon, kaya parang mga 'fossil' silang nagtatago ng kasaysayan ng kung paano nabuo ang solar system.
fact_bis: Gitun-an sa mga syentista ang mga asteroid ug kometa tungod kay halos wala sila mausab sulod sa bilyong tuig, mao nga morag mga 'fossil' sila nga nagtipig sa kasaysayan kon giunsa pagkaporma ang solar system.

q: What did the Cassini spacecraft discover shooting out from cracks near the south pole of Enceladus, a moon of Saturn?
options: Geysers of water and ice particles spraying into space.
Streams of lava flowing from underground volcanoes.
Clouds of ammonia gas escaping from below the crust.
Jets of carbon dioxide released by chemical reactions.
explanation: Cassini found that geysers of water and ice particles shoot into space from cracks near Enceladus's south pole, pointing to a subsurface ocean of liquid water beneath its ice crust.
fact_tl: Ang Enceladus, isang maliit na buwan ng Saturn, ay may isang subsurface na ocean ng liquid water sa ilalim ng makapal nitong crust ng yelo; ang Cassini spacecraft ay natuklasan na ang mga geyser ng tubig at ice particles ay pumupunta sa kalawakan mula sa mga bitak sa timog polo ng buwan.
fact_bis: Ang Enceladus, usa ka gamay nga buwan sa Saturn, adunay subsurface ocean sa liquid water sa ubos sa iyang baga nga ice crust; ang Cassini spacecraft nakakaplag nga ang mga geyser sa tubig ug ice particle nagpuga sa kalawakan gikan sa mga bitak duol sa habagatan nga poste sa buwan.

q: Which vitamins are ripe mangoes especially rich in?
options: Vitamin C and Vitamin A (from beta-carotene).
Vitamin D and Vitamin K.
Vitamin B12 and iron.
Vitamin E and calcium.
explanation: Ripe mango is rich in Vitamin C and beta-carotene, which the body converts to Vitamin A — both important for the immune system and good eyesight.
fact_tl: Ang hinog na mangga ay mayaman sa Vitamin C at beta-carotene (na ginagawang Vitamin A ng katawan)—kapwa mahalaga para sa immune system at para sa maayos na paningin.
fact_bis: Ang hinog nga mangga dato sa Vitamin C ug beta-carotene (nga gi-convert sa lawas ngadto sa Vitamin A)—pareho importante para sa immune system ug maayong panan-aw.

q: Why does an object appear white when light shines on it?
options: It reflects all colors of light back to your eyes.
It absorbs all colors of light into its surface.
It bends light so that all colors mix together.
It produces its own white light from stored energy.
explanation: An object looks white when it reflects all colors of light, just as it looks black when it absorbs all colors.
fact_tl: Itim ang isang bagay kapag sinisipsip nito ang lahat ng kulay ng liwanag, at puti naman kapag sinasalamin nito ang lahat.
fact_bis: Itom ang usa ka butang kung gisuyop niini ang tanang kolor sa kahayag, ug puti kung gibanda niini ang tanan.

q: What is the name of the free PHIVOLCS tool that shows how close a building is to an active fault?
options: FaultFinder
QuakeSafe
FaultMapper
RiskAlert
explanation: PHIVOLCS offers a free tool called FaultFinder that lets people check how close their house or school is to an active fault.
fact_tl: Mayroong libreng tool ang PHIVOLCS na tinatawag na FaultFinder na nagpapakita kung gaano kalapit ang isang bahay o paaralan sa isang aktibong fault.
fact_bis: Adunay libre nga tool ang PHIVOLCS nga gitawag og FaultFinder nga nagpakita kon unsa ka duol ang usa ka balay o eskwelahan sa usa ka aktibo nga fault.

q: How is cleavage different from fracture when a mineral breaks?
options: Cleavage produces flat smooth planes, while fracture produces an uneven break.
Cleavage produces a rough jagged surface, while fracture produces smooth flat edges.
Cleavage happens only in soft minerals, while fracture happens only in hard ones.
Cleavage is caused by heat, while fracture is caused by pressure.
explanation: Cleavage is breaking along flat smooth planes, while fracture is an uneven break — both patterns help identify the mineral.
fact_tl: Ang cleavage ay ang pagbali ng mineral sa maayos na patag na ibabaw, habang ang fracture ay ang hindi pantay na pagbasag; ang paraan ng pagbasag ay tumutulong sa pag-identify ng mineral.
fact_bis: Ang cleavage mao ang pagkabali sa mineral sa patag ug hamis nga nawong, samtang ang fracture mao ang dili pantay nga pagbasag; ang paagi sa pagbasag makatabang sa pag-ila sa mineral.

q: What does a sunbird sometimes do instead of entering the front of a flower to get nectar?
options: It pokes a hole at the base of the flower to steal nectar without helping pollination.
It waits for the flower to open fully before collecting nectar from the center.
It shakes the petals off so it can reach the nectar more easily.
It uses its beak to break the stamen and drink the liquid inside.
explanation: Sometimes a sunbird pierces a hole at the base of a flower to take nectar directly, which skips pollination entirely.
fact_tl: Minsan, sa halip na pumasok sa harap ng bulaklak, tinutusok ng sunbird ang likod nito para makuha ang nektar nang hindi tumutulong sa pagpopolen.
fact_bis: Usahay, imbis nga mosulod sa atubangan sa bulak, ang sunbird motusok og lungag sa punoan niini aron mangawat og nektar nga dili motabang sa pagpolen.

q: In which layer of Earth's atmosphere do rain, typhoons, and clouds occur?
options: The troposphere.
The stratosphere.
The mesosphere.
The thermosphere.
explanation: The troposphere is the lowest layer of Earth's atmosphere and is where all weather events — rain, typhoons, and clouds — take place.
fact_tl: Ang troposphere ang pinakamababang layer ng atmosphere ng Earth (mula 0 hanggang 12 kilometro) at dito nagaganap ang lahat ng weather tulad ng ulan, bagyp, at ulap; ang katamtamang temperatura ng troposphere ay bumababa habang pataas ang altitude.
fact_bis: Ang troposphere mao ang pinakaubos nga layer sa atmosphere sa Yuta (gikan 0 hangtod mga 12 kilometro) ug diri mahitabo ang tanan nga weather events — ulan, bagyo, mga panganod — ang temperatura sa troposphere mohulog habang mosakyat ang altitude.

q: Why do many shorebirds land on mudflats?
options: To feed on the worms and tiny animals living in the mud.
To build nests out of the soft, wet mud.
To cool down their feet after flying long distances.
To drink the water that collects in the mud.
explanation: Mudflats are feeding grounds for shorebirds, which probe the mud to find worms and tiny animals buried inside.
fact_tl: Maraming ibong-dagat ang dumarapo sa mudflat para kumain ng mga bulate at maliliit na hayop sa putik.
fact_bis: Daghang langgam sa baybayon ang motugpa sa mudflat aron mokaon sa mga ulod ug gagmay nga mananap sa lapok.

q: What provides the centripetal force that keeps a car moving in a curve when it turns?
options: Friction between the tires and the road.
The engine pushing the car sideways.
The weight of the car pressing down on the axle.
Air resistance pushing against the side of the car.
explanation: When a car turns, friction between the tires and the road provides the centripetal force needed to keep it on the curved path.
fact_tl: Kapag lumiliko ang sasakyan, ang friction sa pagitan ng gulong at kalsada ang nagbibigay ng centripetal force; kapag madulas ang daan, kulang ito kaya maaaring dumulas ang sasakyan palabas.
fact_bis: Kung moliko ang sakyanan, ang friction tali sa ligid ug dalan maoy maghatag sa centripetal force; sa danlog nga dalan kulang kini nga puwersa, mao nga ang sakyanan mahimong modaplos pagawas.

q: Who proposed the law of universal gravitation, which states that every object pulls on every other object?
options: Isaac Newton
Galileo Galilei
Albert Einstein
Johannes Kepler
explanation: Isaac Newton proposed the law of universal gravitation, which states that every object in the universe pulls on every other object.
fact_tl: Si Isaac Newton ang nagbuo ng batas ng pangkalahatang grabitasyon, na nagsasabing lahat ng bagay ay humihila sa isa't isa.
fact_bis: Si Isaac Newton ang nagmugna sa balaod sa universal nga grabitasyon, nga nag-ingon nga ang tanang butang nag-ibog sa usag usa.

q: What happens to the starch inside rice grains when rice is cooked?
options: The starch dissolves and becomes soft through a process called gelatinization.
The starch turns into sugar and makes the rice taste sweet.
The starch hardens and forms a tough outer shell on each grain.
The starch breaks into tiny pieces and floats out into the water.
explanation: When rice is cooked, the starch inside each grain dissolves and becomes soft through a process called gelatinization.
fact_tl: Kapag niluto ang bigas, natutunaw ang almirol sa loob ng bawat butil at nagiging malambot at masustansiyang kanin dahil sa prosesong tinatawag na gelatinization.
fact_bis: Kon maluto ang bigas, matunaw ang almirol sulod sa matag butil ug mahimong humok ug masustansyang kanin pinaagi sa proseso nga gitawag og gelatinization.

q: What determines whether a sound has a high pitch or a low pitch?
options: The frequency of the sound wave.
The loudness or volume of the sound.
The material the sound is traveling through.
The distance the sound has traveled.
explanation: Frequency determines pitch — a high frequency produces a high-pitched sound, and a low frequency produces a low-pitched sound.
fact_tl: Ang frequency ng tunog ang tumutukoy sa pitch nito; ang mataas na frequency ay nagbibigay ng matinis na tunog, at ang mababang frequency ay nagbibigay ng malalim na tunog.
fact_bis: Ang frequency sa tingog mao ang nagtino sa pitch niini; ang taas nga frequency mohatag og matas nga tingog, ug ang ubos nga frequency mohatag og lawom nga tingog.

q: How do many bean plants support themselves as they grow taller?
options: They climb up sticks or bamboo as they grow and produce pods.
They grow flat along the ground and spread out sideways.
They attach to rocks using tiny roots that grip the surface.
They grow very thick trunks that hold them upright on their own.
explanation: Many bean plants are climbing plants that wrap around sticks or bamboo for support as they grow and produce pods.
fact_tl: Maraming halamang sitaw ay umaakyat sa patpat o kawayan habang lumalaki at namumunga.
fact_bis: Daghang tanom nga sitaw mokatay sa kahoy o kawayan samtang motubo ug mamunga.

q: Why can a single chemical indicator show two different colors?
options: It is a weak acid or base with two forms — one color with hydrogen attached, and another when hydrogen leaves.
It absorbs different colors of light depending on how hot or cold the liquid is.
It reacts with metals in the liquid to produce different pigments each time.
It contains two separate dyes that each respond to different chemicals in the solution.
explanation: An indicator is a weak acid or base that exists in two forms: one color when hydrogen is attached, and another color when hydrogen leaves — that is why it shows two different colors.
fact_tl: Ang isang indicator ay mismong isang mahinang acid o base na may dalawang anyo: isang kulay kapag nakakabit ang hydrogen dito, at ibang kulay kapag nawala iyon. Ito ang dahilan kung bakit may dalawang kulay ang isang indicator.
fact_bis: Ang usa ka indicator usa ka huyang nga acid o base nga adunay duha ka porma: usa ka kolor kon nakakabit ang hydrogen niini, ug lahi nga kolor kon mawala kana. Mao kini ang hinungdan nganong duha ka kolor ang usa ka indicator.

q: What can you find in a single drop of pond water if you look through a microscope?
options: Many tiny living things too small to see with the naked eye.
Hundreds of small fish eggs waiting to hatch.
Tiny rocks and sand grains from the bottom of the pond.
Small bubbles of oxygen produced by underwater plants.
explanation: A single drop of pond water can contain many tiny living things — microorganisms — that are only visible through a microscope.
fact_tl: Ang isang patak ng tubig sa lawa ay maaaring maglaman ng maraming napakaliliit na nilalang na makikita lamang sa pamamagitan ng mikroskopyo.
fact_bis: Ang usa ka tulo sa tubig sa danaw mahimong adunay daghang gagmay kaayo nga mga binuhat nga makita lamang pinaagi sa mikroskopyo.

q: Why does a snake shed its skin?
options: Because it keeps growing and the old skin becomes too tight for its body.
Because the old skin is damaged by the sun and must be replaced.
Because shedding helps the snake stay cool during hot weather.
Because the new skin underneath has better camouflage for hunting.
explanation: A snake sheds its skin because its body keeps growing and the old skin eventually becomes too tight to keep on.
fact_tl: Naghuhubad ng balat ang ahas dahil lumalaki ito, at masikip na ang lumang balat sa katawan nito.
fact_bis: Naglubad ang halas sa panit kay padayon kining nagdako, ug huot na ang daan nga panit sa lawas niini.

q: How far have some whale sharks been tracked traveling from Philippine feeding grounds across the Pacific Ocean?
options: Over 13,000 kilometers.
About 500 kilometers.
Around 3,000 kilometers.
Roughly 7,000 kilometers.
explanation: Scientists have tracked whale sharks traveling over 13,000 kilometers from Philippine feeding grounds to tropical Pacific waters.
fact_tl: Ang mga butanding (whale shark) na na-tag ng mga siyentipiko ay nasubaybayan sa paggawa ng mga napakalayong paglalakbay sa buong Karagatang Pasipiko — ang ilan ay naglakbay ng higit sa 13,000 kilometro mula sa mga feeding ground ng Pilipinas hanggang sa mga tropical Pacific waters.
fact_bis: Ang mga butanding nga na-tag sa mga siyentipiko gisubay sa paghimo og talagsaong layo nga mga migrasyon sa tibuok Kadagatang Pasipiko — ang uban naglakbay og kapin sa 13,000 kilometro gikan sa mga feeding ground sa Pilipinas ngadto sa tropical Pacific waters.

q: What are round bacteria called when two of them stick together after dividing?
options: Diplococci
Streptococci
Staphylococci
Bacilli
explanation: When two round (cocci) bacteria stick together, they are called diplococci — the prefix 'diplo' means two.
fact_tl: Minsan hindi nag-iisa ang mga cocci. Kapag nagkakadikit ang dalawa, tinatawag silang diplococci. Ito ay tungkol sa paano sila nag-aayos pagkatapos maghati.
fact_bis: Usahay dili nag-inusara ang cocci. Kon ang duha magdikit, gitawag sila og diplococci. Mahitungod ni kon giunsa nila pag-areglo human magbahin.

q: What temperature is called absolute zero on the Kelvin scale?
options: 0 Kelvin, which equals about -273°C.
0 Kelvin, which equals 0°C.
100 Kelvin, which equals -173°C.
273 Kelvin, which equals 0°C.
explanation: On the Kelvin scale, absolute zero is 0 K, which is equivalent to about -273°C — the coldest possible temperature.
fact_tl: Sa Kelvin scale, ang absolute zero ay 0 Kelvin (0 K), na katumbas ng mga -273°C.
fact_bis: Sa Kelvin scale, ang absolute zero kay 0 Kelvin (0 K), nga katumbas sa mga -273°C.

q: What is the longest side of a right triangle called?
options: The hypotenuse.
The perpendicular.
The adjacent side.
The base.
explanation: The longest side of a right triangle, which is opposite the right angle, is called the hypotenuse.
fact_tl: Ang pinakamahabang gilid ng isang right triangle, na nasa tapat ng right angle, ay tinatawag na hypotenuse.
fact_bis: Ang pinakataas nga kilid sa usa ka right triangle, atbang sa right angle, gitawag og hypotenuse.

q: About how long is the Cagayan River?
options: About 505 kilometers.
About 200 kilometers.
About 350 kilometers.
About 800 kilometers.
explanation: The Cagayan River is about 505 kilometers long, making it one of the longest rivers in the Philippines.
fact_tl: Ang Ilog Cagayan ay may habang umaabot sa mga 505 kilometro.
fact_bis: Ang Suba sa Cagayan adunay gitas-on nga mga 505 ka kilometro.

q: What are the two layers of the cell membrane made of?
options: Phospholipids, with water-attracting heads on the outside and water-repelling tails on the inside.
Proteins arranged in a rigid grid that controls what enters and exits the cell.
Carbohydrates that form a sugar coat protecting the cell from damage.
Cholesterol molecules that stack to form a solid, waterproof barrier.
explanation: The cell membrane is made of two layers of phospholipids — the heads attract water while the tails repel water, creating a selective barrier.
fact_tl: Ang cell membrane ay binubuo ng dalawang layer ng mga phospholipid — ang mga ulo ng bawat phospholipid ay naghahanap ng tubig (hydrophilic) habang ang mga buntot ay umiwas sa tubig (hydrophobic), na nagbibigay ng proteksyon at kakayahang pumili ng kung ano ang papayaan.
fact_bis: Ang cell membrane hinimo sa duha ka layer sa mga phospholipid — ang mga ulo sa matag phospholipid nagkuha og tubig (hydrophilic) samtang ang mga ikog naglikay sa tubig (hydrophobic), nagbuhat og usa ka selective nga harang.

q: Snakes, fish, frogs, and lizards are all cold-blooded. What does this mean for how they behave in cold weather?
options: They all move more slowly because they take heat from their surroundings.
They all find warm shelters and shiver to generate body heat like mammals.
They all migrate to warmer places so their body temperature stays the same.
They all become more active because cooler air has more oxygen for them.
explanation: Cold-blooded animals like snakes, fish, and frogs take heat from their surroundings, so they move more slowly when the weather or water is cold.
fact_tl: Hindi lang ahas ang cold-blooded—pati isda, palaka, butiki, at buwaya ay ganoon din. Lahat sila kumukuha ng init sa paligid. Kaya kapag malamig ang tubig o ang panahon, mas mabagal kumilos ang isda at palaka, parang ahas din.
fact_bis: Dili lang bitin ang cold-blooded—apil ang isda, baki, tiki, ug buaya. Tanan sila mokuha og kainit gikan sa palibot. Mao nga kon bugnaw ang tubig o ang panahon, mas hinay molihok ang isda ug baki, sama sa bitin.

q: What is the SI unit used to measure voltage?
options: The volt (V), named after Alessandro Volta.
The watt (W), named after James Watt.
The ampere (A), named after André-Marie Ampère.
The ohm (Ω), named after Georg Ohm.
explanation: The SI unit of voltage is the volt, named after Alessandro Volta, the scientist who invented the first electric battery.
fact_tl: Ang SI unit ng boltahe (voltage) ay volt (V), na ipinangalan kay Alessandro Volta.
fact_bis: Ang SI unit sa boltahe (voltage) kay volt (V), nga ginganlan kang Alessandro Volta.

q: What role do crustose coralline algae (CCA) play in a coral reef ecosystem?
options: They coat rock surfaces and provide the surface that coral larvae need to settle and grow.
They produce the oxygen that fish in the reef breathe through their gills.
They filter sediment from the water so sunlight can reach the deeper parts of the reef.
They compete with coral for space and are considered harmful to reef health.
explanation: Crustose coralline algae coat rock surfaces on reefs and provide the critical substrate where coral larvae can settle and grow, making them essential to healthy reefs.
fact_tl: Bukod sa zooxanthellae sa coral, ang mga crustose coralline algae (CCA) ay nagtatago sa ibabaw ng mga bato sa reef at nagbibigay ng mahalagang substrate para sa mga coral larvae na mananatili at lumaki — isa silang mahalagang bahagi ng reef ecosystem.
fact_bis: Gawas sa zooxanthellae sa coral, ang crustose coralline algae (CCA) nagkapay sa mga ibabaw sa bato sa reef ug naghatag og kritikal nga substrate alang sa mga coral larvae nga mopatik ug modako — sila usa ka esensyal nga bahin sa malusog nga reef ecosystem.

q: Who is Ohm's law named after?
options: Georg Ohm, a German physicist.
Alessandro Volta, an Italian scientist.
James Watt, a Scottish engineer.
Michael Faraday, an English chemist.
explanation: Ohm's law is named after Georg Ohm, the German physicist who discovered the relationship between voltage, current, and resistance.
fact_tl: Ang Batas ni Ohm ay ipinangalan kay Georg Ohm, isang Aleman na pisiko.
fact_bis: Ang Balaod ni Ohm ginganlan kay Georg Ohm, usa ka Aleman nga pisiko.

q: Why is it safer for bad-tasting butterflies to gather together rather than fly alone?
options: Birds learn faster that they taste bad when many butterflies with the same color are together, like one big warning sign.
Grouping together makes them look like a larger animal that predators are afraid to attack.
Flying in a group confuses predators so they cannot focus on catching any single butterfly.
Their combined wing flapping creates a breeze that carries their bad smell farther away.
explanation: When many bad-tasting butterflies gather, birds recognize the warning color faster — a big group is like a bigger, easier-to-notice sign, keeping everyone safer.
fact_tl: Kapag maraming paru-paro na pareho ang kulay ang nagtitipon nang sabay, mas mabilis matuto ang mga ibon na masama ang lasa nila. Parang malaking karatula na mas madaling makita kaysa isang maliit lang. Mas ligtas ang lahat kapag magkakasama silang nagbabala.
fact_bis: Kon daghang alibangbang nga parehas og kolor ang magtapok dungan, mas paspas makakat-on ang mga langgam nga baho silag lami. Sama sa usa ka dakong karatula nga mas sayon makita kaysa gamay. Mas luwas ang tanan kon magpasidaan sila nga dungan.

q: How do a centipede's many legs help it move through rocky places?
options: They provide more grip points on rough surfaces and help it squeeze through narrow gaps.
They allow the centipede to run so fast that it barely touches the ground.
They act as sensors that feel vibrations in the ground to detect danger.
They spread the centipede's weight evenly so it can walk on soft mud without sinking.
explanation: A centipede's many legs grip rough surfaces tightly and help it squeeze through narrow gaps, such as spaces between stones — more legs means more points of grip.
fact_tl: Ang dami ng paa ng alupihan ay tumutulong dito na humawak nang mahigpit sa magaspang na ibabaw at makasingit sa makitid na puwang gaya ng pagitan ng mga bato. Mas maraming paa, mas maraming hawak.
fact_bis: Ang kadaghan sa tiil sa alupihan makatabang niini sa pagkupot og hugot sa gansangon nga ibabaw ug makalusot sa sikip nga puwang, sama sa tunga-tunga sa mga bato. Mas daghan ang tiil, mas daghan ang kapyutan.

q: How does a tarsier catch and hold onto an insect?
options: It uses its long fingers with soft pads to grip the insect tightly with its hands.
It catches insects by snatching them out of the air with its mouth.
It pins insects against a branch using its long tail for support.
It traps insects in a web of sticky saliva between its fingers.
explanation: The tarsier has long fingers with soft pads at the tips that allow it to grip insects tightly when it catches them with its hands.
fact_tl: Mahahaba ang mga daliri ng tarsier at may parang malalambot na dulo. Gamit ang mga kamay nito, mahigpit nitong nahahawakan ang insektong nahuli niya.
fact_bis: Tag-as ang mga tudlo sa tarsier nga adunay humok nga tumoy. Gamit ang mga kamot niini, gunitan niini og hugot ang insekto nga nadakpan.

q: What is the function of the umbilical cord during pregnancy?
options: It connects the baby to the placenta and allows food and oxygen to pass to the baby.
It surrounds the baby in the womb to protect it from physical shocks.
It transfers waste from the mother's blood into the baby's blood for removal.
It anchors the baby inside the womb so it does not move too much.
explanation: The umbilical cord connects the baby to the placenta, through which food and oxygen pass from the mother to the baby.
fact_tl: Ang sanggol ay nakakabit sa inunan sa pamamagitan ng pusod, na siyang dinadaanan ng pagkain at hangin.
fact_bis: Ang bata konektado sa placenta pinaagi sa pusod, nga maoy agianan sa pagkaon ug hangin.

q: How can ticks on farm and pet animals be controlled?
options: By regularly checking and cleaning pet dogs, cattle, and carabao.
By keeping the animals indoors at all times so ticks cannot reach them.
By feeding the animals special food that makes their blood taste bad to ticks.
By painting the animals' skin with oil to make it too slippery for ticks to attach.
explanation: Ticks can be controlled by regularly checking and cleaning animals like pet dogs, cattle, and carabao to remove ticks before they spread.
fact_tl: Mapipigilan ang garapata sa pamamagitan ng regular na pag-iinspeksyon at paglilinis sa mga alagang aso, baka, at kalabaw.
fact_bis: Mapugngan ang garapata pinaagi sa regular nga pagsusi ug paglimpyo sa mga binuhing iro, baka, ug kabaw.

q: What does the enzyme amylase in your saliva do while you chew food?
options: It breaks down starch into smaller sugars.
It kills bacteria on the food before it reaches the stomach.
It softens proteins so the stomach can digest them more easily.
It produces acid that begins to dissolve the food in your mouth.
explanation: Saliva contains amylase, an enzyme that breaks down starch into smaller sugars while you chew — starting digestion right in your mouth.
fact_tl: May espesyal na sangkap sa laway na tinatawag na amylase. Ito ang enzyme na sumisira sa starch (almirol) at hinahati ito sa mas maliliit na asukal habang nginunguya mo ang pagkain.
fact_bis: Ang laway naa'y espesyal nga sangkap nga gitawag og amylase. Kini nga enzyme maoy magbungkag sa starch ngadto sa gagmay nga asukal samtang imong gimama ang pagkaon.

q: Which vitamin deficiency causes the disease beriberi?
options: Vitamin B1 (thiamine).
Vitamin C (ascorbic acid).
Vitamin D (calciferol).
Vitamin A (retinol).
explanation: A lack of Vitamin B1 (thiamine) causes beriberi, a disease that affects the nervous system and heart.
fact_tl: Ang kakulangan sa Vitamin B1 (thiamine) ay nagdudulot ng sakit na beriberi.
fact_bis: Ang kakulang sa Vitamin B1 (thiamine) maoy hinungdan sa sakit nga gitawag og beriberi.

q: Why can a sloth turn its head much farther than most other mammals?
options: It has extra neck bones that allow it to rotate its head without moving its whole body.
Its neck muscles are unusually strong, so it can stretch and twist much farther.
Its skull is loosely attached, like a ball-and-socket joint, giving it a wide range of motion.
It has no fixed joints in its neck, so the head moves freely in any direction.
explanation: A sloth has extra neck bones, which let it turn its head far to look around without moving its whole body, helping it save energy.
fact_tl: May dagdag na buto sa leeg ang sloth, kaya kaya nitong iikot ang ulo nang malayo para tumingin sa paligid. Dahil dito, hindi na nito kailangang igalaw ang buong katawan, na tumutulong para makatipid sa enerhiya.
fact_bis: Adunay dugang nga bukog sa liog ang sloth, mao nga matuyok niini ang ulo og layo aron makatan-aw sa palibot. Tungod niini, dili na kinahanglan nga ilihok ang tibuok lawas, nga makatabang sa pagtipig ug enerhiya.

q: What gives a butterfly's wings their colorful appearance?
options: Thousands of tiny colored scales that overlap like roof shingles.
A layer of colored liquid underneath the wings that shows through.
Special cells in the wing that produce light the way fireflies do.
Patterns painted by chemicals released when the butterfly hatches.
explanation: A butterfly's wings are covered with thousands of tiny colored scales that overlap like roof shingles — the powdery dust that comes off when you touch a wing is actually these scales.
fact_tl: Ang makulay na pakpak ng paru-paro ay gawa sa libu-libong maliliit na kaliskis na magkakapatong na parang bubong. Kapag nahawakan mo, may nakakapit na parang alikabok sa daliri mo. Yan pala ang mga kaliskis na may kulay!
fact_bis: Ang mabulukon nga pako sa alibangbang gama sa liboan ka gagmay nga himbis nga nagpatong-patong sama sa atop. Kon imo kuptan, naay sama sa abog nga mopilit sa imong tudlo. Mao kana ang mga himbis nga adunay kolor!

q: What is an important warning sign that a child might have pneumonia?
options: Fast or difficult breathing.
A very high fever with no cough.
Swollen joints and red skin rash.
Sudden loss of appetite for one day.
explanation: Fast or difficult breathing is an important sign that a child may have pneumonia and needs medical attention.
fact_tl: Ang mabilis o mahirap na paghinga ay isang mahalagang palatandaan na maaaring may pulmonya ang isang bata.
fact_bis: Ang paspas o lisud nga pagginhawa usa ka importante nga timailhan nga basin naa nay pulmonya ang usa ka bata.

q: How does grounding remove static charge from an object?
options: It gives electrons an easy path to flow out to (or in from) the ground until the object is neutral.
It blocks electrons from moving so the static charge is trapped safely inside the object.
It heats the electrons until they evaporate off the surface of the object.
It turns the static charge into heat energy that spreads into the surrounding air.
explanation: Grounding works by giving extra electrons an easy path to flow to the ground, and they keep flowing until the object becomes electrically neutral.
fact_tl: Paano gumagana ang grounding? Kapag may sobrang static charge ang isang bagay, ang grounding ay nagbibigay ng madaling daanan para makadaloy palabas (o pumasok) ang mga elektron papunta sa lupa. Umaagos ang mga elektron hanggang maging balanse na muli (neutral) ang bagay.
fact_bis: Unsaon paglihok sa grounding? Kung ang usa ka butang adunay sobra nga static charge, ang grounding mohatag og sayon nga agianan aron moagas ang mga elektron paingon sa yuta. Magpadayon sa pag-agas ang mga elektron hangtod nga mabalanse na usab (neutral) ang butang.

q: What material are a pangolin's protective scales made of?
options: Keratin, the same material as human fingernails and hair.
Calcium, the same material as bones and teeth.
Chitin, the same material as an insect's outer shell.
Collagen, the same material as human skin.
explanation: A pangolin's scales are made of keratin — the same material found in human fingernails and hair — which protects it from predators.
fact_tl: Ang mga kaliskis ng pangolin ay gawa sa keratin, parehong materyal ng ating mga kuko at buhok, na nagpoprotekta dito mula sa mga mandaragit.
fact_bis: Ang mga kaliskis sa pangolin gihimo sa keratin, mao usab ang materyal sa kuko ug buhok sa tawo, nagprotekta niini gikan sa mga manunukob.

q: What is the name of the era when dinosaurs lived on Earth?
options: The Mesozoic Era.
The Paleozoic Era.
The Cenozoic Era.
The Precambrian Era.
explanation: Dinosaurs lived during the Mesozoic Era, which is sometimes called the 'Age of Reptiles.'
fact_tl: Ang panahon kung kailan namuhay ang mga dinosaur ay tinatawag na Mesozoic Era.
fact_bis: Ang panahon nga ang mga dinosaur nabuhi gitawag og Mesozoic Era.

q: Which group of animals goes through complete metamorphosis with four stages?
options: Butterflies, flies, mosquitoes, bees, and beetles.
Grasshoppers, cockroaches, dragonflies, and praying mantises.
Frogs, toads, salamanders, and newts.
Spiders, scorpions, ticks, and mites.
explanation: Butterflies, flies, mosquitoes, bees, and beetles all go through complete metamorphosis — egg, larva, pupa, and adult.
fact_tl: Ang mga paru-paro, langaw, lamok, bubuyog, at salagubang ay dumaraan sa ganap na metamorphosis na may apat na yugto.
fact_bis: Ang mga alibangbang, langaw, lamok, putyukan, ug bakukang moagi sa kompleto nga metamorphosis nga adunay upat ka hugna.

q: How does a dugong feed its young, showing that it is a mammal?
options: It feeds its baby with milk, just like other mammals.
It brings small fish and seagrass to its young in an underwater den.
It feeds its young by chewing food and passing it mouth to mouth.
It lets its young suck nutrients directly from its skin through special pores.
explanation: The dugong is a marine mammal and, like all mammals, it feeds its baby with milk.
fact_tl: Ang dugong ay isang mamalyang dagat, kaya nagpapasuso ito ng gatas sa kanyang anak gaya ng ibang mga mammal.
fact_bis: Ang dugong usa ka mamalya sa dagat, busa nagpasuso kini og gatas sa iyang anak sama sa ubang mga mammal.

q: Who is the unit of force called the 'newton' named after?
options: Isaac Newton, the English scientist who made the laws of motion.
James Watt, the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine.
Galileo Galilei, the Italian scientist who studied falling objects.
Albert Einstein, the German physicist who developed the theory of relativity.
explanation: The newton (the unit of force) is named after Isaac Newton, the English scientist who formulated the laws of motion.
fact_tl: Ang newton, ang yunit ng puwersa, ay ipinangalan kay Isaac Newton, ang Ingles na siyentistang gumawa ng mga batas ng galaw.
fact_bis: Ang newton, ang yunit sa puwersa, ginganlan kang Isaac Newton, ang Ingles nga siyentista nga naghimo sa mga balaod sa paglihok.

q: Why are coal, oil, and natural gas called 'fossil fuels'?
options: They come from the ancient remains of living things buried in rock, just like fossils.
They were discovered in rock layers by scientists who study fossils.
They look like fossils when you dig them up from the ground.
They are fuels made from crushed fossils mixed with stone.
explanation: Fossil fuels get their name because they formed from the remains of living things from very long ago — buried in rock the way fossils are, but burned as fuel instead.
fact_tl: Tinatawag silang fossil fuels dahil galing sila sa mga labi ng mga buhay na bagay noong napakatagal na — parang fossil din silang nakabaon sa bato, kaya lang ito ay ginagamit nating gatong.
fact_bis: Gitawag silang fossil fuels tungod kay naggikan sila sa salin sa mga buhing butang kaniadto kaayo — sama sa fossil, nahilubong sila sa bato, gawas nga kini gamiton natong gatong.

q: Why does a higher concentration of a chemical make a reaction go faster?
options: There are more particles in the same space, so they collide more often.
The particles become larger and hit each other harder.
A higher concentration raises the temperature, which speeds things up.
Fewer particles are needed, so the reaction finishes sooner.
explanation: Higher concentration means more particles are packed into a space, so collisions happen more often and the reaction speeds up.
fact_tl: Pinabibilis ng mas mataas na konsentrasyon ang reaksyon dahil mas maraming partikulo sa isang espasyo, kaya mas madalas ang banggaan.
fact_bis: Ang mas taas nga konsentrasyon magpapaspas sa reaksiyon kay mas daghan ang partikulo sa usa ka luna, busa mas kanunay ang banggaanay.

q: What makes PM2.5 particles especially dangerous to our health?
options: They are so tiny they can travel deep into the lungs and cause health problems.
They are visible to the naked eye and block sunlight from reaching us.
They react with water in the air and turn into acid rain.
They are large enough to be filtered out by our nose hairs.
explanation: PM2.5 particles are smaller than 2.5 micrometres — too tiny to see but small enough to penetrate deep into the lungs and cause health problems.
fact_tl: Ang PM2.5 ay mga napakaliit na particle sa hangin na may diameter na wala pang 2.5 micrometers. Ang mga particle na ito ay masyadong maliit para makita ng ating mata ngunit maaaring pumasok sa ating mga baga at magdulot ng mga problema sa kalusugan.
fact_bis: Ang PM2.5 mga napaka-gagmayng particle sa hangin nga adunay diameter nga ubos sa 2.5 micrometro. Kining mga particle gamay kaayo aron makita apan makalusot sa lawom sa atong mga baga ug mahimong magdulot og mga problema sa kalusugan.

q: A drop of food coloring spreads faster in hot water than in cold water. What is the best reason for this?
options: Particles move faster when it is warm, so diffusion happens more quickly.
Hot water is less dense, so there is more space for the color to spread.
Heat breaks the food coloring into smaller pieces that travel faster.
Cold water pulls the color down to the bottom instead of spreading it.
explanation: Diffusion is faster in warm conditions because particles move faster, spreading through the liquid more quickly.
fact_tl: Mas mabilis ang diffusion kapag mainit dahil mas mabilis gumalaw ang mga particle; mas mabagal kapag malamig.
fact_bis: Mas paspas ang diffusion kon init tungod kay mas paspas molihok ang mga tipik, ug mas hinay kon bugnaw.

q: If a hydra is cut into pieces, what can each piece do?
options: Each piece can grow into a complete new hydra through regeneration.
Each piece will die because animals cannot survive being cut.
Each piece can only survive if it contains the original head part.
Each piece floats away and fuses with another hydra to survive.
explanation: A hydra can regrow lost parts — if cut, each piece can grow into a whole new hydra through a process called regeneration.
fact_tl: Ang hydra ay may kakayahang muling makapagpatubo ng nawalang bahagi. Kapag naputol ito, maaaring tumubo ang bawat piraso bilang ganap na bagong hydra—isang kakayahang tinatawag na regeneration.
fact_bis: Ang hydra makahimo og balik-tubo sa nawala nga bahin. Kon kini maputol, ang matag piraso mahimong motubo nga bug-os nga bag-ong hydra—usa ka katakos nga gitawag og regeneration.

q: Why do most plant leaves look green to us?
options: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light but reflects green light back to our eyes.
Leaves produce green-colored water that fills their cells.
Green is the color of sunlight that passes through the leaves.
Leaves absorb all colors of light and then glow green.
explanation: Leaves look green because chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light but reflects green light back to our eyes.
fact_tl: Mukhang berde ang dahon dahil sinisipsip ng klorophil ang pula at asul na liwanag ngunit ibinabalik nito ang berdeng liwanag sa ating mga mata.
fact_bis: Mura og lunhaw ang dahon kay ang chlorophyll mosuyop sa pula ug asul nga kahayag apan iya ibalik ang lunhaw nga kahayag ngadto sa atong mata.

q: In which region of the Philippines is the province of Sultan Kudarat located?
options: SOCCSKSARGEN (Region XII)
Bangsamoro Autonomous Region (BARMM)
Davao Region (Region XI)
Northern Mindanao (Region X)
explanation: Sultan Kudarat is a province in the SOCCSKSARGEN region (Region XII) on the island of Mindanao, with Isulan as its capital.
fact_tl: Ang Sultan Kudarat ay isang lalawigan (probinsya) ng Pilipinas sa rehiyon ng SOCCSKSARGEN (XII), na bahagi ng Mindanao. Ang kabisera nito ay Isulan.
fact_bis: Ang Sultan Kudarat usa ka probinsya (lalawigan) sa Pilipinas sa rehiyon sa SOCCSKSARGEN (XII), nga bahin sa Mindanao. Ang kaulohan niini mao ang Isulan.

q: Fluorine and chlorine belong to a group of elements called halogens. What is one thing that makes all halogens similar?
options: They are all reactive nonmetals with seven valence electrons.
They are all metals that conduct electricity very well.
They all have eight valence electrons and are very stable.
They are all gases found in Group 1 of the periodic table.
explanation: Halogens like fluorine and chlorine are in Group 17 and share the property of being reactive nonmetals with seven valence electrons.
fact_tl: Ang mga halogen gaya ng fluorine at chlorine ay nasa Group 17, mga reaktibong di-metal na may pitong valence electrons.
fact_bis: Ang mga halogen sama sa fluorine ug chlorine anaa sa Group 17, mga reaktibo nga dili-metal nga adunay pito ka valence electrons.

q: What kind of energy does the rice we eat give our bodies?
options: Chemical energy that our body uses for strength and warmth.
Electrical energy that powers our nerves and muscles.
Light energy that our skin absorbs to keep us warm.
Mechanical energy stored in the grains of rice.
explanation: Food like rice holds chemical energy that our body converts into the strength and warmth we need to live.
fact_tl: Ang pagkain gaya ng kanin ay may kemikal na enerhiya na ginagamit ng katawan natin para magkaroon ng lakas at init.
fact_bis: Ang pagkaon sama sa kan-on adunay kemikal nga enerhiya nga gamiton sa atong lawas aron makabaton ug kusog ug kainit.

q: Why is it often better to eat apples and sweet potatoes with the skin on (after washing them well)?
options: A lot of the vitamins and fiber are found just under the skin, so peeling removes them.
The skin contains the sugar that gives us energy, which is lost when peeled.
The skin protects the vitamins inside from reacting with the air when we eat.
Washing removes all the nutrients on the surface, so the skin must stay on.
explanation: In fruits and vegetables like apples and sweet potatoes, most of the vitamins and fiber sit just under the skin, so eating them unpeeled keeps more nutrition.
fact_tl: Sa maraming prutas at gulay tulad ng mansanas at kamote, marami ang bitamina at hibla na nasa ilalim mismo ng balat. Kaya kung malinis na nahugasan, mas mainam kainin ito nang hindi binabalatan.
fact_bis: Sa daghang prutas ug utanon sama sa mansanas ug kamote, daghan ang bitamina ug fiber nga anaa lang ilalom sa panit. Mao nga kon limpyo nga nahugasan, mas maayo kining kan-on nga dili panitan.

q: How does the Philippine flying fox help forests grow?
options: It spreads fruit seeds as it flies and eats, helping new trees grow.
It digs holes in the soil that let tree roots grow deeper.
It eats insects that would otherwise destroy young trees.
It carries water in its wings to wet the soil for seedlings.
explanation: As the Philippine flying fox flies and eats fruit, it spreads seeds that help new trees grow in the forest.
fact_tl: Habang lumilipad at kumakain, ikinakalat nito ang mga buto ng prutas, kaya tumutulong itong magpatubo ng bagong mga puno sa gubat.
fact_bis: Samtang naglupad ug nagkaon, gisabwag niini ang mga liso sa bunga, busa makatabang kini sa pagpatubo ug bag-ong mga kahoy sa lasang.

q: Why does the flu virus only make your breathing system sick and not, say, your bones?
options: Each virus is specific and usually attacks only a particular type of cell.
Bones are too hard for any virus to enter or damage.
The flu virus is too small to travel all the way to the bones.
Viruses only attack cells that are already weak or old.
explanation: Different viruses attack specific types of cells — for example, a virus that targets the lungs will not attack bone cells.
fact_tl: May iba't ibang uri ng virus, at karaniwang may natatanging uri ng selula ang sinasalakay ng bawat isa, gaya ng virus na tumutok sa baga.
fact_bis: Adunay nagkalain-laing klase sa virus, ug ang matag usa kasagaran mosulong sa usa ka piho nga klase sa selula, sama sa virus nga motutok sa baga.

q: About how long can elephants live?
options: Up to sixty years or more.
About fifteen to twenty years.
Around thirty to thirty-five years.
No more than ten years in the wild.
explanation: Elephants can live a very long time — even up to sixty years or more.
fact_tl: Ang elepante ay maaaring mabuhay nang napakatagal, kahit hanggang animnapung taon o higit pa.
fact_bis: Ang elepante mahimong mabuhi ug dugay kaayo, bisan hangtod sa kan-uman ka tuig o labaw pa.

q: Why do computer technicians wear an antistatic wrist strap when fixing computer parts?
options: It lets static charge drain away slowly so a sudden spark does not damage sensitive chips.
It keeps their hands warm so they do not drop small computer parts.
It monitors their heartbeat to make sure they stay calm while working.
It stops electricity from the computer from passing into their body.
explanation: An antistatic wrist strap connects the technician to ground, allowing static charge to drain away slowly and preventing a damaging spark to sensitive computer chips.
fact_tl: Ang mga tekniko ng kompyuter ay nagsusuot ng antistatic wrist strap — isang pulseras na may kawad na nakakonekta sa lupa. Pinapadaloy nito palabas ang static charge ng katawan nang dahan-dahan, para hindi makasira ng maliliit at sensitibong computer chips ang biglaang spark.
fact_bis: Ang mga tekniko sa kompyuter magsul-ob og antistatic wrist strap — usa ka pulseras nga adunay kawad nga konektado sa yuta. Magpaagas kini sa static charge sa lawas hinay-hinay, aron ang kalit nga spark dili makadaot sa gagmay ug sensitibo nga computer chips.

q: How are whip spiders (Amblypygi) different from true spiders?
options: They have no venom or silk, and use long front legs to find their way in the dark.
They are much larger than true spiders and live only in saltwater caves.
They spin very thick webs and have a more powerful venom than true spiders.
They have six legs instead of eight and belong to the insect family.
explanation: Whip spiders are arachnids found in Philippine caves but they are not true spiders — they have no venom or silk and use very long front legs to navigate in darkness.
fact_tl: Ang whip spiders (Amblypygi) ay isang uri ng arachnid na matatagpuan sa mga kuweba ng Pilipinas; hindi sila gagamba—walang sila hilo o sutla, at ginagamit nila ang napakahabang harapang binti para mag-navigate sa kadiliman.
fact_bis: Ang whip spiders (Amblypygi) usa ka arachnid nga makita sa mga kuweba sa Pilipinas; dili sila tinuod nga gagamba—walay hilo o sutla ug naggamit og grabe ka taas nga unang tiil para mamamala sa kangitngit.

q: What type of lens does a refracting telescope use to gather and magnify light from distant stars?
options: Convex lenses that bend light toward a focus point.
Concave lenses that spread light out to make objects look larger.
Flat mirrors that bounce light from one side to another.
A combination of prisms that separate starlight into colors.
explanation: A refracting telescope uses convex lenses to gather and magnify light from distant stars — this is the type of telescope Galileo used.
fact_tl: Ang refracting telescope ay gumagamit ng convex lens para tipunin ang liwanag ng malalayong bituin at nagpapalaki ng imahe — ito ang klaseng ginamit ni Galileo.
fact_bis: Ang refracting telescope naggamit og convex lens sa pagtipon ug pagpalaki sa suga sa mga layo nga bituon — mao kini ang matang gigamit ni Galileo.

q: What does bile, made by the liver, do in our digestive system?
options: It helps break up fatty food in the small intestine.
It kills bacteria in the large intestine to prevent infection.
It absorbs water from food so the body stays hydrated.
It produces stomach acid to dissolve tough proteins.
explanation: The liver makes bile, which travels to the small intestine and helps break up fatty food so it can be digested.
fact_tl: Gumagawa ang atay ng apdo na tumutulong magdurog ng mataba na pagkaon sa maliit na bituka.
fact_bis: Ang atay mohimo ug apdo nga motabang sa pagdugmok sa tambok nga pagkaon sulod sa gamay nga tinai.

q: What is the conservation status of the giant golden-crowned flying fox according to the IUCN Red List?
options: Critically endangered, requiring international protection.
Least concern, because its population is large and stable.
Vulnerable, meaning it is at risk but not yet in immediate danger.
Near threatened, being watched but not yet classified as at risk.
explanation: The giant golden-crowned flying fox is listed on the IUCN Red List as critically endangered, requiring international protection.
fact_tl: Ang giant golden-crowned flying fox ay nakalista sa IUCN Red List bilang kritikal na nanganganib at kailangan ng internasyonal na proteksyon.
fact_bis: Ang giant golden-crowned flying fox nalista sa IUCN Red List isip kritikal nga nanganganib, nanginahanglan og internasyonal nga proteksyon.

q: Why does a shadow form behind you on a sunny day?
options: Your body blocks the light, so a dark area forms on the other side of you.
Your body absorbs the sunlight and releases it downward as a dark patch.
The ground reflects your shape back up as a dark image.
Shadows are caused by cold air that collects near the ground.
explanation: A shadow forms when something blocks the light — your body blocks sunlight so a dark spot appears on the other side.
fact_tl: Nabubuo ang anino kapag may humaharang sa liwanag. Hindi kayang dumaan ng liwanag sa katawan mo, kaya ang madilim na lugar sa kabilang panig — yan ang anino mo.
fact_bis: Maporma ang landong kung naay mosagang sa kahayag. Dili makaagi ang kahayag sa imong lawas, mao nga ang ngitngit nga dapit sa pikas bahin — kana ang imong landong.

q: A bag of rice is lifted to the top shelf. Compared to when it was on the floor, its gravitational potential energy is —
options: greater, because gravitational potential energy increases with height and mass.
the same, because energy is conserved and nothing was added to it.
less, because moving upward uses up the energy stored in the bag.
zero, because the bag is not moving while it sits on the shelf.
explanation: Gravitational potential energy increases with height and mass (GPE = mgh), so the bag of rice has more GPE when it is higher up.
fact_tl: Ang gravitational potential energy ay tumataas kapag mas mataas ang kinalalagyan ng bagay o mas mabigat ang bagay — sinusukat ito gamit ang formula GPE = mgh (masa x g x taas).
fact_bis: Ang gravitational potential energy nagadugang sa taas ug masa — gisukat gamit ang GPE = mgh, diin m ang masa sa kg, g ang 9.8 m/s², ug h ang taas sa metro.

q: Some people sneeze when they walk from a dark room into bright sunlight. What causes this?
options: The nerves for the eyes and nose are close together, and the signals get crossed.
Bright light dries out the inside of the nose, irritating it.
Sunlight causes a small allergic reaction in sensitive people.
The pupils shrink so fast that it creates pressure that triggers a sneeze.
explanation: The nerves for the eyes and nose lie close together, so a sudden bright-light signal to the eyes can cross into the nose nerves and trigger a sneeze.
fact_tl: May mga taong napapabahing kapag biglang sumilip sa maliwanag na araw mula sa madilim na lugar. Nangyayari ito dahil sa magkalapit na nerbiyo ng mata at ilong na nagkakamali ng senyas; normal lang ito sa ilang tao.
fact_bis: Adunay mga tawo nga mobahin kung kalit silang mogawas sa hayag nga adlaw gikan sa ngitngit nga lugar. Mahitabo kini tungod kay ang mga nerbiyo sa mata ug ilong duol ra ug magkasaylo ang signal; normal ra kini sa pipila ka tawo.

q: What do mosquito coils (katol) and repellent lotions like DEET do for people?
options: They protect people from mosquito bites.
They kill all mosquitoes within a large area.
They treat the itching and swelling from a mosquito bite.
They attract mosquitoes away from people toward a safe area.
explanation: Mosquito coils and repellent lotions such as DEET protect people from mosquito bites and are widely used by Filipinos in the evening.
fact_tl: Ang katol (mosquito coil) at mga lotion na repellent tulad ng DEET ay nagpoprotekta sa tao mula sa kagat ng lamok; ang mga ito ay ginagamit ng maraming Pilipino tuwing gabi.
fact_bis: Ang katol (mosquito coil) ug mga lotion nga repellent sama sa DEET nagpanalipod sa mga tawo gikan sa kagat sa lamok; kini kaylap nga gigamit sa mga Pilipino sa gabii.

q: Why does the skin around a healing wound often feel warm and look red?
options: Extra blood is sent to the area, bringing repair cells that make it warm and red.
The wound produces heat as new skin cells burn energy to grow quickly.
Bacteria in the wound release a chemical that warms the surrounding skin.
The skin tightens around the wound, trapping heat and turning red.
explanation: The body sends extra blood to a healing wound, and that blood brings cleaning and repair cells — making the area feel warm and look red.
fact_tl: Kapag may sugat na ginagamot ng katawan, nagpapadala ito ng mas maraming dugo sa lugar na iyon. Kaya minsan mainit at mamula ang paligid ng sugat — dala ng dugo ang mga panlinis at panggamot na selula.
fact_bis: Kung ang lawas nag-ayo og samad, magpadala kini og mas daghan nga dugo sa maong dapit. Mao nga usahay init ug mapula ang palibot sa samad — ang dugo nagdala sa mga selula nga manglimpyo ug mang-ayo.

q: Where does the gasoline used in cars originally come from?
options: Crude oil, a fossil fuel that is separated into gasoline, diesel, and other products at a refinery.
Natural gas that is compressed and converted into liquid fuel.
Coal that is heated until it melts and turns into a liquid fuel.
Plant seeds that are pressed to release their natural oils.
explanation: Gasoline comes from crude oil — at a refinery, crude oil is separated into gasoline, diesel, and even plastic.
fact_tl: Ang gasolina sa kotse ay galing sa krudo o crude oil na isang fossil fuel. Sa refinery, hinahati ang krudo para gawing gasolina, diesel, at kahit plastik. Kaya marami sa gamit natin araw-araw ay nagmula sa langis.
fact_bis: Ang gasolina sa awto naggikan sa krudo o crude oil nga usa ka fossil fuel. Sa refinery, gibahin ang krudo aron mahimong gasolina, diesel, ug bisan plastik. Daghan diay sa atong gamit adlaw-adlaw naggikan sa lana.

q: On what kind of plant does a durian fruit grow?
options: A very tall tree, taller than a house, with heavy fruits hanging from the branches.
A low climbing vine that spreads along the forest floor.
A medium-sized bush with sharp thorns around its trunk.
An underground plant whose fruits must be dug up from the soil.
explanation: Durian grows on a very tall tree that can be taller than a house, with heavy fruits hanging from its branches.
fact_tl: Tumutubo ang durian sa napakataas na puno na maaaring umabot nang mas mataas pa sa bahay. Nakabitin ang mabibigat na bunga sa mga sanga, kaya kailangang mag-ingat kapag nahuhulog ang mga ito.
fact_bis: Motubo ang durian sa taas kaayo nga kahoy nga mas taas pa sa balay. Nagbitay ang bug-at nga mga bunga sa mga sanga, mao nga mag-amping kung mahulog kini.

q: What is one way that the University of the Philippines and other local universities help the country?
options: They conduct research in science and technology to help national development.
They print all the school textbooks used by public school students.
They train government soldiers for national defense.
They manage the country's national museums and cultural centers.
explanation: Universities like the University of the Philippines conduct research in science, technology, and other fields to support national development.
fact_tl: Ang Unibersidad ng Pilipinas at iba pang unibersidad sa bansa ay nagsasagawa ng mga pananaliksik sa agham, teknolohiya, at iba pang larangan upang makatulong sa pag-unlad ng bansa.
fact_bis: Ang Unibersidad ng Pilipinas ug uban pang mga unibersidad sa nasod nagpadagan og mga panukiduki sa siyensiya, teknolohiya, ug uban pang larangan aron matabangan ang pag-uswag sa nasod.

q: What nationality was the famous astronomer and physicist Galileo Galilei?
options: Italian
Greek
Spanish
German
explanation: Galileo Galilei was an Italian astronomer and physicist.
fact_tl: Si Galileo Galilei ay isang Italyano (Italian) na astronomo at pisisista.
fact_bis: Si Galileo Galilei usa ka Italyano (Italian) nga astronomo ug pisisista.

q: Why are mangrove forests important for young fish and shrimp?
options: Their tangled roots form a safe nursery where young fish and shrimp can grow.
They produce a special chemical that young sea creatures eat.
Their shade keeps the ocean water cool enough for young fish to survive.
They trap large predators, preventing them from reaching the open sea.
explanation: The tangled roots of mangroves form a safe nursery where young fish and shrimp grow before heading out to the open sea.
fact_tl: Ang magulong ugat ng bakawan ay nagiging ligtas na taguan kung saan lumalaki ang maliliit na isda at hipon bago lumabas sa malawak na dagat.
fact_bis: Ang nagkagubot nga gamot sa bakhaw mahimong luwas nga tagoanan diin modako ang gagmayng isda ug pasayan sa dili pa mogawas sa lapad nga dagat.

q: Why is water said to be essential for ALL living things — both animals and plants?
options: The cells of all living things are filled with water, and all life processes depend on it.
Water gives all living things the energy they need to grow and move.
All living things need water to keep their bodies at the right temperature.
Living things absorb sunlight through water held in their cells.
explanation: Water is essential for all living things because their cells are filled with water and all life processes depend on it.
fact_tl: Ang tubig ay mahalaga para sa lahat ng nabubuhay na bagay — ang mga cell ng mga hayop at halaman ay puno ng tubig, at ang lahat ng proseso ng buhay ay nakasalalay sa tubig.
fact_bis: Ang tubig mahinungdanon alang sa tanang mga nabubuhay nga butang — ang mga cell sa mga mananap ug tanom napuno sa tubig, ug ang tanang proseso sa kinabuhi nagsalig sa tubig.

q: Why do tiny new blood vessels grow into a wound as it heals?
options: They carry the oxygen and nutrients that new cells need to live and grow.
They seal the wound shut by forming a wall of blood.
They bring chemicals that harden the skin into a permanent scar.
They remove damaged cells by flushing them out with blood.
explanation: As a wound heals, tiny new blood vessels grow into it to carry the oxygen and nutrients that the new skin cells need.
fact_tl: Habang gumagaling ang sugat, tumutubo ang bagong maliliit na ugat ng dugo papunta rito. Dala ng mga ugat na ito ang oxygen at sustansya na kailangan ng bagong selula para mabuhay at lumaki.
fact_bis: Samtang nag-ayo ang samad, magtubo ang gagmayng bag-ong ugat sa dugo paingon niini. Kini nga mga ugat magdala og oxygen ug sustansya nga gikinahanglan sa bag-ong selula aron mabuhi ug motubo.

q: Water hyacinth is often seen as a problem weed, but it has one useful ability. What is it?
options: Its roots can soak up dirt and toxins from water, helping to clean polluted channels.
Its large leaves block sunlight so algae cannot grow in the water.
It produces a natural chemical that kills harmful bacteria in rivers.
It grows so fast that it pushes pollutants to the banks where they dry out.
explanation: Water hyacinth roots can absorb dirt and toxins from water, so it is sometimes grown on purpose in polluted wastewater channels to help clean them.
fact_tl: May kakaibang kakayahan ang water hyacinth: nasisipsip ng mga ugat nito ang ilang dumi at lason sa tubig. Kaya minsan, sinasadyang itanim ito sa mga maruming lagusan ng tubig para makatulong itong maglinis—pero kailangang bantayan para hindi naman ito kumalat nang sobra.
fact_bis: Naa'y talagsaon nga abilidad ang water hyacinth: ang mga gamot niini makasuyop sa pipila ka hugaw ug hilo sa tubig. Busa usahay tinuyo kining itanom sa mga hugaw nga agianan sa tubig aron makatabang sa paghinlo—apan kinahanglan bantayan aron dili kini mokatag og sobra.

q: How does geothermal energy produce electricity?
options: Heat deep underground turns water into steam, and that steam spins a turbine to make electricity.
Rainwater is collected and dropped from a great height to spin a turbine.
Sunlight heats panels buried underground, which then power a generator.
Underground volcanoes burn coal, and the heat is collected as electricity.
explanation: Geothermal energy works because intense heat deep underground turns water into steam, and that steam spins a turbine to generate electricity.
fact_tl: Sa ilalim ng lupa, sobrang init kaya umuusok ang tubig at nagiging singaw. Ang singaw na ito ang umiikot sa turbine para gumawa ng kuryente. Iyan ang geothermal energy: kuryenteng galing sa init ng Mundo.
fact_bis: Sa ilawom sa yuta, init kaayo busa ang tubig mahimong singaw. Kini nga singaw maoy mutuyok sa turbine aron mahimong kuryente. Mao na ang geothermal: kuryente gikan sa init sa Kalibutan.

q: Movies often show mutations giving people superpowers. What really happens when a mutation occurs in a person's DNA?
options: It is usually a tiny change that has little or no effect — no one has ever gained the power to fly from a mutation.
It always causes a serious disease that must be treated by doctors.
It copies the traits of a nearby animal, giving the person animal-like abilities.
It makes the body produce extra muscles, increasing the person's strength.
explanation: In reality, a mutation is a tiny change in DNA that usually has no effect or only a small one — no person has ever gained a superpower like flying from a mutation.
fact_tl: Sa mga pelikula, ang mutation daw ang dahilan kung bakit may lumilipad o may super lakas. Sa totoong buhay, hindi ganoon. Ang totoong mutation ay napakaliit na pagbabago sa DNA na karaniwang walang epekto o kaya'y maliit lamang. Walang taong nagkaroon ng kapangyarihang lumipad dahil sa mutation.
fact_bis: Sa mga sine, ang mutation kuno mao ang hinungdan nganong may makalupad o may super kusog. Sa tinuod nga kinabuhi, dili ingon ana. Ang tinuod nga mutation usa ka gamay kaayo nga kausaban sa DNA nga kasagaran walay epekto o gamay ra. Wala pa gyoy tawo nga nakaangkon og gahum sa paglupad tungod sa mutation.

q: Is hard water safe for people to drink?
options: Yes, it is usually safe to drink, and its minerals like calcium can even be good for the body.
No, the extra minerals in hard water are poisonous to humans.
No, hard water must always be boiled first to remove the dangerous minerals.
Yes, but only if filtered first because the hard particles can damage the throat.
explanation: Hard water is usually safe to drink, and some of its minerals such as calcium are actually good for the body.
fact_tl: Karaniwang ligtas pa rin inumin ang matigas na tubig, at ang ilang mineral dito gaya ng calcium ay mabuti pa para sa katawan.
fact_bis: Sagad luwas gihapon imnon ang gahi nga tubig, ug ang uban niini nga mineral sama sa calcium maayo pa para sa lawas.

q: Why is a full box harder to push across the floor than an empty box of the same size?
options: The full box is heavier, so it presses the surfaces together more, creating more friction.
The full box has more air inside it, which pushes down and increases resistance.
The contents of the full box shift around and create extra bumps against the floor.
A full box has a different shape than an empty one, so it catches more air.
explanation: Heavier objects press the two surfaces together more, which increases friction — that is why a full box is harder to push than an empty one.
fact_tl: Mas malaki ang friction kapag mas mabigat ang bagay na gumagalaw sa isang ibabaw. Kaya mas mahirap itulak ang isang punong kahon kaysa sa isang walang laman — ang bigat ay mas idinidiin ang dalawang ibabaw, kaya mas malakas silang magkiskis. Mas mabigat, mas malaking friction.
fact_bis: Mas dako ang friction kung mas bug-at ang butang nga naglihok sa usa ka nawong. Mao nga mas lisod itulod ang puno nga kahon kaysa walay sulod — ang kabug-at mas magdiin sa duha ka nawong, mao nga mas kusog silang magkuskos. Mas bug-at, mas dako nga friction.

q: When do jellyfish sting people?
options: Only when their tentacles accidentally touch a person's skin.
Whenever they sense a person swimming nearby.
Only when a person makes loud noises in the water.
Whenever they are hungry and looking for food.
explanation: Jellyfish do not chase people — they only sting when their tentacles touch our skin by accident.
fact_tl: Hindi hinahabol ng dikya ang tao; nakakapaso lang ito kapag nadikit ang galamay nito sa balat natin.
fact_bis: Dili gukoron sa dikya ang tao; makapaso lang kini kon madikit ang galamay niini sa atong panit.

q: Which of the following best describes how Philippine land is used?
options: For farming, forests, and urban areas, with agriculture covering a large portion of the land.
Almost entirely for forests, with only a small amount used for farming.
Mostly for cities and urban areas, with very little land left for farming.
Equally divided between farming, urban areas, and ocean fish farms.
explanation: Philippine land is used for farming, forests, and urban areas, with agriculture covering a large portion of the country's land area.
fact_tl: Ang lupain ng Pilipinas ay ginagamit para sa pagsasaka, kagubatan, at mga lungsod; ang pagsasaka ay sumasaklaw ng malaking bahagi ng lupain sa buong bansa.
fact_bis: Ang yuta sa Pilipinas gigamit alang sa pagsasaka, kagubatan, ug mga lungsod; ang agrikultura nagsakop sa dakong bahin sa sukat sa yuta sa nasud.

q: What happened to the land around Mount Pinatubo in the decades after its 1991 eruption?
options: Pioneer plants gradually returned and slowly opened the way for more complex ecosystems.
The land stayed completely barren for over a hundred years with no plant life.
Only grasses returned, as trees can never grow again on volcanic soil.
Animals returned first, then attracted plants by spreading seeds quickly.
explanation: Within a few decades after the 1991 eruption, pioneer plant species colonized the barren landscape and opened the way for more complex ecosystems to develop over time.
fact_tl: Sa loob ng ilang dekada pagkatapos ng 1991 na pagsabog ng Pinatubo, ang mga puno at halaman ay unti-unting bumalik sa dating barren na landscape; ang mga pangunahing halaman na luminisya ng lugar ay mga pioneer species na nagbukas ng daan para sa mas kumplikadong mga ecosystem sa paglipas ng panahon.
fact_bis: Sulod sa pipila ka dekada human sa pagsabog sa Pinatubo sa 1991, ang mga kahon ug halaman hinay-hinay nakabalik sa kanhing barren nga talan-awon; ang una nga mga halaman nga nag-kolonya mao ang mga pioneer species nga nagbukas sa dalan alang sa mas komplikado nga mga ecosystem sa paglabay sa oras.

q: What is one way that freshwater marshes and mangrove forests are different from each other?
options: Marshes have fresh water while mangrove forests have salty water.
Marshes are found in the ocean while mangroves grow only on dry land.
Marshes are made by people while mangroves grow naturally.
Marshes are deeper than mangroves and hold more water year-round.
explanation: Some wetlands like marshes have fresh water, while others like mangrove forests have salty water — both are types of wetlands.
fact_tl: May mga latian na may tabang na tubig tulad ng marsh, at may maalat na tubig tulad ng bakawan.
fact_bis: Adunay mga lamakan nga tab-ang ang tubig sama sa marsh, ug adunay parat sama sa kabakhawan.

q: Lead is described as a heavy, dense metal. Which value best describes its density?
options: About 11.3 g/cm³
About 1.0 g/cm³, similar to water
About 2.7 g/cm³, similar to aluminum
About 7.9 g/cm³, similar to iron
explanation: Lead has a density of about 11.3 g/cm³, making it much denser and heavier than most common metals.
fact_tl: Ang tingga (lead) ay isang mabigat at siksik na metal, na may densidad na mga 11.3 g/cm³.
fact_bis: Ang tingga (lead) usa ka bug-at ug dasok nga metal, nga adunay densidad nga mga 11.3 g/cm³.

q: In countries far from the equator, how does the length of daytime change through the year?
options: Days are longer in summer and shorter in winter.
Days are longer in winter and shorter in summer.
The length of daytime stays the same all year round.
Days are longest in spring and shortest in autumn.
explanation: In countries far from the equator, daytime is longer in summer and shorter in winter because of how Earth is tilted as it orbits the Sun.
fact_tl: Sa mga bansang malayo sa ekwador, nagbabago ang haba ng araw sa buong taon — mahaba ang araw kapag tag-init at maikli kapag taglamig.
fact_bis: Sa mga nasod nga layo sa ekwador, ang gitas-on sa adlaw nagbag-o sa tibuok tuig — taas ang adlaw sa ting-init ug mubo sa tingtugnaw.

q: In an isobaric process involving a gas, what stays constant while temperature and volume can change?
options: Pressure stays constant.
Volume stays constant.
Temperature stays constant.
The number of gas particles stays constant.
explanation: An isobaric process is one where pressure stays constant — Charles's Law describes how volume and temperature change together at constant pressure.
fact_tl: Sa isang isobaric na proseso, ang presyon ng gas ay nanatiling pareho habang nagbabago ang temperatura at dami. Ang Charles's Law ay naglalarawan ng ganitong proseso: ang V/T ay pare-pareho (habang pantay ang presyon).
fact_bis: Sa usa ka isobaric nga proseso, ang presyon sa gas nagpabilin nga pareho habang nagbabago ang temperatura ug dami. Ang Charles's Law naghulagway niining proseso: ang V/T kanunay (sa kanunay nga presyon).

q: Aside from destroying coral reefs, blast fishing is also dangerous because —
options: the fishers themselves can be injured or lose a hand if the bomb explodes early.
the loud sound scares fish away from the area permanently.
the chemicals in the explosives poison the fishers' drinking water.
the weight of the nets used with explosives can capsize small boats.
explanation: Blast fishing is dangerous to the fishers themselves — if the bomb explodes too soon, they can be injured or lose a hand.
fact_tl: Delikado rin ang pangbobomba sa mismong mga mangingisda dahil maaari silang masugatan o mawalan ng kamay kapag pumutok ito nang maaga.
fact_bis: Delikado usab ang pagbomba sa mismong mga mangingisda kay mahimo silang masamdan o mawad-an og kamot kung mobuto kini og sayo.

q: What separates one island from another in the Philippines?
options: Water surrounds every island, keeping them apart
Mountains and rivers divide the islands from each other
Deep valleys cut through the land between islands
Thick forests form natural borders between islands
explanation: Every island in the Philippines is surrounded by water, which is what separates the islands from one another.
fact_tl: Ang bawat pulo ng Pilipinas ay napapaligiran ng tubig kaya naghihiwalay ang mga ito sa isa't isa.
fact_bis: Ang matag isla sa Pilipinas gilibutan sa tubig, mao kana ang nagbulag sa mga isla sa usag-usa.

q: Why do some people wear eyeglasses?
options: To protect their eyes from the sun during outdoor activities
To help them see more clearly when their vision is blurry
To magnify tiny objects like insects and small print
To keep dust and wind out of their eyes
explanation: Eyeglasses help people with blurry vision so they can see more clearly.
fact_tl: Ang salamin sa mata ay tumutulong sa mga taong malabo ang paningin para mas malinaw silang makakita.
fact_bis: Ang salamin sa mata makatabang sa mga tawo nga hanap ang panan-aw aron mas tin-aw silang makakita.

q: How many main body parts does a spider have?
options: Three — head, thorax, and abdomen
Two — the head-chest and the abdomen
Four — head, neck, chest, and abdomen
One single fused body segment
explanation: A spider's body has two main parts: the head-chest and the abdomen.
fact_tl: Ang katawan ng gagamba ay nahahati sa dalawang bahagi: ulo-dibdib at tiyan.
fact_bis: Ang lawas sa lawalawa adunay duha ka bahin: ang ulo-dughan ug ang tiyan.

q: Why do jet airplanes prefer to fly in the stratosphere?
options: The stratosphere has thick clouds that hide planes from storms below
The air in the stratosphere is calm, making flight smooth and efficient
The stratosphere is the warmest layer, keeping engines running better
Oxygen levels are highest in the stratosphere, improving fuel burn
explanation: The stratosphere contains the ozone layer and its air is calm, which is why jet airplanes fly in it.
fact_tl: Ang stratosphere ay nasa itaas ng troposphere at dito matatagpuan ang ozone layer; kalmado ang hangin dito kaya dito lumilipad ang mga jet na eroplano.
fact_bis: Ang stratosphere anaa sa ibabaw sa troposphere ug dinhi makita ang ozone layer; kalmado ang hangin dinhi maong dinhi manglupad ang mga jet nga ayroplano.

q: What is the difference between weathering and erosion?
options: Weathering and erosion are two names for the same process of rock breaking
Weathering breaks rock where it sits, while erosion carries the broken pieces away
Erosion breaks down rock in place, while weathering moves pieces to new locations
Weathering only happens in cold places, while erosion only happens near rivers
explanation: Weathering breaks rock where it sits, while erosion carries the broken pieces away using water, wind, or ice.
fact_tl: Ang weathering ang nagbabasag ng bato sa kinalalagyan nito, samantalang ang erosion ang nagdadala ng mga durog na bato palayo gamit ang tubig, hangin, o yelo. Magkaibang bagay sila.
fact_bis: Ang weathering moguba sa bato sa nahimutangan niini, samtang ang erosion magdala sa naguba nga mga tipik palayo gamit ang tubig, hangin, o yelo. Lahi sila nga butang.

q: How far did the Wright brothers travel on their very first powered airplane flight?
options: About 500 feet, roughly the length of a football field
About 120 feet, roughly the length of 12 large steps
About 1 kilometer, nearly crossing a small town
About 50 feet, just clearing a small fence
explanation: The Wright brothers' first airplane flight covered only about 120 feet (about 36 meters).
fact_tl: Ang unang lipad ng eroplano ng Wright brothers ay umabot lamang ng mga 120 talampakan (mga 36 metro).
fact_bis: Ang unang paglupad sa eroplano sa managsoong Wright miabot lang ug mga 120 ka tiil (mga 36 metro).

q: Which statement about diamond and electricity is correct?
options: Diamond conducts electricity well because it is made of tightly packed carbon atoms
Diamond does not conduct electricity, even though it carries heat well
Diamond conducts both heat and electricity just like most metals do
Diamond only conducts electricity when it is heated to high temperatures
explanation: Even though diamond carries heat well, electricity does not flow through it, unlike graphite which can conduct electricity.
fact_tl: Kahit dala nito nang mabuti ang init, hindi dumadaloy ang kuryente sa diamante, kaya kabaligtaran ito ng grapayt na nagpapadaloy ng kuryente.
fact_bis: Bisan maayo kini modala sa kainit, ang koryente dili moagi sa diamante, lahi sa grapayt nga makapaagi og koryente.

q: Besides leaves, what else do some millipedes eat that helps forests recycle nutrients?
options: Living roots and underground tubers from plants
Rotting wood and tree bark from decaying logs
Dead insects and small worms in the soil
Mushrooms and mosses growing on rocks
explanation: Besides leaves, some millipedes also eat rotting wood and tree bark, helping turn decaying logs back into soil.
fact_tl: Bukod sa dahon, may mga millipede na kumakain din ng bulok na kahoy at balat ng puno. Tinutulungan nila na maging lupa ang mga nabubulok na troso sa gubat.
fact_bis: Gawas sa dahon, naay mga millipede nga mokaon usab og malata nga kahoy ug panit sa kahoy. Motabang sila aron ang malata nga troso sa lasang mahimong yuta.

q: What color does the areca palm fruit turn when it is ripe?
options: Green or dark blue when fully mature
Orange or yellow-red when ripe
Purple or deep red when ready to pick
White or pale yellow as it ripens
explanation: The fruit of the areca palm turns orange or yellow-red when it is ripe.
