q: Sodium is a metal, but it behaves very differently from iron or copper. Which unusual property does sodium share with other alkali metals?
options: It is so hard that it can scratch glass and other metal surfaces
It is so soft that it can be cut with an ordinary knife
It is so light that it floats above a table when exposed to air
It is so shiny that it reflects more light than any other metal
explanation: Alkali metals like sodium are so soft they can be cut with a knife, unlike hard metals such as iron or steel.
fact_tl: Ang mga alkali metal tulad ng sodium ay napakalambot kaya kayang putulin ng kutsilyo.
fact_bis: Ang mga alkali metal sama sa sodium humok kaayo mao nga mahimong putlon sa kutsilyo.

q: If you could zoom into a single atom, what would you find makes up most of its volume?
options: A solid core of protons and neutrons that fills most of the atom
Mostly empty space, with a tiny dense nucleus and an electron cloud around it
A thick layer of electrons packed tightly around the nucleus
Equal amounts of protons, neutrons, and electrons spread evenly throughout
explanation: More than 99.9% of an atom's volume is empty space — it has a tiny dense nucleus surrounded by a diffuse electron cloud.
fact_tl: Ang atom ay binubuo ng isang maliit, masiksik na nucleus (naglalaman ng mga proton at neutron) na napapaligiran ng maluwag na electron cloud — higit sa 99.9% ng isang atom ay walang laman.
fact_bis: Ang atom adunay gamay, siksik nga nucleus (nagdala sa mga proton ug neutron) nga gipalibutan sa bagsok nga electron cloud; labaw sa 99.9% sa volume sa usa ka atom walay sulod.

q: Which mountain range protects Cagayan Valley and western Luzon from the heaviest typhoon rains?
options: The Cordillera Central which runs along the western side of Luzon
The Sierra Madre range in eastern Luzon which blocks Pacific typhoons
The Zambales Mountains which face the South China Sea side of Luzon
The Caraballo Mountains which separate Central and Northern Luzon
explanation: The Sierra Madre mountain range in eastern Luzon acts as a natural barrier against Pacific typhoons, shielding Cagayan Valley and western Luzon from the heaviest rainfall.
fact_tl: Ang Sierra Madre mountain range sa silangang Luzon ay nagsisilbing natural na hadlang laban sa mga bagyo mula sa Pacific, pinoprotektahan ang Cagayan Valley at kanlurang Luzon mula sa pinaka-matinding buhos ng ulan.
fact_bis: Ang Sierra Madre mountain range sa sidlakang Luzon nagsilbing natural nga hadlang batok sa mga bagyo sa Pasipiko, nagpanalipod sa Cagayan Valley ug kasadpanong Luzon gikan sa pinakamabug-at nga ulan.

q: Mangrove trees grow in salty seawater that would kill most plants. How do different mangrove species deal with all that salt?
options: They all pump salt into their flowers to keep the leaves and roots salt-free
Some exclude salt at the roots while others push out excess salt through leaf glands
They absorb the salt and store it safely inside their thick trunk wood
They mix the salt with fresh rainwater they collect in hollow branches
explanation: Different mangrove species handle saltwater in different ways — some exclude salt at the roots, while others secrete excess salt through special glands on their leaves.
fact_tl: Ang iba't ibang species ng bakawan ay may iba't ibang paraan para harapin ang maalat na tubig — ang ilan ay humahadlang sa pagpasok ng asin sa kanilang mga ugat, ang iba ay naglalabas ng asin sa pamamagitan ng mga espesyal na gland sa kanilang mga dahon.
fact_bis: Ang lain-laing species sa bakawan adunay lain-laing pamaagi sa pagtubos sa maalat nga tubig — ang uban nagpugong sa pagpasulod sa asin sa ilang mga ugat, samtang ang uban nagpalabas og sobra nga asin pinaagi sa mga espesyal nga gland sa ilang mga dahon.

q: What keeps the bones inside your knee joint from grinding painfully against each other when you walk?
options: A thin layer of solid cartilage is the only thing preventing bone-to-bone contact
A slippery fluid inside the joint acts like oil and keeps the bones moving smoothly
Tiny air pockets between the bones cushion them from shock and friction
The tendons wrap tightly around both bones to hold them apart from each other
explanation: A slippery fluid called synovial fluid inside the joint acts like oil, keeping the bones moving smoothly against each other.
fact_tl: May madulas na likido sa loob ng kasukasuan na parang langis na nagpapadulas sa galaw ng mga buto.
fact_bis: Adunay danlog nga likido sa sulod sa lutahan nga sama sa lana nga maghimog hamis sa lihok sa mga bukog.

q: How does a vaccine protect you from getting sick with a serious disease?
options: It kills all the germs already inside your body so none are left to make you ill
It helps your immune system learn to fight a specific germ ahead of time so your body is ready
It strengthens your skin and throat so germs cannot enter your body at all
It makes you slightly sick right away so your body becomes permanently immune to all diseases
explanation: A vaccine helps the immune system recognize and learn to fight a particular germ before a real infection happens, so you stay healthy or get less sick when you meet that germ later.
fact_tl: Ang bakuna ay tumutulong sa immune system na matutunang labanan ang isang partikular na mikrobyo nang maaga, kaya hindi na tayo o mas hindi tayo magkakasakit kapag nakasalubong natin ito.
fact_bis: Ang bakuna motabang sa immune system nga makakat-on pagpakigbatok sa usa ka piho nga mikrobyo daan, mao nga dili na ta magsakit o mas dili magsakit kon mahisugat nato kini unya.

q: A carabao eats only grass and leaves. What type of animal is it based on what it eats?
options: An omnivore because it eats both grass and insects found in the soil
A herbivore because it eats only plants
A carnivore because it is a large and powerful animal that could hunt
A decomposer because it breaks down plant material in the field
explanation: A herbivore eats only plants, and since the carabao eats grass and leaves, it is a herbivore.
fact_tl: Ayon sa kinakain: ang herbivore ay kumakain ng halaman (tulad ng kalabaw), ang carnivore ay kumakain ng ibang hayop (tulad ng pusa), at ang omnivore ay kumakain ng halaman at hayop (tulad ng tao at baboy).
fact_bis: Sumala sa gikaon: ang herbivore mokaon og tanom (sama sa kabaw), ang carnivore mokaon og ubang hayop (sama sa iring), ug ang omnivore mokaon og tanom ug hayop (sama sa tawo ug baboy).

q: What effect did the massive 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo have on the world's climate?
options: The eruption warmed the whole Earth by releasing large amounts of heat into the sky
The ash and gas from Pinatubo slightly cooled global temperatures for a few years
The eruption had no effect on global temperature because it was in just one country
Pinatubo's eruption created a permanent cloud layer that keeps the Philippines warmer
explanation: The ash and gas released by Pinatubo's eruption spread through the upper atmosphere and slightly cooled global temperatures for a few years.
fact_tl: Ang abo at gas mula sa pagputok ng Pinatubo ay nagpalamig nang kaunti sa temperatura ng buong mundo sa loob ng ilang taon.
fact_bis: Ang abo ug gas gikan sa pagbuto sa Pinatubo nakapabugnaw og gamay sa temperatura sa tibuok kalibutan sulod sa pipila ka tuig.

q: Why does an umbrella sometimes flip inside-out during a strong storm?
options: Heavy rain adds too much weight to one side and tips the umbrella over
Strong wind pushes a force against the umbrella's wide surface and flips it
The handle shrinks in cold rain making it impossible to hold the umbrella straight
Lightning nearby creates a magnetic force that attracts the metal ribs of the umbrella
explanation: The wind pushes a force against the wide surface of the umbrella, which is strong enough to flip it inside-out.
fact_tl: Natutuwad ang payong sa malakas na hangin dahil ang hangin ay nagtutulak ng puwersa sa malapad na tela nito.
fact_bis: Mabaliktad ang payong sa kusog nga hangin kay ang hangin magduso ug kusog batok sa lapad nga panapton niini.

q: Why do typhoons that pass over the Philippines spin in a circular pattern instead of moving in a straight line?
options: The heat from the ocean surface pushes the typhoon into a spiral spin
The Coriolis effect bends the inflowing air around the low-pressure center, causing the spin
The mountains of the Philippines force the wind to swirl as it passes over them
Typhoons spin because the water they carry creates a rotating weight that pulls them around
explanation: The Coriolis effect — caused by Earth's rotation — bends the inflowing air around the typhoon's low-pressure center, making it spin.
fact_tl: Ang mga bagyong dumaraan sa Pilipinas ay umiikot dahil hinahatak ng Coriolis effect ang papasok na hangin sa paligid ng mababang presyon.
fact_bis: Ang mga bagyo nga moagi sa Pilipinas motuyok tungod kay ang Coriolis effect mokurba sa nagsulod nga hangin palibot sa ubos nga presyur.

q: The caves of Palawan took millions of years to form. What makes limestone dissolve so slowly?
options: Limestone is one of the hardest rocks on Earth so almost nothing can break it down
The weak carbonic acid from rain dissolves limestone extremely slowly — just one centimeter can take 100 to 1,000 years
Caves form by water pressure blasting through solid rock all at once not by slow dissolving
Limestone melts only when underground magma heats it which rarely happens under Palawan
explanation: Weak carbonic acid from rain dissolves limestone extremely slowly — one centimeter may take 100 to 1,000 years — so large cave systems like those in Palawan took millions of years to form.
fact_tl: Ang paglulaw ng limestone ng mahinang carbonic acid (mula sa ulan at CO2 sa hangin) ay isang napakabagal na proseso; ang isang centimeter ng limestone ay maaaring tumaas ng 100 hanggang 1,000 taon para matunaw; kaya ang mga malaking karst cave system tulad ng sa Palawan ay tumagal ng milyun-milyong taon para mabuo.
fact_bis: Ang paglusaw sa limestone sa mahuyang carbonic acid (gikan sa ulan ug air CO2) usa ka grabe ka hinay nga proseso; ang usa ka centimetro sa limestone mahimong mokabat og 100 hangtod 1,000 ka tuig aron matunaw; mao nga ang dagkong karst cave systems sama sa Palawan gigamit og milyun-milyon nga tuig aron maporma.

q: Why is it bad for your teeth to eat sweets and drink soda very often?
options: Sweets make your saliva dry up so your teeth crack from lack of moisture
Eating sweets and drinking soda too often makes more acid that can damage the teeth
The sugar sticks to your teeth so tightly that it blocks you from tasting food properly
Soda turns your saliva into a hard layer that prevents new teeth from growing
explanation: Eating sweets and drinking soda too often produces more acid in the mouth, which can damage and decay the teeth.
fact_tl: Ang madalas na pagkain ng matamis at pag-inom ng softdrink ay nagpapadami ng asido na nakakasira ng ngipin.
fact_bis: Ang kanunay nga pagkaon ug tam-is ug pag-inom ug softdrink magpadaghan sa asido nga makadaot sa ngipon.

q: What are the four main human blood types in the ABO system?
options: X, Y, Z, and W
A, B, AB, and O
Positive, Negative, Neutral, and Mixed
Red, White, Blue, and Clear
explanation: There are four main blood types — A, B, AB, and O — based on tiny markers found on the surface of red blood cells.
fact_tl: May apat na pangunahing uri ng dugo — A, B, AB, at O — depende sa maliliit na markang nasa ibabaw ng pulang selula ng dugo.
fact_bis: Adunay upat ka nag-unang klase sa dugo — A, B, AB, ug O — depende sa gagmay nga mga marka sa ibabaw sa pula nga selula sa dugo.

q: A student says plants only breathe when the sun is shining. Is the student correct?
options: Yes, plants breathe and make food at the same time so both stop at night
No, plants carry out cellular respiration all the time day and night, while photosynthesis only happens during the day
Yes, without sunlight no chemical reactions at all can happen inside a plant
No, plants only breathe at night and completely stop breathing when the sun is up
explanation: Plants carry out cellular respiration all the time, day and night, to produce energy — photosynthesis only occurs during the day, so at night plants take in oxygen and release CO2.
fact_tl: Ang mga halaman ay gumaganap ng cellular respiration sa lahat ng oras (araw at gabi) para makagawa ng enerhiya—ngunit ang photosynthesis ay nagaganap lamang sa araw; kaya sa gabi, ang halaman ay gumamit ng oxygen at naglalabas ng CO2.
fact_bis: Ang mga tanum nagtuman sa cellular respiration sa tanan nga oras (adlaw ug gabii) aron makahimo og enerhiya, apan ang photosynthesis mahitabo lamang sa adlaw; kaya sa gabii, ang tanum naggamit og oxygen ug nagpagawas og CO2.

q: How does the Agusan Marsh help clean the water that flows through it?
options: It uses heat from the sun to boil and sterilize the water before it moves on
As water passes through its plants and mud, dirt and silt are left behind so cleaner water flows out
It filters water through underground limestone rocks that absorb all the pollution
The fish living in the marsh eat the dirt particles and keep the water clean
explanation: The Agusan Marsh cleans water naturally — as water moves through the plants and mud, dirt and silt are trapped so cleaner water flows out toward other areas.
fact_tl: Tumutulong ang Agusan Marsh na linisin ang tubig. Habang dumadaan ang tubig sa mga halaman at putik nito, naiiwan ang mga dumi at putik, kaya mas malinis na tubig ang lumalabas papunta sa ibang lugar.
fact_bis: Ang Agusan Marsh nagtabang sa paglimpyo sa tubig. Samtang moagi ang tubig sa mga tanom ug lapok niini, mahibilin ang mga hugaw ug lapok, busa mas limpyo nga tubig ang mogawas padulong sa ubang dapit.

q: About how fast does an average person walk, and how does jogging compare to that speed?
options: Walking is about 2 km/h and jogging is about 4 km/h so jogging is twice as fast
Walking is about 5 km/h and jogging reaches about 10 km/h or more so running is at least twice as fast
Walking is about 10 km/h and jogging is about 15 km/h so running is 50% faster
Walking is about 3 km/h and jogging is about 6 km/h making running exactly twice as fast
explanation: An average person walks about 5 km/h while jogging reaches about 10 km/h or more, making running at least twice as fast as walking.
fact_tl: Ang karaniwang taong naglalakad ay gumagalaw ng mga 5 kilometro kada oras, samtang ang naghahabol-takbo ay umaabot ng mga 10 kilometro kada oras o higit pa. Ibig sabihin, doble o higit pa ang bilis ng pagtakbo kaysa sa paglakad. Kaya mas mabilis kang nakakarating kapag tumakbo, pero mas madali kang mapapagod.
fact_bis: Ang ordinaryong tawo nga naglakaw molihok og mga 5 ka kilometro kada oras, samtang ang nagdagan moabot og mga 10 ka kilometro kada oras o labaw pa. Buot pasabot, doble o labaw pa ang katulin sa pagdagan kaysa sa paglakaw. Busa mas paspas ka makaabot kung modagan ka, apan mas dali ka usab kapuyon.

q: On the two equinoxes each year, where on Earth is the Sun directly overhead at noon?
options: Directly above the North Pole where all time zones meet
Directly above the equator
Directly above the Tropic of Cancer in the northern hemisphere
Directly above the Tropic of Capricorn in the southern hemisphere
explanation: On an equinox, the Sun is directly overhead at noon at the equator.
fact_tl: Sa equinox, ang Araw ay tuwid sa ulunan (directly overhead) sa tanghali sa ekwador (equator).
fact_bis: Sa equinox, ang Adlaw direkta sa ibabaw (overhead) sa udto didto sa ekwador (equator).

q: What does the green sea turtle mainly eat?
options: Small crabs and shrimp found on the ocean floor
Seagrass and algae, making plants its main food
Jellyfish and soft-bodied animals floating in the water
Small fish and squid that it chases near coral reefs
explanation: The green sea turtle eats seagrass and algae, so plants are its main food.
fact_tl: Ang berdeng pawikan ay kumakain ng damong-dagat at lumot, kaya halaman ang pangunahing pagkain nito.
fact_bis: Ang berde nga pawikan mokaon og sagbot sa dagat ug lumot, mao nga tanom ang nag-unang pagkaon niini.

q: Can a person actually be inside an umbra — the darkest part of a shadow?
options: No, the umbra is only a shape in space and no physical object can enter it
Yes, when you stand in the dark center of a big shadow at noon you are standing inside the umbra itself
No, the umbra is so small it is only a single point of complete darkness
Yes, but only astronauts can enter an umbra because it exists only in outer space
explanation: The umbra is the darkest center of a shadow — when you stand in the dark center of a large shadow, you are standing inside the umbra itself.
fact_tl: Tanong ng mga bata: pwede ka bang tumayo sa loob ng umbra? Oo! Kapag nasa anino ka ng malaking bagay tuwing tanghali, ang madilim na gitna kung saan ka nakatayo ay ang umbra mismo.
fact_bis: Mangutana ang mga bata: makatindog ka ba sa sulod sa umbra? Oo! Kon naa ka sa landong sa dako nga butang panghaponon, ang ngitngit nga tunga diin ka nagtindog mao ang umbra mismo.

q: How many eggs does a female Philippine eagle usually lay in a single breeding season?
options: Three to four eggs in a large nest high in a tree
Two eggs, one after the other, a few days apart
Only one egg per breeding season
Five to six eggs so that at least some chicks survive
explanation: The female Philippine eagle usually lays only one egg each breeding season.
fact_tl: Karaniwang isang itlog lamang ang inilalabas ng babaeng agilang Pilipino sa bawat panahon ng pag-aanak.
fact_bis: Ang baye nga agila sa Pilipinas kasagaran mangitlog lang ug usa ka itlog matag panahon sa pagpangitlog.

q: The Draco lizard can spread wing-like ribs to glide through the forest. About how far can it travel in a single glide?
options: Only a few centimeters before it must land on the same tree
Several meters to a nearby tree in a single glide
Hundreds of meters allowing it to cross open clearings easily
It can glide but only drops straight down along the same trunk it started on
explanation: In a single glide, a Draco can travel several meters to reach a nearby tree.
fact_tl: Sa isang paglutang, kaya ng Draco na umabot ng ilang metrong layo papunta sa kalapit na puno.
fact_bis: Sa usa ka paglutaw, makaabot ang Draco og pipila ka metro ngadto sa duol nga kahoy.

q: Where does a big part of the oxygen we breathe every day come from?
options: From underground where gases trapped in rocks slowly seep out
From plants and trees that make oxygen using sunlight and release it into the air
From the ocean water which breaks apart into oxygen and hydrogen in sunlight
From clouds that collect air from space and release it as rain falls
explanation: A big part of the oxygen we breathe comes from plants and trees, which make oxygen using sunlight and release it into the air.
fact_tl: Malaking bahagi ng oxygen na nilalanghap natin ay galing sa mga halaman at puno. Gumagawa sila ng oxygen gamit ang liwanag ng araw, at inilalabas ito sa hangin para mahinga natin.
fact_bis: Dako nga bahin sa oxygen nga atong ginhanga naggikan sa mga tanom ug kahoy. Maghimo silag oxygen gamit ang kahayag sa adlaw, ug ipagawas kini sa hangin aron atong mahingahan.

q: How many legs does an ant have?
options: Four legs like most small crawling animals
Six legs because it is an insect
Eight legs like a spider
Ten legs like a crab
explanation: An ant has six legs because it is an insect, and all insects have exactly six legs.
fact_tl: Ang langgam (ant) ay may anim na (6) paa dahil ito ay isang insekto.
fact_bis: Ang hulmigas (langgam) adunay unom (6) ka tiil tungod kay insekto kini.

q: Besides drinking it fresh, what foods can be made from cow milk?
options: Bread and rice cakes, because milk is mainly used for baking grains
Cheese, butter, and other tasty foods
Oil and vinegar, because milk separates into these liquids
Sugar and honey, because milk is naturally very sweet
explanation: Cow milk is made into cheese, butter, and other tasty foods.
fact_tl: Ang gatas ng baka ay ginagawang keso, mantikilya, at iba pang masasarap na pagkain.
fact_bis: Ang gatas sa baka himuon nga keso, mantikilya, ug uban pang lamian nga pagkaon.

q: How is the Agusan Marsh different from a mangrove forest?
options: The Agusan Marsh is found along the sea coast while mangroves grow only beside rivers
The Agusan Marsh has fresh water from rivers while mangroves grow along the coast in salty seawater
Both the marsh and mangroves have identical salty water but different types of trees
The Agusan Marsh has no water plants while mangrove forests are completely underwater
explanation: The Agusan Marsh is a freshwater wetland fed by rivers, while mangroves grow along the coast in salty seawater — both are wet places but the water and plants are different.
fact_tl: Magkaiba ang Agusan Marsh at ang isang kagubatan ng bakawan (mangrove). Ang Agusan Marsh ay may tabang o sariwang tubig mula sa ilog, samantalang ang bakawan ay nasa baybayin na may maalat na tubig-dagat. Pareho silang basang lugar pero magkaiba ang tubig at halaman.
fact_bis: Lahi ang Agusan Marsh ug ang kalasangan sa bakawan (mangrove). Ang Agusan Marsh adunay tab-ang nga tubig gikan sa suba, samtang ang bakawan motubo sa baybayon nga adunay parat nga tubig-dagat. Parehong basa nga dapit sila apan lahi ang tubig ug mga tanom.

q: How small are most of the tiny organisms found in pond water?
options: About the size of a grain of rice so you can just barely see them with good eyes
Most are thinner than a single strand of your hair and hundreds could fit inside one pencil dot
About the size of a sesame seed so they are visible if you look carefully
Each one is roughly as wide as your fingernail but too thin to see easily
explanation: Most pond-water organisms are thinner than a single strand of hair, and hundreds of paramecia could line up inside one dot made by a pencil.
fact_tl: Gaano kaliit ang mga nilalang sa pond water? Karamihan sa kanila ay mas manipis pa kaysa sa isang hibla ng buhok mo. Maaaring may daan-daang paramecium na magkakasunod-sunod sa loob lang ng isang tuldok na ginawa ng lapis.
fact_bis: Unsa ka gamay ang mga binuhat sa pond water? Kadaghanan kanila mas nipis pa kaysa sa usa ka lugas sa imong buhok. Mahimong gatusan ka paramecium ang magsunod-sunod sulod lang sa usa ka tuldok nga gihimo sa lapis.

q: Bats live in caves, but scientists do not consider them true cave animals. Why not?
options: Bats are blind so they cannot navigate inside caves and only wander in by accident
Bats only use caves as shelter but go outside to feed, so they do not live their whole lives in caves
Bats prefer trees and only move into caves during the rainy season when trees get too wet
Bats are actually nocturnal birds and birds are never classified as cave animals
explanation: Bats use caves as shelter but leave to feed outside, so they are not true cave animals (troglobites) that spend their entire lives in caves.
fact_tl: Ang paniki ay gumagamit lamang ng kuweba bilang tirahan ngunit lumalabas para kumain, kaya hindi ito tunay na hayop-kuweba tulad ng troglobite.
fact_bis: Ang kabog naggamit lang sa langob isip puy-anan apan mogawas aron mokaon, mao nga dili kini tinuod nga mananap sa langob sama sa troglobite.

q: When you push a paddle backward through the water, what happens to the boat?
options: The boat slows down because pushing water backward creates drag against the front of the hull
The boat moves forward because pushing on the water makes the water push the boat forward in return
The boat turns sideways because water resists the backward push and deflects to the side
The boat moves backward too because water always pulls objects in the same direction as the force
explanation: When a paddle pushes water backward, the water pushes the boat forward in return — for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.
fact_tl: Kapag itinutulak pabalik ng sagwan ang tubig, ipinapasulong nito ang bangka dahil ang pagtulak sa tubig ay sumasagot ng pagtulak na pasulong sa bangka.
fact_bis: Kon ang bugsay moduso sa tubig paatras, mopaduso kini sa bangka paunahan, kay ang pagduso sa tubig motubag ug pagduso sa bangka paunahan.

q: What does a bird's egg need in order to hatch into a chick?
options: Darkness and complete silence so the chick inside can grow without being disturbed
Warmth so the egg can develop and the chick can hatch
Lots of water poured on it each day to keep the shell from drying out
Cool temperatures to slow down the chick's growth so it develops properly
explanation: An egg needs warmth so it can develop and hatch into a healthy chick.
fact_tl: Kailangan ng init ang itlog upang mapisa ito at lumabas ang sisiw.
fact_bis: Ang itlog nagkinahanglan ug kainit aron kini mapusa ug mogawas ang piso.

q: How does a vaccine prepare your immune system to fight a serious disease?
options: It fills your blood with medicine that stays active and kills germs as soon as they enter
It trains the immune system using a dead or weakened germ so it remembers and can fight fast if the real disease comes
It removes the parts of your body that germs normally attack so they have nowhere to go
It raises your body temperature permanently making your blood too hot for germs to survive in
explanation: A vaccine trains the immune system by exposing it to a dead or weakened germ — the immune system remembers this enemy and can respond quickly if the real disease arrives later.
fact_tl: Ang bakuna ay nagsasanay sa immune system gamit ang patay o mahinang germ para maalala nito ang kaaway at mabilis lumaban kapag dumating ang tunay na sakit.
fact_bis: Ang bakuna mobansay sa immune system gamit ang patay o huyang nga germ aron mahinumdoman niini ang kaaway ug paspas molaban kon moabot ang tinuod nga sakit.

q: What did NASA's MESSENGER spacecraft discover when it studied the planet Mercury?
options: It found liquid water oceans beneath Mercury's rocky crust near the equator
It discovered ice hidden inside craters at Mercury's poles and mapped the entire surface
It confirmed that Mercury has a thick atmosphere similar in size to Earth's
It found active volcanoes still erupting on Mercury's surface near the south pole
explanation: NASA's MESSENGER spacecraft entered Mercury's orbit in 2011, mapped its entire surface, and discovered ice hidden inside craters at the planet's poles.
fact_tl: Ang MESSENGER spacecraft ng NASA ay pumasok sa orbit ng Mercury noong 2011 at nag-mapa ng buong ibabaw nito; natuklasan nito ang yelo sa mga crater sa mga polo ng planeta.
fact_bis: Ang MESSENGER spacecraft sa NASA misulod sa orbit sa Mercury niadtong 2011 ug gi-mapa ang tibuok nawong niini; nakakaplag kini og yelo sulod sa mga crater sa mga poste sa planeta.

q: What would happen to Earth's temperatures if there were no ocean currents?
options: All places on Earth would have the same comfortable temperature because the sun heats everything evenly
The equator would be much hotter and the poles much colder because heat would not be spread around
Coastal areas would flood as currents stopping would cause sea levels to rise dramatically
The poles would actually get warmer because melting ice would release heat stored underground
explanation: Without ocean currents to carry heat from the equator toward the poles, the equator would be far hotter and the poles far colder than they are today.
fact_tl: Kung walang mga agos ng dagat, magiging sobrang init ang ekwador at sobrang lamig ang mga polo dahil hindi naipapamahagi ang init.
fact_bis: Kon walay mga sulog sa dagat, mainit kaayo ang ekwador ug bugnaw kaayo ang mga polo kay dili maapod-apod ang kainit.

q: The Beaufort scale is used to measure wind speed. How many levels does it have in total?
options: 5 levels from calm to gale
10 levels from calm to storm
13 levels from Force 0 (calm) to Force 12 (hurricane force)
20 levels from a light breeze to a super typhoon
explanation: The Beaufort scale has 13 levels, from Force 0 (completely calm) to Force 12 (hurricane-force winds).
fact_tl: Ang Beaufort scale ay may 13 antas mula Force 0 (kalmado, walang hangin) hanggang Force 12 (lakas ng bagyo).
fact_bis: Ang Beaufort scale adunay 13 ka lebel gikan sa Force 0 (kalma, walay hangin) ngadto sa Force 12 (kakusog sa bagyo).

q: In hot weather in the Philippines you sweat a lot and lose water. What does the kidney do to help?
options: The kidney produces extra sweat to cool the body down faster in the heat
The kidney helps keep water in the blood, but you still need to drink enough water so it does not struggle
The kidney releases stored water back into the stomach so you do not feel thirsty
The kidney shuts down sweating by sending a signal to the skin to close its pores
explanation: In hot weather, sweating causes the body to lose water, so the kidney works to keep water in the blood — but you must still drink enough water to help the kidney maintain this balance.
fact_tl: Sa mainit na panahon sa Pilipinas, marami tayong pawis kaya nababawasan ang tubig sa katawan. Tumutulong ang bato sa pamamagitan ng pagtatago ng tubig pabalik sa dugo. Pero kailangan pa rin nating uminom ng sapat na tubig para hindi mahirapan ang bato sa pag-iingat ng balanse.
fact_bis: Sa init nga panahon sa Pilipinas, daghan tang singot mao nga maminusan ang tubig sa lawas. Motabang ang kidney pinaagi sa pagtipig sa tubig balik sa dugo. Pero kinahanglan gihapon ta moinom og igong tubig aron dili maglisod ang kidney sa pagtipig sa balanse.

q: Why do typhoons produce heavier rainfall when they pass over warmer ocean water?
options: Warmer water adds more water vapour to the typhoon, making rainfall heavier.
Warmer water slows the typhoon down so it rains in one place longer.
Warmer water makes typhoon winds spin faster, squeezing out more rain.
Warmer water reflects sunlight upward, which turns into rainfall.
explanation: Warmer oceans evaporate more water into the air, giving the typhoon extra water vapour that falls as heavier rain.
fact_tl: Ang mas mainit na dagat ay nagbibigay ng mas maraming singaw para sa mga bagyo, nagdudulot ng mas malakas na ulan; ito ang isa sa mga dahilan kung bakit ang mga bagyo ay mas maulan sa mga lugar na may mainit na tubig-dagat.
fact_bis: Ang mas mainit nga kadagatan naghatag og mas daghang water vapor sa mga bagyo, nagdulot og mas kusog nga ulan; kini usa sa mga hinungdan kung ngano ang mga bagyo mas maulanon sa mga lugar nga adunay mas mainit nga temperatura sa dagat.

q: What is the English name for the Filipino vegetable plant malunggay?
options: Moringa
Pandan
Bangus herb
Taro leaf
explanation: In English, malunggay is called moringa or the drumstick tree.
fact_tl: Sa Ingles, ang malunggay ay tinatawag na moringa o drumstick tree.
fact_bis: Sa Ininglis, ang malunggay gitawag nga moringa o drumstick tree.

q: In a sound wave, what happens to air particles during a compression?
options: They are bunched close together with high pressure.
They spread far apart with low pressure.
They stop moving and form a vacuum.
They vibrate sideways instead of forward.
explanation: A compression is the part of a sound wave where air particles are crowded together, creating high pressure.
fact_tl: Sa compression, ang mga particle ng hangin ay masyadong siksik at mataas ang presyon; sa rarefaction, ang mga particle ay malayo sa isa't isa at mababa ang presyon.
fact_bis: Sa compression, ang mga particle sa hangin nasiksik nga magkaisog ug taas ang presyon; sa rarefaction, ang mga particle nagbulag ug ubos ang presyon.

q: Who won the very first Nobel Prize in Physics, given in 1901?
options: Wilhelm Roentgen
Marie Curie
Albert Einstein
Nikola Tesla
explanation: Wilhelm Roentgen won the first-ever Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901 for discovering X-rays.
fact_tl: Si Wilhelm Roentgen ang unang nanalo ng Nobel Prize sa Physics noong 1901, dahil sa X-rays.
fact_bis: Si Wilhelm Roentgen ang unang nidaog og Nobel Prize sa Physics niadtong 1901, tungod sa X-rays.

q: Is baking soda an acid, a base, or neutral?
options: It is a base with a pH of about 9.
It is an acid with a pH of about 4.
It is neutral with a pH of exactly 7.
It is an acid with a pH of about 5.
explanation: Baking soda is alkaline (basic), with a pH of about 9.
fact_tl: Ang baking soda ay base (alkaline), na may pH na halos 9.
fact_bis: Ang baking soda kay base (alkaline), nga may pH nga mga 9.

q: How is wind erosion different from water erosion?
options: Wind can carry dust upward and in any direction, while water mainly moves material downhill due to gravity.
Wind always moves more material than water because it covers a larger area.
Water can lift soil upward, while wind can only move material sideways.
Wind and water erode land in exactly the same way.
explanation: Water is stronger and moves material downhill, while wind is weaker but can lift dust upward and carry it in any direction.
fact_tl: Parehong nagdadala ng lupa ang hangin at tubig, pero may pagkakaiba. Ang tubig (ilog, ulan) ay mas malakas at madalas na pababa lang ang dala dahil sa gravity. Ang hangin ay mas mahina pero kayang magdala ng alikabok pataas at sa anumang direksyon, kahit napakalayo.
fact_bis: Parehong magdala og yuta ang hangin ug tubig, apan adunay kalainan. Ang tubig (suba, ulan) mas kusog ug kasagaran paubos lang ang dala tungod sa gravity. Ang hangin mas huyang apan kaya magdala og abog pataas ug sa bisan asa nga direksyon, bisan layo kaayo.

q: How can a newborn baby receive temporary protection against measles?
options: The mother can pass protection to the baby if she has been vaccinated or had measles herself.
The baby is born with its own measles antibodies that last for life.
Doctors give measles vaccines to newborns in the first week of life.
The mother's breast milk cannot carry any disease protection at all.
explanation: A vaccinated mother can pass temporary measles protection to her newborn during the first months of life.
fact_tl: Ang nanay na nabakunahan o nagkaroon na ng tigdas ay maaaring makapagbigay ng pansamantalang proteksyon sa kaniyang bagong silang na sanggol sa mga unang buwan. Ito ang isa sa mga dahilan kung bakit mahalaga ang pagpapabakuna bago pa magkaanak.
fact_bis: Ang inahan nga nabakunahan o nakaagi na og tigdas mahimong makahatag og temporaryong panalipod sa iyang bag-ong natawo nga bata sulod sa unang mga bulan. Usa kini sa mga rason ngano importante ang pagpabakuna bisan sa wala pa manganak.

q: How is makahiya used in traditional Philippine herbal medicine?
options: Its roots or leaves are boiled to make a medicinal drink.
Its flowers are dried and ground into a healing powder.
Its seeds are eaten raw as a natural vitamin.
Its stem sap is applied directly to skin as a cream.
explanation: In the Philippines, the roots or leaves of makahiya are boiled to make a drink used in traditional herbal medicine.
fact_tl: Sa Pilipinas, ginagamit din ang makahiya bilang halamang gamot sa lumang paraan. Pinakukuluan ang ugat o dahon nito bilang inumin. Mahalaga pa ring magtanong sa doktor bago gumamit ng anumang halamang gamot.
fact_bis: Sa Pilipinas, gigamit usab ang makahiya isip tambal nga tanom sa karaang paagi. Ginalat-an ang gamot o dahon niini aron mainom. Importante gihapon nga mangutana sa doktor una mogamit og bisan unsang tambal nga tanom.

q: Why must cassava always be cooked well before eating?
options: Raw cassava contains a natural poison that cooking removes.
Raw cassava is too hard and tough to chew safely.
Raw cassava tastes extremely bitter but is not harmful.
Raw cassava loses all its nutrients if left uncooked.
explanation: Cassava is a root crop that must be thoroughly cooked because raw cassava contains a natural poison.
fact_tl: Ang cassava o kamoteng-kahoy ay isang ugat na pananim na masarap gawing kakanin, ngunit kailangan itong lutuing mabuti dahil ang hilaw na cassava ay may likas na lason.
fact_bis: Ang cassava o balanghoy usa ka ugat nga tanom nga lami himoon nga kakanin, apan kinahanglan kini lutoon ug maayo kay ang hilaw nga cassava adunay natural nga hilo.

q: What is the name for the specific body part that a hormone affects?
options: Target organ
Trigger gland
Receptor duct
Signal node
explanation: Each hormone affects a specific part of the body called its target organ.
fact_tl: Ang bawat hormone ay may tiyak na bahagi ng katawan na inaapektuhan nito, na tinatawag na target organ.
fact_bis: Ang matag hormone adunay piho nga bahin sa lawas nga apektuhan niini, gitawag nga target organ.

q: Where are kelp forests found, and what are they made of?
options: In cold oceans, formed by tall brown algae.
In warm tropical seas, formed by coral skeletons.
In deep ocean trenches, formed by red seaweed.
In freshwater lakes, formed by green water plants.
explanation: Kelp forests are large ecosystems in cold oceans formed by tall brown algae that shelter hundreds of marine species.
fact_tl: Ang mga kelp forest ay malalaking ekosistema sa malamig na dagat na binubuo ng napakahabang brown algae — nagbibigay sila ng tirahan at pagkain para sa daan-daang uri ng hayop.
fact_bis: Ang mga kelp forest dagkong ekosistema sa bugnaw nga dagat nga binuo sa hataas nga brown algae — naghatag sila og silong ug pagkain para sa gatusan nga klase sa mga mananap sa dagat.

q: What is the Sun mainly made of?
options: Hot gas, mostly hydrogen and helium.
Solid rock and iron, like the Earth's core.
Liquid magma, similar to lava inside a volcano.
Burning coal and other fuel minerals.
explanation: The Sun is a giant ball of super-hot gas, mostly hydrogen and helium — it is not a solid rock.
fact_tl: Kahit napakalaki ng Araw, hindi ito matigas na bato na pwedeng tapakan. Ito ay isang higanteng bola ng sobrang init na gas, karamihan ay hydrogen at helium. Ang dami ng gas na ito ang dahilan kung bakit napakalaki at mabigat nito.
fact_bis: Bisan og dako kaayo ang Adlaw, dili kini gahi nga bato nga matumban. Kini usa ka higante nga bula sa init kaayo nga gas, kasagaran hydrogen ug helium. Ang kadaghan niini nga gas maoy hinungdan nganong dako ug bug-at kaayo kini.

q: What condition is bright light therapy used to treat?
options: Seasonal affective disorder, a type of depression linked to reduced sunlight in winter.
Short-sightedness caused by spending too much time indoors.
Vitamin A deficiency from not eating enough vegetables.
Skin rashes caused by ultraviolet radiation from the sun.
explanation: Light therapy uses bright artificial light to treat seasonal affective disorder, a depression linked to reduced winter sunlight.
fact_tl: Ang light therapy ay gumagamit ng maliwanag na artificial na liwanag na katulad ng liwanag ng araw para gamutin ang seasonal affective disorder — isang uri ng depresyon na nauugnay sa kawalan ng araw sa taglamig.
fact_bis: Ang light therapy naggamit og hayag nga artificial nga suga nga kapareho sa kahayag sa adlaw sa pagtambal sa seasonal affective disorder — usa ka matang depresyon nga konektado sa ubos nga kahayag sa adlaw sa ting-tugnaw.

q: What feature of shark skin did scientists copy to design faster swimsuits?
options: The tiny denticles (tooth-like scales) that smooth water flow.
The slippery mucus coating that covers the skin.
The dark coloring that reduces light reflection in water.
The flexible cartilage bones that allow quick turns.
explanation: Scientists copied the denticles on shark skin to make swimsuits that smooth water flow and help swimmers go faster.
fact_tl: Pinag-aralan ng mga siyentista ang balat ng pating at gumawa sila ng mga espesyal na swimsuit para sa mga manlalangoy na ginaya ang denticle nito. Layunin nitong pakinisin ang daloy ng tubig para mas mabilis lumangoy — magandang halimbawa ng paggaya sa disenyo ng kalikasan.
fact_bis: Gitun-an sa mga siyentista ang panit sa iho ug naghimo silag espesyal nga swimsuit alang sa mga maglalangoy nga nagsundog sa denticle niini. Tumong niini nga himuong hamis ang dagayday sa tubig aron mas paspas molangoy — usa ka maayong panig-ingnan sa pagsundog sa disenyo sa kinaiyahan.

q: How do some young birds know where to migrate for the first time?
options: They follow the route by natural instinct, even without older birds to guide them.
They memorise a map from their parents before hatching.
They follow rivers and roads they can see from the air.
They only migrate after watching adult birds for two full seasons.
explanation: Some young birds know how to migrate by natural instinct and do not need to follow older birds.
fact_tl: Ang ilang batang ibon ay marunong nang lumipat kahit walang kasamang matatanda, dahil ito ay likas na ugali nila.
fact_bis: Ang ubang batan-ong langgam kahibalo na mobalhin bisan walay kauban nga tigulang, kay kini ilang kinaiyanhong gawi.

q: Who is Morse code named after?
options: Samuel Morse, who helped create the dot-and-dash system.
Alexander Bell, who invented the telephone.
Guglielmo Marconi, who sent the first radio signal.
Thomas Edison, who developed the telegraph machine.
explanation: Morse code, which uses dots and dashes, is named after Samuel Morse who helped create it.
fact_tl: Ang Morse code, na gumagamit ng mga tuldok at gitling, ay pinangalan kay Samuel Morse na tumulong gumawa nito.
fact_bis: Ang Morse code, nga naggamit og mga tuldok ug gitling, ginganlan kang Samuel Morse nga mitabang paghimo niini.

q: How does a barnacle catch its food from the water?
options: It sticks out its feathery legs and kicks them to sweep food in.
It opens its hard shell and sucks in water like a pump.
It shoots out a sticky tongue to trap passing plankton.
It waits for dead animals to sink down and land on it.
explanation: When underwater, a barnacle sticks out its feathery legs to kick and catch tiny bits of food from the water.
fact_tl: Kapag nasa ilalim ng tubig ang barnacle, inilalabas nito ang mabalahibong mga paa upang sipain at hulihin ang maliliit na pagkain sa tubig.
fact_bis: Kon naa sa ilawom sa tubig, ipagawas sa barnacle ang iyang balhiboong mga tiil aron sikaron ug dakpon ang gagmayng pagkaon sa tubig.

q: Which continent has the fewest people living on it?
options: Antarctica
Australia
South America
Africa
explanation: Antarctica has the fewest people; only scientists live there temporarily.
fact_tl: Ang Antarctica ang kontinenteng may pinakakaunting tao; mga siyentipiko lamang ang pansamantalang naninirahan doon.
fact_bis: Ang Antarctica mao ang kontinente nga adunay pinakagamay nga tawo; mga siyentista lamang ang temporaryong nagpuyo didto.

q: What is the habagat and what kind of weather does it bring to the Philippines?
options: A southwest wind from June to September that brings the rainy season.
A northeast wind from December to February that brings cool dry weather.
A sea breeze that blows only along the coast during summer mornings.
A storm wind that forms in the Pacific Ocean during typhoon season.
explanation: The habagat blows from the southwest from June to September, carrying moist sea air that brings the rainy season.
fact_tl: Ang habagat ay hanging humihihip mula sa timog-kanluran, kadalasan mula Hunyo hanggang Setyembre. Dala nito ang basa at mahalumigmig na hangin mula sa dagat, kaya ito ang nagdadala ng tag-ulan sa Pilipinas.
fact_bis: Ang habagat mao ang hangin nga mohuyop gikan sa habagatan-kasadpan, kasagaran gikan Hunyo hangtod Setyembre. Magdala kini og basa ug umog nga hangin gikan sa dagat, mao nga magdala kini sa ting-ulan sa Pilipinas.

q: What does a buffer solution do when a small amount of acid or base is added to it?
options: It resists the change and keeps the pH nearly the same.
It reacts violently and produces a large amount of gas.
It immediately becomes neutral with a pH of exactly 7.
It separates into layers so the acid sinks to the bottom.
explanation: A buffer solution resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added, like human blood which stays near pH 7.4.
fact_tl: Ang buffer solution ay isang solusyon na lumalaban sa pagbabago ng pH kapag may dagdag na maliit na acid o base — ang dugo ng tao ay isang natural na buffer na nagpapanatili ng pH na 7.35 hanggang 7.45.
fact_bis: Ang buffer solution usa ka solusyon nga lumalaban sa pagbag-o sa pH kon gamay nga acid o base idugang; ang dugo sa tawo usa ka natural nga buffer nga nagpadayon sa pH nga 7.35 hangtod 7.45 alang sa hustong pagtrabaho sa lawas.

q: Does the ozone layer block ALL ultraviolet (UV) rays from the Sun?
options: No — it blocks the most dangerous UV but some UV still reaches us, so we can get sunburned.
Yes — the ozone layer blocks every UV ray so we can never get sunburned outdoors.
No — the ozone layer only blocks visible light, not UV rays at all.
Yes — UV only reaches Earth when the ozone layer has a hole above your city.
explanation: The ozone layer blocks the most dangerous UV but a little UV still slips through, which is why we can still get sunburned.
fact_tl: Akala ng iba, lahat ng UV ay hinaharang ng ozone kaya hindi na tayo dapat mapaso. Mali ito. Hinaharang ng ozone ang pinakadelikadong UV, pero may konting UV pa ring nakakalusot pababa sa atin, kaya pwede pa rin tayong mapaso kung sobra sa araw.
fact_bis: Maghunahuna ang uban nga tanang UV gibabagan sa ozone mao nga dili na ta mapaso. Sayop kini. Gibabagan sa ozone ang labing peligrosong UV, apan adunay gamayng UV nga makalusot gihapon kanato, mao nga mapaso gihapon ta kung sobra ka dugay sa adlaw.

q: What does a sea anemone do when it feels threatened or when the tide goes out?
options: It pulls in its tentacles and closes up into a small blob to protect itself.
It releases a cloud of ink to confuse any attacker nearby.
It detaches from the rock and swims away to a safer spot.
It extends its tentacles as wide as possible to look bigger.
explanation: When threatened or exposed at low tide, a sea anemone pulls in its tentacles and closes up to protect them from drying out or from enemies.
fact_tl: Kapag may panganib o kapag humupa ang tubig, maaaring umurong at magsara ang sea anemone na nagiging parang maliit na globo. Inililigtas nito ang malambot nitong galamay sa pagkatuyo o sa mga kaaway.
fact_bis: Kon adunay kakuyaw o kon mohubas ang tubig, ang sea anemone makakuom ug makasira nga mahimong gamay nga globo. Niini mapanalipdan ang humok niini nga mga galamay gikan sa pagkauga o sa mga kaaway.

q: What do your eyes do when sunlight is very bright?
options: You blink or squint more to protect your eyes.
Your pupils open up as wide as possible to let in more light.
Your eyelashes grow longer to shade your eyes automatically.
Your eyes water less so you can see the brightness more clearly.
explanation: We blink or squint more when sunlight is too bright, protecting our eyes from the harsh light.
fact_tl: Madalas tayong kumukurap o kumukunot ng mata kapag masyadong maliwanag ang araw.
fact_bis: Kasagaran ta mopilok o mokunot sa mata kon sobra ka hayag ang adlaw.

q: What gives hair its color?
options: A substance called melanin — the more of it there is, the darker the hair.
The amount of oil produced by the scalp underneath the hair.
Tiny blood vessels inside each hair strand that carry color.
The thickness of each hair strand — thicker hair appears darker.
explanation: Hair color comes from melanin; more melanin means darker hair.
fact_tl: Ang kulay ng buhok ay nagmumula sa isang tinta na tinatawag na melanin; mas marami nito, mas maitim ang buhok.
fact_bis: Ang kolor sa buhok gikan sa tinta nga gitawag og melanin; kung daghan kini, mas itom ang buhok.

q: Who discovered nuclear fission in 1938?
options: Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann, later explained by Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch.
Marie Curie and Pierre Curie, who were studying uranium decay.
Albert Einstein and Niels Bohr, who designed the first reactor.
Enrico Fermi and Robert Oppenheimer, who worked on the Manhattan Project.
explanation: Nuclear fission was discovered in 1938 by Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann, and explained by Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch.
fact_tl: Natuklasan ang nuclear fission noong 1938 nina Otto Hahn at Fritz Strassmann, na ipinaliwanag nina Lise Meitner at Otto Frisch.
fact_bis: Ang nuclear fission nadiskobrehan niadtong 1938 nila Otto Hahn ug Fritz Strassmann, ug gipasabot nila Lise Meitner ug Otto Frisch.

q: Why does a cold glass get wet on the outside when left in a warm, humid room?
options: Water vapour hidden in the air touches the cold glass and turns into water droplets.
The glass slowly leaks water through tiny holes in its surface.
The cold glass pulls moisture from inside the drink through the glass walls.
Air produces liquid water when it is squeezed against a cold surface.
explanation: Air holds invisible water vapour; when warm moist air touches a cold glass, the vapour condenses into droplets on the outside.
fact_tl: May nakatagong tubig sa hangin bilang water vapor (singaw) — kaya nararamdaman nating mahalumigmig o 'mainit-init at basa' ang panahon sa Pilipinas. Kapag humipo ang mainit na hangin na ito sa malamig na baso, nagiging patak ng tubig ang singaw sa labas ng baso.
fact_bis: Adunay tinago nga tubig sa hangin isip water vapor (alisngaw) — mao nga kasagaran mabati nato nga humid o 'init ug basa' ang panahon sa Pilipinas. Kung ang init nga umog nga hangin mosaghid sa bugnaw nga baso, mahimong tulo sa tubig ang alisngaw sa gawas sa baso.

q: Which planet in our Solar System is the smallest?
options: Mercury
Mars
Pluto
Venus
explanation: Mercury is the smallest planet in the Solar System.
fact_tl: Ang Mercury ang pinakamaliit na planeta sa Solar System.
fact_bis: Ang Mercury mao ang pinakagamay nga planeta sa Solar System.

q: How do different animals prepare food supplies for winter — do they all store fat?
options: No — some store fat in their bodies, while others store food in their burrow and wake up to eat it.
Yes — all hibernating animals store fat; none of them keep food outside their body.
No — most animals eat more during winter rather than storing anything ahead of time.
Yes — every hibernating animal buries food and sleeps the whole winter without waking.
explanation: Some animals store fat in their bodies for winter, while others store food in their burrow and wake occasionally to eat it.
fact_tl: May mga hayop na nag-iimbak ng taba sa katawan, at may iba namang nag-iimbak ng pagkain sa lungga at panaka-nakang nagigising para kumain sa taglamig.
fact_bis: Adunay mananap nga magtigom og tambok sa lawas, ug adunay lain nga magtigom og pagkaon sa lungib ug magmata-mata aron mokaon panahon sa tingtugnaw.

q: What do shorebirds eat when they feed on muddy coastlines?
options: Small worms, shellfish, and crabs buried in the mudflats.
Seeds and berries that wash up along the shoreline.
Small fish they catch by diving into the shallow water.
Algae and seaweed growing on rocks near the water.
explanation: On muddy shores, shorebirds eat small worms, shellfish, and crabs buried in the mudflats.
fact_tl: Sa mga putikang baybayin, kinakain ng mga ibong dagat ang maliliit na uod, kabibi, at alimango na nakabaon sa lapok.
fact_bis: Sa mga lapokon nga baybayon, ginakaon sa mga langgam sa baybayon ang gagmay nga mga ulod, kinhason, ug alimango nga nalubong sa lapok.

q: What do the three sides of the white triangle on the Philippine flag represent?
options: Liberty, equality, and fraternity.
Peace, courage, and loyalty.
Land, sea, and sky of the Philippines.
Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.
explanation: The white triangle on the Philippine flag stands for liberty, equality, and fraternity.
fact_tl: Ang puting tatsulok ng bandila ay kumakatawan sa kalayaan, pagkakapantay-pantay, at pagkakapatiran.
fact_bis: Ang puti nga triyanggulo sa bandera nagrepresentar sa kagawasan, pagkaparehas, ug panag-igsoonay.

q: How does soap help remove germs when you wash your hands?
options: Soap breaks apart the oily coat around some germs so water can rinse them away.
Soap kills germs instantly by releasing a disinfecting chemical into the skin.
Soap makes your hands slippery so germs slide off without being broken apart.
Soap changes the pH of water so germs cannot survive in it.
explanation: Soap breaks apart the oily coat around some germs, allowing water to rinse them off your hands.
fact_tl: Ang sabon ay sumisira sa malangis na balot ng ilang mikrobyo kaya madali silang matanggal ng tubig.
fact_bis: Ang sabon nagbungkag sa malana nga panit sa pipila ka mikrobyo aron ma-banlas sila sa tubig.

q: What dangerous substance does Clostridium botulinum produce in improperly canned food?
options: Botulinum toxin, one of the most poisonous chemicals known to science.
Salmonella acid, which sours the food and causes stomach pain.
Carbon dioxide gas, which causes the cans to swell and burst.
Penicillin mold, which ruins the food's taste and smell.
explanation: Clostridium botulinum bacteria grow in improperly canned food and produce botulinum toxin, one of the most poisonous chemicals known.
fact_tl: Ang Clostridium botulinum ay isang bacteria na lumalaki sa mga de lata na pagkain nang walang sapat na init at gumagawa ng botulinum toxin — isa sa mga pinaka-nakakalason na kemikal na kilala ng agham.
fact_bis: Ang Clostridium botulinum mga bakterya nga motubo sa mga de lata nga pagkain nga walay saktong init ug nagbuhat og botulinum toxin — usa sa labing nakakalason nga mga kemikal nga nahibaw-an sa siyensya.

q: Which gas is the third most abundant in Earth's air?
options: Argon
Carbon dioxide
Water vapour
Helium
explanation: Argon makes up about 0.9% of the air, making it the third most abundant gas after nitrogen and oxygen.
fact_tl: Ang argon ang pangatlong pinaka-maraming gas sa hangin, mga 0.9%.
fact_bis: Ang argon mao ang ikatlo nga labing daghan nga gas sa hangin, mga 0.9%.

q: What basic body features do ALL vertebrates share, even though they look very different?
options: A backbone, a skull protecting the brain, and a spinal cord.
Four limbs, warm blood, and a heart with four chambers.
Two eyes, a nose, and skin covered in scales or feathers.
Lungs for breathing air, a tail, and identical bone count.
explanation: All vertebrates share the same basic inner plan: a backbone, a skull protecting the brain, and a spinal cord.
fact_tl: Lahat ng vertebrate ay may parehong pangkalahatang balangkas sa loob: isang gulugod, isang bungo na nagpoprotekta sa utak, at isang spinal cord — kahit ibang-iba ang anyo nila sa labas.
fact_bis: Ang tanang vertebrate adunay parehong sukaranang han-ay sa sulod: usa ka gulugod, usa ka bagol nga nagpanalipod sa utok, ug usa ka spinal cord — bisan lahi kaayo silag dagway sa gawas.

q: What did scientist Marie Curie study that made her famous?
options: Radioactivity — the hidden energy given off by certain minerals.
Electromagnetism — how moving magnets produce electric currents.
Thermodynamics — how heat transfers between different materials.
Optics — how lenses bend and focus light to form images.
explanation: Marie Curie studied radioactivity, the hidden energy given off by certain minerals.
fact_tl: Si Marie Curie ay isang siyentista na nag-aral ng radioactivity o radyaktibidad, ang lihim na enerhiyang inilalabas ng ilang mineral.
fact_bis: Si Marie Curie usa ka siyentista nga nagtuon sa radioactivity, ang tinago nga enerhiya nga gibuga sa pipila ka mineral.

q: Where is the remora's suction disc located on its body?
options: On top of the head, separate from the real mouth at the front.
In place of the mouth — the disc IS the remora's mouth.
Under the belly, so it attaches to the bottom of the shark.
At the end of the tail, acting like an anchor.
explanation: The remora's suction disc sits on top of its head, separate from its real mouth — allowing it to eat while attached to a shark.
fact_tl: Maraming akala na ang suction disc ay bibig ng remora — mali iyon. Ang disc ay nasa IBABAW ng ulo, hiwalay sa tunay na bibig na nasa harap. Kaya kayang kumain ng remora habang nakadikit pa rin ang disc sa pating.
fact_bis: Daghan ang naghunahuna nga ang suction disc mao ang baba sa remora — sayop kana. Ang disc anaa sa IBABAW sa ulo, lahi sa tinuod nga baba sa atubangan. Mao nga makakaon gihapon ang remora samtang nagtapot pa ang disc sa iho.

q: Why are metals used for electric wires and cooking pot bottoms?
options: Metal atoms are tightly joined, letting heat and electricity flow through quickly.
Metals are the lightest materials, making wires and pots easy to carry.
Metals are flexible, so wires and pots can be shaped without breaking.
Metals repel water, keeping wires safe from moisture and rust.
explanation: The tightly joined atoms in solid metals let heat and electricity flow through quickly, which is why metals are used for wires and pot bottoms.
fact_tl: Dahil magkakadikit nang mahigpit ang mga atomo sa solid na metal, mabilis dumaloy dito ang init at kuryente. Kaya gawa sa metal ang mga kawad ng kuryente at ang ilalim ng kaldero na kailangang mabilis uminit.
fact_bis: Tungod kay hugot nga nagdikit ang mga atomo sa solid nga metal, paspas modagan ang kainit ug kuryente niini. Mao nga gama sa metal ang mga kawad sa kuryente ug ang ilawom sa kaldero nga kinahanglan paspas nga moinit.

q: What problem do barnacles cause when they grow on the hull (bottom) of a ship?
options: The ship slows down and burns more fuel.
The ship rusts faster because barnacles trap salt water.
The ship's steering becomes impossible to control.
The ship floats higher because barnacles add air pockets.
explanation: When many barnacles grow on a ship's hull, the added roughness slows the ship down and forces it to burn more fuel.
fact_tl: Kapag dumami ang mga barnacle sa ilalim ng barko, bumabagal ito at mas dumadami ang gamit na gasolina.
fact_bis: Kon modaghan ang mga barnacle sa ilawom sa barko, mohinay kini ug modaghan ang gigamit nga gasolina.

q: What traditional remedy is made from the leaves of the lagundi plant?
options: A boiled brew used to treat cough and colds.
A paste rubbed on skin to heal insect bites.
A powdered drink taken to lower fever quickly.
A leaf extract applied to the eyes to improve vision.
explanation: Lagundi leaves are boiled to make a brew used as a remedy for cough and colds.
fact_tl: Ang lagundi ay isang halamang-gamot na may dahong hugis-kamay na binubuo ng limang dahon, at ang pinakuluang dahon nito ay ginagamit bilang lunas sa ubo at sipon.
fact_bis: Ang lagundi usa ka tanom nga tambal nga adunay dahon nga porma og kamot nga gilangkuban og lima ka dahon, ug ang gilat-an niini nga dahon gigamit isip tambal sa ubo ug sip-on.

q: According to the nebular hypothesis, how did our Solar System form?
options: A large cloud of gas and dust collapsed; its centre became the Sun and the rest formed the planets.
Two stars collided and the pieces that flew apart became the Sun and planets.
The Sun exploded and the fragments that broke off became the planets.
A giant black hole pulled passing gas clouds together to form the Sun and planets.
explanation: The nebular hypothesis says the Solar System formed about 4.6 billion years ago from the collapse of a gas and dust cloud, with the centre becoming the Sun and the rest forming planets.
fact_tl: Ayon sa nebular hypothesis, ang aming solar system ay nabuo mga 4.6 bilyong taon na ang nakalipas mula sa pagtitipon ng isang malaking ulap ng gas at alikabok; ang sentro ay naging Araw habang ang natitirang materyal ay naging protoplanetary disk kung saan nagtipon ang mga planeta.
fact_bis: Sumala sa nebular hypothesis, ang atong solar system naporma mga 4.6 bilyong tuig na ang milabay gikan sa pagtipon sa usa ka dakong panganod sa gas ug abug; ang sentro nahimong Adlaw samtang ang nabilin nga materyal naghimo og protoplanetary disk diin ang mga planeta nagtapon.

q: What causes the sound of thunder during a storm?
options: Lightning quickly heats the air around it, making the air expand very fast and produce a boom.
Heavy raindrops hit the ground with so much force that they create a loud booming sound.
Cold and warm air masses crash into each other high in the clouds.
Electricity jumping between clouds rubs them together and creates a rumbling vibration.
explanation: Thunder is the sound made when lightning suddenly heats the surrounding air and causes it to expand very rapidly.
fact_tl: Ang kulog ay ang tunog na nalilikha kapag biglang pinapainit at pinapalobo ng kidlat ang hangin sa paligid nito.
fact_bis: Ang dalugdog mao ang tingog nga matawo kung ang kilat kalit nga mopainit ug mopalapad sa hangin sa palibot niini.

q: Why does an electric shock from an animal make your muscles feel a sudden jolt or go numb?
options: The electricity scrambles the nerve signals in your muscles, which causes the jolt and can stop you from moving.
The electricity heats your skin so fast that your nerves send a pain message to your brain.
The electricity pulls water out of your muscles so they cramp and cannot move.
The electricity travels to your brain and temporarily switches off your thinking.
explanation: An electric shock scrambles the signals in your muscles, causing a sudden jolt or numbness and briefly stopping movement.
fact_tl: Kapag natamaan ng kuryente ng hayop ang tao, parang biglang kibot o pangangalay ang nararamdaman, dahil ginugulo ng kuryente ang mga signal sa ating mga kalamnan. Masakit ito at maaaring makapagpatigil ng galaw saglit.
fact_bis: Kung ang kuryente sa mananap motama sa tawo, mura og kalit nga kibot o pagkamanhid ang mabati, kay ang kuryente makagubot sa mga senyas sa atong kaunoran. Sakit kini ug makapahunong sa imong paglihok sa makadiyot.

q: Why are pitcher plants often brightly colored?
options: To attract insects into the pitcher more easily, like a flower does.
To warn animals that the plant is poisonous and should not be eaten.
To absorb more sunlight for photosynthesis in dark forest areas.
To match the colors of nearby flowers so predators ignore the plant.
explanation: Pitcher plants are often brightly colored like flowers to attract insects, which then fall into the pitcher.
fact_tl: Madalas na makulay at parang bulaklak ang tabo upang mas maakit ang mga insekto.
fact_bis: Ang mga tabo kasagaran mabulokon nga morag bulak aron mas madani ang mga insekto.

q: By about how much has Earth's average temperature risen since pre-industrial times?
options: About 1.1°C
About 5°C
About 0.1°C
About 10°C
explanation: Earth's average temperature has risen by about 1.1°C since pre-industrial times, which is clear evidence of ongoing climate change.
fact_tl: Ang average na temperatura ng Mundo ay tumaas ng humigit-kumulang 1.1°C mula sa panahon bago ang industriyalisasyon; ang pinakamalinaw na ebidensya ng climate change ito.
fact_bis: Ang average nga temperatura sa Yuta misaka og mga 1.1°C gikan sa panahon bago ang industriyalisasyon; kini klaro nga ebidensya sa nagpadayon nga climate change.

q: What is the chemical formula for ordinary table salt?
options: NaCl
H2O
CO2
KCl
explanation: NaCl (sodium chloride) is the chemical formula for table salt, made of sodium and chloride ions held together by opposite electrical charges.
fact_tl: Ang NaCl ay ang chemical formula ng table salt (sodium chloride) — ito ay isang ionic compound na binubuo ng sodium (Na) at chlorine (Cl) ions na nagkakapit dahil sa kabaligtarang charges.
fact_bis: Ang NaCl mao ang chemical formula sa table salt (sodium chloride); usa kini ka ionic compound nga binubuo sa sodium (Na+) ug chloride (Cl-) ions nga nagkupot pinaagi sa magkaatbang nga electrical charges.

q: What number is the metric system based on?
options: Ten — so units differ by 10, 100, or 1,000.
Two — so units double each step (2, 4, 8, 16 …).
Twelve — like inches in a foot or months in a year.
Sixty — like seconds in a minute or minutes in an hour.
explanation: The metric system is based on tens, so each unit is 10, 100, or 1,000 times larger or smaller than the next.
fact_tl: Ang sistemang metriko ay nakabatay sa sampu, kaya ang mga yunit ay 10, 100, o 1,000 ang pagitan.
fact_bis: Ang sistemang metriko gibase sa napulo, mao nga ang mga yunit nagkalainlain og 10, 100, o 1,000.

q: What keeps all the planets, including Earth, orbiting around the Sun?
options: The Sun's strong gravity, which comes from its huge size.
The Sun's light, which pushes the planets in a circle like a spinning top.
Magnetic forces between the planets that keep them linked together.
The speed at which the planets were launched when the Solar System formed.
explanation: The Sun's enormous size gives it strong gravity that holds all the planets in orbit; without it, they would fly off into space.
fact_tl: Napakalakas ng grabidad ng Araw dahil sa laki nito kaya hinihila nito ang lahat ng planeta, kasama ang Mundo, na umikot paligid dito — kung wala ang grabidad ng Araw, lilipad palayo ang mga planeta sa kalawakan.
fact_bis: Kusog kaayo ang grabidad sa Adlaw tungod sa kadako niini mao nga gibira niini ang tanang planeta, lakip ang Kalibutan, nga molibot palibot niini — kung walay grabidad sa Adlaw, molupad palayo ang mga planeta ngadto sa kawanangan.

q: What is unusual about how Triton, Neptune's largest moon, orbits the planet?
options: It orbits in the opposite direction to Neptune's spin, which is unusual for moons.
It orbits much closer to Neptune than any other moon in the Solar System.
It orbits so fast that it completes a full revolution every 24 hours.
It orbits at a perfect 90-degree tilt so it passes over both poles.
explanation: Triton orbits backward compared to Neptune's rotation, which is unusual among the moons in our Solar System.
fact_tl: Ang Triton, ang pinakamalaking buwan ng Neptune, ay umiikot nang pasalungat sa pag-ikot ng planeta — kakaiba ito sa karamihan ng buwan.
fact_bis: Ang Triton, ang pinakadako nga bulan sa Neptune, molibot nga sukwahi sa pagtuyok sa planeta — lahi kini sa kadaghanan sa mga bulan.

q: Why does a moray eel often keep its mouth open?
options: To push water over its gills so it can breathe, not because it is angry.
To show its teeth as a warning to predators that might attack it.
To catch small fish that swim too close to its hiding spot.
To cool its body down because it cannot regulate its own temperature.
explanation: A moray eel holds its mouth open to move water over its gills for breathing, not as a sign of aggression.
fact_tl: Madalas nakabukas ang bibig ng moray eel hindi dahil galit ito kundi para padaluyin ang tubig sa hasang nito at makahinga.
fact_bis: Kanunay abli ang baba sa moray eel dili tungod kay nasuko kini kondili aron paagion ang tubig sa hasang niini aron makaginhawa.

q: In many Philippine provinces, how do people reach groundwater underground?
options: They dig a well or use a jetmatic pump down to the water table
They collect rain in large tanks on their rooftops
They melt ice stored in deep caves under the ground
They pipe water directly from nearby rivers into their homes
explanation: People dig wells or use jetmatic pumps to reach the water table underground, then draw up the water for drinking, cooking, and watering plants.
fact_tl: Sa maraming probinsya sa Pilipinas, kumukuha ng groundwater ang mga tao gamit ang balon o jetmatic pump. Hinuhukay ang lupa hanggang umabot sa water table, tapos hinihila pataas ang tubig para inumin, magluto, at magdilig.
fact_bis: Sa daghang probinsya sa Pilipinas, mokuha ang mga tawo og groundwater gamit ang atabay o jetmatic pump. Magkalot sila paubos hangtod moabot sa water table, dayon birahon pataas ang tubig para imnon, magluto, ug magbisbis.

q: What starts breaking down starch from rice and bread even before you swallow it?
options: Acid in your stomach
An enzyme in your saliva while you chew
Bile produced by your liver
Enzymes released in your small intestine
explanation: An enzyme in saliva begins breaking down starch from rice and bread while you chew, so digestion starts in the mouth.
fact_tl: May enzyme sa laway na nagsisimulang tunawin ang almirol mula sa kanin at tinapay habang nginunguya mo ito.
fact_bis: Adunay enzyme sa laway nga magsugod pagtunaw sa starch gikan sa kan-on ug pan samtang imong gisapsap.

q: Which group of plants do mung beans, peanuts, peas, and string beans all belong to?
options: Grains
Legumes
Root crops
Tubers
explanation: Mung beans, string beans, peas, peanuts, and pigeon peas all belong to one family called legumes.
fact_tl: Ang munggo, sitaw, gisantes, mani, at kadyos ay magkakapamilya at tinatawag na legumes.
fact_bis: Ang munggo, sitaw, gisantes, mani, ug kadyos managsoon ug gitawag nga legumes.

q: What happens to nutrients in soil after decomposers break down dead plants and animals?
options: The nutrients disappear permanently into the air
The nutrients are recycled back into the soil for plants to use again
The nutrients turn into rocks over hundreds of years
The nutrients wash away into the ocean and are lost forever
explanation: Decomposers return nutrients to the soil when they break down dead matter, so nutrients are recycled in nature rather than used up.
fact_tl: Kapag nilalansag ng mga decomposers ang patay na bagay, ibinabalik nila ang mga sustansya (nutrients) sa lupa. Magagamit muli ng mga halaman ang mga sustansyang ito para lumaki — kaya hindi nauubos ang sustansya sa kalikasan.
fact_bis: Kon gub-on sa mga decomposers ang patay nga butang, ibalik nila ang mga sustansya (nutrients) sa yuta. Magamit pag-usab sa mga tanom kini nga mga sustansya aron motubo — busa dili mahurot ang sustansya sa kinaiyahan.

q: What word describes a close, long-term relationship between two different kinds of living things?
options: Predation
Competition
Symbiosis
Migration
explanation: Symbiosis is a close, long-term relationship between two different kinds of living things.
fact_tl: Ang simbiyosis ay ang pamumuhay nang magkasama ng dalawang magkaibang uri ng nabubuhay na bagay nang matagalan.
fact_bis: Ang simbiyosis mao ang dugay nga pagpuyo nga magkuyog sa duha ka lain-laing matang sa buhing butang.

q: A barchan is a type of sand dune shaped like a crescent. Which direction do its two tips point?
options: Toward where the wind is coming from
In the direction the wind is blowing
Toward the nearest body of water
Straight up toward the sky
explanation: A barchan is a crescent-shaped dune whose two tips point in the direction the wind is blowing.
fact_tl: Ang barchan ay isang uri ng dune na hugis-gasuklay, kung saan ang dalawang dulo nito ay nakaturo sa direksyong tinatahak ng hangin.
fact_bis: Ang barchan usa ka matang sa dune nga sama sa bag-ong bulan, diin ang duha ka tumoy niini nagtumong sa direksyon sa paghuyop sa hangin.

q: How is true hibernation different from ordinary deep sleep?
options: Hibernating animals wake up every few hours to eat
The animal's body temperature and heartbeat drop very low for weeks or months
The animal stays in exactly the same spot but keeps eating stored food
Hibernating animals sleep with their eyes open to watch for danger
explanation: True hibernation is not just deep sleep — the animal's body temperature and heartbeat drop very low for weeks or months to save energy while food is scarce in winter.
fact_tl: Ang tunay na hibernation ay hindi lang basta mahimbing na tulog — bumababa nang husto ang temperatura at tibok ng puso ng hayop nang maraming linggo o buwan para makatipid ng lakas habang walang pagkain sa taglamig.
fact_bis: Ang tinuod nga hibernation dili lang ordinaryong tulog — ang temperatura ug pitik sa kasingkasing sa mananap mokunhod pag-ayo sulod sa daghang semana o bulan aron makadaginot og kusog samtang walay pagkaon sa tingtugnaw.

q: How do baby ducklings move when they are with their mother on the water?
options: They swim ahead of their mother in a wide group
They float in a circle around their mother
They follow their mother and swim behind her in a line
They wait on the shore while their mother swims alone
explanation: Baby ducklings follow their mother and swim along behind her in a line.
fact_tl: Ang munting sisiw ng bibe ay sumusunod sa kanyang ina at lumalangoy kasama nito.
fact_bis: Ang gagmay nga piso sa bibe nagsunod sa ilang inahan ug nagalangoy kuyog niini.

q: How does a junkyard crane pick up and then drop heavy steel and old cars?
options: It uses a giant hook that locks onto metal with a special clamp
It uses a huge electromagnet that can be switched on and off
It uses a very powerful permanent magnet that a worker attaches by hand
It uses a vacuum suction cup that grips smooth metal surfaces
explanation: Junkyard cranes have a huge electromagnet that is switched on to lift heavy steel and old cars, then switched off to drop them somewhere else.
fact_tl: Sa mga junkyard, may malalaking crane na may electromagnet sa dulo. Binubuksan nila ito para buhatin ang mabibigat na bakal at lumang kotse, tapos pinapatay para ibagsak ang mga ito sa ibang lugar.
fact_bis: Sa mga junkyard, ang dagkong crane adunay dakong electromagnet sa tumoy. Sindihan nila kini aron alsahon ang bug-at nga puthaw ug daang sakyanan, dayon palungon aron ihulog kini sa laing dapit.

q: When a spring is stretched or squeezed, what does it do?
options: It stays in its new shape and does not move back
It pushes back with a force that tries to return it to its rest shape
It breaks apart because the force is too strong
It heats up and slowly melts back to its original length
explanation: When a spring is stretched or squeezed, it pushes back with a restoring force that opposes the motion and pulls it toward its rest shape.
fact_tl: Kapag inunat o ipinit ang spring, gumagawa ito ng pwersa na sumasalungat sa galaw at humihila pabalik sa pahinga nitong hugis.
fact_bis: Kon banaton o ipiton ang spring, mohatag kini og pwersa nga makontra sa lihok ug mobira balik ngadto sa iyang pahulay nga porma.

q: Why does a dry mouth and throat make us feel thirsty?
options: The stomach sends a signal that it is completely empty and needs liquid
There is less saliva, making the mouth and throat dry, which is a signal to drink
The lungs use up all available water during breathing
The kidneys stop working when they run out of liquid to filter
explanation: Feeling thirsty is partly caused by less saliva making the mouth and throat dry, which tells us we need to drink to become moist and fresh again.
fact_tl: Bahagi ng pakiramdam ng uhaw ay kapag natutuyo ang bibig at lalamunan dahil kulang na ang laway. Sinasabi nito sa atin na kailangan na nating uminom para bumalik ang basa at sariwa nating bibig.
fact_bis: Bahin sa pamati sa kauhaw mao kon mauga ang baba ug tutunlan tungod kay kulang na ang laway. Mosulti kini kanato nga kinahanglan na ta moinom aron mobalik ang kaumog ug kabag-o sa atong baba.

q: Why is the top of most leaves a deeper green than the underside?
options: The top has a waxy coating that reflects more light and looks darker
There is more chlorophyll on the top, the side that faces the sun
The underside loses its green color from rainwater washing it away
The bottom of the leaf is older and has been in the shade longer
explanation: The top of many leaves is a deeper green because there is more chlorophyll there — it is the side facing the sun and catching the most light.
fact_tl: Ang ibabaw ng maraming dahon ay mas matingkad na berde kaysa sa ilalim dahil mas maraming chlorophyll doon — iyon ang bahaging humaharap sa araw at humuhuli ng pinakamaraming liwanag.
fact_bis: Ang ibabaw sa daghang dahon mas labong nga berde kaysa sa ilawom tungod kay mas daghan ang chlorophyll didto — kana ang bahin nga nag-atubang sa adlaw ug nagdakop sa pinakadaghang kahayag.

q: Who was the first person to see living microbes like bacteria using a microscope?
options: Louis Pasteur
Anton van Leeuwenhoek
Isaac Newton
Charles Darwin
explanation: Anton van Leeuwenhoek was the first person to see living microbes, such as bacteria, using a microscope he made himself.
fact_tl: Si Anton van Leeuwenhoek ang unang nakakita ng mga buhay na mikrobyo gaya ng bakterya sa pamamagitan ng kanyang sariling gawang mikroskopyo.
fact_bis: Si Anton van Leeuwenhoek mao ang unang tawo nga nakakita sa buhing mikrobyo, sama sa bakterya, gamit ang mikroskopyo nga iyang gibuhat.

q: What is the largest lake in the Philippines?
options: Lake Lanao
Taal Lake
Laguna de Bay
Lake Sebu
explanation: The largest lake in the Philippines is Laguna de Bay, located near Manila.
fact_tl: Ang pinakamalaking lawa sa Pilipinas ay ang Laguna de Bay malapit sa Maynila.
fact_bis: Ang labing dako nga lanaw sa Pilipinas mao ang Laguna de Bay duol sa Manila.

q: What is the first step to understanding your emotions like happiness, sadness, or anger?
options: Ignoring the feeling until it goes away on its own
Telling someone else what to feel on your behalf
Naming what you feel
Waiting until you are older to think about feelings
explanation: Naming what you feel — such as happiness, sadness, anger, or fear — is the first step to understanding it.
fact_tl: May iba't ibang damdamin tulad ng saya, lungkot, galit, at takot — ang pagbibigay ng pangalan sa nararamdaman mo ang unang hakbang para maunawaan ito.
fact_bis: Adunay nagkalainlaing pagbati sama sa kalipay, kaguol, kasuko, ug kahadlok — ang paghatag og ngalan sa imong gibati maoy unang lakang aron masabtan kini.

q: In a suspension bridge, what holds up the roadway?
options: Thick concrete columns placed under the road at regular intervals
Steel beams welded along the bottom of the bridge deck
Cables attached to tall towers that are under tension bearing the weight
Air pressure from below that pushes up on the flat road surface
explanation: A suspension bridge hangs its roadway from cables attached to tall towers — the cables are under tension as they bear the weight of the bridge and traffic.
fact_tl: Ang suspension bridge ay nagbitay ng kalsada gamit ang mga cable na nakakabit sa mataas na tore — ang mga cable ay nasa tension habang tinatanggap ang timbang ng tulay.
fact_bis: Ang suspension bridge nagbitay sa dalan gamit ang mga cable nga gikabit sa mataas nga mga tore — ang mga cable naa sa tension samtang ginadala ang timbang sa tulay ug trapiko.

q: What would happen if there were no decomposers in nature?
options: Plants would grow faster because there would be more space
Animals would live longer without competing for food
Dead animals and plants would pile up and never go away
The water cycle would stop because clouds need decomposers
explanation: Without decomposers, dead animals and plants would pile up and never be broken down, burying the world in dead matter.
fact_tl: Ang mga decomposers ay parang taga-linis ng kalikasan: nilalansag nila ang mga patay na hayop at halaman bago pa ito magtambak. Kung wala sila, mababalot ang mundo ng patay na bagay na hindi nawawala.
fact_bis: Ang mga decomposers sama sa tiglimpyo sa kinaiyahan: gub-on nila ang patay nga hayop ug tanom sa dili pa kini magtapok. Kon wala sila, matabunan ang kalibotan sa patay nga butang nga dili gyud mawala.

q: When does coconut water taste the sweetest and best?
options: After it has been stored in a bottle for several days
When it has been left open in the air overnight
Right after the coconut is freshly opened
When it is mixed with sugar and ice before drinking
explanation: Coconut water tastes best when the coconut is freshly opened; once left out in the air for a long time, its fresh sweetness slowly fades away.
fact_tl: Pinakamasarap inumin ang tubig ng buko kapag bagong bukas pa lang ito. Kapag matagal nang nakalantad sa hangin, unti-unting nawawala ang sariwang tamis at lasa nito.
fact_bis: Pinakalami imnon ang tubig sa buko kung bag-o pa kining giablihan. Kung dugay na kining nabilin sa hangin, hinay-hinay nga mawala ang presko nga katam-is ug lami niini.

q: Why does red tide poison cause numbness and weakness in a person's body?
options: It destroys red blood cells so oxygen cannot reach the muscles
It blocks the tiny doorways in nerves (sodium channels) that carry signals, so the brain cannot command muscles
It attacks the stomach lining and prevents food from being digested
