fact_tl: Ang calamansi ay isang maliit at maasim na prutas na karaniwang berde ang balat at madalas itinatanim sa mga bahay sa Pilipinas.
fact_bis: Ang kalamansi usa ka gamay ug maaslom nga prutas nga kasagaran lunhaw ang panit ug kanunay gitanom sa mga balay sa Pilipinas.

q: What happens during fermentation?
options: Microbes like yeast and bacteria change the sugars in food.
Heat breaks down the starch in food into simpler sugars.
Oxygen reacts with food to preserve it for a longer time.
Salt draws water out of food to stop bacteria from growing.
explanation: Fermentation is the process where microbes such as yeast and bacteria break down the sugars in food.
fact_tl: Ang fermentation ay paraan ng mga microbyo tulad ng lebadura at bakterya para palitan ang asukal sa pagkain.
fact_bis: Ang fermentation maoy paagi sa mga microbyo sama sa lebadura ug bakterya nga mag-usab sa asukal sa pagkaon.

q: Why is rabies mainly spread through fresh bites or wounds rather than through dried saliva?
options: The rabies virus is fragile outside the body and dies quickly when saliva dries out or is exposed to sunlight and air.
The rabies virus cannot survive at body temperature and only lives in cool environments.
Dried saliva still carries the virus, but it cannot pass through unbroken skin.
The virus is destroyed by the enzymes in fresh saliva, so it only survives in wounds.
explanation: The rabies virus dies quickly once saliva dries, sits in sunlight, or is exposed to air, so it is mainly transmitted through fresh saliva entering a bite or wound.
fact_tl: Ang rabies virus ay mahina sa labas ng katawan — mabilis itong mamatay kapag natuyo ang laway, nabilad sa araw, o nahanginan. Kaya pangunahing nakukuha ito sa sariwang laway na direktang napapasok sa sugat o kagat, hindi sa mga lumang patak.
fact_bis: Ang rabies nga bayrus huyang sa gawas sa lawas — dali kini mamatay kon mauga na ang laway, mainitan sa adlaw, o mahanginan. Mao nga kasagaran makuha kini gikan sa lab-as nga laway nga direktang mosulod sa samad o paak, dili sa daan nga uga nga tinulo.

q: What makes some plankton involved in red tide dangerous?
options: They produce a natural poison that is harmful to animals and people.
They release carbon dioxide that lowers the oxygen level in the water.
They grow so thickly that they block sunlight needed by coral reefs.
They attract large schools of jellyfish that sting swimmers.
explanation: Certain plankton that cause red tide produce a natural toxin that is dangerous to both animals and humans.
fact_tl: Hindi lahat ng plankton ay nakakalason, pero ilang uri na sangkot sa red tide ay gumagawa ng natural na lason na delikado sa mga hayop at tao.
fact_bis: Dili tanang plankton makahilo, apan pipila ka klase nga apil sa red tide naghimo og natural nga hilo nga peligroso sa mga mananap ug tawo.

q: Why is the sailfin lizard (ibid) protected by Philippine law?
options: Its habitat is being destroyed and it is captured for the pet trade, making it a threatened animal.
It has been declared a national symbol and may not be used for any commercial purpose.
It is poisonous, so capturing it is dangerous and therefore forbidden.
It is considered sacred in many Philippine communities and is protected by tradition.
explanation: The sailfin lizard is threatened because habitat destruction and capture for the pet trade have reduced its numbers, so Philippine law forbids catching or selling it.
fact_tl: Ang ibid ay isang nanganganib na hayop dahil nawawasak ang tirahan nito at hinuhuli ito para sa pet trade — kaya ipinagbabawal ng batas ng Pilipinas na hulihin o ipagbili ito.
fact_bis: Ang ibid usa ka namiligro nga hayop tungod kay nagun-ob ang puy-anan niini ug gidakop kini alang sa pet trade — mao nga gidili sa balaod sa Pilipinas ang pagdakop o pagbaligya niini.

q: Why does a spinning object eventually slow down and stop?
options: Friction with the surface and air gradually takes away its energy.
Gravity pulls the spinning object downward, converting spin into downward movement.
The weight of the object pushes against the spin and cancels it out.
The object uses up the energy stored inside it until none is left.
explanation: Friction from the surface and the air gradually removes energy from a spinning object until it finally stops.
fact_tl: Walang umiikot na bagay na umiikot magpakailanman. Ang kuskusan (friction) sa pader o lupa at ang hangin ay unti-unting nagpapabagal dito hanggang sa huminto. Kung wala ang mga ito, magpapatuloy ang pag-ikot nang napakatagal.
fact_bis: Walay nagtuyok nga butang nga magtuyok hangtod sa kahangtoran. Ang gisaw (friction) sa salog ug ang hangin maoy hinay-hinay nga mopahinay niini hangtod nga mohunong. Kung wala kana, magpadayon ang pagtuyok og dugay kaayo.

q: How do we replace the water our body loses every day?
options: By drinking and by eating watery foods like fruits and vegetables
By breathing, since air contains enough moisture for the body
By absorbing water through our skin when we shower or swim
By eating salty foods that help the body hold onto water better
explanation: We replace lost body water by drinking fluids and eating water-rich foods such as fruits and vegetables.
fact_tl: Pinapalitan natin ang nawawalang tubig sa pag-inom at sa pagkain ng mga basang pagkain tulad ng prutas at gulay.
fact_bis: Atong gibalik ang nawala nga tubig pinaagi sa pag-inom ug sa pagkaon og basa nga pagkaon sama sa prutas ug utanon.

q: What do the blood vessels in your skin do when your body gets too hot?
options: They widen to release extra heat from the body.
They narrow to keep the warmth inside the body.
They send signals to the brain to start shivering.
They push sweat glands to produce less fluid to save water.
explanation: When hot, blood vessels in the skin dilate (widen) so that more heat can escape from the blood into the air, cooling the body down.
fact_tl: Kapag mainit, ang mga blood vessel sa balat ay lumalawak (dilates) upang palabasin ang init; kapag malamig, ito ay kumikitid (constricts) upang mapanatili ang init sa katawan.
fact_bis: Kung mainit, ang mga blood vessel sa panit nagdako (nagdilate) aron palabasin ang init; kung malamig, naghinay kini (nagconstrict) aron mapugngan ang kainit sa lawas.

q: Where do Australia's bogong moths travel to every summer?
options: Cool mountain caves thousands of kilometers away
Warm coastal beaches to lay their eggs near the sea
Underground burrows in the outback desert to avoid the heat
The rainforest canopy to feed on nectar from flowering trees
explanation: Australia's bogong moth travels thousands of kilometers each summer to gather in cool mountain caves, making it one of the best-known insect migrations in the Southern Hemisphere.
fact_tl: Ang bogong moth ng Australia ay lumalakbay ng libu-libong kilometro sa tuwing tag-araw para magtipon sa mga malamig na bundok—isa sa pinakakilalang migrasyong insekto.
fact_bis: Ang bogong moth sa Australia molakaw og libo-libong kilometro sa matag ting-init para magtipon sa mabugnaw nga mga guwang sa bundok—usa sa labing nahibaloan nga paglalin sa insekto sa Southern Hemisphere.

q: During which sleep stage do our eyes move quickly and we often dream?
options: REM sleep
Deep sleep (slow-wave sleep)
Light sleep (Stage 1)
The falling-asleep stage (hypnic stage)
explanation: REM (rapid eye movement) sleep is the stage where our eyes move quickly beneath our eyelids and we most often experience dreams.
fact_tl: May yugto ng tulog na tinatawag na REM kung saan mabilis gumagalaw ang ating mga mata at madalas tayong nananaginip.
fact_bis: Adunay bahin sa tulog nga gitawag og REM, diin paspas molihok ang atong mga mata ug kanunay kita magdamgo.

q: Where was Filipino computer-chip engineer Diosdado Banatao born?
options: Cagayan province in the Philippines
Cebu City in the Visayas
Manila, Metro Manila
Ilocos Norte in Northern Luzon
explanation: Diosdado Banatao was born in Cagayan province in the Philippines before becoming a famous computer-chip engineer.
fact_tl: Si Diosdado Banatao ay isinilang sa lalawigan ng Cagayan sa Pilipinas bago naging tanyag na engineer sa computer chips.
fact_bis: Si Diosdado Banatao natawo sa lalawigan sa Cagayan sa Pilipinas una pa siya nahimong inila nga engineer sa computer chips.

q: What happens to sugar when it is heated to make leche flan caramel and then allowed to cool?
options: It melts and turns golden brown, then hardens into solid caramel as it cools.
It dissolves in the egg mixture and stays liquid even after cooling.
It turns black immediately and cannot be used for caramel anymore.
It keeps its white color but becomes sticky instead of hard.
explanation: When heated, sugar melts and turns golden brown; as it cools it hardens into the solid caramel layer on top of leche flan.
fact_tl: Kapag pinainit ang asukal para sa leche flan, ito ay natutunaw, naninilaw, at nagiging karamelo na tumitigas kapag lumamig.
fact_bis: Kon init-on ang asukal alang sa leche flan, kini matunaw, magbrown, ug mahimong karamelo nga magahi kon mabugnaw.

q: What is the flat marked part of a sundial called, and what does it tell you?
options: The dial face—when the shadow falls on a line, that line tells you the hour.
The gnomon—the vertical part that casts the shadow onto the ground.
The base plate—it keeps the sundial level so the readings are accurate.
The hour ring—a separate ring placed around the sundial for decoration.
explanation: The flat part of a sundial with marked lines and numbers is called the dial face; the shadow falls on a line that shows the current hour.
fact_tl: Ang patag na bahagi ng sundial na may mga guhit at numero ay tinatawag na dial. Kapag tumama ang anino sa isang linya, doon mo nababasa ang oras.
fact_bis: Ang patag nga bahin sa sundial nga may mga badlis ug numero gitawag ug dial. Kon motungtong ang landong sa usa ka badlis, didto nimo mabasa ang oras.

q: How does the thresher shark use its extremely long tail fin to hunt?
options: It whips the tail like a club to stun schooling fish before eating them.
It wraps the tail around prey to hold it still while biting.
It uses the tail to create a current that herds fish into shallow water.
It slaps the water surface to confuse fish and make them swim toward its mouth.
explanation: The thresher shark uses its long upper tail fin as a whip to stun groups of fish, making them easy to eat.
fact_tl: Ang thresher shark ay may napakahaba ng buntot na halos kasinghaba ng kanyang katawan; ginagamit nito ang buntot bilang whip upang paluin at atakuhin ang mga isda bago kainin.
fact_bis: Ang thresher shark adunay labing hataas nga buntot na halos kapareho sa gitas-on sa iyang lawas; gigamit niya kining buntot isip latig aron pahilantan ang mga gruponggrupong isda sa wala pa sila kaonon.

q: What effect does arecoline—the substance found in betel nut—have on the body?
options: It speeds up the heartbeat as a mild stimulant.
It slows the heartbeat and makes a person feel calmer.
It causes numbness in the tongue and gums only.
It lowers blood pressure and helps a person sleep.
explanation: Betel nut contains arecoline, a mild stimulant that can speed up the heartbeat.
fact_tl: Ang bunga ay may sangkap na arecoline na isang banayad na stimulant na nakapagpapabilis ng tibok ng puso.
fact_bis: Ang bunga adunay arecoline, usa ka hinay nga stimulant nga makapadali sa pitik sa kasingkasing.

q: Where are a jellyfish's tentacles located on its body?
options: They hang below and trail behind the jellyfish as it drifts.
They stick out from the sides of the bell like wings to steer.
They coil on top of the bell and shoot out quickly to grab prey.
They are attached to the center of the top of the bell.
explanation: A jellyfish's tentacles hang below its body and trail behind as it drifts—prey that bumps into them gets caught.
fact_tl: Ang mga galamay ng dikya ay nakalaylay sa ilalim ng katawan nito at sumusunod ito habang naaanod. Dito tumatama ang biktima na nadadaanan nito sa tubig.
fact_bis: Ang mga galamay sa dikya nagbitay sa ilawom sa lawas niini ug nagsunod samtang anod kini. Didto madakpan ang tukbonon nga makabangga niini sa tubig.

q: At what body temperature is a person considered to have a fever?
options: 38 degrees Celsius or higher
37 degrees Celsius or higher
39 degrees Celsius or higher
36.5 degrees Celsius or higher
explanation: A person is said to have a fever when their body temperature reaches 38°C or higher.
fact_tl: Itinuturing na may lagnat ang isang tao kapag ang temperatura ng katawan ay umabot sa 38 degrees Celsius o mas mataas.
fact_bis: Giisip nga adunay hilanat ang usa ka tawo kung ang temperatura sa lawas moabot sa 38 degrees Celsius o mas taas.

q: How does an abacus help you count and calculate?
options: Beads slide along rods, with each row representing ones, tens, hundreds, and so on.
You press buttons that light up to show each number as you count.
You move coins along grooves carved in a flat board to keep track of totals.
You spin numbered wheels that click into place to display the answer.
explanation: An abacus uses beads that slide along rods, where each row stands for a place value—ones, tens, hundreds—making counting and calculation easier.
fact_tl: Ang abacus ay isang lumang kasangkapan sa pagbilang na may mga butones na dumudulas sa mga kawad, at bawat hilera ng butones ay kumakatawan sa mga numero.
fact_bis: Ang abacus usa ka karaan nga galamiton sa pag-ihap nga adunay mga bola nga modan-as sa mga alambre, ug ang matag laray sa bola nagrepresentar sa mga numero.

q: Why do chameleons change color?
options: To show how they feel or to control their body temperature—not just to hide.
Only to blend into their background so predators cannot see them.
To warn enemies that they are poisonous and should not be eaten.
To attract insects by mimicking the color of flowers in their habitat.
explanation: Chameleons change color for several reasons—to communicate their mood and to regulate body heat—not only for camouflage.
fact_tl: Nagbabago ng kulay ang chameleon hindi lang para magtago kundi para ipakita ang damdamin nito o para itimpla ang init ng katawan.
fact_bis: Mag-usab og kolor ang chameleon dili lang aron motago kondili aron ipakita ang ilang gibati o aron pugngan ang kainit sa ilang lawas.

q: What triggers a neuron to release its chemical messenger at a synapse?
options: Tiny bits of calcium rush into the neuron's tip when the signal arrives.
The signal reaches a high enough voltage and automatically opens the sacs.
The next neuron sends a pull signal that draws the messenger across the gap.
Oxygen delivered by the blood causes the sacs to open and release the chemical.
explanation: When a nerve signal reaches the neuron's tip, calcium ions rush in—that is the trigger that causes the sacs to open and release the chemical messenger.
fact_tl: Pagdating ng signal sa dulo ng neuron, may maliit na mineral na tinatawag na calcium na pumapasok. Ito ang hudyat na magbubukas ng mga supot para ilabas ang kemikal na mensahero.
fact_bis: Pag-abot sa signal sa tumoy sa neuron, naay gagmay nga mineral nga gitawag og calcium nga mosulod. Mao kini ang senyas nga moabli sa mga supot aron ipagawas ang kemikal nga mensahero.

q: If you are caught outside in an open area during lightning, what should you avoid doing?
options: Standing tall or being the tallest object around
Crouching low with your feet together on the ground
Staying away from lone trees or metal poles
Moving to a low-lying area away from hilltops
explanation: If caught in an open area during lightning, you should never stand tall or be the highest object around because lightning strikes the tallest point.
fact_tl: Kung naabutan ka ng kidlat sa malawak na lugar, huwag tumayo at huwag maging pinakamataas na bagay sa paligid.
fact_bis: Kung maabtan ka sa kilat sa hawan nga dapit, ayaw pagbarog ug ayaw himoa ang imong kaugalingon nga pinakahataas nga butang.

q: How do pine trees and other cone-bearing plants spread their pollen?
options: Wind carries pollen from male cones to female cones.
Bees and butterflies carry pollen between flowers on different trees.
The cones release pollen into streams, which carries it to other trees.
Animals eat the cones and spread pollen through their droppings.
explanation: Cone-bearing plants like pines have no flowers; instead, wind carries pollen from male cones to female cones for pollination.
fact_tl: Ang mga halaman tulad ng pine trees ay hindi gumagawa ng bulaklak — ang kanilang mga buto ay nakaimbak sa mga cone na bukas sa hangin at ang pollination ay ginagawa ng hangin na nagdadala ng pollen mula sa lalaking cone patungo sa babae.
fact_bis: Ang mga tanom sama sa pine trees dili nagbuhat og bulaklak — ang ilang mga buto gibitay sa mga cone nga bukas sa hangin ug ang pollination gibuhat sa hangin nga nagdala sa pollen gikan sa lalaki nga cone ngadto sa babae.

q: What can a tadpole do if its tail is cut off before it fully becomes a frog?
options: It can regrow the tail.
It dies because the tail is needed to breathe underwater.
It immediately changes into a frog faster to survive without a tail.
It cannot swim and sinks to the bottom of the pond.
explanation: A tadpole can regrow its tail if it is cut off before the tadpole has fully transformed into a frog.
fact_tl: Ang butete o ulo-ulo, ang batang palaka, ay kayang patubuin muli ang buntot nito kapag naputol bago ito tuluyang maging palaka.
fact_bis: Ang butete, ang batan-ong baki, makahimo sa pagpatubo pag-usab sa iyang ikog kung kini maputol sa wala pa kini mahimong hingpit nga baki.

q: What causes the booming sound of thunder during a storm?
options: Air suddenly expands and explodes outward when heated by lightning.
Raindrops collide and burst apart high in the clouds.
Thunder is an echo of the lightning bolt bouncing off the ground.
Cold and warm air masses crash into each other above the clouds.
explanation: Lightning is hotter than the surface of the sun, so the air around it suddenly expands and bursts outward, and that explosion of air is the thunder we hear.
fact_tl: Ang kulog ay tunog lang ng kidlat. Napakainit ng kidlat mas mainit pa kaysa ibabaw ng araw kaya biglang lumolobo't sumasabog ang hangin sa paligid nito. Ang biglang pagsabog na ito ng hangin ang naririnig nating dagundong na kulog.
fact_bis: Ang dalugdog mao lang ang tingog sa kilat. Init kaayo ang kilat mas init pa kay sa ibabaw sa adlaw mao nga ang hangin sa palibot kalit nga mobukhad ug mobuto. Kana nga kalit nga pagbuto sa hangin mao ang dahunog nga atong madungog.

q: Besides chloroplasts, what other important organelle do plant cells have?
options: Mitochondria, which break down glucose to produce energy for cell activities.
Ribosomes, which capture sunlight to power photosynthesis.
Vacuoles, which store extra chlorophyll for making food.
Lysosomes, which convert carbon dioxide into oxygen for the cell.
explanation: Plant cells also contain mitochondria that carry out cellular respiration, breaking down glucose to produce ATP energy for all cell activities.
fact_tl: Bukod sa chloroplast, ang mga selula ng halaman ay mayroon ding mitochondria na gumaganap ng cellular respiration—sinisira ang glucose para makagawa ng ATP na enerhiya para sa lahat ng gawain ng selula.
fact_bis: Bukod sa chloroplast, ang mga selula sa tanum adunay usab mitochondria nga nagtuman sa cellular respiration—gibali ang glucose aron makahimo og ATP nga enerhiya para sa tanan nga gawain sa selula.

q: Why does a clownfish rarely swim far from its anemone?
options: The anemone protects it from predators, keeping it safe.
The anemone feeds it directly through its tentacles.
The anemone keeps the water around it warmer than the open ocean.
The clownfish cannot breathe properly away from the anemone.
explanation: A clownfish stays close to its anemone because the anemone provides protection from predators.
fact_tl: Bihira lumayo ang clownfish sa anemone nito dahil dito ito ligtas sa mga mandaragit sa labas.
fact_bis: Panagsa ra molayo ang clownfish sa iyang anemone kay didto siya luwas gikan sa mga manunukob sa gawas.

q: Why is it important to finish ALL of your antibiotic tablets, even if you feel better before they are gone?
options: Some bacteria may survive and come back stronger if you stop early.
Leftover tablets will expire quickly and become poisonous.
The medicine only starts working after you take the last tablet.
Doctors check the empty bottle to confirm you took every tablet.
explanation: Stopping antibiotics early can leave some bacteria alive; those survivors can return and become resistant to the medicine.

q: Why is the UV index especially high in the Philippines compared to countries farther from the equator?
options: The Philippines is near the equator, so the sun's rays hit the ground more directly.
The Philippines has very little cloud cover throughout the year.
The ozone layer is completely absent above the Philippines.
The Philippines is at high altitude, which makes UV rays stronger.
explanation: Being near the equator means the sun's rays strike the Philippines more directly, resulting in a high UV index.
fact_tl: Dahil malapit ang Pilipinas sa ekwador, mataas ang UV index dito, kaya mahalaga ang ozone at proteksyon laban sa araw.
fact_bis: Tungod kay duol ang Pilipinas sa ekwador, taas ang UV index dinhi, busa importante ang ozone ug panalipod batok sa adlaw.

q: What are the worker ants that you see carrying food and building the nest?
options: Almost all females, daughters of the queen, but they do not lay eggs.
Male ants whose job is to gather food for the queen.
Young queen ants that have not yet started laying eggs.
A mix of males and females working together equally.
explanation: Worker ants are almost all females and daughters of the queen, but their role is only to work for the colony, not to lay eggs.
fact_tl: Ang mga manggagawang langgam (worker ants) na nakikita natin ay halos lahat babae at mga anak ng reyna, pero hindi sila nangingitlog—nagtatrabaho lang sila para sa kolonya.
fact_bis: Ang mga trabahanteng hulmigas (worker ants) nga atong makita halos tanan mga babaye ug mga anak sa reyna, apan dili sila mangitlog—nagtrabaho lang sila para sa kolonya.

q: What is the single biggest source of electricity in the Philippines?
options: Coal, which provides more than half of the country's power.
Hydropower from large dams on major rivers.
Geothermal energy from volcanic areas.
Solar panels installed across the islands.
explanation: Coal is the biggest source of electricity in the Philippines, supplying more than half of the country's power.
fact_tl: Ang pinakamalaking pinagkukunan ng kuryente sa Pilipinas ay ang karbon (coal), na nagbibigay ng higit sa kalahati ng kuryente ng bansa.
fact_bis: Ang pinakadako nga tinubdan sa koryente sa Pilipinas mao ang karbon (coal), nga naghatag ug labaw sa katunga sa kuryente sa nasod.

q: What does the name of the Ati-Atihan festival mean?
options: Making like the Ati, the first natives of Aklan.
Dancing for the patron saint of the sea.
Giving thanks for the year's bountiful harvest.
Wearing costumes to honor ancient Filipino warriors.
explanation: Ati-Atihan means 'making like the Ati,' which refers to the indigenous Ati people who are the first natives of Aklan.
fact_tl: Ang 'Ati-Atihan' ay nangangahulugang paggaya sa mga Ati, ang mga unang katutubo ng Aklan.
fact_bis: Ang Ati-Atihan nagpasabot og pagsundog sa mga Ati, ang unang lumad sa Aklan.

q: What natural materials are traditional Filipino woven hand fans usually made from?
options: Dried buri palm leaves or strips of bamboo.
Woven cotton threads from the cotton plant.
Flattened sugarcane stalks sewn together.
Dried coconut husks pressed into flat sheets.
explanation: Traditional woven hand fans are made from dried buri palm leaves or strips of bamboo, both of which come from plants.
fact_tl: Ang hinabing pamaypay ay madalas gawa sa pinatuyong dahon ng buri o tinabas na kawayan, mga materyales na galing sa mga halaman.
fact_bis: Ang hinablang pamaypay kasagaran hinimo gikan sa pinauga nga dahon sa buri o gitabas nga kawayan, mga materyales nga gikan sa mga tanom.

q: Who gave vitamins their name in 1912?
options: Casimir Funk, a Polish scientist.
Louis Pasteur, a French chemist.
Gregor Mendel, an Austrian monk and scientist.
Marie Curie, a Polish-French physicist.
explanation: Casimir Funk, a Polish scientist, coined the name 'vitamine' in 1912 when he identified these essential nutrients.
fact_tl: Si Casimir Funk, isang Polish na siyentipiko, ang nagbigay ng pangalang "vitamine" noong 1912.
fact_bis: Si Casimir Funk, usa ka Polish nga siyentipiko, maoy naghatag sa ngalan nga "vitamine" niadtong 1912.

q: Where do most modern fabric dyes come from?
options: Chemicals derived from petroleum or coal tar.
Crushed minerals and colored rocks found in nature.
Extracts taken from tropical plants and flowers.
Compounds produced by bacteria in laboratory tanks.
explanation: Most modern fabric dyes are synthetic and come from chemicals derived from petroleum or coal tar, producing brighter and longer-lasting colors than natural dyes.
fact_tl: Ang karamihan sa mga modernong tina sa tela ay synthetic — gawa mula sa mga kemikal na kinuha sa petrolyo o coal tar — at nagbibigay ng mas maliwanag at matibay na mga kulay kaysa natural na dye.
fact_bis: Ang kadaghanan sa modernong mga tina sa tela synthetic — gihimo gikan sa mga kemikal gikan sa petrolyo o coal tar — ug nagprodyus og mas hayag ug mas durable nga mga kolor kaysa natural nga dye.

q: What two forms of energy make up an object's total mechanical energy?
options: Kinetic energy and potential energy.
Thermal energy and kinetic energy.
Potential energy and chemical energy.
Electrical energy and potential energy.
explanation: Mechanical energy is the sum of kinetic energy and potential energy, and without friction these two forms convert into each other while the total stays the same.
fact_tl: Ang mechanical energy ay ang kabuuang halaga ng kinetic energy at potential energy ng isang bagay — sa kawalan ng friction, ang kabuuang mechanical energy ay nananatiling pare-pareho.
fact_bis: Ang mechanical energy mao ang kabuuang kinetic energy ug potential energy sa usa ka butang — kung wala ang kiskisan, ang kinatibuk-ang mechanical energy nagpabilin nga kanunay samtang nagabalhin tali sa duha ka porma.

q: On a distance-time graph, what does a steeper line tell you about how an object is moving?
options: The object is moving faster.
The object is slowing down and about to stop.
The object is changing direction.
The object is moving at the same speed as a flatter line.
explanation: On a distance-time graph, a steeper line means the object is covering more distance in less time, so it is moving faster.
fact_tl: Sa isang distance-time graph, ang tarik ng linya ay nagsasabi kung gaano kabilis ang bagay. Ang mas tarik na linya ay nangangahulugang mas mabilis, habang ang patag na linya ay nangangahulugang nakatigil ang bagay. Kaya madali mong masasabi ang bilis sa pamamagitan lang ng pagtingin sa hugis ng linya.
fact_bis: Sa usa ka distance-time graph, ang katarik sa linya nagsulti kung unsa kapaspas ang butang nga naglihok. Ang mas tarik nga linya nagpasabot mas paspas, samtang ang patag nga linya nagpasabot nga ang butang naghunong. Busa masulti nimo ang katulin pinaagi lang sa pagtan-aw sa porma sa linya.

q: What can happen if the tail end of some earthworms is cut off?
options: The earthworm can regrow the lost tail part.
The earthworm dies immediately without its tail.
The cut-off piece becomes a brand-new earthworm.
The earthworm grows two tails to replace the lost one.
explanation: Some earthworms can regrow a lost tail end if it is cut off, which is a form of regeneration.
fact_tl: Kung maputol ang dulo ng buntot ng ilang bulate, kaya nitong tubuan muli ang nawalang bahagi.
fact_bis: Kon maputol ang tumoy sa ikog sa pipila ka bulate, makahimo kini pagtubo balik sa nawala nga bahin.

q: How does a kingfisher hunt for fish?
options: It perches quietly on a branch, watches the water, then strikes at a fish.
It dives in circles above the water to scare fish to the surface.
It wades through shallow water, grabbing fish with its feet.
It skims along the water's surface and catches fish in its net-like beak.
explanation: A kingfisher quietly perches on a branch above the water, watches for prey below, and then dives to strike at a fish.
fact_tl: Ang kingfisher ay tahimik na dumadapo sa isang sanga at nagbabantay sa tubig bago sumalakay sa isda.
fact_bis: Ang kingfisher hilom nga modapo sa sanga ug magbantay sa tubig sa dili pa moataki sa isda.

q: How does the sinking of one tectonic plate beneath another lead to a volcano?
options: The sinking plate melts in Earth's heat and forms new magma that feeds a volcano.
The collision pushes rocks so fast they catch fire and erupt as lava.
The sinking plate carries ocean water underground, which boils and erupts.
The gap left behind by the sinking plate fills with magma from space.
explanation: When one plate sinks beneath another it melts in Earth's intense heat, creating new magma that can rise and feed a volcano above.
fact_tl: Kapag ang isang plaka ay lumulubog sa ilalim ng iba, ito ay natutunaw sa init sa loob ng Daigdig at bumubuo ng bagong magma.
fact_bis: Kung ang usa ka plaka molubog ilalom sa lain, kini matunaw sa kainit sulod sa Kalibotan ug maghimo ug bag-ong magma.

q: A tick sucks blood from a dog. What type of relationship does this show?
options: Parasitism, where the tick benefits and the dog is harmed.
Mutualism, where both the tick and dog benefit.
Commensalism, where the tick benefits and the dog is unaffected.
Competition, where both the tick and the dog struggle against each other.
explanation: This is parasitism because the tick gains a meal from the dog's blood while the dog is harmed by the feeding.
fact_tl: Ang garapata na sumisipsip ng dugo ng aso ay halimbawa ng parasitismo: nakikinabang ang garapata habang nasasaktan ang aso.
fact_bis: Ang garapata nga magsupsop sa dugo sa iro usa ka panig-ingnan sa parasitismo: makabenepisyo ang garapata samtang masakitan ang iro.

q: Why is prolonged heavy rain the most dangerous time for a landslide?
options: Water soaks into the slope, making the ground heavy and weak.
Heavy rain washes away the trees that hold the soil in place.
Rain freezes at night and splits rocks apart on the hillside.
Floodwater from rivers undercuts the base of the slope.
explanation: After long rain, water builds up underground until the whole slope is soaked, making it very heavy and weak and greatly increasing landslide risk.
fact_tl: Kapag matagal na umuulan, dumarami ang tubig na naiipon sa ilalim ng lupa hanggang sa mabasa ang buong dalisdis. Ang punong-puno ng tubig na lupa ay napakabigat at mahina, kaya ito ang pinakadelikadong oras para sa landslide.
fact_bis: Kung dugay nga mag-ulan, modaghan ang tubig nga matipon sa ilalom sa yuta hangtod nga mabasa ang tibuok bakilid. Ang yuta nga puno sa tubig bug-at kaayo ug huyang, mao nga kini ang labing delikado nga panahon alang sa landslide.

q: What must you do to cassava before cooking it to make it safe to eat?
options: Peel it and soak it in water to reduce the natural poison.
Boil it with salt for at least two hours before eating.
Dry it in the sun for several days to remove the toxin.
Freeze it overnight so the cold destroys the harmful substance.
explanation: Peeling and soaking cassava in water before cooking helps reduce the toxic compounds it naturally contains.
fact_tl: Ang pagbabalat at pagbababad sa tubig ng kamoteng kahoy ay nakatutulong bawasan ang lason bago ito lutuin.
fact_bis: Ang pagpanit ug pagtuhmoy sa balanghoy sa tubig makatabang pakunhuran ang hilo sa dili pa kini lutoon.

q: Why are sea cucumbers sometimes called the 'vacuum cleaners of the reef'?
options: They swallow sand and sediment, extract organic matter, and release processed sand that enriches the reef.
They filter seawater by pumping it through their bodies to remove harmful chemicals.
They eat dead fish and coral skeletons, breaking them down into tiny pieces.
They suck up algae growing on coral to keep the reef surface clean.
explanation: Sea cucumbers earn the nickname by swallowing sand, extracting nutrients, and expelling processed sand that enriches reef sediment.
fact_tl: Ang sea cucumber ay karaniwang tinatawag na 'vacuum cleaners of the reef' — nilolunok nila ang buhangin at latak, kinukuha ang organikong bagay, at inilalabas ang nadisesyong buhangin na nagpapayaman sa lapak ng coral reef.
fact_bis: Ang sea cucumber kasagaran gitawag og 'vacuum cleaners sa reef' — gilunod nila ang balas ug latak, gikuha ang organikong bagay, ug gilabasan ang naprosesong balas nga nagpapamunot sa lapak sa coral reef.

q: What often happens when you see another person yawning?
options: You yawn too, because yawning is contagious.
You feel hungry, because yawning is a hunger signal to others.
You feel sleepy right away, because yawning releases a sleep chemical.
Nothing changes, because yawning only affects the person who is tired.
explanation: Yawning is contagious — seeing someone else yawn often makes you yawn as well.
fact_tl: Ang paghikab ay 'nakakahawa'—kapag nakita mong humikab ang iba, malamang humikab ka rin.
fact_bis: Ang paghuy-ab 'makahawa'—kung makita nimo nga mohuy-ab ang uban, lagmit mohuy-ab usab ka.

q: What does the species name 'pustulatus' in the Philippine sailfin lizard's scientific name refer to?
options: The small bumps on its skin.
Its ability to inflate a sail-like crest on its back.
The way it runs across water on its hind legs.
Its preference for living near freshwater streams.
explanation: 'Pustulatus' refers to the small bumps on the skin of Hydrosaurus pustulatus, the Philippine sailfin lizard.
fact_tl: Ang siyentipikong pangalan ng Philippine sailfin lizard ay Hydrosaurus pustulatus. Ang 'Hydrosaurus' ay nangangahulugang 'butiki ng tubig', at ang 'pustulatus' ay tumutukoy sa mga maliliit na bukol o butlig sa balat niya.
fact_bis: Ang siyentipikong ngalan sa Philippine sailfin lizard mao ang Hydrosaurus pustulatus. Ang 'Hydrosaurus' nagpasabot og 'tubig nga butiki,' ug ang 'pustulatus' nagtumong sa gagmay nga mga bukol sa iyang panit.

q: Who built the first electric motor and in what year?
options: Michael Faraday in 1821.
Thomas Edison in 1879.
Nikola Tesla in 1888.
James Watt in 1769.
explanation: Michael Faraday built the first electric motor in 1821.
fact_tl: Si Michael Faraday ang gumawa ng unang elektrikong motor noong 1821.
fact_bis: Si Michael Faraday mao ang naghimo sa unang elektrikong motor niadtong 1821.

q: What is the difference between a native species and an invasive species?
options: A native species belongs naturally in a place; an invasive species is a newcomer that upsets the natural balance.
A native species was brought by humans; an invasive species evolved in the wild on its own.
A native species is endangered; an invasive species is thriving and common.
A native species is a plant; an invasive species is always an animal.
explanation: A native species has been part of an ecosystem for a long time, while an invasive species is a newcomer that disrupts the natural balance.
fact_tl: Ang native species ay matagal nang naninirahan sa isang lugar at bahagi ng balanse ng kalikasan doon. Kaiba ito sa invasive species na bagong dating at sumisira sa balanseng iyon.
fact_bis: Ang native species dugay na nga nagpuyo sa usa ka dapit ug kabahin sa balanse sa kinaiyahan didto. Lahi kini sa invasive species nga bag-o lang miabot ug nakaguba sa maong balanse.

q: Why are weather stations placed in open fields, away from trees and buildings?
options: Trees and buildings change wind flow and heat readings, making them less accurate.
The equipment needs a lot of sunlight that is blocked by trees and buildings.
Open fields allow weather balloons to be launched without obstacles.
Rain gauges fill up faster when placed away from the shade of trees.
explanation: Obstacles like trees and buildings interfere with wind flow and heat measurements, so an open field gives the most accurate weather readings.
fact_tl: Bakit inilalagay ang weather station sa bukas na parang at malayo sa mga puno at gusali? Dahil kung may humaharang, mababago ang daloy ng hangin at ang init na nasusukat. Sa bukas na lugar, mas tama ang sukat ng totoong panahon sa paligid.
fact_bis: Ngano nga ang weather station gibutang sa bukas nga uma, layo sa mga kahoy ug building? Tungod kay kung adunay babag, mausab ang dagan sa hangin ug ang init nga masukod. Sa bukas nga dapit, mas saktong masukod ang tinuod nga panahon sa palibot.

q: How do sea snails breathe when they are underwater?
options: They breathe with gills.
They breathe through tiny pores in their shells.
They hold their breath like a diver until they surface.
They absorb oxygen directly through their soft bodies.
explanation: Sea snails use gills to breathe underwater, while some land snails have a simple lung for breathing air.
fact_tl: Ang mga suso sa dagat ay humihinga gamit ang hasang sa ilalim ng tubig, samantalang ang ilang susong panlupa ay may parang baga.
fact_bis: Ang mga kuhol sa dagat moginhawa gamit ang hasang ilalom sa tubig, samtang ang uban nga kuhol sa yuta adunay sama sa baga.

q: Does a pitcher plant still make its own food through photosynthesis, even though it also eats insects?
options: Yes, it still uses sunlight to make its own food.
No, it gets all its energy from digesting insects.
No, it absorbs nutrients from the soil instead of photosynthesizing.
Yes, but only during the dry season when insects are scarce.
explanation: Even though the pitcher plant traps and digests insects for extra nutrients, it still makes its own food using sunlight through photosynthesis.
fact_tl: Kahit kumakain ito ng insekto, gumagawa pa rin ito ng sariling pagkain gamit ang sikat ng araw.
fact_bis: Bisan mokaon kini ug insekto, naghimo gihapon kini sa kaugalingong pagkaon gamit ang adlaw.

q: What does a cactus grow in order to make seeds, even though it has sharp spines?
options: Bright flowers.
Thick green pods.
Underground bulbs.
Sticky pollen sacs on its stem.
explanation: Even a spiny cactus grows bright flowers that allow it to produce seeds for reproduction.
fact_tl: Kahit may tinik, namumukadkad pa rin ng magagandang bulaklak ang kaktus para makagawa ng buto.
fact_bis: Bisan tunokon, ang kaktus mamulak gihapon og nindot nga bulak aron makahimo og liso.

q: Can crabs see colors the same way humans do?
options: No, crabs can see only a few colors and are better at detecting light, dark, and movement.
Yes, crabs can see every color humans see and even some we cannot.
No, crabs are completely color-blind and see only in black and white.
Yes, but only red and orange colors that match the color of their shells.
explanation: Crabs can detect a few colors but are much better at distinguishing light, dark, and movement rather than seeing a full range of colors like humans.
fact_tl: Madalas itanong ng mga bata kung nakakakita ba ng kulay ang alimango. Ang sagot, kayang makakita ng ilang alimango ng kaunting kulay, pero hindi kasing dami ng kulay na nakikita natin. Mas mahusay sila sa pagtukoy ng liwanag, dilim, at galaw kaysa sa magagandang kulay.
fact_bis: Kasagaran mangutana ang mga bata kon makakita ba og kolor ang alimango. Ang tubag, makakita ang pipila ka alimango og pipila ka kolor, apan dili sama kadaghan sa atong makita. Mas maayo sila mo-ila sa kahayag, kangitngit, ug lihok kaysa makakita og nindot nga mga kolor.

q: What happens to Laguna Lake during heavy rain and typhoons that affects nearby communities?
options: The lake level rises and can flood surrounding communities.
The lake water becomes too salty and kills freshwater fish.
Strong typhoon winds push the lake water underground.
The lake drains rapidly into Manila Bay, leaving it nearly empty.
explanation: Laguna Lake serves as a natural water reservoir, and during heavy rain and typhoons its level rises, threatening to flood surrounding communities.
fact_tl: Ang Laguna Lake ay nagsisilbing natural na imbakan ng tubig para sa Metro Manila; sa panahon ng malakas na ulan at bagyo, ang antas ng lawa ay tumataas at maaaring magbaha sa mga komunidad sa tabi nito.
fact_bis: Ang Laguna Lake nagsilbi isip natural nga imbakan sa tubig alang sa Metro Manila; sa panahon sa kusog nga ulan ug bagyo, ang antas sa lanaw mosaka ug mahimong mabaha ang mga komunidad sa palibot niini.

q: How many times a day do high tide and low tide usually happen along a coastline?
options: Twice each day.
Once each day, at noon.
Four times each day, one every six hours.
Once a week, when the moon is full.
explanation: Along the coast the sea rises to high tide and drops to low tide roughly twice each day.
fact_tl: Sa baybayin, may oras na tumataas ang tubig (high tide) at may oras na bumababa (low tide), at karaniwang nangyayari ito nang dalawang beses sa isang araw.
fact_bis: Sa baybayon, adunay panahon nga mosaka ang tubig (taob) ug mokanaog (hunas), ug kasagaran kini mahitabo makaduha sa usa ka adlaw.

q: Why can a hermit crab fit so well inside a coiled shell it finds?
options: Its tail is curled and spiral-shaped so it fits perfectly inside a coiled shell.
Its body can flatten itself to squeeze into any shape of shell.
It softens the shell with a chemical so the shell reshapes to fit.
Its legs push outward to wedge itself tightly inside any shell.
explanation: A hermit crab has a naturally curled, spiral-shaped tail that fits perfectly inside a coiled shell, allowing it to use empty shells as a home.
fact_tl: Nakapulupot at hugis-ikid ang puwitan ng hermit crab para perpektong magkasya sa paikot na loob ng kabibe.
fact_bis: Ang ikog sa umang nalikaw ug daw lukut aron mohaom pag-ayo sa sulod sa lukut nga kabibi.

q: Where are the three smallest bones in the human body found?
options: In the middle ear, where they pass sound vibrations along.
In the tips of the fingers, which need precise small bones for touch.
In the inner wrist, connecting the hand to the arm.
In the bridge of the nose, supporting it from inside.
explanation: The three smallest bones in the human body are in the middle ear, and their job is to pass sound vibrations along toward the inner ear.
fact_tl: Sa gitnang tainga ay may tatlong pinakamaliliit na buto sa ating katawan na nagpapasa ng panginig ng tunog.
fact_bis: Sa tunga nga dalunggan adunay tulo ka kinagamyan nga bukog sa lawas sa tawo nga maoy mopasa sa pag-uyog sa tingog.

q: How long does it take our Sun to travel once around the center of the Milky Way?
options: Hundreds of millions of years.
About 365 days, the same as Earth's year.
About 26,000 years, the same as one precession cycle.
Roughly one million years.
explanation: Our Sun orbits the center of the Milky Way galaxy, and one complete trip takes hundreds of millions of years.
fact_tl: Ang ating Araw ay umiikot sa sentro ng Milky Way, at isang ikot ay tumatagal ng daan-daang milyong taon.
fact_bis: Ang atong Adlaw naglibot sa sentro sa Milky Way, ug ang usa ka libot mokabat ug gatusan ka milyon ka tuig.

q: Why would you feel much heavier if you could stand on Jupiter than you do on Earth?
options: Jupiter is so massive that its gravity pulls more than twice as strongly as Earth's.
Jupiter spins so fast that the centrifugal force pushes you outward and feels heavier.
Jupiter's thick atmosphere presses down on you with extra air pressure.
Jupiter is colder, and cold air is denser, making you feel heavier.
explanation: Jupiter's enormous mass creates very strong gravity, so a person standing there would feel more than twice as heavy as on Earth.
fact_tl: Napakalakas ng hila ng gravity ng Jupiter dahil napakalaki nito. Kung may matitindigan ka roon, magiging mahigit doble ang bigat mo kaysa sa Earth — parang may bumababang malaking bagay sa likod mo.
fact_bis: Kusog kaayo ang pagbira sa gravity sa Jupiter kay dako kaayo kini. Kung makatindog ka didto, mahimong sobra sa doble ang imong gibug-aton kaysa sa Earth — morag naay bug-at nga butang nga nagduot kanimo.

q: Which animal is known to have thousands of tiny teeth on its tongue?
options: A snail, which can have more than 10,000 teeth on its radula.
A shark, which regrows rows of teeth throughout its life.
A crocodile, which replaces each tooth up to 50 times.
A blue whale, which uses hundreds of baleen plates like teeth.
explanation: A snail has thousands of tiny teeth on its tongue-like radula, often more than 10,000, which it uses to scrape food.
fact_tl: Ang kuhol ay may libu-libong maliliit na ngipin sa kanilang dila (radula), kadalasang mahigit 10,000 ngipin.
fact_bis: Ang kuhol adunay liboan ka gagmay nga ngipon sa ilang dila (radula), kasagaran kapin sa 10,000 ka ngipon.

q: Why are sap-sucking insects considered pests by farmers?
options: Because they harm the crops that farmers grow.
Because they sting farm workers who try to protect the plants.
Because they eat the soil's nutrients and make the ground infertile.
Because they block sunlight from reaching the plant's leaves.
explanation: Sap-sucking insects are considered pests because they damage crops by feeding on the plant's sap, harming the plants farmers depend on.
fact_tl: Itinuturing na peste ang mga sap-sumususong insekto dahil sinisira nila ang pananim ng mga magsasaka.
fact_bis: Ang mga insekto nga nagasupsop ug duga giisip nga peste kay makadaot sa pananom sa mga mag-uuma.

q: Why does bread or grilled food turn brown when cooked with heat?
options: Heat causes a chemical change that forms new substances giving the brown color, smell, and flavor.
Heat dries out the water in food, and dry food naturally turns brown.
The sugar in food melts and caramelizes only when it is burned black.
Oxygen in the air reacts with the food surface to paint it brown.
explanation: Cooking heat causes a chemical change in food that forms new substances responsible for the brown color, appealing smell, and tasty flavor.
fact_tl: Ang init sa pagluluto ang dahilan kung bakit nag-kayumanggi ang tinapay, prito, at iniihaw na pagkain — bumubuo ng bagong sangkap na nagbibigay ng masarap na kulay, amoy, at lasa (isang chemical change).
fact_bis: Ang kainit sa pagluto maoy hinungdan nganong mahimong brown ang pan, prito, ug sinugbang pagkaon — maghimo kini og bag-ong sustansya nga maghatag sa lami nga kolor, baho, ug lami (usa ka chemical change).

q: What is an algal bloom?
options: A sudden, rapid increase in plankton when water has plenty of nutrients and warmth.
A colorful flower-like pattern that forms on the surface of still ponds.
A slow build-up of dead algae that sinks to the bottom of a lake.
A type of harmful jellyfish that multiplies quickly in warm ocean water.
explanation: An algal bloom is a sudden, rapid growth of plankton that happens when water conditions offer plenty of nutrients and warmth.
fact_tl: Ang algal bloom ay ang mabilis na pagdami ng plankton kapag sobra ang sustansya at init sa tubig.
fact_bis: Ang algal bloom mao ang kalit nga pagdaghan sa plankton kung daghan ang sustansya ug init sa tubig.

q: How do animals that give live birth usually differ from egg-layers in the number of young they have and how they care for them?
options: They have fewer babies but take better care of them.
They have more babies and spend more time protecting each one.
They have fewer babies and leave them to survive on their own.
They have the same number of young but care for them for a shorter time.
explanation: Animals that give live birth typically produce fewer offspring but invest more effort in caring for each one.
fact_tl: Ang mga hayop na nanganganak ng buhay na anak ay kadalasang kaunti lang ang anak ngunit mas inaalagaan ito.
fact_bis: Ang mga hayop nga nanganak ug buhi nga anak kasagaran pipila lang ka anak apan mas giatiman kini.

q: Why does the air at a Philippine beach feel cool on a hot afternoon even when the sun is still strong?
options: A sea breeze blows in from the cooler water over the land.
The sand absorbs heat so quickly that it pulls warmth away from the air.
Rain clouds form above the coast each afternoon and block the sun.
Ocean water evaporates and causes the surrounding air to freeze slightly.
explanation: Because the Philippines is surrounded by sea, sea breezes are common — cool air from the water flows inland on hot afternoons, making beach areas feel cooler.
fact_tl: Dahil isang kapuluan ang Pilipinas, halos lahat ng lugar ay malapit sa dagat, kaya karaniwan ang sea breeze. Kaya nga sa hapon sa mga beach gaya ng sa Batangas o Cebu, malamig-lamig ang hangin kahit mainit ang araw — dahil iyon sa sea breeze.
fact_bis: Tungod kay ang Pilipinas usa ka pundok sa mga isla, halos tanang lugar duol sa dagat, mao nga komon ang sea breeze. Mao nga sa hapon sa mga baybayon sama sa Batangas o Cebu, presko ang hangin bisan init ang adlaw — kana ang sea breeze.

q: Which planet takes the longest to orbit the Sun?
options: Neptune, which takes about 165 Earth years to complete one orbit.
Saturn, which takes about 29 Earth years to complete one orbit.
Uranus, which takes about 84 Earth years to complete one orbit.
Jupiter, which takes about 12 Earth years to complete one orbit.
explanation: Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun and has the longest year, taking about 165 Earth years to complete one orbit.
fact_tl: Ang Neptune ang planetang may pinakamahabang taon—iniikot nito ang Araw sa halos 165 taon ng Earth.
fact_bis: Ang Neptune mao ang planeta nga adunay pinakataas nga tuig—molibot kini sa Adlaw sulod sa mga 165 ka tuig sa Yuta.

q: Which lake holds the most fresh water of any lake in the world?
options: Lake Baikal in Russia.
Lake Superior in North America.
Lake Victoria in Africa.
Lake Titicaca in South America.
explanation: Lake Baikal holds more fresh water than any other lake in the world.
fact_tl: Ang Lake Baikal ang may pinakamaraming tabang na tubig sa lahat ng lawa sa mundo.
fact_bis: Ang Lake Baikal mao ang adunay pinakadaghang tab-ang nga tubig sa tanang lanaw sa kalibutan.

q: Which metal conducts electricity the best?
options: Silver, followed by copper, then gold and aluminum.
Gold, because it never rusts and stays a pure conductor.
Copper, because it is the metal most commonly used in wires.
Aluminum, because it is lightweight and conducts well.
explanation: Silver is the best conductor of electricity among metals, followed by copper, gold, and aluminum — not all metals conduct equally well.
fact_tl: Hindi pare-pareho ang lahat ng metal sa kahusayan magdala ng kuryente. Ang pilak ang pinakamagaling, sumunod ang tanso, tapos ang ginto at aluminum. Mas kaunti ang malayang electron o mas magulo ang loob ng ibang metal kaya bahagyang mas mabagal ang daloy ng kuryente sa mga ito.
fact_bis: Dili managsama ang tanan nga metal sa kaayo sa pagdala sa kuryente. Ang pilak ang labing maayo, sunod ang tumbaga, dayon ang bulawan ug aluminum. Ang ubang metal adunay gamay nga gawasnon nga electron o mas magubot ang sulod, mao nga gamay nga mas hinay ang dagan sa kuryente niini.

q: What happens to the solid bits in a suspension if you leave it standing still for a while?
options: They slowly settle to the bottom because they are not truly dissolved.
They dissolve completely into the liquid over time.
They rise to the top and form a solid layer.
They stay evenly spread throughout the liquid forever.
explanation: In a suspension, solid particles float in the liquid at first but slowly settle to the bottom over time because they are not truly dissolved.
fact_tl: Ang suspension ay timpla kung saan ang maliliit na solidong piraso ay lumulutang muna sa likido pero dahan-dahang lumulubog kapag iniwan — gaya ng putik sa tubig. Hindi ito tunay na natunaw.
fact_bis: Ang suspension usa ka sagol diin ang gagmayng solidong piraso molutaw una sa likido apan hinay-hinayng molubog kon pasagdan — sama sa lapok sa tubig. Dili kini tinuod nga natunaw.

q: How does an anglerfish use its glowing lure to catch prey?
options: It attracts small fish with the glowing esca, then gulps them down when they swim close.
It shines the light to blind nearby fish so they cannot swim away.
It uses the glow to call other anglerfish to help surround their prey.
It flashes the light rapidly to confuse fish so they swim into rocks.
explanation: The anglerfish's glowing esca looks like tasty bait; when curious prey swim close to inspect it, the anglerfish suddenly swallows them with its huge mouth.
fact_tl: Paano humuhuli ang anglerfish? Inaakit nito ang maliliit na isda gamit ang nagliliwanag na esca na para bang masarap na paon. Kapag lumapit na ang biktima para tingnan ang ilaw, biglang nilalamon ito ng anglerfish sa malaki nitong bibig.
fact_bis: Unsaon pagdakop sa anglerfish? Modani kini sa gagmay nga isda gamit ang nagsiga nga esca nga morag lami nga paon. Kung moduol na ang biktima aron tan-awon ang kahayag, kalit nga molamoy niini ang anglerfish sa iyang dako nga baba.

q: In what year did Yuri Gagarin become the first human to fly into space?
explanation: Yuri Gagarin flew into space on April 12, 1961, making him the first human to orbit the Earth.
fact_tl: Si Yuri Gagarin ay umakyat sa kalawakan noong Abril 12, 1961.
fact_bis: Si Yuri Gagarin misaka sa kawanangan niadtong Abril 12, 1961.

q: What should you do right away if an animal bites you?
options: Tell a parent or adult immediately so you can get treatment quickly.
Wash the bite with water and then wait a few days to see if it gets worse.
Put a bandage on the bite and tell your teacher the next day at school.
Rub soil on the bite to clean it and stop the bleeding on your own.
explanation: If an animal bites you, you must tell a parent or adult right away so that proper treatment, including possible rabies prevention, can begin quickly.
fact_tl: Kapag nakagat ka ng hayop, agad sabihin sa magulang o nakatatandang tao para makapagpagamot ka kaagad.
fact_bis: Kon mapaakan ka sa hayop, sultihi dayon ang ginikanan o hamtong nga tawo aron makapatambal ka dayon.

q: If you could place Mount Everest (8,849 meters tall) inside the Mariana Trench, what would happen?
options: It would stick out above the water's surface
The mountain top would reach exactly the rim of the trench
The entire mountain would be submerged with room to spare
The mountain would be too wide to fit inside the trench
explanation: The Mariana Trench is deeper than Mount Everest is tall, so the whole of Everest would sink into it and be completely covered.
fact_tl: Mas malalim ang Mariana Trench kaysa sa taas ng Mount Everest na 8,849 metro — lulubog pa ang buong Everest doon.
fact_bis: Mas lawom ang Mariana Trench kaysa sa katas-on sa Mount Everest nga 8,849 metros — malubong pa ang tibuok Everest didto.

q: A bird builds its nest on a tree branch. The bird gets a safe home, and the tree is not helped or harmed. What kind of relationship is this?
options: Mutualism
Commensalism
Parasitism
Predation
explanation: When only one organism benefits and the other is neither helped nor harmed, the relationship is called commensalism.
fact_tl: Kapag nagpupugad ang isang ibon sa sanga ng puno, nakakakuha ito ng ligtas na tirahan, samantalang ang puno naman ay hindi naman natutulungan o nasasaktan—commensalism ito.
fact_bis: Kung mosalag ang langgam sa sanga sa kahoy, makakuha kini og luwas nga puy-anan, samtang ang kahoy dili matabangan o madaot—commensalism kini.

q: How does your sense of touch help protect your body?
options: It lets you see danger coming from far away
It allows you to feel sharp, hot, or dangerous things so you can avoid harm
It helps your heart pump blood faster when you are hurt
It sends messages to your ears so you can hear pain
explanation: The sense of touch protects us by letting us feel sharp, hot, or dangerous things before they cause serious injury.
fact_tl: Tinutulungan tayo ng pandamang hipo na maingatan ang sarili dahil nararamdaman natin ang matalim, mainit, o mapanganib na bagay.
fact_bis: Ang paghikap motabang kanato sa pagbantay sa atong kaugalingon kay mabati nato ang hait, init, o makuyaw nga butang.

q: Why are mangroves sometimes called 'nurseries' for reef fish like grouper and snapper?
options: They provide the same food sources as coral reefs
Young fish hide and grow in mangroves before moving to coral reefs as adults
Mangroves filter the water so that it is clean enough for adult fish
Adult reef fish lay their eggs only in mangrove leaves
explanation: Young reef fish like grouper and snapper grow up in mangroves before moving to coral reefs as adults, making mangroves essential fish nurseries.
fact_tl: Maraming mahahalagang isda sa reef tulad ng lapu-lapu (grouper) at maya-maya (snapper) ay gugugol ng kanilang kabataan sa mga bakawan bago lumipat sa coral reef bilang mga matatanda — ginagawa ang bakawan bilang mahalagang nursery para sa mga reef fish.
fact_bis: Daghang mahalagang isda sa reef sama sa lapu-lapu ug maya-maya mogugol sa ilang kabatan-onan sa mga bakawan sa dili pa mobalhin sa mga coral reef isip mga hamtong — nagpahimo sa bakawan isip mahinungdanon nga nursery alang sa mga reef fish.

q: Why is the water inside a mangrove forest a good place for tiny, weak-swimming fish?
options: Mangrove roots release chemicals that feed the baby fish
Mangrove trees block strong waves, making the water calm and gentle
The water is saltier inside mangroves, which helps small fish breathe
Mangroves heat the water, so the baby fish grow faster
explanation: Mangrove trees block strong waves and currents, keeping the water calm and gentle — perfect for tiny fish that are still weak swimmers.
fact_tl: Hinaharang ng mga puno ng bakawan ang malalakas na alon at agos ng tubig. Kaya naman tahimik at mahina ang tubig sa loob, na siyang tamang lugar para sa maliliit na isda na mahina pa lumangoy.
fact_bis: Ang mga kahoy sa bakawan nagababag sa kusog nga balud ug sulog sa tubig. Mao nga kalmado ug hinay ang tubig sa sulod, nga maoy hustong dapit alang sa gagmayng isda nga huyang pa molangoy.

q: A movable pulley makes lifting easier, but what is the trade-off you must accept?
options: You must pull the rope in the opposite direction of the load
You must pull a longer length of rope to raise the load
The pulley only works for very heavy objects
You need two people to operate a movable pulley
explanation: A movable pulley reduces the force needed to lift, but in exchange you must pull a longer length of rope.
fact_tl: Kapalit ng mas magaang paghila sa natitinag na kalo, kailangan mong humila ng mas mahabang lubid.
fact_bis: Baylo sa mas sayon nga pagbira, ang mabalhin nga polea naghimo nimo nga mobira ug mas taas nga pisi.

q: Some people think ordinary snails bite people or suck blood. What does a snail's radula actually do?
options: It bites and pierces skin to drink blood
It scrapes and rasps plant material for eating
It produces venom that paralyzes insects
It digs holes in the ground for the snail to hide
explanation: A snail's radula is designed only for scraping plants — ordinary snails do not bite or suck blood.
fact_tl: Hindi totoo na nangangagat o sumisipsip ng dugo ang ordinaryong kuhol. Ang radula nila ay pang-kayod lang ng halaman, hindi pangkagat sa tao.
fact_bis: Dili tinuod nga ang ordinaryong kuhol mopaak o mosuyop og dugo. Ang ilang radula para lang sa pagkiskis sa tanom, dili para mopaak og tawo.

q: Why do crabs usually walk sideways instead of forward?
options: Their eyes are only on one side of their body
Their legs are too long to walk straight ahead
The way their leg joints bend makes sideways movement natural
Crabs are afraid of what is directly in front of them
explanation: Crabs walk sideways because of the way their leg joints are structured — the joint design makes sideways movement the most natural direction.
fact_tl: Karaniwang naglalakad nang patagilid ang alimango dahil ganoon ang pagkakabuko ng mga binti nito.
fact_bis: Ang alimango kasagaran naglakaw nga patagilid tungod sa pagkaliko sa mga buko-buko sa iyang tiil.

q: How high do weather balloons like those released by PAGASA go to collect data?
options: They stay in the troposphere, just a few kilometers up
They rise into the stratosphere, far above everyday weather
They orbit the Earth like satellites, circling the globe
They float just above the clouds and return within minutes
explanation: Weather balloons rise into the stratosphere to measure temperature and air conditions high above the surface.
fact_tl: Ang mga weather balloon ng PAGASA ay umaakyat hanggang stratosphere upang sukatin ang temperatura at hangin sa itaas.
fact_bis: Ang mga weather balloon, sama sa gigamit sa PAGASA, mosaka hangtod sa stratosphere aron sukdon ang temperatura ug hangin sa ibabaw.

q: Why do termites build thin tubes made of mud to travel through?
options: The mud tubes hide their food supply from ants
The mud tubes keep their bodies from drying out as they move
The mud tubes amplify vibrations so termites can communicate
The mud tubes collect rainwater for the termite colony
explanation: Termites build mud tubes so they can travel safely without their bodies drying out in the open air.
fact_tl: Gumagawa ang anay ng manipis na tubo ng putik para makapaglakbay nang ligtas at hindi matuyo ang katawan nila.
fact_bis: Ang anay maghimo ug nipis nga tubo sa lapok aron makalakaw nga luwas ug dili mauga ang ilang lawas.

q: How does a solar panel actually produce electricity?
options: The panel heats up and that heat is converted into electric current
Light hits the silicon material and knocks electrons loose, creating a flow of electricity
The panel uses mirrors to focus sunlight onto a wire, which then glows
Sunlight causes water inside the panel to spin a small turbine
explanation: A solar panel produces electricity when light hits silicon inside it, knocking electrons loose — that flow of electrons is the electric current.
fact_tl: Hindi iniinit ng solar panel ang araw para gumawa ng kuryente — sa halip, kapag tinatamaan ng liwanag ang espesyal na materyales (silicon) sa loob nito, natutulak ang maliliit na partikulo (electrons) at iyon ang dumadaloy bilang kuryente.
fact_bis: Ang solar panel dili maghimo ug kuryente pinaagi sa kainit — hinuon, kung ang kahayag motama sa espesyal nga materyales (silicon) sa sulod niini, ang gagmay nga partikulo (electrons) matuklod, ug kana nga pag-agos mao ang kuryente.

q: What causes color blindness in a person's eyes?
options: The lens of the eye becomes cloudy and blocks certain colors
Some cones in the retina are missing or do not work correctly
The optic nerve sends color signals too slowly to the brain
The pupil is too large and lets in too much light, washing out colors
explanation: Color blindness happens when some cones in the retina are missing or do not function properly, making it hard to distinguish certain colors like red and green.
fact_tl: Ang color blindness ay nangyayari kapag ang ilan sa mga cones sa retina ay kulang o hindi gumagana nang tama — ang pinakakaraniwan ay ang hindi makilala ng tao ang pula at berde.
fact_bis: Ang color blindness mahitabo kung ang pipila ka cones sa retina kulang o dili maayong naglihok — ang labing sagad nga matang mao ang kahirapan sa pagkilala sa pula ug berde.

q: Which of the following is an example of a lever?
options: A screw used to hold two pieces of wood together
A seesaw on a playground
A wheel on a bicycle
A nail hammered into a wall
explanation: A seesaw is a lever — it is a bar that turns on a fixed point to lift or move something, just like scissors, a bottle opener, or a spoon.
fact_tl: Maraming lever sa paligid natin araw-araw! Ang gunting, seesaw, pambukas ng bote, at maging ang kutsara na ginagamit mong pang-sandok ay mga lever. Kapag nakakita ka ng baras na umiikot sa isang punto para magbuhat o gumalaw, malamang lever iyon.
fact_bis: Daghan ang lever sa atong palibot kada adlaw! Ang gunting, seesaw, pang-abli sa botelya, ug bisan ang kutsara nga imong gigamit pangkalos mga lever. Kon makakita ka ug bara nga magtuyok sa usa ka punto aron mag-alsa o maglihok, lagmit lever kana.

q: Why does ice float on liquid water instead of sinking?
options: Ice is warmer than liquid water so it rises to the surface
Water expands when it freezes, making ice less dense than liquid water
Ice contains trapped air bubbles that push it upward
Liquid water is lighter than ice and sinks below it
explanation: Unlike most substances, water expands when it freezes, which makes ice less dense than liquid water — so ice floats.
fact_tl: Kakaiba ang tubig: kapag nagyeyelo, ito ay lumalawak sa halip na umurong, kaya lumulutang ang yelo.
fact_bis: Lahi ang tubig: kung kini moyelo, kini molapad imbis nga mokunhod, mao nga molutaw ang yelo.

q: In a hornbill's nest, the female is sealed inside with her chicks. What serious danger does this create?
options: The female and chicks can overheat because the nest has no airflow
If the male dies, the female and chicks may starve since she depends on him for food
Predators can easily dig through the sealed nest to reach the chicks
The sealed nest prevents the chicks from learning to fly
explanation: The sealed female hornbill depends entirely on the male to bring food, so if the male dies, both she and her chicks can starve.
fact_tl: Dahil nakasalalay ang nakakulong na babae sa lalaki para sa pagkain, kapag namatay ang lalaki ay maaaring magutom ang babae at mga inakay.
fact_bis: Tungod kay ang nakulong nga baye nagsalig sa laki alang sa pagkaon, kung mamatay ang laki mahimong magutom ang baye ug mga piso.

q: What does a free-body diagram show?
options: The path an object takes as it moves through space
All the forces acting on an object, shown as arrows indicating direction and size
The internal parts and structure of a machine
A timeline of how fast an object speeds up or slows down
explanation: A free-body diagram is a drawing that uses arrows to show all the forces acting on an object, including their direction and size.
fact_tl: Ang free-body diagram ay isang guhit na nagpapakita ng lahat ng puwersang kumikilos sa isang bagay, gamit ang mga panang nagtuturo sa direksyon at lakas ng bawat puwersa.
fact_bis: Ang free-body diagram usa ka drowing nga nagpakita sa tanang kusog nga naglihok sa usa ka butang, ginamit ang mga pana nga nagtudlo sa direksyon ug kakusog sa matag puwersa.

q: You have two balls that are exactly the same size. One floats in water and the other sinks. What explains this difference?
options: The ball that floats must be hollow inside, while the other is completely solid
The lighter ball floats and the heavier ball sinks, even though they are the same size
The ball made of rubber always floats regardless of its weight
The ball placed in the water first will always float on top
explanation: Two objects of the same size can behave differently in water — the lighter one floats and the heavier one sinks because of differences in their density.
fact_tl: Dalawang bagay na magkasing-laki ay maaaring magkaiba ang kapalaran: lumulutang ang mas magaan, lumulubog ang mas mabigat.
fact_bis: Duha ka butang nga parehas og gidak-on mahimong magkalahi: ang mas gaan molutaw, ang mas bug-at molubog.

q: Inside a cave, which formation grows DOWN from the ceiling?
options: A stalagmite
A stalactite
A geode
A mineral vein
explanation: Stalactites grow down from the ceiling of a cave as mineral-filled water drips over many years, while stalagmites grow up from the floor.
fact_tl: Sa loob ng kuweba, ang stalactite ay tumutubong pababa mula sa kisame, habang ang stalagmite ay tumutubong pataas mula sa sahig dahil sa tumutulong tubig na may mineral.
fact_bis: Sulod sa langob, ang stalactite motubo paubos gikan sa kisame, samtang ang stalagmite motubo pataas gikan sa salog tungod sa nagtulo nga tubig nga adunay mineral.

q: How does a belt or chain help transfer movement between two wheels that are far apart?
options: The belt stretches to push one wheel directly against the other
It connects the two wheels so that turning one wheel also turns the other
The chain stores energy from one wheel and releases it to the other later
A belt makes both wheels spin in the same direction at the same speed
explanation: A belt or chain connects two far-apart wheels and transfers the turning motion from one to the other.
fact_tl: Ang belt o kadena ay maaaring magkonekta ng dalawang gulong o pulley na magkalayo, para mailipat ang pag-ikot mula sa isa papunta sa kabila.
fact_bis: Ang belt o kadena makakonekta sa duha ka gulong o pulley nga magkalayo, aron mabalhin ang pagtuyok gikan sa usa ngadto sa pikas.

q: A scientist takes a cell from your skin and another from your bone. How do their DNA copies compare?
options: Skin cells have more DNA because they divide faster than bone cells
Both cells carry the exact same copy of your DNA double helix
Bone cells have simpler DNA because they do not need to do as much work
Each cell type has a different DNA copy suited to its special job
explanation: Almost every cell in your body carries the exact same copy of your DNA double helix — from skin to bone, the instructions are identical.
fact_tl: Halos lahat ng selula sa iyong katawan, mula balat hanggang buto, ay may eksaktong parehong kopya ng iyong DNA double helix. Kaya kahit isang ugat ng buhok mo, dala na nito ang buong instruksyon ng iyong katawan.
fact_bis: Halos tanan nga selula sa imong lawas, gikan sa panit hangtod sa bukog, adunay eksakto nga parehas nga kopya sa imong DNA double helix. Mao nga bisan usa lang ka gamot sa imong buhok, dala na niini ang tibuok instruksyon sa imong lawas.

q: What is the difference between a cocoon and a chrysalis?
options: A cocoon is made by a butterfly and a chrysalis is made by a moth
A cocoon is silk spun by a moth caterpillar, while a chrysalis is the hard shell formed by a butterfly pupa
A cocoon is only found underground, while a chrysalis hangs from branches
A cocoon holds eggs, while a chrysalis protects a fully grown insect
explanation: Moths spin silk cocoons around themselves, while butterflies form a hard chrysalis with no silk — both are the pupa stage, but they are made differently.
fact_tl: Magkaiba ang kokon at chrysalis kahit pareho silang pupa. Ang kokon ay gawa sa hibla ng sutla na iniikot ng higad ng gamugamo (moth) sa paligid ng sarili. Ang chrysalis naman ay ang matigas na balot ng pupa ng paru-paro, na walang sutla. Kaya may kokon ang gamugamo, pero chrysalis ang paru-paro.
fact_bis: Lahi ang kokon ug chrysalis bisan pareho silang pupa. Ang kokon hinimo sa mga hilo sa sutla nga giliki sa ulod sa anunugba palibot sa kaugalingon. Ang chrysalis mao ang gahi nga sapaw sa pupa sa alibangbang, nga walay sutla. Mao nga ang anunugba mohimo og kokon, apan ang alibangbang mohimo og chrysalis.

q: What happens when you wash clothes in hard water?
options: The clothes become softer because minerals act like fabric softener
The clothes can feel stiff or rough because of leftover soap and minerals
Hard water removes stains better because it is more acidic
The clothes shrink faster in hard water than in regular water
explanation: In hard water, soap and minerals are left behind on clothes after washing, making them feel stiff or rough.
fact_tl: Sa matigas na tubig, mas mahirap labhan ang damit at minsan ay nagiging matigas o magaspang ito dahil sa natitirang sabon at mineral.
fact_bis: Sa gahi nga tubig, mas lisod labhan ang sinina ug usahay mahimo kining gahi o magaspang tungod sa nabilin nga sabon ug mineral.

q: How does regular exercise like running and playing help your body?
options: It stops you from needing sleep because you are already tired
It strengthens your muscles and heart, keeping you healthy
It shrinks your bones so that you become more flexible
It replaces the need to eat because exercise produces energy
explanation: Regular exercise like running and playing strengthens our muscles and heart, which keeps us healthy.
fact_tl: Ang regular na ehersisyo tulad ng pagtakbo at paglalaro ay nagpapalakas ng ating mga kalamnan at puso, kaya tayo nagiging malusog.
fact_bis: Ang regular nga ehersisyo sama sa pagdagan ug pagdula nagpalig-on sa atong mga kaunoran ug kasingkasing, busa kita mahimong himsog.

q: Why is a pufferfish NOT eaten as an everyday food fish like tilapia or milkfish?
options: Pufferfish have too many small bones, making them hard to cook
Pufferfish carry poison that makes them unsafe to eat
Pufferfish taste too bitter even when cooked properly
Pufferfish are too small to provide a good meal
explanation: Unlike safe everyday fish such as tilapia or milkfish, the pufferfish carries poison that makes it unsafe to eat.
fact_tl: Hindi tulad ng tilapia o bangus na ligtas kainin, ang butete ay may lason kaya hindi ito karaniwang ulam.
fact_bis: Dili sama sa tilapia o bangus nga luwas kan-on, ang butete adunay hilo busa dili kini ordinaryong sud-an.

q: Why can a broken rib or skull be more dangerous than breaking a bone in your finger?
options: Ribs and the skull take much longer to heal because they are bigger bones
The rib and skull protect important organs, so breaking them can put those organs at risk
Broken ribs and skulls are always more painful than other broken bones
The finger has no important blood vessels, so breaking it is always minor
explanation: Bones protect important organs — a broken rib or skull is especially dangerous because the organs those bones shield can also be injured.
fact_tl: Pinoprotektahan ng buto ang mahahalagang bahagi ng katawan, kaya ang baling tadyang o bungo ay maaaring delikado.
fact_bis: Ang bukog manalipod sa importante nga bahin sa lawas, mao nga ang bali nga gusok o bagolbagol mahimong delikado.

q: A forest animal has not been hunted at all, but its population is disappearing. What is the most likely reason?
options: The animal decided to migrate permanently to another country
Its forest habitat was destroyed, removing its home and food sources
Other animals in the forest started competing for the same water
Scientists accidentally released a disease while studying the animal
explanation: Species can vanish even without direct hunting when their habitat is destroyed — losing their home removes shelter, food, and the whole web of life they depend on.
fact_tl: Hindi lang sa pangangaso nawawala ang species. Madalas, dahil ito sa pagkasira ng kanilang tirahan, tulad ng pagputol ng gubat o pagdumi sa ilog. Kahit hindi direktang pinapatay, kapag nasira ang tahanan nila, mawawala sila at maaapektuhan ang buong web.
fact_bis: Dili lang sa pagpangayam mawala ang species. Kasagaran, tungod sa pagkaguba sa ilang puy-anan, sama sa pagputol sa kalasangan o paghugaw sa suba. Bisan dili direktang patyon, kon maguba ang ilang puy-anan mawala sila ug maapektohan ang tibuok web.

q: What do the small lines on a thermometer represent?
options: The number of minutes the thermometer has been in use
Each degree of temperature
The different materials the thermometer is made of
The maximum and minimum temperatures the thermometer can measure
explanation: The small lines on a thermometer each stand for one degree of temperature, helping you read the exact temperature.
fact_tl: Ang maliliit na guhit sa termometro ay tumutukoy sa bawat degree ng temperatura.
fact_bis: Ang gagmay nga mga linya sa termometro nagkahulogan sa matag degree sa temperatura.

q: Why does one Philippine Eagle family need a very large area of forest to survive?
options: Philippine Eagles are social birds that need space to gather in large flocks
As a top predator at the peak of the food pyramid, there are very few of them and each family needs a big territory
Philippine Eagles build enormous nests that require many trees to support
Eagles avoid other animals, so they need large forests to stay hidden
explanation: As a top predator, the Philippine Eagle is very few in number and one family needs a large forest territory to find enough food.
fact_tl: Ang Agila ng Pilipinas ay nasa tuktok ng pyramid kaya napakakaunti nito, at maraming gubat ang kailangan para mabuhay ang isang pamilya nito.
fact_bis: Ang Agila sa Pilipinas anaa sa tumoy sa pyramid mao nga diyutay ra kaayo, ug dakong lasang ang gikinahanglan aron mabuhi ang usa ka pamilya niini.

q: Why do mountain roads in the Philippines often zigzag back and forth instead of going straight up?
options: Zigzag roads are easier for road workers to build on rocky ground
Zigzagging reduces the steepness of the climb, making it easier for vehicles to go up
Straight roads on mountains are illegal because they cause landslides
Zigzag roads allow two vehicles to pass each other going in opposite directions
explanation: Mountain roads zigzag to reduce the steepness — this is the inclined-plane principle, making it easier for vehicles to climb.
fact_tl: Ang mga daan sa bundok sa Pilipinas ay madalas na kumikiling ng zigzag para mabawasan ang anggulo ng daan at mapigilan ang sasakyan mula sa mahirap na pag-akyat.
fact_bis: Ang mga daan sa bukid sa Pilipinas kasagaran nagzigzag aron mabawasan ang katarong sa daan, mas sayon ang pag-akyat sa mga sasakyan.

q: Why does so much sugarcane grow on the island of Negros?
options: Negros has the flattest land in the Philippines, which suits all crops
The climate in Negros is hot with plenty of rain and good soil — perfect for sugarcane
The government built special sugarcane factories there first
Negros is closest to the ocean, so sugarcane gets extra moisture from sea spray
explanation: Sugarcane loves hot, wet places, and Negros has exactly that — a hot climate with plenty of rain and good soil for crops.
fact_tl: Bakit sa Negros maraming tubo? Mainit at maraming ulan ang klima roon, at maganda ang lupa para sa pananim. Gusto ng tubo ang mainit at basang lugar, kaya mabilis itong lumaki sa isla ng Negros.
fact_bis: Nganong daghan ang tubo sa Negros? Init ug daghan ang ulan ang klima didto, ug maayo ang yuta para sa tanom. Gusto sa tubo ang init ug basa nga dapit, mao nga paspas kini motubo sa isla sa Negros.

q: Where does the buzzing sound of a bee come from?
options: The bee rubbing its legs together very quickly
The bee's wings beating very fast
The bee pushing air out of a special hole in its body
The bee's stinger vibrating when it flies
explanation: The buzzing sound you hear from a bee is caused by its wings beating very rapidly as it flies.
fact_tl: Ang huni ng bubuyog ay nanggagaling sa napakabilis na pagpapagaspas ng kanyang mga pakpak.
fact_bis: Ang huni sa putyukan naggikan sa kusog kaayo nga pagkapakapa sa iyang mga pako.

q: Aquamarine is a blue gemstone. What mineral is it made of?
options: Quartz, the same mineral that makes up sand
Beryl, the same mineral as emerald but a different color
Corundum, the same mineral as ruby and sapphire
Feldspar, a very common mineral found in granite
explanation: Aquamarine is a variety of beryl — the same mineral as emerald — but it is blue or blue-green in color.
fact_tl: Ang aquamarine ay beryl din, kapareho ng emerald, pero asul o bughaw-berde ang kulay.
fact_bis: Ang aquamarine beryl usab, parehas sa emerald, apan asul o asul-berde ang kolor.

q: Giant clams were nearly gone from many Philippine reefs. How have scientists helped bring them back?
options: They passed laws making it illegal to visit any reef where giant clams once lived
SEAFDEC and BFAR bred thousands of giant clams in laboratories and replanted them on reefs
Scientists trained local fishermen to carry giant clams on their boats
Giant clams were imported from other countries to replace the lost ones
explanation: After giant clams were heavily over-harvested, SEAFDEC and BFAR programs bred thousands in laboratories and replanted them on Philippine reefs.
