explanation: Trilobite fossils are common because their hard armor-like shell preserved well and easily turned to stone after death.
fact_tl: Madalas matagpuan ang fossil ng trilobite dahil mayroon silang matigas na balat na parang baluti na madaling maging bato matapos silang mamatay.
fact_bis: Kasagarang makit-an ang fossil sa trilobite tungod kay sila adunay gahi nga panit nga morag baluti nga dali rang nahimong bato human sila mamatay.

q: Why are radio waves from cellphones considered safe for the body, unlike X-rays?
options: Radio waves are blocked by the skull before they can reach brain tissue
Radio waves are non-ionizing and too low in energy to damage cells or DNA
Radio waves only travel along the outside of the body and never enter it
Radio waves cancel each other out when they meet inside living tissue
explanation: Radio waves are non-ionizing and very low in energy, so they cannot damage cells or DNA the way X-rays or gamma rays can.
fact_tl: Marami ang natatakot na nakakasama ang radio waves mula sa cellphone, pero ang mga ito ay non-ionizing at napakababa ng enerhiya — hindi kayang sirain ang mga cell o DNA tulad ng X-ray o gamma. Ligtas silang naglalakbay palagi sa paligid natin.
fact_bis: Daghang tawo ang nahadlok nga makadaot ang radio waves gikan sa cellphone, apan kini non-ionizing ug ubos kaayo og enerhiya — dili kini makaguba sa selula o DNA sama sa X-ray o gamma. Luwas silang naglibot kanato sa kanunay.

q: What type of volcano is Taal, and what makes it unusual?
options: A shield volcano, with wide flat slopes built from many lava flows
A stratovolcano, with steep sides and alternating lava and ash layers
A complex volcano, made of many vents sitting inside a large lake
A cinder cone, formed by a single explosive eruption of loose rock
explanation: Taal Volcano is a complex volcano, made of many vents sitting inside a large lake.
fact_tl: Ang Bulkang Taal ay isang complex volcano, isang pangkat ng maraming bunganga sa loob ng isang malaking lawa.
fact_bis: Ang Bulkang Taal usa ka complex volcano, daghan nga mga buho nga naa sulod sa usa ka dako nga lanaw.

q: Why is gold used in small electronics parts, in addition to jewelry and coins?
options: It is very light, making devices easier to carry
It can store electricity better than any other metal
It does not rust, so it stays reliable inside electronic devices
It melts at a very low temperature, making it easy to shape
explanation: Gold is used in jewelry, coins, and electronics because it does not rust, keeping connections reliable.
fact_tl: Ang gold (ginto) ay ginagamit sa alahas, barya at salapi, at sa maliliit na bahagi ng electronics dahil hindi ito kinakalawang.
fact_bis: Ang gold (bulawan) gamiton sa alahas, sensilyo ug salapi, ug sa gagmay nga parte sa electronics tungod kay dili kini magkalawang.

q: How do baby house lizards begin their lives?
options: They are born live, like puppies, directly from the mother
They hatch from eggs, inside which they grew before hatching
They start as tiny larvae that live in water before changing form
They grow inside a pouch on the mother's belly until fully formed
explanation: House lizards lay eggs, and the baby lizards grow inside the eggs before they hatch.
fact_tl: Ang butiki ay nangingitlog, at sa loob ng itlog lumalaki ang maliliit na butiki bago mapisa.
fact_bis: Ang tiki mangitlog, ug sulod sa itlog motubo ang gagmayng tiki una kini mapisa.

q: What is the hard helmet-like crest on top of a cassowary's head called?
options: A crown
A comb
A casque
A wattle
explanation: The cassowary has a hard helmet-like crest on its head called a casque.
fact_tl: Ang cassowary ay may matigas na parang helmet sa ulo na tinatawag na casque.
fact_bis: Ang cassowary adunay gahi nga sama sa helmet sa ulo nga gitawag og casque.

q: Besides chewing it, how was the betel leaf traditionally used in the Philippines?
options: As a natural dye for weaving colorful cloth
As a folk medicine applied as a poultice for certain ailments
As a spice added to cooked rice dishes for flavor
As a material woven into baskets and sleeping mats
explanation: Besides chewing, the betel leaf was used in traditional folk medicine, for example as a poultice applied to treat certain ailments.
fact_tl: Bukod sa pagnganga, ginamit din noon ang dahon ng ikmo sa tradisyonal na panggagamot, halimbawa bilang pamahid sa ilang karamdaman, bagaman dapat itong gawin nang may pag-iingat.
fact_bis: Gawas sa pagnganga, ang dahon sa ikmo gigamit usab kaniadto sa tradisyonal nga tambal, pananglitan ingong haplas sa pipila ka sakit, bisan kinahanglan kining buhaton nga mabinantayon.

q: When you lift a book up to a high shelf, what kind of energy does it gain?
options: Kinetic energy, because it is moving upward
Chemical energy, stored in the material of the book
Potential energy, which can be released if the book falls
Thermal energy, from the warmth of your hands
explanation: When you lift an object up, you give it potential energy that can be released when it drops.
fact_tl: Kapag itinaas mo ang isang bagay, nagbibigay ka rito ng potential energy na maaaring ilabas kapag ito ay bumagsak.
fact_bis: Kon imong ibayaw ang usa ka butang, gihatagan nimo kini og potential energy nga mahimong gawason kon kini mahulog.

q: How does a jellyfish (a type of cnidarian) eat food and get rid of waste?
options: It has a separate mouth and anus like most animals
It absorbs nutrients directly through its skin without any opening
It uses the same single opening as both its mouth and its waste exit
It filters water through many small pores that line its body
explanation: A cnidarian has only one body opening that serves as both mouth and anus — food enters and waste exits through the same opening.
fact_tl: Ang cnidarian ay may iisang butas lamang na nagsisilbing bibig at puwit nang sabay. Pumapasok dito ang pagkain at sa parehong butas din ibinubuga ang dumi.
fact_bis: Ang cnidarian adunay usa ra ka lungag nga mao ang baba ug lubot dungan. Mosulod ang pagkaon dinhi, ug sa samang lungag usab mogawas ang hugaw.

q: Who created the Celsius temperature scale, and in what year?
options: Isaac Newton, an English physicist, in 1687
Gabriel Fahrenheit, a German physicist, in 1724
Anders Celsius, a Swedish astronomer, in 1742
Lord Kelvin, a Scottish scientist, in 1848
explanation: Anders Celsius, a Swedish astronomer, created the Celsius scale in 1742.
fact_tl: Si Anders Celsius, isang Swedish na astronomo, ang gumawa ng Celsius scale noong 1742.
fact_bis: Si Anders Celsius, usa ka Swedish nga astronomo, naghimo sa Celsius scale niadtong 1742.

q: What happens to micro-organisms in a pond when the pond dries up completely?
options: They float up into the air and travel to the nearest water source
They quickly change into a different form of life that needs no water
They die or go dormant until the water returns
They burrow deep into the soil where moisture is still available
explanation: Micro-organisms need water to live, so when a pond dries up, many die or go dormant until water returns.
fact_tl: Kailangan ng mikroorganismo ng tubig para mabuhay, kaya kapag natuyo ang lawa, marami sa kanila ang namamatay o natutulog hanggang bumalik ang tubig.
fact_bis: Ang mikroorganismo nanginahanglan og tubig aron mabuhi, mao nga kung mauga ang danaw, daghan kanila ang mamatay o matulog hangtod mobalik ang tubig.

q: Which part of the malunggay plant do people usually eat?
options: The roots
The bark
The leaves
The flowers
explanation: In malunggay, the plant part people usually eat is the leaves.
fact_tl: Sa malunggay, ang bahagi ng halamang madalas nating kainin ay ang mga dahon.
fact_bis: Sa malunggay, ang parte sa tanom nga atong kasagaran kan-on mao ang mga dahon.

q: How does electroplating protect a metal object from rusting?
options: It heats the metal surface until a hard oxide layer forms naturally
It uses electricity to deposit a thin protective metal coating onto the surface
It dissolves the outer layer of metal so a smoother rust-resistant core is exposed
It sprays a plastic film onto the metal that seals out air and moisture
explanation: Electroplating uses electricity to deposit a thin layer of a protective metal like chrome or nickel onto another metal surface to prevent corrosion.
fact_tl: Ang electroplating ay gumagamit ng kuryente para magdeposito ng manipis na patong ng protektibong metal (tulad ng chrome o nickel) sa ibabaw ng isa pang metal para pigilan ang korrosyon.
fact_bis: Ang electroplating naggamit og kuryente aron mag-deposito og manipis nga layer sa protektibong metal sama sa chrome o nickel sa ibabaw sa laing metal aron mapugngan ang korrosyon.

q: How far away from Earth is Polaris, the North Star?
options: About 4.3 light-years away
About 43 light-years away
About 433 light-years away
About 4,330 light-years away
explanation: Polaris is about 433 light-years away from Earth.
fact_tl: Ang Polaris ay nasa layong mga 433 taon-liwanag (light-years) mula sa Earth.
fact_bis: Ang Polaris mga 433 ka tuig-kahayag (light-years) ang gilay-on gikan sa Yuta.

q: Why are most of the Philippines' endemic freshwater turtles threatened today?
options: They are threatened by volcanic eruptions that destroy their river habitats
They are threatened by hunting for food and the pet trade
They are threatened by invasive fish species that eat their eggs
They are threatened by pollution from agricultural fertilizers in rivers
explanation: Most Philippine endemic freshwater turtle species are threatened by hunting for food and capture for the pet trade.
fact_tl: Ang Pilipinas ay may ilang endemic na uri ng freshwater turtle na nakatira sa mga ilog at lawa, ngunit karamihan ay nanganganib dahil sa pangangaso para sa pagkain at kalakal ng mga alaga.
fact_bis: Ang Pilipinas adunay pipila ka endemic nga freshwater turtle species nga nagpuyo sa mga suba ug lawa, apan ang kadaghanan nanganganib tungod sa pagbuno alang sa pagkaon ug pet trade.

q: What happens to the pitch of sound when a stretched rubber band is pulled even tighter?
options: The pitch gets lower because the rubber band vibrates more slowly
The pitch stays the same because the length of the rubber band does not change
The pitch gets higher because the rubber band vibrates faster
The rubber band stops making sound because it is stretched too tight
explanation: When a rubber band is pulled tighter, it vibrates faster and makes a higher-pitched sound.
fact_tl: Kapag mas hinihila o hinihigpitan ang isang goma na ginagawang gitara, mas mataas ang tono ng tunog na nalilikha nito dahil mas mabilis itong nanginginig.
fact_bis: Kon mas hugot ang goma nga gihimong gitara, mas taas ang tono sa tingog nga mahimo niini tungod kay mas paspas kini mokurog.

q: Why does a bouncing ball reach a lower height with each bounce?
options: Gravity pulls harder on the ball each time it hits the floor
The ball slowly loses air through its surface, making it lighter
Some of its energy turns into heat and sound at every bounce
The floor absorbs the ball's speed and stores it as electrical energy
explanation: Each time a ball bounces, some of its energy turns into heat and sound, so it rises a little lower each time.
fact_tl: Tuwing tumatalbog ang bola, mas mababa ang taas nito dahil naubos ang ilang enerhiya na nagiging init at tunog sa bawat pagtama.
fact_bis: Matag higayon nga mosumbalik ang bola, mas ubos kini moabot kay ang uban niini nga enerhiya mahimong kainit ug tingog sa matag bunal.

q: How does a bird control its speed and direction while flying?
options: By spinning its tail like a propeller to steer left or right
By flapping faster or slower without changing the shape of its wings
By changing the shape and spread of its wings during flight
By holding its legs out as brakes to slow down or turn
explanation: A bird changes the shape and spread of its wings while flying to control its speed and direction.
fact_tl: Binabago ng ibon ang hubog at lapad ng pakpak habang lumilipad para kontrolin ang bilis at direksyon nito.
fact_bis: Usbon sa langgam ang korte ug gilapdon sa iyang pako samtang molupad aron kontrolon ang katulin ug direksyon niini.

q: Joseph Priestley, who is credited with discovering oxygen, was a scientist from which country?
options: France
Germany
Scotland
England
explanation: Joseph Priestley, who discovered oxygen, was an English scientist.
fact_tl: Si Joseph Priestley, na tumuklas ng oxygen, ay isang Ingles (English) na siyentista.
fact_bis: Si Joseph Priestley, nga nakadiskobre sa oxygen, usa ka English nga siyentista.

q: Besides growing by budding, how do coral polyps reproduce sexually?
options: A single polyp splits itself in two, creating two identical copies
Polyps release eggs and sperm into the water, which join to form larvae that drift and settle
Adult polyps carry developing young inside a special pouch until they are ready to attach
Female polyps lay fertilized eggs directly onto the reef surface for other polyps to guard
explanation: Coral polyps release eggs and sperm into the water together on certain nights; these join to form larvae that drift before settling into a new home.
fact_tl: Bukod sa pagkopya sa sarili (budding), ang mga coral polyp ay sabay-sabay ding naglalabas ng itlog at sperm sa tubig sa ilang gabi ng taon; nagsasama ang mga ito para gumawa ng bagong batang coral na lalangoy bago mahanap ang sariling tirahan.
fact_bis: Gawas sa pagkopya sa kaugalingon (budding), ang mga coral polyp managsabay usab paggawas og itlog ug sperm sa tubig sa pipila ka gabii sa tuig; magsumpay kini aron mahimong batan-ong coral nga molutaw una mopuyo sa bag-ong puy-anan.

q: What causes the water level in mangrove areas to rise and fall with the tides?
options: Seasonal rainfall fills the mangrove channels and then slowly drains away
The roots of the mangrove trees pump water in and out of the ground
The gravity pull of the moon and sun on the ocean creates the tides
Wind pushes ocean water into shore areas and then pulls it back out
explanation: The gravity pull of the moon and sun on the ocean creates the tides that cause the water in mangrove areas to rise and fall.
fact_tl: Bakit umaakyat at bumababa ang tubig sa bakawan? Dahil sa hila (gravity) ng buwan at araw sa karagatan. Kapag malapit ang hila ng buwan sa isang bahagi ng dagat, doon tumataas ang tubig — ito ang nagbibigay ng tide na binubuhay ng bakawan.
fact_bis: Nganong mosaka ug mohubas man ang tubig sa bakhaw? Tungod sa bira (gravity) sa bulan ug adlaw sa kadagatan. Kung kusog ang bira sa bulan sa usa ka bahin sa dagat, didto mosaka ang tubig — kana ang taog nga gipuy-an sa bakhaw.

q: What holds water molecules together and explains water's high surface tension and high boiling point?
options: Covalent bonds that permanently link water molecules into chains
Ionic bonds formed when water loses electrons to nearby molecules
Hydrogen bonds — special attractions between the H of one molecule and the O of a neighbor
Magnetic forces between the oxygen atoms at the center of each molecule
explanation: Water molecules stick to each other through hydrogen bonds, which explain water's high surface tension and high boiling point.
fact_tl: Ang mga molekula ng tubig ay nagkakahawak sa isa't isa sa pamamagitan ng hydrogen bonds — espesyal na mga pagkakahawak sa pagitan ng H ng isang molekula at O ng kalapit. Ang mga hydrogen bonds na ito ang dahilan ng mataas na surface tension, specific heat, at boiling point ng tubig.
fact_bis: Ang mga molekula sa tubig nagkahawak sa usag-usa pinaagi sa hydrogen bonds — espesyal nga mga pag-akit tali sa H sa usa ka molekula ug sa O sa silingan. Kining hydrogen bonds nagpasabot sa taas nga surface tension, specific heat, ug boiling point sa tubig.

q: Why can we still see the sun for a short while after it has actually set below the horizon?
options: The sun's light reflects off the moon before reaching our eyes, adding extra time
Our eyes continue to see an afterimage of the sun even after it disappears
Light from the sun bends (refracts) as it passes through the atmosphere, making the sun appear higher than it really is
Clouds near the horizon act as mirrors that bounce the sun's light upward toward us
explanation: Because of refraction, the sun's light bends as it passes through the thick atmosphere, making the sun look higher than its real position even after it has set.
fact_tl: Dahil sa refraction, nakikita pa natin ang araw nang ilang sandali kahit lumubog na ito sa totoong posisyon. Yumuyuko ang liwanag ng araw habang dumadaan sa makapal na hangin ng atmospera, kaya parang nakaangat pa ito kaysa sa totoong lugar nito.
fact_bis: Tungod sa refraction, makita pa nato ang adlaw og pipila ka gutlo bisan og nisalop na kini sa tinuod niini nga nahimutangan. Mubawog ang kahayag sa adlaw samtang muagi sa baga nga hangin sa atmospera, maong morag mas taas pa kini kaysa sa tinuod niini nga dapit.

q: Why do oil and water not mix together?
options: Oil is lighter than water so it always floats, and floating layers can never mix
Oil molecules are much larger than water molecules so they cannot fit between them
Water molecules are polar and oil is nonpolar, so they do not attract each other and stay separate
Oil is solid at room temperature, while water is liquid, so they exist in different states
explanation: Oil and water do not mix because water molecules are polar while oil is nonpolar, so they do not attract each other and stay separate.
fact_tl: Hindi nahahalo ang langis at tubig dahil polar ang mga molekula ng tubig habang nonpolar ang langis, kaya hindi sila naghihilaan; nananatiling magkahiwalay sila sa halip na magtunaw.
fact_bis: Ang lana ug tubig dili magsagol kay polar ang mga molekula sa tubig samtang nonpolar ang lana, mao nga dili sila magbiraay; magpabilin silang bulag imbis matunaw.

q: What materials are traditionally used to weave a banig sleeping mat?
options: Thin strips of bamboo split from young stalks
Dried plant leaves such as pandan, buri, or tikog
Woven cotton or abaca cloth dyed with natural colors
Flattened pieces of rattan vine soaked in water
explanation: A banig mat is woven from dried plant leaves such as pandan, buri, or tikog, which are split and interlaced into a strong sleeping mat.
fact_tl: Ang banig ay hinahabi mula sa pinatuyong dahon ng mga halaman tulad ng pandan, buri, o tikog, na pinipilipit at pinagsasalit-salit upang maging matibay na higaan.
fact_bis: Ang banig gilala gikan sa giuga nga dahon sa mga tanom sama sa pandan, buri, o tikog, nga gipikas ug gisalapid aron mahimong lig-on nga higdaanan.

q: How does a lever allow you to lift a heavy object using less force?
options: It stores energy from your push and releases it all at once to overcome weight
It spreads the work over a longer distance, so the farther you are from the fulcrum the less force you need
It increases the speed of your push so the momentum is enough to move the heavy load
It reduces the weight of the object by supporting part of it on the ground
explanation: A lever spreads the work over a longer distance — the farther you push from the fulcrum, the less force you need to lift a heavy object.
fact_tl: Gumagana ang lever sa pamamagitan ng paghahati ng trabaho sa mas mahabang layo. Kapag mas malayo ka sa fulcrum, mas kaunting puwersa ang kailangan mo para buhatin ang mabigat na bagay. Para itong pinaparami ang lakas mo.
fact_bis: Ang lever molihok pinaagi sa pagbahin sa trabaho ngadto sa mas taas nga gilay-on. Kung mas layo ka sa fulcrum, mas gamay nga kusog ang imong gikinahanglan aron mag-alsa og bug-at. Sama ni sa pagdaghan sa imong kusog.

q: Why have some animals that live deep in dark caves lost their eyesight over time?
options: The cold temperature in caves causes the eyes to freeze and stop working
Predators inside caves always attack the eyes first, so blind animals survive longer
Eyesight is useless where there is no light, so eyes became unnecessary over generations
Cave water contains minerals that slowly dissolve the eyes of any animal living there
explanation: Some cave animals have lost their eyes because eyesight is useless where there is no light, so it was no longer needed over time.
fact_tl: Ang ilang hayop na tumitira sa loob ng madilim na kweba ay nawalan na ng mata o naging bulag sa paglipas ng panahon, dahil walang silbi ang paningin kung saan walang liwanag.
fact_bis: Ang ubang mananap nga nagpuyo sa sulod sa ngitngit nga langob nawad-an na og mata o nahimong buta sa paglabay sa panahon, kay walay pulos ang panan-aw kon walay kahayag.

q: Why do doctors choose a specific antibiotic for each infection rather than using just one type for everything?
options: Different antibiotics have different flavors so doctors match them to what the patient prefers
Antibiotics must be matched to the patient's age, and different ages need different medicines
Not every antibiotic works on every kind of bacteria, so the right one must be chosen
All antibiotics work the same way, but doctors change them to prevent the patient from getting bored
explanation: Doctors choose the right antibiotic for a specific bacteria because not every antibiotic works on every infection.
fact_tl: Pinipili ng doktor ang tamang antibiotiko para sa tiyak na bakterya, dahil hindi lahat ng antibiotiko ay tumatalab sa lahat ng impeksyon.
fact_bis: Pilion sa doktor ang saktong antibyotiko para sa piho nga bakterya, kay dili tanan nga antibyotiko molihok sa tanang impeksiyon.

q: What is the correct order of stages when growing rice?
options: Plant seedlings → let the field dry out → harvest green stalks
Scatter seeds in dry soil → flood the field after sprouting → harvest early
Plant seedlings → transplant into a flooded paddy → harvest when grain-heads turn golden
Flood the field first → plant seeds directly in water → harvest before the plant flowers
explanation: Rice grows in stages: planted as seedlings, transplanted into a flooded paddy, and harvested when the grain-heads turn golden.
fact_tl: Ang palay ay tumutubo sa ilang yugto: una itong itinatanim bilang punla, pagkatapos ay inililipat sa pinabahang palayan, at sa wakas ay umaani kapag naging ginto na ang mga uhay.
fact_bis: Ang humay motubo sa mga ang-ang: una kini itanom isip semilya, dayon ibalhin ngadto sa gibahaan nga palayan, ug sa kataposan anihon kon mahimong bulawan na ang mga uhay.

q: What is soil creep, and what are some signs that it is happening on a hillside?
options: A fast mudslide triggered by heavy rain, seen when large chunks of slope suddenly collapse
The fastest type of mass wasting, visible when whole sections of cliff fall into a valley
The slowest type of mass wasting, with signs like tilted trees, bent fences, and cracks in walls
A type of underground erosion where soil is washed into hidden caves beneath the slope
explanation: Soil creep is the slowest type of mass wasting, moving just a few millimetres per year; signs include tilted trees, bent fences, and cracks in walls.
fact_tl: Ang soil creep ay ang pinakabagal na uri ng mass wasting kung saan ang lupa ay dahan-dahang gumagalaw pababa ng dalisdis sa bilis na ilang millimeter bawat taon; ang mga tanda ng soil creep ay kinabibilangan ng mga nakatagilid na puno, bent fences, at mga bitak sa mga pader.
fact_bis: Ang soil creep mao ang pinaka-hinay nga klase sa mass wasting diin ang yuta hinay-hinay naglihok pababa sa dalisdis sa pipila ka millimeter matag tuig; ang mga tanda sa creep naglakip sa nakatilap nga mga kahon, bent fences, ug mga bitak sa mga pader.

q: Why does an ocean wave break and crash when it reaches shallow water near the shore?
options: The wave runs into cold water near the shore, which freezes its surface and causes it to collapse
The wind stops pushing the wave when it nears land, so the wave loses its forward motion and falls
The bottom of the wave slows down in shallow water and the crest grows taller until it topples over
The sandy bottom absorbs energy from the wave and makes it bounce back upward
explanation: When a wave reaches shallow water, its bottom slows down and the crest grows taller until it topples over and breaks as a surf wave.
fact_tl: Kapag ang alon ay umaabot sa mababaw na tubig malapit sa baybayin, bumabagal ang ilalim nito at tumataas ang taluktok hanggang sa ito ay tumagilid at pumutok bilang nasasakyang alon.
fact_bis: Kung ang balod moabot sa mabaw nga tubig duol sa baybayon, mohinay ang ubos niini ug motaas ang taluktok hangtod nga motakilid kini ug mobuto isip surf nga balod.

q: Where does the strongest lightning and rain in a typhoon come from?
options: From the large calm eye at the center of the typhoon
From the outer rain bands that spiral far away from the center
From the eyewall, which contains the tallest clouds in the storm
From high-altitude clouds above the typhoon that shed ice crystals downward
explanation: The clouds in the eyewall are among the tallest on Earth and are the source of the typhoon's strongest lightning and rain.
fact_tl: Ang mga ulap sa eyewall ay kabilang sa pinakamataas sa mundo, umaabot sa tuktok ng kalangitan na halos hindi na makaakyat pa ang hangin. Dito nagmumula ang pinakamalakas na kidlat at ulan ng buong bagyo.
fact_bis: Ang mga panganod sa eyewall maoy uban sa pinakataas sa kalibotan, moabot sa kinatumyan sa ubos nga kawanangan diin halos dili na makasaka ang hangin. Dinhi gikan ang pinakakusog nga kilat ug ulan sa tibuok bagyo.

q: Why do many Filipino farmers treat their carabao like a member of the family?
options: Because the carabao is a rare and expensive animal that needs careful protection
Because the carabao is loved for how much it helps with farm work and is even given a name
Because the government requires farmers to register and care for their carabao officially
Because the carabao guards the farm and the family from strangers at night
explanation: For many Filipino farmers, the carabao is like a member of the family — loved and even given a name because of how much it helps.
fact_tl: Para sa maraming magsasakang Pilipino, ang kalabaw ay parang kasama sa pamilya na minamahal at binibigyan pa ng pangalan dahil sa malaki nitong tulong.
fact_bis: Alang sa daghang mag-uumang Pilipino, ang kabaw sama sa membro sa pamilya nga ginamahal ug ginahatagan pa og ngalan tungod sa dako niini nga tabang.

q: Because the hummingbird is so small, what kinds of animals can hunt it?
options: Only large birds of prey like eagles and hawks can catch hummingbirds
Even large insects, spiders, or snakes can hunt hummingbirds because of their tiny size
Only cats and small mammals are fast enough to catch a hummingbird
Hummingbirds are too fast for any predator and are rarely caught
explanation: Because the hummingbird is so tiny, even large insects, spiders, or snakes can hunt it.
fact_tl: Dahil napakaliit ng hummingbird, kahit malalaking insekto, gagamba, o ahas ay maaaring manghuli nito. Kaya laging maingat at mabilis ang maliit na ibong ito.
fact_bis: Tungod kay gamay kaayo ang hummingbird, bisan ang dagkong insekto, lawa, o bitin makahimo sa pagdakop niini. Mao nga kanunay nga maampingon ug paspas kini nga gamay nga langgam.

q: Both the Philippines and Indonesia are archipelagos in Southeast Asia. Which one has more islands?
options: The Philippines has more islands than Indonesia
Indonesia has more islands than the Philippines
They have exactly the same number of islands
Neither is an archipelago — only one of them has multiple islands
explanation: Both the Philippines and Indonesia are archipelagos in Southeast Asia, but Indonesia has even more islands than the Philippines.
fact_tl: Ang Pilipinas at Indonesia ay parehong arkipelago sa Timog-Silangang Asya, pero mas marami pang pulo ang Indonesia kaysa Pilipinas.
fact_bis: Ang Pilipinas ug Indonesia parehong arkipelago sa Habagatan-Sidlakang Asya, apan mas daghan pa og pulo ang Indonesia kay sa Pilipinas.

q: Oil spills are dangerous to fish partly because oil floats on the water's surface and does what?
options: It blocks air from getting into the water, reducing the oxygen fish breathe
It makes the water too cold for fish to survive
It sinks to the ocean floor and buries the fish's food
It turns the water acidic and burns the fish's skin
explanation: Floating oil covers the surface and blocks air from entering the water, leaving fish and other sea animals without enough oxygen to breathe.
fact_tl: Dahil lumulutang ang langis at tumatakip sa ibabaw ng tubig, nahihirapan ang hangin na makapasok sa tubig. Kaya nawawalan ng sapat na oxygen ang mga isda at iba pang hayop sa dagat.
fact_bis: Tungod kay naglutaw ang lana ug motabon sa ibabaw sa tubig, mababagan ang hangin nga mosulod sa tubig. Mao nga makulangan og oxygen ang mga isda ug uban pang hayop sa dagat.

q: About how long does one year last on Jupiter compared to Earth?
options: About 12 Earth years
About 365 Earth days (the same as Earth)
About 30 Earth years
About 2 Earth years
explanation: Because Jupiter is much farther from the Sun, one year on Jupiter lasts about 12 Earth years.
fact_tl: Ang isang taon sa Jupiter ay tumatagal ng halos 12 taon ng Earth.
fact_bis: Ang usa ka tuig sa Jupiter molungtad ug mga 12 ka tuig sa Yuta.

q: Which organ does TWO jobs — making digestive enzymes AND making insulin to control blood sugar?
options: The pancreas
The liver
The stomach
The gallbladder
explanation: The pancreas acts as both an exocrine gland (making digestive enzymes) and an endocrine gland (making insulin and glucagon to control blood sugar).
fact_tl: Ang pancreas ay may dalawang pag-andar: bilang exocrine gland, ito ay gumagawa ng digestive enzymes; bilang endocrine gland, ito ay gumagawa ng insulin at glucagon na nagkokontrol ng blood sugar.
fact_bis: Ang pancreas adunay duha ka pag-andar: ingon exocrine gland nagpatubas kini ug digestive enzymes, ug ingon endocrine gland nagpatubas kini ug insulin ug glucagon aron makontrol ang mga antas sa blood sugar.

q: Why does practicing something over and over help you remember it better?
options: Repeating something makes the neuron connections in your brain grow stronger
Repeating something fills a special memory sac in your stomach
Repeating something shrinks your brain so information is closer together
Repeating something adds extra blood flow that stores the memory in your heart
explanation: When we repeat something, the neuron connections formed in the brain grow stronger, making those memories easier to recall.
fact_tl: Iniimbak natin ang mga alaala kapag bumubuo ng bagong koneksyon ang mga neuron sa utak. Lumalakas ang koneksyon kapag inuulit-ulit natin ang isang bagay, kaya mas madaling matandaan ang madalas nating ginagawa.
fact_bis: Tipigan nato ang mga panumduman kon ang mga neuron sa utok maghimo og bag-ong koneksyon. Molig-on ang koneksyon kon balik-balikon nato ang usa ka butang, mao nga mas sayon hinumduman ang kanunay natong buhaton.

q: Why do phone and TV screens get dusty so quickly when they are turned on?
options: The screen builds up a static charge that pulls tiny dust bits from the air
The screen heats up and causes dust particles to stick with glue
The fan inside the device blows dust outward onto the screen
The bright light from the screen attracts dust like moths to a flame
explanation: When a screen is on, it builds up a static charge that attracts and holds tiny dust particles from the surrounding air.
fact_tl: Bakit parang laging maraming alikabok sa screen ng TV o cellphone? Kapag bukas ang screen, nagkakaroon ito ng static charge, kaya hinihila nito ang maliliit na alikabok sa hangin at dumidikit ang mga ito. Kaya madalas mong punasan ito.
fact_bis: Ngano nga daw kanunay daghang abog sa screen sa TV o cellphone? Kung naka-on ang screen, magtigom kini og static charge, mao nga mobira kini sa gagmay nga abog sa hangin ug modikit kini. Mao nga kanunay nimo kining trapuhan.

q: Who was the first President of the Philippines?
options: Emilio Aguinaldo
Manuel Quezon
Andres Bonifacio
Jose Rizal
explanation: Emilio Aguinaldo was the first President of the Philippines.
fact_tl: Si Emilio Aguinaldo ang unang Pangulo ng Pilipinas.
fact_bis: Si Emilio Aguinaldo ang unang Presidente sa Pilipinas.

q: Why can visible light not be used to see objects that are extremely tiny?
options: Objects much smaller than the wavelength of light barely affect the light wave, so the light passes them as if they are not there
Visible light travels too fast to bounce off very small objects before it disappears
Very small objects absorb all colors of light, making them appear invisible
Visible light is only strong enough to reflect off large, flat surfaces like mirrors
explanation: When an object is much smaller than a light wave's wavelength, the wave is barely affected by it — which is why some things are too small to see with visible light.
fact_tl: Kapag ang isang bagay ay napakaliit kumpara sa wavelength ng isang alon, halos hindi ito naaapektuhan ng bagay, kaya't may mga bagay na napakaliit para makita gamit ang nakikitang liwanag.
fact_bis: Kung ang usa ka butang gamay kaayo kumpara sa wavelength sa usa ka balod, halos dili kini maapektuhan sa butang, mao nga adunay mga butang nga gamay ra kaayo aron makita gamit ang makita nga kahayag.

q: How do forests help reduce flooding in an area?
options: The soil and tree roots absorb rainwater slowly, preventing it from rushing away
The tree canopy evaporates all rain before it ever reaches the ground
Forests cool the air so much that rain turns back into clouds
Tree trunks act as walls that physically block floodwater from moving
explanation: Forests reduce flooding because their soil and roots soak up rainwater slowly, keeping it from rushing off and causing floods.
fact_tl: Tumutulong ang mga gubat na bawasan ang baha dahil sinisipsip ng lupa at ugat ang tubig-ulan nang dahan-dahan.
fact_bis: Ang mga lasang makatabang sa pagkunhod sa baha kay ang yuta ug gamot mosuyop sa tubig-ulan og hinay-hinay.

q: What is one of the most effective ways to keep viruses from getting into your body?
options: Washing your hands often with soap
Drinking cold water every hour
Wearing a hat when going outside
Eating spicy food to kill germs
explanation: Washing your hands often with soap is one of the best ways to prevent viruses from entering your body.
fact_tl: Ang madalas na paghuhugas ng kamay gamit ang sabon ay nakakatulong na hindi makapasok sa katawan ang virus.
fact_bis: Ang kanunay nga panghugas sa kamot gamit ang sabon makatabang nga dili makasulod sa lawas ang bayrus.

q: Both barnacles and mussels cling to rocks, but how are their methods different?
options: Barnacles use hard cement while mussels use thread-like fibers
Barnacles use thread-like fibers while mussels use hard cement
Barnacles use suction cups while mussels use sticky mucus
Barnacles dig into the rock while mussels use tiny claws
explanation: A barnacle secretes hard cement to stick to surfaces, while a mussel uses flexible thread-like fibers to hold on.
fact_tl: Parehong kumakapit sa bato ang barnacle at tahong, pero gumagamit ang barnacle ng tigas na pandikit habang ang tahong ay may parang mga sinulid na panghawak.
fact_bis: Parehong mokupot sa bato ang barnacle ug litob, apan ang barnacle mogamit og gahi nga pandikit samtang ang litob adunay murag mga hilo nga ihawid.

q: How are modern seismographs different from the old ones that used pen and paper?
options: Modern ones use electronic sensors that send data to a computer, making readings faster and more precise
Modern ones are larger machines that need a whole building to operate
Modern ones use a bucket of sand that shifts when the ground shakes
Modern ones rely on trained scientists who write down shaking by hand in real time
explanation: Today's seismographs use electronic sensors that send data to a computer, making earthquake readings much faster and more precise than old pen-and-paper versions.
fact_tl: Noong unang panahon, panulat at papel ang ginagamit ng seismograph, pero ngayon karamihan ay digital na: gumagamit ng electronic sensor na nagpapadala ng datos sa computer, kaya mas mabilis at mas tumpak ang pagbasa ng mga lindol.
fact_bis: Kaniadto, panulat ug papel ang gigamit sa seismograph, apan karon kadaghanan digital na: naggamit og electronic sensor nga magpadala og datos sa computer, mao nga mas paspas ug mas tukma ang pagbasa sa mga linog.

q: Stars appear to move from east to west each night AND different constellations appear in different months. What causes the nightly east-to-west movement?
options: Earth spinning on its axis each day
Earth orbiting the Sun over a year
The Moon pulling the stars sideways
The Sun's gravity rotating the stars around Earth
explanation: The nightly east-to-west drift of stars is caused by Earth spinning on its axis; the monthly change in visible constellations is caused by Earth's yearly orbit around the Sun.
fact_tl: May dalawang magkaibang galaw na dapat tandaan: tuwing gabi, mukhang gumagalaw ang mga bituin mula silangan patungong kanluran dahil umiikot ang Earth sa sarili nito; ngunit ang pagpapalit ng buong konstelasyon mula buwan-buwan ay dahil naman sa pag-ikot ng Earth sa Araw sa loob ng isang taon.
fact_bis: Adunay duha ka lahi nga lihok nga angay hinumdoman: matag gabii, ang mga bituon morag mokuyog gikan sa sidlakan paingon sa kasadpan tungod kay ang Earth molibot sa iyang kaugalingon; apan ang pag-ilis sa tibuok konstelasyon matag bulan mahitabo tungod kay ang Earth molibot sa Adlaw sulod sa usa ka tuig.

q: Why does keeping food in the refrigerator help it stay fresh longer?
options: The cold temperature slows down the microbes that make food spoil
The cold temperature adds a protective coating that seals out germs
The cold temperature removes all the water so bacteria cannot grow at all
The cold temperature kills every microbe inside the food instantly
explanation: Food spoils because microbes multiply in it; refrigeration slows those microbes down so food stays fresh longer.
fact_tl: Nabubulok ang pagkain dahil sa pagdami ng mga mikrobyo, kaya ang pagtatago sa lamig na refrigerator ay nagpapabagal sa kanila at nagpapatagal sa pagkain.
fact_bis: Madunot ang pagkaon tungod kay nagdaghan ang mga mikrobyo niini, busa ang pagtipig sa bugnaw nga refrigerator makapahinay kanila ug makapadugay sa kapresko sa pagkaon.

q: What happens when you accidentally touch something very hot?
options: You jerk your hand back even before you feel the pain
You freeze in place until your brain registers the pain
You feel the pain first and then slowly move your hand away
You shout first, then your hand moves after about one second
explanation: Touching something hot triggers a reflex — your hand pulls back automatically before the pain signal even reaches your brain.
fact_tl: Kapag nahawakan mo ang mainit na bagay, agad mong inuurong ang kamay bago mo pa maramdaman ang sakit.
fact_bis: Kung makahikap ka sa init nga butang, kalit nimong ibawi ang kamot sa dili pa nimo bati-on ang sakit.

q: What is one key difference between a lotus and a water lily?
options: Lotus leaves and flowers often stand high above the water, while water lily ones usually float on the surface
Lotus flowers always float flat on the water, while water lily flowers reach high above it
Lotus plants only grow in rivers, while water lilies only grow in ponds
Lotus and water lily are actually the same plant with different local names
explanation: Lotus leaves and flowers typically stand up high above the water, while water lily leaves and flowers usually rest right on the water's surface.
fact_tl: Magkaiba ang lotus at water lily: ang dahon at bulaklak ng lotus ay madalas na umaangat nang mataas sa ibabaw ng tubig, samantalang ang sa water lily ay karaniwang nakalapat lang sa tubig.
fact_bis: Lahi ang lotus ug ang water lily: ang dahon ug bulak sa lotus kasagaran motindog og taas ibabaw sa tubig, samtang ang sa water lily kasagaran nakahapa lang sa tubig.

q: Why should a dengue fever never be ignored, even when the temperature drops?
options: The time the fever drops can be the most critical and dangerous period of dengue
A dropping fever always means the patient is fully cured and safe
A dropping fever means dengue has spread to the lungs and needs surgery
A fever drop in dengue means the patient must eat spicy food to raise it again
explanation: Doctors track dengue fever carefully because the time when the fever drops can actually be the most critical stage, so a dengue fever should never be ignored.
fact_tl: Sa Pilipinas, ang lagnat ay mahalagang palatandaan para sa mga doktor lalo na sa dengue. Sinusubaybayan nila kung paano umaakyat at bumababa ang lagnat dahil minsan ang panahong bumababa na ito ang pinaka-kritikal — kaya hindi dapat ipagwalang-bahala ang dengue na lagnat.
fact_bis: Sa Pilipinas, ang hilanat usa ka importante nga timailhan para sa mga doktor ilabina sa dengue. Ilang ginabantayan kon unsaon pagsaka ug pagkanaog sa hilanat kay usahay ang panahon nga monaog na mao ang pinakakritikal — busa dili gyud angay ibaliwala ang hilanat sa dengue.

q: How does a millipede's eating change as it grows bigger?
options: A bigger millipede eats more rotting leaf material than a baby millipede does
A bigger millipede eats less because it stores energy in its extra legs
A millipede always eats the same amount no matter how big it gets
A baby millipede eats more because it needs food to grow its extra segments
explanation: As a millipede grows and adds more segments and legs, it also eats more rotting leaf material than when it was a baby.
fact_tl: Habang lumalaki ang millipede at nagdaragdag ng mga segment at paa, mas marami rin itong kinakain. Ang batang millipede ay maliit lang kumain, pero ang malaki ay mas maraming bulok na dahon ang nadudurog.
fact_bis: Samtang modako ang millipede ug magdugang og mga segment ug tiil, mas daghan usab kini mokaon. Ang batan-ong millipede gamay ra mokaon, apan ang dako mas daghan og malata nga dahon ang madugmok.

q: How do deep-sea communities near hydrothermal vents get their energy without any sunlight?
options: Bacteria use chemical energy from hydrogen sulfide through chemosynthesis to produce food
Animals at vents absorb heat energy directly from the hot water to survive
Special plants at the seafloor use bioluminescence instead of sunlight for photosynthesis
Vent animals eat food that sinks down from the sunlit ocean surface above them
explanation: Bacteria near hydrothermal vents use chemosynthesis — converting chemical energy from hydrogen sulfide — to produce food for the entire ecosystem, with no sunlight needed.
fact_tl: Sa paligid ng mga hydrothermal vent sa kailaliman ng dagat, ang mga bacterial community ay gumagamit ng chemosynthesis — ginagamit nila ang kemikal na enerhiya mula sa hydrogen sulfide imbes na sunlight — upang gumawa ng pagkain para sa buong ecosystem na walang solar energy.
fact_bis: Sa palibot sa mga hydrothermal vent sa kailalman sa dagat, ang mga bacterial community naggamit sa chemosynthesis — naggamit sa kemikal nga enerhiya gikan sa hydrogen sulfide imbes sa sunlight — aron magbuhat og pagkain alang sa tibuok ecosystem nga nagdagan nga walay solar energy.

q: What does a coral polyp do when it senses danger?
options: It pulls back down into the stony limestone cup it built around itself
It shoots venom from its tentacles and swims away quickly
It changes color to blend in with the surrounding reef
It puffs up its body to look bigger and scare away threats
explanation: Each coral polyp builds its own small stony limestone cup (corallite), and when danger comes it pulls back inside that cup to hide.
fact_tl: Bawat coral polyp ay nakaupo sa loob ng sarili nitong maliit na tasa o lukob na bato (limestone) na gawa nito; kapag may panganib, umuurong ito papasok sa tasang ito para magtago.
fact_bis: Ang matag coral polyp naglingkod sulod sa kaugalingong gamay nga tasa o lungag nga bato (limestone) nga gihimo niini; kung adunay kakuyaw, mosulod kini balik sa maong tasa aron motago.

q: Scientists think jellyfish populations are growing explosively in many oceans. What two things are believed to be causing this?
options: Ocean warming and overfishing of the fish that eat jellyfish
Increased rainfall and growing amounts of seaweed for jellyfish to eat
Cooler ocean temperatures and higher salt levels in the water
More plastic in the ocean that jellyfish use as shelter to breed
explanation: Scientists link jellyfish population explosions to ocean warming and overfishing of the fish species that normally eat jellyfish.
fact_tl: Ang mga jellyfish ay nagpapalaki ng kanilang bilang nang malaki sa maraming karagatan — ang mga siyentipiko ay naniniwala na ang pag-init ng karagatan at labis na pangingisda ng mga isda na kumakain ng jellyfish ay nagdudulot ng mga pagsabog na ito.
fact_bis: Ang mga jellyfish nagdaghan pag-ayo sa daghang karagatan — nagtuo ang mga siyentipiko nga ang pag-init sa karagatan ug sobrang pangisda sa mga isda nga mokaon sa jellyfish ang nagpahinabo niining mga pagsabak sa populasyon.

q: Which scientist studied radioactivity and discovered the elements radium and polonium?
options: Marie Curie
Albert Einstein
Isaac Newton
Louis Pasteur
explanation: Marie Curie is the scientist who studied radioactivity and discovered two new elements: radium and polonium.
fact_tl: Si Marie Curie ang nag-aral ng radyaktibidad at natuklasan ang dalawang bagong elemento, ang radium at polonium.
fact_bis: Si Marie Curie mao ang nagtuon sa radyaktibidad ug nakadiskobre sa duha ka bag-ong elemento, ang radium ug polonium.

q: What is a fever, and how does it help your body fight sickness?
options: A fever raises body temperature above 37.5°C and can help kill some microbes that are sensitive to heat
A fever lowers body temperature so viruses slow down and cannot replicate
A fever is always dangerous and should immediately be treated with ice water
A fever is caused by eating too much sugar, not by an infection
explanation: A fever is a natural immune response that raises body temperature above 37.5°C, which can help kill microbes that are sensitive to heat.
fact_tl: Ang lagnat ay nagpapataas ng temperatura ng katawan sa higit sa 37.5°C — ito ay isang natural na tugon ng immune system na tumutulong na patayin ang mga mikrobyo na sensitibo sa init.
fact_bis: Ang lagnat nagapataas sa temperatura sa lawas labaw sa 37.5°C — kini usa ka natural nga immune response nga nagtabang sa pagpatay sa pipila ka mga mikrobyo nga sensitibo sa init.

q: What does blood carry from the lungs to your muscles so they can work?
options: Oxygen
Carbon dioxide
Nutrients from food only
White blood cells to fight infection
explanation: Blood carries oxygen from the lungs to the muscles, giving them what they need to move.
fact_tl: Ang dugo ang nagdadala ng oxygen mula sa mga baga papunta sa iyong mga kalamnan.
fact_bis: Ang dugo maoy nagdala sa oxygen gikan sa mga baga padulong sa imong mga unod.

q: Even though jellyfish have venom, what animals still eat them?
options: Sea turtles and some large fish
Crabs and seahorses
Dolphins and whales
Sharks and electric eels
explanation: Despite their venom, jellyfish are eaten by sea turtles and some large fish, making them part of the ocean food web.
fact_tl: Kahit may kamandag ang dikya, may mga hayop na kumakain pa rin nito — gaya ng pawikan (sea turtle) at ilang malalaking isda. Bahagi ang dikya ng pagkain sa dagat.
fact_bis: Bisan adunay hilo ang dikya, naa gihapoy mga mananap nga mokaon niini — sama sa pawikan (sea turtle) ug pipila ka dagkong isda. Bahin ang dikya sa pagkaon sa dagat.

q: What are the two main threats to hawks and kites in the Philippines?
options: Loss of forests and illegal hunting
Ocean pollution and rising sea levels
Droughts and soil erosion
Disease and competition from invasive birds
explanation: Many Philippine hawks and kites are threatened by deforestation (loss of forests) and illegal hunting.
fact_tl: Maraming lawin at ibong mandaragit sa Pilipinas ang nanganganib dahil sa pagkawala ng kagubatan at iligal na pangangaso.
fact_bis: Daghang lawin ug langgam nga mananakmal sa Pilipinas ang nameligro tungod sa pagkawala sa kalasangan ug iligal nga pagpangayam.

q: Why do weaverbirds prefer to build their nests with fresh green grass instead of dry grass?
options: Fresh green grass is flexible and easier to weave than dry grass
Fresh green grass is heavier and makes the nest sturdier against wind
Fresh green grass smells good and attracts a mate to the nest
Fresh green grass is less likely to be eaten by insects
explanation: Weaverbirds prefer fresh green grass because it is flexible and easier to weave into their intricate nests, unlike dry grass which breaks more easily.
fact_tl: Mas gusto ng weaverbird ang sariwa at berdeng damo dahil malambot ito at madaling habihin kaysa sa tuyot na damo.
fact_bis: Mas gusto sa weaverbird ang lab-as ug lunhaw nga sagbot kay humok kini ug sayon habihon kaysa uga nga sagbot.

q: Why is it important to cook food thoroughly before eating it?
options: Cooking food well kills harmful bacteria inside it
Cooking food makes vitamins stronger and doubles them
Cooking food removes all fat so it becomes completely healthy
Cooking food adds a protective layer that stops germs from entering later
explanation: Cooking food well kills the harmful bacteria that can be present in raw or undercooked food.
fact_tl: Ang mabuting pagluluto ay pumapatay sa nakakasamang bakterya sa pagkain.
fact_bis: Ang maayong pagluto mopatay sa makadaot nga bakterya sa pagkaon.

q: Why is rubber used to make tires and shoe soles?
options: Rubber grips surfaces well and keeps them from slipping
Rubber is the lightest material available for these products
Rubber changes color when it gets wet, warning of slippery surfaces
Rubber bounces off the ground, making movement faster
explanation: Rubber grips surfaces well due to friction, which is why it is used on tires and shoe soles to prevent slipping.
fact_tl: Ang goma ay mahusay kumapit sa ibabaw, kaya ginagamit ito sa gulong at suwelas ng sapatos para hindi madulas.
fact_bis: Ang goma maayo mogunit sa ibabaw, mao nga gigamit kini sa ligid ug suwelas sa sapatos aron dili madakin-as.

q: Which ancient artifact found in Palawan shows that Filipinos have been making clay pottery for thousands of years?
options: The Manunggul jar
The Golden Tara of Agusan
The Laguna Copperplate Inscription
The Calatagan pot
explanation: The ancient Manunggul jar found in Palawan is made of clay pottery, showing that ceramics are thousands of years old in the Philippines.
fact_tl: Libo-libong taon na ang seramika; ang sinaunang Manunggul jar sa Palawan ay gawa sa luwad na palayok.
fact_bis: Liboan na ka tuig ang seramika; ang karaang Manunggul jar sa Palawan hinimo sa yutang kolonon nga kolon.

q: What is unusual about the ability to make light in deep-sea animals compared to animals at the ocean surface?
options: In the deep sea, most animals can produce their own light, making bioluminescence very common there
In the deep sea, only a few rare animals can glow, which is why they are hard to find
In the deep sea, animals absorb light from underwater volcanoes and reflect it
Bioluminescence is equally common at the surface and in the deep sea
explanation: Unlike at the surface, most deep-sea animals can produce their own light, making bioluminescence extremely common in the deep ocean.
fact_tl: Sa kailaliman ng dagat, karamihan sa mga hayop ay nakakagawa ng sariling liwanag, kaya napaka-karaniwan ng bioluminescence doon.
fact_bis: Sa kailaloman sa dagat, kadaghanan sa mga mananap makahimo sa ilang kaugalingong suga, mao nga komon kaayo ang bioluminescence didto.

q: Where and how was Jose Rizal executed on December 30, 1896?
options: He was executed by firing squad at Bagumbayan (now Luneta)
He was hanged at Fort Santiago in Intramuros
He was executed by firing squad at Plaza Miranda in Quiapo
He was drowned in Manila Bay by the Spanish authorities
explanation: Jose Rizal was executed by firing squad on December 30, 1896, at Bagumbayan (Luneta), which is now commemorated as Rizal Day.
fact_tl: Si Jose Rizal ay binaril at namatay noong Disyembre 30, 1896, sa Bagumbayan (Luneta) — kaya tinatawag itong Rizal Day.
fact_bis: Si Jose Rizal gipusil ug namatay niadtong Disyembre 30, 1896, sa Bagumbayan (Luneta) — mao nga gitawag kining Rizal Day.

q: Long ago, what animal's scent was used as an ingredient in perfume?
options: The civet
The pangolin
The tarsier
The monitor lizard
explanation: Long ago, perfume makers used the civet's special scent as an ingredient, but today many use lab-made substitutes so the animals are not disturbed.
fact_tl: Noong unang panahon, ginagamit ng mga gumagawa ng pabango ang espesyal na amoy ng musang bilang sangkap. Ngayon, mas marami nang gumagamit ng mga gawa-sa-laboratoryo na sangkap para hindi na kailangang abalahin ang mga hayop.
fact_bis: Kaniadto, ang mga maghihimo og pahumot mogamit sa espesyal nga baho sa musang isip sangkap. Karon, daghan na ang mogamit og hinimo-sa-laboratoryo nga sangkap aron dili na kinahanglan samokon ang mga mananap.

q: Even though a single fungus thread (hypha) is super thin, why is a fungus's underground network impressive in size?
options: When all the hyphae are put together, the mycelium can spread across several hectares of forest underground
All fungus threads join together above ground and form a visible mushroom that is very large
A single hypha can stretch for hundreds of kilometers because it grows in a straight line
Fungi grow vertically downward, reaching several kilometers into the earth's crust
explanation: Although each hypha is very thin, a fungus's mycelium — all its hyphae combined — can spread across several hectares underground, mostly hidden from view.
fact_tl: Kahit napakanipis ng bawat hyphae, kapag pinagsama-sama ang mycelium ng isang fungi, kaya nitong kumalat sa napakalawak na lugar sa ilalim ng lupa — minsan umaabot ng ilang ektarya sa isang gubat. Halos lahat ng ito ay nakatago, kaya hindi natin ito nakikita.
fact_bis: Bisan nipis kaayo ang matag hypha, kon tapunon ang mycelium sa usa ka fungi, makakatap kini sa hilabihan kalapad nga dapit sa ilalom sa yuta — usahay muabot og pipila ka ektarya sa usa ka lasang. Halos tanan niini natago, mao nga dili nato kini makita.

q: How do fruit bats help new trees grow in places far from the parent tree?
options: Bats fly far before dropping their waste, so seeds land far away from the parent tree
Bats carry seeds in their fur and shake them off when they groom themselves
Bats spit undigested seeds while flying, aiming them at open clearings
Bats bury seeds underground near rivers during their nightly migration
explanation: Because bats fly far before dropping their waste, seeds are deposited far from the parent tree, helping new trees grow in fresh places.
fact_tl: Dahil malayo ang nililipad ng paniki bago dumumi, naitatanim ang mga buto nang malayo sa puno na pinanggalingan, kaya tumutubo ang mga bagong puno sa ibang lugar.
fact_bis: Tungod kay layo ang gilupad sa kabog usa moiti, ang mga liso matanom nga layo sa inahang kahoy, mao nga motubo ang bag-ong mga kahoy sa laing dapit.

q: How does smoking harm the tiny hairs (cilia) inside your airways?
options: Smoking weakens and stills the cilia so they can no longer sweep out smoke and dust, causing dirt to build up in the lungs
Smoking makes cilia grow faster and longer until they block the airways completely
Smoking turns cilia into scar tissue that makes breathing slightly easier
Smoking has no effect on cilia but coats the lungs in tar so cilia cannot be seen
explanation: Cilia sweep dirt and smoke out of the airways, but smoking weakens and paralyzes them so that dirt builds up and the lungs work less well.
fact_tl: Sa loob ng baga may maliliit na buhok-buhok na tinatawag na cilia na naglilinis ng usok at alikabok. Pinapahina at pinapatigil ng paninigarilyo ang mga ito, kaya naiipon ang dumi at bumababa ang kakayahan ng baga.
fact_bis: Sa sulod sa baga adunay gagmay nga balahibo nga gitawag og cilia nga nagasilhig sa aso ug abog. Ang panigarilyo magpaluya ug magpahunong niini, busa magtipon ang hugaw ug mokunhod ang katakus sa baga.

q: What is special about how some kinds of stick insects reproduce?
options: The female can lay eggs that hatch without needing a male, and all the babies are female
The male builds a nest and guards eggs until they hatch without any help from the female
Both male and female stick insects hatch from the same single egg in pairs
Stick insects need two males and one female to produce eggs that will hatch
explanation: In some stick insect species, females can reproduce without a male — the eggs still hatch, and all the offspring are female.
fact_tl: Sa ilang uri ng stick insect, kaya ng babae na magkaroon ng anak kahit walang lalaki. Ang mga itlog ay napipisa pa rin at lahat ng anak ay babae rin.
fact_bis: Sa ubang matang sa stick insect, makahimo ang baye og anak bisan walay laki. Mapusa gihapon ang mga itlog, ug ang tanang anak baye usab.

q: In what year was Saturn's large moon Titan discovered?
explanation: Titan, Saturn's largest moon, was discovered in the year 1655.
fact_tl: Natuklasan ang Titan noong taong 1655.
fact_bis: Nadiskobre ang Titan niadtong tuig 1655.

q: Besides being sweet, what else is found in coconut water that helps keep our body balanced?
options: Tiny amounts of natural salts and minerals from the soil
Extra sugar that provides a burst of energy for sports
Proteins that build muscle when you drink it after exercise
Large amounts of vitamin C that prevent colds
explanation: Coconut water contains tiny amounts of natural salts and minerals absorbed from the soil, which help keep the water balance in our body.
fact_tl: Bukod sa tamis, ang tubig ng buko ay may maliliit na halaga ng natural na asin at minerals na galing sa lupa. Ito ang nakakatulong para mapanatiling balanse ang tubig sa ating katawan.
fact_bis: Gawas sa katam-is, ang tubig sa buko adunay gagmay nga kantidad sa natural nga asin ug minerals nga gikan sa yuta. Kini motabang aron mabalanse ang tubig sa atong lawas.

q: How can a gecko climb smooth glass without falling?
options: Its special toe-grip works on even the flattest, shiniest surfaces
Its claws are sharp enough to scratch tiny grooves into the glass
It produces a sticky glue from glands in its feet that dries on contact
It uses suction cups on its toes like those found on bathroom toys
explanation: A gecko's toe-grip works on smooth, flat surfaces — even glass — so it can climb walls and ceilings without falling.
fact_tl: Kayang umakyat ng gecko kahit sa makinis na salamin at maglakad nang patiwarik sa kisame. Hindi sila nahuhulog dahil ang dikit ng kanilang mga daliri ay gumagana kahit sa pinakapatag at pinakamakintab na ibabaw na walang mahahawakan.
fact_bis: Makasaka ang gecko bisan sa hamis nga bildo ug makalakaw nga balit-ad sa kisame. Dili kini mahulog kay ang pagdikit sa iyang mga tudlo molihok bisan sa pinakapatag ug pinakasinaw nga bahin nga walay makuptan.

q: Where does a female grasshopper lay her eggs and how does she protect them?
options: She places them underground inside a hardened pouch called an egg pod
She glues them to the underside of leaves wrapped in silk
She carries them on her back in a sticky mass until they hatch
She buries them one by one in the soil and covers each with a leaf
explanation: The female grasshopper lays her eggs underground grouped inside a hardened egg pod that protects them until they hatch.
fact_tl: Ang inahing tipaklong ay naglalagay ng mga itlog sa ilalim ng lupa, nakatipon sa isang parang sako (egg pod) na tumigas para maprotektahan ang mga itlog hanggang sa pumisa.
fact_bis: Ang inahan nga apan magbutang sa iyang mga itlog ilalom sa yuta, gitipon sa usa ka murag puyo (egg pod) nga migahi aron mapanalipdan ang mga itlog hangtod mapusa.

q: Which group of foods gives you energy to play and study?
options: Go foods such as rice, bread, and sweet potato (kamote)
Grow foods such as meat, fish, and eggs
Glow foods such as fruits and vegetables
Slow foods such as candy and softdrinks
explanation: Go foods — like rice, bread, sweet potato, corn, and potatoes — give us the energy we need to play and study.
fact_tl: Ang Go foods ay nagbibigay sa atin ng lakas (energy) para makapaglaro at makapag-aral. Halimbawa nito ang kanin, tinapay, kamote, mais, at patatas.
fact_bis: Ang Go foods naghatag kanato og kusog (energy) aron makaduwa ug makatuon. Mga pananglitan niini ang kan-on, tinapay, kamote, mais, ug patatas.

q: How is a baby stick insect different from a baby butterfly?
options: A baby stick insect looks like a tiny adult and has no caterpillar or cocoon stage
A baby stick insect spins a silky cocoon just like a caterpillar does
A baby stick insect hatches without legs and grows them slowly like a caterpillar
A baby stick insect is completely white and only gets its color after forming a cocoon
explanation: Unlike a butterfly, a stick insect skips the caterpillar and cocoon stages — its baby (nymph) looks like a tiny version of the adult and just grows bigger.
fact_tl: Hindi tulad ng paru-paro, walang yugto na uod o pupa ang stick insect. Ang sanggol nito ay parang maliit na bersyon na ng matanda, at unti-unti lang itong lumalaki.
fact_bis: Dili sama sa alibangbang, ang stick insect walay yugto nga ulod o pupa. Ang gamay niini morag gamay nga bersyon na sa hamtong, ug hinay-hinay lang kini modako.

q: What body of water separates the islands of Mindanao and Leyte, and what is it known for?
options: The Surigao Strait, known for its strong water currents
The San Bernardino Strait, known for its calm, clear waters
The Basilan Strait, known for being the deepest channel in the Philippines
The Verde Island Passage, known for its strong tidal currents between Luzon and Mindoro
explanation: The Surigao Strait separates Mindanao from Leyte and is well known for its strong water currents.
fact_tl: Ang Kipot ng Surigao ay naghihiwalay ng Mindanao at Leyte at kilala sa malakas na agos ng tubig nito.
fact_bis: Ang Kipot Surigao nagseparar sa Mindanao gikan sa Leyte ug bantog sa kusog nga mga koriyente sa tubig.

q: What worldwide agreement was made in 1987 to protect the ozone layer?
options: The Montreal Protocol, which banned chemicals that destroy ozone
The Kyoto Protocol, which limited carbon dioxide from factories
The Paris Agreement, which set targets for reducing global warming gases
The Geneva Convention, which protected rainforests from being cut down
explanation: In 1987, the Montreal Protocol was signed by almost every country, banning ozone-destroying chemicals; as a result, the ozone layer is slowly recovering.
fact_tl: Noong 1987, halos lahat ng bansa sa mundo ay sumang-ayon sa kasunduang tinatawag na Montreal Protocol para ipagbawal ang mga kemikal na sumisira sa ozone. Dahil dito, dahan-dahan nang gumagaling ang ozone layer.
fact_bis: Niadtong 1987, halos tanang nasod sa kalibutan miuyon sa kasabotan nga gitawag og Montreal Protocol aron idili ang mga kemikal nga muguba sa ozone. Tungod niini, hinay-hinay nang naayo ang ozone layer.

q: Why can some plastics be recycled but not others?
options: Some plastics soften and melt when heated, so they can be remolded into new things
Some plastics are colored and the dye can only be removed by melting them
Some plastics are thicker and only thick materials can be melted for recycling
All plastics can be recycled, but some are just too expensive to collect
explanation: Certain plastics — called thermoplastics — soften and melt when heated, making it possible to remold them into new objects and recycle them.
fact_tl: Ang ilang plastik ay lumalambot at natutunaw kapag pinainit, kaya puwede itong hubuging muli sa bagong bagay — ito ang dahilan kung bakit may mga plastik na puwedeng i-recycle.
fact_bis: Ang ubang plastik mohumok ug matunaw kon initon, mao nga mahimo kining hulmahon pag-usab ngadto sa bag-ong butang — mao kini ang hinungdan nganong ang ubang plastik mahimong i-recycle.

q: What government agency in the Philippines operates a network of seismographs across the country?
options: PHIVOLCS
PAGASA
DOST
DENR
explanation: PHIVOLCS runs many seismograph stations spread across the Philippines and can determine the location and strength of an earthquake within minutes.
fact_tl: Sa Pilipinas, ang PHIVOLCS ang nagpapatakbo ng maraming seismograph na nakakalat sa buong bansa; mula sa mga istasyong ito, nalalaman nila kung saan at gaano kalakas ang isang lindol nang ilang minuto lang.
fact_bis: Sa Pilipinas, ang PHIVOLCS maoy nagpadagan sa daghang seismograph nga nagkatag sa tibuok nasod; gikan niini nga mga estasyon, mahibaw-an nila kung asa ug unsa kakusog ang linog sulod sa pipila lang ka minuto.

q: Where does the white frost inside a freezer come from?
options: Water vapor from the air settles on the cold freezer walls and freezes directly into ice
Liquid water from food inside the freezer drips and freezes on the walls
The freezer produces its own ice crystals when it reaches very low temperatures
Frost forms when melted ice cream refreezes and coats the inside of the freezer
explanation: Frost on freezer walls forms when water vapor in the air settles onto the cold surface and freezes directly — this is an example of freezing that does not start from liquid water.
fact_tl: Ang puting frost sa dingding ng freezer ay galing sa singaw ng tubig sa hangin na namumuo at nagyeyelo agad sa malamig na ibabaw. Ito ay isang halimbawa ng pagyeyelo na hindi galing sa likidong tubig.
fact_bis: Ang puti nga frost sa bongbong sa freezer naggikan sa alisngaw sa tubig sa hangin nga mopahimutang ug mag-yelo dayon sa bugnaw nga ibabaw. Usa kini ka pananglitan sa pag-yelo nga dili naggikan sa likidong tubig.

q: How can certain mutations in a cell lead to cancer?
options: Mutations can cause cells to divide without control, forming a mass of abnormal cells
Mutations shrink cells so much that they can no longer carry oxygen through the body
Mutations make cells too large to pass through blood vessels, blocking circulation
Mutations cause healthy cells to fuse together into one giant cell that crowds organs
explanation: Some mutations cause cells to divide without control, which can lead to cancer; exposure to certain chemicals and radiation increases the risk of these mutations.
fact_tl: Ang ilang mutation sa selula ay maaaring magdulot ng kanser, kung saan walang-kontrol na nagdadami ang selula; pinapataas ng pagkakalantad sa ilang kemikal at radiation ang tsansa ng ganitong mutation.
fact_bis: Ang pipila ka mutation sa selula mahimong mosangpot sa kanser, diin ang mga selula magdaghan nga walay kontrol; ang pagkaladlad sa pipila ka kemikal ug radiation makadugang sa kahigayonan sa maong mutation.

q: What is the momentum of an object that is sitting completely still?
options: Zero, because its speed is zero
The same as its weight in kilograms
Half its mass, because it has resting energy
Depends on how heavy the object is
explanation: An object at rest has zero momentum because momentum depends on speed, and a stationary object has zero speed.
fact_tl: Ang isang bagay na nakatigil at hindi gumagalaw ay walang momentum dahil zero ang bilis nito.
fact_bis: Ang usa ka butang nga naghunong ug wala maglihok walay momentum kay zero ang tulin niini.

q: How fast does sea level rise each year?
options: A few millimeters each year
About one meter each year
About ten centimeters each year
Several meters each decade
explanation: Sea level rises slowly — only a few millimeters per year — but the total adds up significantly over time.
fact_tl: Ang dagat ay tumataas nang dahan-dahan, ilang milimetro bawat taon, pero patuloy itong nag-iipon.
fact_bis: Ang dagat mosaka hinay-hinay, pipila ka milimetro matag tuig, apan magpadayon kini sa pagtigom.

q: Which disease can spread through contaminated floodwater after a flood?
options: Leptospirosis
Malaria
Dengue fever
Chickenpox
explanation: Leptospirosis is one of the diseases that can spread through contaminated floodwater after flooding recedes.
fact_tl: Pagkatapos ng baha, ang mga pisikal na peligro (tulad ng malalim na tubig) ay kaagapay ng mga panganib sa kalusugan; ang leptospirosis, dyarya, at iba pang sakit ay maaaring kumalat sa pamamagitan ng maruming tubig-baha.
fact_bis: Pagkahuman sa baha, ang mga pisikal nga peligro (sama sa lawom nga tubig) kanunay adunay mga panganib sa kalusugan; ang leptospirosis, nati-asan, ug uban pang mga sakit mahimong mokatag pinaagi sa hugaw nga tubig-baha.

q: What happens to oil when you cool it down?
options: It becomes thicker and flows more slowly
It becomes thinner and flows more quickly
It evaporates into a gas
It breaks apart into separate layers
explanation: When you cool a liquid like oil, it becomes thicker and flows more slowly because cooling increases its viscosity.
fact_tl: Kapag pinalamig mo ang likido tulad ng mantika, ito ay nagiging mas malapot at mas mabagal dumaloy.
fact_bis: Kung palamigon nimo ang likido sama sa lana, mahimo kining mas baga ug mas hinay modagayday.

q: When does the katala (Philippine cockatoo) raise the crest on top of its head?
options: When it is alarmed, excited, or threatened
Only when it wants to attract a mate
Only when it is sleeping
Only when it is searching for food
explanation: The katala raises its crest when it is alarmed, excited, or threatened by another animal.
fact_tl: Ang katala ay nagtatayo ng crest sa tuktok ng ulo nito kapag siya ay nababahala, nasasabik, o nililipol ng ibang hayop.
fact_bis: Ang katala nagtindog sa crest sa ibabaw sa ulo niini kung siya mahadlok, nasaligon, o gikulbaan sa ubang mananap.

q: Which of these reflexes can a person voluntarily control for a short time?
options: Blinking
Sneezing
A knee-jerk reaction
Pupil dilation in bright light
explanation: Blinking is one of the few reflexes a person can consciously control for a short while, though the reflex eventually takes over again on its own.
fact_tl: Karamihan ng reflex ay talagang hindi mapigilan, pero may ilang tulad ng pagkurap o paghinga na pansamantala mong makokontrol. Pero kahit ito, babalik pa rin sa sarili nito kapag tumagal — kaya hindi mo talaga kayang labanan nang tuluyan.
fact_bis: Kadaghanan sa reflex tinuod nga dili mapugngan, apan adunay pipila sama sa pagpamilok o pagginhawa nga matandi nimo og kontrol sa makadiyot. Bisan pa niini, mobalik gihapon kini sa kaugalingon niini sa paglabay sa panahon — mao nga dili gyud nimo kini mabuntog hangtod sa kataposan.

q: How does a microwave oven heat food?
options: Its waves make water molecules in the food vibrate
It uses hot air to warm the outside of the food
It produces flames that heat the food directly
It uses infrared light to melt the food's surface
explanation: A microwave heats food by making the water molecules inside the food vibrate, which produces heat.
fact_tl: Umiinit ang pagkain sa microwave dahil pinagagalaw ng mga alon nito ang mga molekula ng tubig sa pagkain.
fact_bis: Ang microwave moinit sa pagkaon tungod kay ang mga balod niini magpalihok sa mga molekula sa tubig sa pagkaon.

q: How did dinosaurs reproduce?
options: They laid eggs
They gave birth to live young like mammals
They divided into two like single-celled organisms
They released spores into the environment
explanation: Like many reptiles today, dinosaurs laid eggs, and scientists have found fossils of dinosaur eggs to prove this.
fact_tl: Tulad ng maraming reptilya ngayon, ang mga dinosaur ay nangingitlog at may natagpuang fossil ng kanilang mga itlog.
fact_bis: Sama sa daghang reptilya karon, ang mga dinosaur nangitlog, ug nakakaplag pa gani ang mga siyentista og fosil sa mga itlog sa dinosaur.

q: Why should you crawl low when escaping a building fire?
options: Hot smoke rises, so cleaner air stays near the floor
The floor is the fastest path to an exit
Crawling protects you from falling debris
The fire always burns from the top downward
explanation: Hot smoke rises, so the air near the floor is cleaner, making it safer to crawl low when escaping a fire.
fact_tl: Pumapailanlang ang mainit na usok, kaya gumapang ka nang mababa kung saan mas malinis ang hangin habang lumalabas sa sunog.
fact_bis: Mosaka ang init nga aso, mao nga kamang ka ubos diin mas limpyo ang hangin samtang mogawas sa sunog.

q: If you feel tired and hungry, what should you do first?
options: Eat real food
Take a vitamin supplement
Drink an energy drink
Rest and wait for the feeling to pass
explanation: Vitamins are not a substitute for real food — if you are hungry and tired, you need to eat first because vitamins alone cannot instantly restore your energy.
fact_tl: May maling akala na kapag pagod ka, uminom ka lang ng bitamina at babalik agad ang lakas. Ang totoo, kung gutom ka, kailangan mo munang kumain. Ang bitamina ay hindi pamalit sa tunay na pagkain.
fact_bis: Naay sayop nga pagtuo nga kung kapoy ka, mag-inom lang og bitamina ug mobalik dayon ang kusog. Ang tinuod, kung gigutom ka, kinahanglan una nimong mokaon. Ang bitamina dili puli sa tinuod nga pagkaon.

q: Why can you see far more stars from the countryside than from a city?
options: City lights brighten the night sky and hide the stars
City buildings block the view of the sky
The atmosphere is thicker above cities
Stars only appear over areas with less population
explanation: Light pollution from cities brightens the night sky, making it hard to see stars — so far more are visible in rural areas away from city lights.
fact_tl: Ang light pollution mula sa mga lungsod ay nagpapalabaw ng langit at nagpapahirap na makita ang mga bituin sa gabi — kaya mas maraming mga bituin ang nakikita sa mga lugar na malayo sa lunsod.
fact_bis: Ang light pollution gikan sa mga lungsod nagapasilaw sa gabii nga langit ug nagahimo nga lisod ang pagkita sa mga bituon — mao nang mas daghang mga bituon ang makita sa mga lugar nga layo sa mga suga sa lungsod.

q: Why was the first air conditioner invented?
options: To control humidity in a printing plant
To keep office workers cool in summer
To store food at low temperatures
To help people sleep better at night
explanation: Willis Carrier first built the air conditioner to control humidity in a printing plant, not to cool people.
fact_tl: Ginawa muna ni Willis Carrier ang air conditioner para kontrolin ang halumigmig (humidity) sa isang imprenta, hindi para palamigin ang tao.
fact_bis: Gihimo una ni Willis Carrier ang air conditioner aron kontrolon ang halumigmig (humidity) sa usa ka imprenta, dili aron palamigon ang tawo.

q: How does having a regular daily routine help you?
options: It helps reduce stress
It guarantees you will get top grades
It prevents you from getting sick
It makes you need less sleep
explanation: Having a steady daily routine — like regular sleep and study times — helps reduce stress.
fact_tl: Ang pagkakaroon ng maayos na rutina araw-araw — gaya ng tamang oras ng tulog at pag-aaral — ay tumutulong bawasan ang stress.
fact_bis: Ang pagbaton og maayong rutina matag adlaw — sama sa hustong oras sa katulog ug pagtuon — makatabang sa pagkunhod sa stress.

q: In a force diagram, what does the length of an arrow represent?
options: The strength of the force
The direction of the force
The speed of the moving object
The mass of the object
explanation: Forces are shown using arrows where the length stands for the strength (magnitude) and the point shows the direction.
fact_tl: Ipinapakita ang mga pwersa gamit ang mga palaso, kung saan ang haba ay para sa lakas at ang turo ay para sa direksyon.
fact_bis: Ang mga pwersa gipakita gamit ang mga pana, diin ang gitas-on nagrepresentar sa kusog ug ang tumoy nagpakita sa direksyon.

q: Why does the body raise its temperature during an infection?
options: To slow the growth of bacteria and viruses
To speed up digestion and absorb medicine faster
To signal other people that you are sick
To increase the production of saliva
explanation: Fever is a natural defense; elevated body temperature slows the growth of many bacteria and viruses and activates some immune system components.
fact_tl: Ang lagnat ay isang natural na depensa ng katawan — ang mataas na temperatura ay pumipigil sa paglaki ng maraming bacteria at virus at nagpapalakas ng ilang bahagi ng immune system.
fact_bis: Ang lagnat usa ka natural nga depensa sa lawas — ang taas nga temperatura nagpahinay sa paglaki sa daghang bakterya ug virus ug nagpaaktibo sa pipila ka bahin sa immune system.

q: Why are scientists able to predict exactly when a solar or lunar eclipse will happen?
options: Because the Earth and Moon move in steady, regular paths
Because eclipses are created artificially in a laboratory
Because every eclipse is identical to the previous one
Because the Sun's position never changes
explanation: Scientists can predict the date of an eclipse far in advance because the Earth and Moon move in steady, regular ways.
fact_tl: Mahuhulaan ng mga siyentista nang maaga ang petsa ng eclipse dahil pare-pareho ang galaw ng Lupa at Buwan.
fact_bis: Matagna sa mga siyentista ang petsa sa eklipse daan kay ang Yuta ug Bulan adunay regular ug kanunay nga paglihok.

q: Why is the pangolin considered one of the most endangered mammals in the world?
options: It is heavily hunted for its scales and meat
Its natural habitat is almost entirely underwater
It cannot reproduce in the wild
Pollution has destroyed all its food sources
explanation: The pangolin is one of the most heavily trafficked animals in the world, hunted for its scales and meat, making it critically endangered.
fact_tl: Ang pangolin ay isa sa pinakamalubhang nameligrong hayop dahil labis itong hinuhuli para sa kaliskis at karne nito.
fact_bis: Ang pangolin usa sa labing grabe nga nameligrong hayop tungod kay sobra kini nga gipangdakop alang sa iyang himbis ug unod.

q: What is soil liquefaction?
options: When earthquake shaking makes water-saturated sandy soil behave like a liquid
When lava melts the top layer of soil during a volcanic eruption
When soil turns to dust after a long dry season
When ocean water floods underground soil during a tsunami
explanation: Soil liquefaction happens when strong earthquake shaking causes water in saturated sandy soil to act like a liquid, causing buildings above to sink or tilt.
fact_tl: Ang soil liquefaction ay nangyayari kapag ang malakas na lindol ay nagpapaikot ng tubig sa saturated sandy soil, na ginagawa itong parang likido; ang mga gusali sa ibabaw ay maaaring lumubog o lumingid, at ang mga manhole ay maaaring tumaas.
fact_bis: Ang soil liquefaction mahitabo kon ang kusog nga pagyanig sa lindol nagpaikot sa tubig sa saturated sandy soil, naghimo niini nga sama sa likido; ang mga gusali sa ibabaw mahimong mosalod o maalinggaw, ug ang mga manhole cover mahimong mosaka.

q: Who is credited with adding pedals to the bicycle around 1839?
options: Kirkpatrick Macmillan
James Watt
Alexander Graham Bell
Isaac Newton
explanation: Kirkpatrick Macmillan, a Scottish inventor, is credited with adding pedals to the bicycle around 1839.
fact_tl: Si Kirkpatrick Macmillan, isang Scottish, ang sinasabing nagdagdag ng mga pedal sa bisikleta noong mga 1839.
fact_bis: Si Kirkpatrick Macmillan, usa ka Scottish, ang giila nga nagdugang og mga pedal sa bisikleta niadtong mga 1839.

q: Why is rinsing your hands with water alone not enough to remove germs?
options: Water cannot lift the oil that germs cling to — you need soap
Water is not hot enough to kill germs
Germs are too heavy to be washed away by water
Water makes germs stick to the skin more strongly
explanation: Water alone cannot lift the oil where germs cling — you need soap to truly remove germs from your hands.
